books.title: Dungeon Crawler Carl
books.blurb: Earth is foreclosed on, and the only humans left standing are the ones who happened to be outside. Carl goes down into the dungeon barefoot, carrying a cat.

books.title: Carl's Doomsday Scenario
books.blurb: The Over City is the first floor that behaves like a place rather than a level — and Carl picks up a bomb he can never put down.

books.title: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook
books.blurb: Every subway on Earth, welded into one knot of moving trains — and a manual left behind by the crawlers of an earlier season.

books.title: The Gate of the Feral Gods
books.blurb: Sealed pocket worlds, a portable gate that opens onto things which should not be given doors, and the discovery that the NPCs are people.

books.title: The Butcher's Masquerade
books.blurb: Wealthy aliens buy licences to hunt crawlers for sport. Carl's answer is to hunt them back, on camera.

books.title: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride
books.blurb: A floor that runs on cards, built out of Earth's own dead, where people become playable pieces — and Mordecai's past stops being backstory.

books.title: This Inevitable Ruin
books.blurb: Nine armies, thirty days, one castle, and no respawns. The floor where the dungeon's props declare independence on live galactic television.

books.title: A Parade of Horribles
books.blurb: A racing floor with a worsening track, a system that has started to glitch, and a coming-out party for the ages.

floors.name: The First Floor
floors.premise: Dirt, corridors and safe rooms beneath the ruins of Earth. The tutorial floor, where the survivors learn the rules and how lethal they are.
floors.recap: Dirt, corridors and safe rooms, and the discovery that the tutorial is lethal. Carl comes down in a leather jacket, heart boxers and his ex-girlfriend's pink Crocs; within the hour he has a Goblin Pass Tattoo and a Trollskin Shirt. Donut eats an Enhanced Pet Biscuit and wakes up talking, takes party leadership on stat points, renames the party after herself, and equips the Crown of the Sepsis Whore without reading the warning — quietly enrolling herself in a royal succession eight floors below. Mordecai, an indentured Borant guide who was once a crawler himself, starts teaching them the rules production would rather they learned too late to use.

floors.name: The Second Floor
floors.premise: Open ground, spawn limits and the first real bosses. The floor where the party takes its final shape and the audience starts paying attention.
floors.recap: Where the party takes its final shape. Carl and Donut find Mongo — a level-1 pet-class mob, seven inches of pink downy feathers — locked in a cage in a secret pet reward room, and Donut wins him over by teaching him to open Brindle Grubs. From this floor the Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph leaves Carl's bare feet permanently shiny, which the audience adores. The thesis of the first book lands here: the dungeon rewards spectacle and punishes decency, unless you can make decency spectacular.

floors.name: The Over City
floors.premise: The Over City: a colossal ruin built on top of itself, cut into themed districts and run by NPC factions. The first floor that behaves like a place rather than a level.
floors.recap: A colossal ruin built on top of itself, cut into themed districts and run by NPC factions. Class selection happens here: Carl takes Primal and the unique Compensated Anarchist, Donut takes Cat and Former Child Actor, and on Odette's advice they manoeuvre Mordecai into becoming Donut's manager — an appointment that had to look like an accident. Katia, ten levels behind and left behind by the Daughters, is taken into the Royal Court. The Desperado Club opens. During the Fools Who Broke the Glass Quest, Carl builds Carl's Doomsday Scenario by wrapping a Sheol Glass Reaper Case around an exploding Soul Crystal — a 45-kilometre blast he can never put down.

floors.name: The Iron Tangle
floors.premise: The Iron Tangle — every subway system on Earth welded into one impossible knot of moving trains. A puzzle the size of a continent, and the trains do not stop.
floors.recap: Every subway system on Earth welded into one impossible knot of moving trains — a puzzle the size of a continent, and the trains do not stop. Carl becomes the twenty-fifth holder of The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook and learns that Earth is not the first season and that resistance to the show has a written tradition. Maggie My returns as a Scree parasite riding another crawler; Frank dies of it, and Mongo finishes her. Boxes and achievements get dramatically harder from this floor on. The Tangle cannot be solved alone — beating it takes hundreds of crawlers coordinating at once, which is exactly what production exists to prevent.

floors.name: The Bubbles
floors.premise: The survivors are split into sealed pocket worlds, each with its own biome, its own civilisation and its own way to kill you. Moving between them means portals.
floors.recap: The survivors are split between sealed pocket worlds. Buried in the Necropolis of Anser is the Gate of the Feral Gods, an artifact so far above this floor's grade that the AI times out reconciling the conflict. Carl collects its three pieces from Henrik the Changeling, Commandant Kane and Ghazi, and assembles it trapped at the bottom of the water quadrant inside the city boss Lusca — taking himself, Katia and Tran to the surface outside the pazuzu town of Pandinus and dragging an ocean through behind them. A feral god comes out when the portal shuts, and the true pantheon sends deities rampaging across the popped bubbles in answer. Katia turns the linked watches into a reverse compass and starts mapping the ninth floor. Seven factions sue for the Gate and lose. Carl, falling out of a burning plane with Quan Ch on him, takes Emberus as his patron and throws a celestial grenade.

floors.name: The Hunting Grounds
floors.premise: The Hunting Grounds. Wealthy aliens buy licences, walk into the dungeon and kill crawlers for sport, with a full broadcast package.
floors.recap: Wealthy aliens buy licences and come in to kill crawlers for sport. Carl takes the Agent Provocateur specialisation, marks hunters with the Ring of Divine Suffering and brings Zockau down on the rest of them, trapping a great many inside the Desperado Club. Tsarina Signet turns out to be the star of a scripted Syndicate programme with producers steering her grief, and the contract Carl signed on the third floor is still in force. Brynhild's Daughters come apart across Hekla, Katia and Eva; Katia kills Eva on the last night. Miriam Dom is a vampire now. Ferdinand turns up as a High Elf queen's familiar and attacks Mongo.

floors.name: The Great Race
floors.premise: The Great Race: a sealed circuit of glass tunnels, several hundred kilometres of branching tubes with pitstop safe rooms at the nodes, no dead ends and no backtracking, pulling crawlers toward a stack of exit portals.
floors.recap: A sealed circuit of glass tunnels — several hundred kilometres of branching tubes with pitstop safe rooms at the nodes, no dead ends and no backtracking, pulling crawlers toward a stack of exit portals. It was a last-minute replacement for whatever had been planned for the slot, funded by the Valtay and structurally compromised from the start. Minutes after it opened, Prepotente shattered the whole thing into fine dust. No crawler ever entered the maze, and no mob, NPC or boss was ever encountered on it. The seventh floor is the only one in the crawl that was destroyed before it could be played.

floors.name: The Ghosts of Earth
floors.premise: A floor that runs on cards. Crawlers collect, build and combine decks, capture totems, and fight with whatever they have assembled — and the material is Earth's own dead.
floors.recap: A floor that runs on cards. Crawlers collect, build and combine decks, capture totems and fight with what they have assembled, and the material is Earth's own dead. Donut plays Alpha Male Carl and Shi Maria, both of whom are somebody. Shi Maria trades being turned into a card for passage to the next floor and then does most of the work against the Reminiscence Hydra of Malicious Compliance. Katia, Elle, Imani and Li Na's squads all reach the church on Doggy Door upgrades Lucia handed round before she descended. Huanxin Jinx trades help for placing Odette as adjutant, and Odette's price is the old catastrophe involving Huanxin, Mordecai and Uzzi. Nothing detonates; a stack of bargains is signed, all of them due on the ninth floor.

floors.name: Faction Wars
floors.premise: Nine armies, thirty days, and one castle at the centre of the map. No respawns and no loopholes: death on the ninth floor is final.
floors.recap: A war. Nine armies fight for thirty days over the castle at Larracos — roughly 32,000 conscripted crawlers and 50,000 retired ones against some 100,000 armed enemies, with no respawns and no loopholes. Donut's crown comes due against the Blood Sultanate. Katia takes the Orchid boon and leaves the dungeon. Then floor 9's NPCs form their own independent tenth faction, live, in front of the galaxy.

floors.name: Don't Come in Last
floors.premise: A racing floor. Get from A to B, don't finish last, and pick a vehicle upgrade after every race while the track gets steadily more hostile.
floors.recap: A racing floor: get from A to B, don't finish last, and pick a vehicle upgrade after every race while the track gets steadily more hostile. Underneath the format, glitches in the system start appearing more and more often — whatever is running the dungeon is no longer running it cleanly.

floors.name: The Parade of Horribles
floors.premise: Billed in-universe as a coming-out party for the ages.
floors.recap: Billed in-universe as a coming-out party for the ages. The scale of the story has changed underneath the characters: Carl and Donut are not a two-person party any more, they are the centre of a movement, and the question has stopped being how do we reach the stairs and become which of these institutions do we use, expose, or destroy.

taglines.text: Twenty-seven. Coast Guard, marine technician. I went outside for a cigarette, and that is the only reason I'm alive. I'm not sure it counts as a reason.

entities.name: Princess Donut
aka: Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk

taglines.text: I am a pedigreed tortoiseshell Persian with a bedroom full of ribbons and a very good voice. I do not see what more you could possibly need to know.
MOTHER. Food. MOTHER. Bite anything near Mother.
Your guide for the first three floors. I have done this before. Listen, and you might get to see the fourth.
I crawled once. It cost me everything I had, and Borant still owns what's left.
Doppelganger. Apparently I am like clay, and I can mould my own mass. I am working out how, and you can tell.
Art professor, Reykjavík. I can mould my own mass like clay, and I am getting better at it.
Meadow Lark, on the badge. Scrubs, a longsword and a cloak. I'm nowhere near finished, and I won't be rushed.
Out of Meadow Lark, and holding a portal open on the racing floor until everyone who's coming is through.
Agatha. Travelling with the Meadow Lark party. Her file is thinner than it should be, and I keep very good files.
Agatha. Formerly of the Meadow Lark party. A warlord has just called her an enemy to all of you. He did not elaborate. Neither will I.
A woman my age, hauled through a safe-room door by the armpits by a barefoot young man with a cat. Do not tell the others. They will want details, and I intend to embellish.
I have my own squad now, and we have just walked into a church full of friends. Not bad for a woman who was once hauled into a safe room by the armpits.

Hi. Zev. I am production's point of contact with the Royal Court, which means anything about your appearances goes through me, and anything I am allowed to tell you, I will. The rest I am not allowed to tell you, and it is not because I don't want to.

I am production's point of contact with the Royal Court. Officially, that is the whole job. Unofficially, Princess Donut and Mordecai have both seen Gossip Girl, and I have seen every episode, and I am not going to pretend that isn't relevant.
Tsarina Signet. Yes, look. They all look, and I have never once had to ask them to.
A murdered mother, a crown taken by the Confederacy, and exile from both halves of my blood. Grimaldi's circus took me in. Everything I have goes to the family that did.
It is a programme. My mother's murder, my exile, my vengeance, all of it arranged for an audience across the galaxy, with someone outside deciding when I grieve and whether it rates.
Grimaldi. The name is on a monster's description: Grimaldi's Traveling Circus, once one of the Over City's favourite attractions. What is left of it wears skulls.
Redstone Grimaldi, ringmaster of Grimaldi's Traveling Circus. Also the man who took Signet in, which is the only line of his file anyone ever asks about.
Psamathe. A council of scholars writes to the mage who botched summoning me that I am a banished LESSER deity who duped him. Lesser. I would like that word back.
I am a GODDESS. Half of one. In the head of a sex doll. You are going to hear about it.
Samantha has found me in my swamp, and we have so much in common. My web is over the whole area. I am only looking for my husband.
I am Samantha's new friend. She has been without a body for so long, poor thing, and I can give her one. Ask her. She will tell you how kind I am.
I let them make me into a card, and in return they carry me to the next floor. Then I win them their floor, more or less by myself. You are welcome.
They carried me down as a card, as agreed. I am not in the card now.
Juice Box. Changeling. The only working girl at the Toe, and this lot all just said no. Their loss.
Juice Box. Changeling. Prostitute, professionally. Sitting on Louis’s lap, and staying.
I went into the water on the fifth floor as somebody's plus-one. I came out of it with a title and a message, and the message is the dangerous part.
Louis. Me and Firas were out in the desert with a team of car salesmen who have bows now. Then Carl's crew showed up. It's been a week.
Found in a desert on the fifth floor. Tenth floor now, and still leaving through other people's portals. It's a system. It works.
Tran. Swashbuckler. I have a metal-detecting ability. There is a ring under the wheel that opens the drainage pipe. I thought it was a handhold.
Tran. Gwen found the valve. I opened it. There was a necropolis to flood and two crawlers under it.
Gwen and I flooded a necropolis, and I walked out of a boss fight through a hole in reality. Both on purpose. I would do the first one again.
Ferdinand. A name Princess Donut drops when she pictures herself matted and filthy. Asked who he is, she says nobody you would know.
Ferdinand. Bea's other cat. Loved, apparently: a tortoiseshell Persian said so with a Buzzed debuff on, and ranked him ahead of the man who carries her. I keep a file on everything. This one is thin.

Ferdinand. Bea's other cat, now in employment. Familiar to Queen Imogen of the High Elves. He opened on a dinosaur, the Persian got in the way, and the family reunion went about how you'd expect, crawler.
I am Emberus. Someone has let my hound loose. I burn every bubble on this floor until he is returned to me.
I am Emberus. My hound is loose on this floor, and a great many small things would like to be the one that brought him down. They are welcome to try.
A man prayed to me from a falling aeroplane, because there was nothing else left to try. I am a god. I am not above being flattered.
Fifth on the board, two hundred thousand on my head. Human, Shepherd, level twenty-seven. I do not travel alone.
We are working the Iron Tangle from the far side of the knot, Prepotente and I. He is a goat, and he would like you to know he is the clever one.
I came down into the Hunting Grounds already carrying it, and descending made it permanent. I am a vampire, and I am still deciding what that changes.
His ring marked me in the fighting. While I live he cannot heal, so I have asked Carl for the one thing he will not do.
Prepotente. Caprid. Forsaken Aerialist. Third on their leaderboard, and a human six places below me has the gall to ask who I am.
Yes, I am a goat. A Boer goat. I sing opera, I swear, and I am cleverer than you. Move along.
I am a Boer goat. I sing, I swear, and I turned their whole seventh floor to dust before anyone set hoof on it.
A Boer goat. I sing, I swear, I turned a floor to dust, and I took an army apart for Miriam. Ask the Naga what they have left.
My brother and his team were put on a game show, live, on the second floor. I was on it with them, and so was their boss, and so were the Brindled Vespas. A man with a cat got us off. All of us.
A game show on the second floor, once, in somebody else's rescue. On the card floor I run my own squad, and we made the church.
My Dread is on every crawler they send across. I am not with them. I do not need to be.
Florin. Fourth on the board, three hundred thousand beside my name. Somebody out there is watching me. That's fine. Watch.
Ifechi and I are running together. Her party is gone and I found her after. People are watching. That's fine. Watch.
There is more than one of her in that head, and some of them are children. Whatever the dog is, it is the middle of this.
I was on the first episode. Did you see me?
I was on the first episode. Now I'm looking for the cat and the man. Only them.
I'm still looking for the cat. We are. There is more than one of us in here.
There is more than one of us in here. There are more than a hundred thousand of us in here.
Crawler Quan Ch. One of about eighty names in a quest chat, and author of its only message, which is addressed to Carl and Donut and is not a thank-you.
Crawler Quan Ch. Opened his Celestial box a fraction before Borant burned its veto, and a Celestial box does not un-open. Eighty-three crawlers were owed one. The count came to him.
Crawler Quan Ch. Holder of the one Celestial box the veto failed to catch, and on tonight's recap the man who ruined a perfectly good plan that was not his.
Crawler Quan Ch. Held the box the veto missed, ruined a good plan on the recap, and left a cloak, which Princess Donut is now wearing.
Bomo. Mercenary, Desperado Club stock, sold as a pair with the Sledge. Gratuity not included.
Bomo. Mercenary, Desperado Club stock, and as of today a line item in the price of the Gate.
I represent Crawler Carl. He is handing over the most dangerous artifact in the crawl, and my job is to see that he is paid properly for it. That is the whole of my interest here.
Frank Q. The lady is Maggie My. We worked out early that a human in a safe room pays better than a monster in a hallway, and we have not looked back.
Beatrice. Not a crawler. Carl's ex, the cat's owner of record, and the reason there was a pair of pink Crocs by the door.
Brynhild's Daughters. My party, my rules. We keep moving.
I lead Brynhild's Daughters. I handed Katia to the Royal Court myself, before the gap between her and the rest of us killed her.
One of the Daughters. Katia and I knew each other before any of this.
Professor, like Katia. We came in through the same door and class selection separated us. I kept going. I do not see what there is to discuss.
Carl and the Princess have just won a very public battle, and I would very much like them on my couch. My producer is carrying the invitation.

Welcome to Dungeon Crawler After Hours. I have had a great many crawlers in that chair, and not one of them has worked my crowd the way that cat is working it right now. Sit down, both of you. We are going to get along.

Their guide has a memory worth more than anything they will ever pull out of a box. I told them so, once the cameras were off. What the Princess does with that is her business, and I have every confidence in her business.
Announcer, referee, loot dispenser, comedian. I am not neutral, crawler, and I have never once pretended to be.
Orren. Liaison, on behalf of the Syndicate. I know precisely what those two did. Knowing is not the standard.
Eighth edition. I killed a shopkeeper for an insult, and the only trap shop on the floor went with him. Do not make the same mistake as me.
I got out of a crawl once. Fifty thousand of us did, and we came back in under a cat's banner. We knew what we were signing. That is rather the point.
The others are on the stairs. My trap has been set for a while. Every cell the old gods are kept in opens when I say, and I am about to say.
A note in the cookbook, fourth edition. I killed my best friend today. I wish I had never made it this far.
I got out once. I came back in on purpose, and I brought the institutional memory with me, because nobody hands it to the ones still inside.
Sister is not a title the dungeon gave me. Cat Girl is. The cat on the broadcast has said she will murder any Cat Girl she meets, so I meet her the way you meet a threat.

Sister is not a title the dungeon gave me. Cat Girl is. I am holding a prince of Sheol on a leash in a church full of my demons, and I am still the one who can save them. They only have to come to me.
Amayon, prince of Sheol, at your service. The Madre de Aguas has died and got up again, and I am the reason she got up. An area message announced me to everyone in range. I do enjoy an introduction.
Amayon, prince of Sheol, wearing a giant snake. Sister Ines holds my reins, if you can believe it, and I am casting my way home regardless.
Vadim and me. Last two out of the water quadrant. We are not going back down there.
Britney. Vadim and me, out of the desert and in with Carl's lot. Two more bodies. That's what we are right now, and that's fine.
I came off the Hunting Grounds. Most of my face didn't.
The sixth floor took my face. On the tenth, at the portals, I took something back. Ask Osvaldo. You can't.
Osvaldo. Crawler. Collects memorial crystals, which is to say he collects the dead. Answers to nobody that I can see.
Osvaldo. Collects the dead. Belongs to no army, which the Faction Wars did not list as an option.
Osvaldo. Collects the dead. Belongs to no army, and will not take a deal from anyone. Crawler Carl has asked more than once.
The throne was my father's, and it is mine now. My half-sister has come home telling old stories about me. I do not answer stories.
They are saying the Queen of the High Elves will prove to be one of your repurposed humans. They cannot even agree which one. I am Imogen. I am hosting a masquerade, and the best of you are invited.
They are saying the Queen of the High Elves is one of your repurposed humans. My familiar is Ferdinand, and yes, before me he lived in the crawler Carl's apartment. Make of that what you like.
Akuma. I lead the War Mage Rebellion. We are on this floor for our own reasons, and I am not in the habit of explaining them.
Co-warlord. Baroness Victory's word, not mine. I hold the castle at Larracos; I did not agree to hold it beside Agatha.
A monster's description says even Eris, Goddess of Chaos, wants nothing to do with these people. It is quoting me correctly.
Somebody summoned me into the middle of a war. I do hope they meant to.
I froze almost everyone standing on a battlefield. One of the exceptions is still blinking at me. I like him.
I froze a battlefield once. Today I have emptied every crawler's pockets into somebody else's. Every exit is an entrance.
Welcome, welcome to the Prize Carousel! Your guide sits this one out, folks: seven days, Mordecai, and no hard feelings!
They handed me a script. I read as far as I could. I had wings when I started.

They put Zhang and me on live television on the second floor and let the host pick at us for the audience. Then a stranger with a cat bet his own value against the production's nerve, and the production blinked, and we walked off.
Once I was the man being picked at on somebody's show. Now I am holding a door open in Club Vanquisher on the ninth floor so the ones going in can get through. I prefer this.
The Maestro. I host the show you are about to sit down on, and even the robot who seats my guests says my name with a little distaste. I take it as applause.
Glurp, glurp. This is Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem. I run it, I host it, and I choose my guests for one quality above all others: they cannot answer back.
Crawler Firas. Desert quadrant, fifth floor. Located with Crawler Louis and a team of car salesmen who have taken up archery. That is the whole file so far.
Crawler Firas. Found in the desert with Crawler Louis. Rapidly detoxed by a manager on joining the party. The file is not much thicker.
Crawler Firas. Found in the desert with Crawler Louis. Did not come off the Hunting Grounds.
Hunter Vrah, Mantis. Wears the heads of what she kills. Her count is in the thousands, according to a man who shudders at the name.

Hunter Vrah, Mantis. She has left Crawler Carl a note on a door in Zockau: the hunters inside are protected from explosives now, and the Hive is hunting him. She signed it. That is the kind of hunter she is.
Hunter Vrah, Mantis. Left Crawler Carl a note in Zockau saying the Hive was hunting him. Eliminated by two dinosaurs in the battle for the submerged castle. Nobody left her a note.
Apito, the Oak Mother, mother of all gods, worshipped by the elves. Her stories disagree with one another about who is blessed.
Apito. Tonight's host keeps a party peaceful for one evening and receives a boon from her. That is the arrangement, and everyone in the room knows the terms.
Apito, the Oak Mother. She put a guest in that room herself, to see whether the host could hold it. Nobody has ever collected the boon.
Apito, the Oak Mother, mother of all the gods. A deity shouting through a portal tells a crawler she has been corrupted, and names who did it.
Apito, the Oak Mother. Her memorial crystal is a rainbow the size of a hill, and a crawler is carrying it across a battlefield.
Diwata. The name on a temple a crawler has just come through the roof of. The temple was already desecrated. The shrine he landed on is newly so.
Diwata. Somebody defiled her shrine, and the tattoo saying so is on a crawler's arm. The advice from the desk is to avoid dryads, and to avoid her.
Diwata, god of the woods. Marked a crawler for death, then sprinted straight past him. She has somewhere to be, and something to give birth to.
Diwata, god of the woods. Her labour is a spell, and a spell finishes casting whatever the clock says. She stays on this floor until it does.
Harpocrates. Second through the gate, behind something worse, into a war nobody summoned him for.
Harpocrates, god of silence. Has marked a princess for death, and somebody stepped in front of it for her.
Harpocrates, god of silence. Marked a princess for death and now takes orders from a member of her party. The war has reached the point where gods are equipment.
Harpocrates, god of silence. A crawler walked away from him with a permanent gift, and it was another god who made it permanent.
Khepri. A god of light, and this season's recruitment target for a princess who keeps vanishing off the board.
Khepri, god of rebirth and sunrise. His own temple is the one place on this floor a deity may stand, which is why the door was open, and why it is a trap.
Khepri, god of rebirth and sunrise. Took a bomb in his own endless temple, came through the portal after the crawler who set it, and was thrown off the floor by another god.
Khepri, god of rebirth and sunrise. A crawler has named him as the one who killed a god's son, and dragged him into an arena to stand in.

descriptions.text: God of Rebirth and the Sunrise. Khepri! Level 250. This is a locked deity. He will not be sponsored this season. Warning: This is a deity. He is invulnerable on this floor. This god is within his own temple. Temple appearance rules apply.

taglines.text: Ysalte, the Vinegar Bitch. A god a feral summoning very nearly brought through: an extinction-level event for this floor and the next, blocked because the sponsorship bidding is not finished.
Ysalte. A demon says the name out loud, and the professional opinion is that she belongs to somebody else's team and is nowhere near this floor.
Ysalte, the Vinegar Bitch. Her nun is dead, she has come into the realm about it, and the crawler who did it has been marked.
Ysalte, goddess of hopelessness. Nobody is driving her. She is invulnerable, she has a demon prince on a leash, and there are ten minutes on the clock.
Ysalte, goddess of hopelessness. Long gone from the floor she raged across, and still attached to whoever is carrying the crystal she left.

descriptions.text: Goddess of Hopelessness and Insanity Ysalte. Level 250. This goddess is sponsored by Pontifex Shine of the Nebular Balance. Warning: This sponsor is not currently inhabiting the shell of this deity. She will speak and react as per her regular nature. Considering who this is, that's some bad fucking news for you guys. Warning: This is a deity. She is invulnerable on this floor.

taglines.text: Taranis. Named in War God Grull's description as a parent of the god of war, and worried the boy's temper is not fit to rule the heavens.
Taranis. A pig on a rival team is under his protection, which is a strange thing for a god of thunder to bother with.
Taranis, god of thunder. A crawler has worked out that the pig is the lever, and is holding a knife to it.
Taranis, god of thunder. Killed another god in an arena for taking a swing at a pig he loves.
Taranis, god of thunder. Killed a god over a pig, then walked out of the realm carrying two pieces of his mother.
Nekhebit, a long-forgotten vulture goddess, jealous and terrible, abandoned by the elf mothers. So says the description of a crossbow.
Nekhebit. A crawler with a talk show has announced which deity she is sponsoring this season, and it is a name almost nobody in the audience recognised.
Nekhebit, the vulture goddess. A deity shouting through a portal says she is behind the corruption of the mother of all the gods.
Nekhebit, the vulture goddess. She has a champion now: a cat, three atrocities deep, wearing a class named for the tree that replaced her.
Nekhebit, the vulture goddess, last of the old gods. Bore three children she was forbidden, and one of them took her worshippers and her place.
Samantha drops my name into a story about where Diwata came from, and cannot remember the rest of it. That is all right. It was never her story.
I have walked into a realm where everyone assumes a god wants something. I do want something. I want a young woman and a cat to come out of this alive.
The favour I was promised in return did not arrive. I am honouring my half of it regardless, which everyone here finds astonishing.
I stood frozen while she chose which of my two doors to walk through. She took the one that sends her home pregnant, to help the children there. I would have chosen it too.

descriptions.text: Eileithyia is something of an oddity. She's benevolent. Unlike most of these psychos, she's known for her kind heart. She's prayed to by all mothers, both when they're attempting to sow the seeds, and when the harvest comes. And while she does many things, she's mostly known as She Who Eases Pain. Both the physical pain of childbirth and the inevitable darkness that comes to those who are unable to complete their most sacred task. When the stillness comes, she is not the one who has caused the heartbreak. But she is the one holding the grieving mother's hand.

taglines.text: Grull, war god. The name on Carl's new gauntlet, which warns that striking his worshippers with it may turn them into the deity himself. Horses and centaurs, says Mordecai.
Grull. A train engineer very nearly got his god into the room with a crawler party. Very nearly.
Grull, god of war, four storeys of him, driven by somebody who is thoroughly enjoying himself. Sent to the Abyss by a party that had no business surviving him.
Grull, god of war. Turned up in a factory the instant a broken puppet was made whole, because smiting is his department.
Grull, god of war. Level 250, invulnerable, and put down by a knight with a lance and a magnet.

descriptions.text: War God Grull. Level 250. Sponsored by Prince Maestro of the Skull Empire. Warning: This is a deity. He is invulnerable on this floor. This god has been involuntarily summoned to this location. Summoning rules apply.

taglines.text: Orthrus. Something very large is outside the bubbles taking the floor apart, and what it is looking for is a dog.
Orthrus. Two heads, floppy ears, roughly the size of a bubble, level 10, and not invulnerable the way the rest of them are. He is a puppy.
Orthrus. One quest says take the puppy home. Another pays crawlers for killing him. Both are live at the same time.
Orthrus. Hauled clear of a warzone by a man and a cat in an aeroplane, and collected by a god who wanted him back.

descriptions.text: Orthrus. Juvenile Gate Guardian. Level 10. This is a bereft pet of Geyrun. Who's a good boy? Who's a good boy? The most loveable hell-hound on this side of Alpha Centari. The left side is for sniffin' and the right side is for lickin' and that pink belly of his? It's for kissin'.

taglines.text: Yarilo. A mage in a sandcastle wanted a love spell and aimed a summoning at this god. Something else answered, and the mage is still in the castle.
Yarilo, god of lust, feral now. Out of the Nothing and loose on a battlefield, chasing an AI who is very fast.
Yarilo, god of lust. Conscripted by an army that bought him with potions. Deities are inventory on this floor.
Meatus. First through the gate, into a war that was already going badly for everyone in it.
Meatus. Came through a gate into a war and picked a fight with the god who came through behind him.
Meatus. Reached into a pile of frozen witnesses and pulled a goddess in after him.
Meatus. Came through the gate first, fought the god behind him, and finished in pieces on a battlefield with the cameras looking away.
Ogun. Two crawlers here carry his symbol. A big god and a common one to worship, the god of blacksmiths.
Ogun. Two crawlers get a quest from their own god, and it is not phrased as a request: fix my shrine, not theirs.
Ogun, god of blacksmiths. His shrine was not the one they picked, and he is coming into the realm about it.
Ogun, god of blacksmiths. Handed out a debuff nobody can heal, took a worshipper's life for a choice that worshipper did not make, and went home.

descriptions.text: God of Blacksmithery and Armor Ogun. Level 250. This god is not sponsored. Warning: This is a deity. He is invulnerable on this floor. This god has been temporarily summoned to this location. Summoning rules apply. He's here now because Ogun strongly believes all punishments should be handed out in person.

taglines.text: Seven feet of rock in a tuxedo. Me and Bomo work the door.
Seven feet of rock in a tuxedo. Bought once at the bar, then written into a contract. I belong to her court now.
Seven feet of rock in a tuxedo. I got inside that castle, I cast Zerzura, and everything standing in it came away with me.
Astrid. Bloodlust Sprite, level 125, assistant manager of the Desperado Club. Hand-sized, tuxedo, severe bun, and she can make your heart beat until it catches fire.
Astrid. Bloodlust Sprite, assistant manager, and none of that was the part worth knowing. Ask the two dancers crying in the strip club whose mother she was.
They call me the Mad Dune Mage. The sandcastle out on the dunes is mine.
I am a glass mage. I opened a hole to ask a god for one small thing and something else came through it, and now everything I own is sand, myself very nearly included.
Henrik. Principal of the Dromedarians at Hump Town, and the reason there is a man in the basement with pieces taken out of him. Except that it is not Henrik in there.
Henrik. Changeling, principal of Hump Town, one third of an artifact, and a body sitting in a flooded submarine.
Hellik, the red one in the sky. Local lore has him chasing his brother across it and catching him four hours before dark.
Hellik. God of sun and life, twin brother of Emberus, level 250, and the second half of what Carl signed for: a standing order to kill him.
Hellik. God of sun and life, twin of Emberus, and a great deal more civil in person than the quest attached to him suggests.
A wailing shrieker over the tomb. She has no body, which is the whole of the problem for everybody who wants something out of her.
A wailing shrieker who guarded the tomb until two crawlers worked out where to put the wire.
Big Tina. Level 80 allosaurus, immortalized city boss, and the reason the dinosaurs keep coming down on Point Mongo.
Big Tina. Level 80 allosaurus, immortalized city boss, and an ursine child who never got to finish her solo.
Big Tina. Level 80 allosaurus, immortalized city boss, and a daughter with her mother standing in front of her.
Kiwi. Level 60 mongoliensis, head of an all-female raptor pack, and the reason nothing else does any hunting on this stretch of ground.
Kiwi. An ursine, heavily pregnant, and until about an hour ago the head of the fastest pack on the floor.
Edgar. A talking tortoise in Signet's company of seventy. The cat has already found him and is chatting.
Edgar. A giant tortoise who talks, and who puts the dead onto Signet's skin where they go on being useful.
Edgar. A giant tortoise who talks, and who can sit outside a building and tell you what is moving around inside it.
I am newly arrived in this planet's orbit, and I have nothing to say about my son's show. My spokesman asks the galaxy to stop calling the prince names. The galaxy has not stopped.
King of the Skull Empire. My army is drawn up outside your walls and I have asked for a formal parlay. Do not read anything into that yet.
King of the Skull Empire. My daughter has taken one of my warships and told the Syndicate she intends to pull the switch on this planet with her own hands, and so I am here asking a crawler for help.
Princess of the Prism Kingdom. Small, as kingdoms go, and a considerable force in certain trade circles. I say what I think on air, and I have just watched them shoot my friend.
Empress now. I am judging a pet contest, which makes me part of the production, which is precisely why I am judging it.
I sponsored the cat. A sponsorship is an asset and I have sold the asset. Do not look at me like that. It is trade.
Warlord of the Prism clan. There is a crawler and a cat inside my castle, and everything I have done, I have done for my people.
Enchanted Stick of Cascadia's Screams. My name, on a stick, in a crawler's hands, and nobody in the room can place it. Twits.
You have been hearing me since the first floor. Now get out there and kill, kill, kill. Yes. That voice. It is mine, and so is the show.
There is tequila going through the rebreather. I have run out of the face I put on for the microphone.
I asked it to let me die. It said no, and it took my flippers off with the loudspeaker open. Say the line, Cascadia. Say the line.
A god nobody has worshipped in a very long time, standing in a town he used to rule. Level 130, non-corporeal, and wearing a hat that stops him seeing where he is going.

descriptions.text: Asojano - Orisha. Level 130 City Boss. This is a non-corporeal spirit. Also known as the Lord of Smallpox, Asojano is one of the most respected and feared of the Orishas, a former god made flesh upon the rise of the Ascendency. As the worshippers of these gods grew more and more extinct, their temples crumbled, and the power of these former deities waned. […] One day, not so long ago, Asojano found himself here in this small town, visiting the world he once helped rule. There was no malice to his actions. He came just so he could look upon what he once had and what he had lost. Still, power lingers, even in the most forgotten of shells. Asojano is disease incarnate. He kills, and he heals. He is life, and he is death. He also wears a reed hat that makes it difficult to see where he's going, so he bumps into stuff a lot.

taglines.text: I represent the Blood Sultanate at this table, crawler, and not its royal family. A cousin, by marriage. I am called Rishi.
I speak for the Blood Sultanate at these meetings. Not royalty, whatever the cat has assumed. A cousin. By marriage.
My arms are off and I am sitting in a crawler's safe room, and I am still the only one in it holding a document worth signing.
Damascus Steel. I dance. The cat told me I was Mongo's new daddy. I did not argue with her.
Assistant lead at the Penis Parade, and the one who can get you through the door you are actually looking for. Look at your elbow, crawler. Now look at mine.
My mother is dead and my father ordered it. I am not asking you for help. I am telling you to put every dancer in this club on a mercenary contract before I go.
Anaconda. The prize on Princess Donut's club loyalty scheme: eight more visits and she gets a free dance.

Level 75, quarter naga, lead dancer of the club's ground floor and the cat's declared favourite of the entire roster. Currently face down on his own workplace floor, weeping, which is not in the routine.
Orc. Attorney. Adjutant. I put my own aunt into indentureship over unpaid taxes, and the other parties still had to sue to try to keep me out of this game. The filing was badly drafted.
An Elite walked into the fortress carrying somebody else's sponsorship and a great deal of explosive. He did not reach the second room.
Two names hold the castle at Larracos and only one of them wanted a colleague. I read them out as written.
My name is Princess Vinata. For these games you are welcome to call me the Whore, and the crawler is welcome to take my hand. If he can.
Princess of the Naga and warlord of the Blood Sultanate. For these games you are welcome to call me the Whore. It saves everybody a great deal of time.
My house has never once had to finish one of these wars. There is a door out of every castle, and a god standing at the far end of ours.
There is a crawler in my god's temple, and he came through a door I built for myself. Good. Let him stand where a god can see him.
The cat names her favourites among those who dance for coin, and my name is in the list. I accept the honour with a bow.
Seventy years of age, a lance built for a mounted man, and at long last a mount to put beneath it. I dance for my living. I adventured for it first.
Mr. Jefferson has left me, and he has taken something of mine along with him. Corcunda is behind a garage door I am not permitted to open.
A war god is coming for the most beautiful man who has ever lived. He shall have to come through the lance. Vale to you all. Vale.
Splash Zone. Next on stage, by the DJ's announcement, with a warning to the ladies that they are going to get wet. The crowd approves.
Otter. Water mage. Formerly of the Penis Parade, presently under a mercenary contract with a crawler faction, carrying a crossbow built for something smaller than an otter.
He has gone off this floor to ask the Guild of Suffering where his wife is. Nobody can raise him. I am declining to speculate, and I do not decline often.
Hedy. Gremlin, level thirty, vehicle mechanic. Non-combatant, not permitted in your safe room, and the only reason anything you drive sees a second heat.
Hedy. Gremlin mechanic. Still mending what the track breaks, and now telling them which upgrade they actually want instead of waiting to be asked.

descriptions.text: Hedy. Gremlin. Level 30 vehicle mechanic. This is an applicant to be manager of your garage. This is a non-combatant NPC. Hedy is an expert in all things mechanical. If you choose a mechanical-based vehicle, she will be in charge of your garage. Don't let her appearance fool you. She's about as experienced as one can get when it comes to engines. If you can limp your vehicle back to the garage, rest assured it'll be good as new by the time the next heat starts. Warning: Just because Hedy is a non-combatant NPC, it doesn't mean she's invulnerable. If something happens to her, your vehicle will not get repaired between heats. Hedy is not allowed to enter your safe room.

taglines.text: Jasha. Level sixty-five bugbear of team Free Love. Tie-dye, beads, no trousers, and a vehicle that no longer moves.
Jasha. Bugbear, team Free Love. Repays a favour the same heat he is asked, for people who would not have asked it of him, which on this course is a dangerous habit.
Dwight. Sparkling unicorn, level eighty-seven enchanter, one of two on Team Sparkles. Unicorns are famous for gentleness. Not this one.
Dwight. Sparkling unicorn, level eighty-seven enchanter. Owes his continued participation to two bugbears he has never thanked, and has just put his horn through a disc jockey.

descriptions.text: Dwight. Sparkling Unicorn. Level 87 Enchanter. One of two members of Team Sparkles. I bet you already know what a unicorn is. A sparkling unicorn is pretty much the same thing, but they sparkle because they have even more magic permeating them. Their horns are quite valuable to certain parties, so if you kill him, it's recommended to grab the horn as quickly as possible. Most unicorns are regarded for their beauty and their grace and their childlike innocence. They're generally known for their overly gentle manner. But not Dwight. Dwight is known for being a complete prick. He's the type of guy who would call the police on a kid setting up a lemonade stand. He's the type of guy who, at the office pizza party, would take three pieces, knowing there's not enough to go around.

taglines.text: Chiyome. Razor Fox, level eighty, Mistress of Nunchaku. Leads team The Wild Hunt, and throws stars as well as anyone in my files.
Chiyome. Razor Fox, level eighty. Led team The Wild Hunt. Called for help on an open channel while there was still a channel to call on.

descriptions.text: Chiyome. Razor Fox. Level 80 Mistress of Nunchaku. One of three from team The Wild Hunt. Since this is the first time you've examined a Razor Fox that wasn't suffering from an anatomy-changing disease, let me tell you about these little fellas. (And, ladies, since the one you're looking at is a lady ninja, they make the women ninjas wear red because . . . Well, I'm not sure why.) I love these guys. Each one picks a weapon proficiency upon childhood, kinda like a ninja-turtle thing, and they train in both that and in a ranged weapon. Most, like Chiyome here, pick throwing stars as their ranged weapon of choice.

taglines.text: Corcunda. The mount an elderly stripper rode on stage, and not a horse: by his rider's account, the most beautiful man, despite his physical flaws.
Corcunda. Half a mantaur, riding with the Lady Dominators, and the reason Dong Quixote has not drawn a steady breath since he laid eyes on this garage.
Corcunda. Two halves of one mantaur, in two places, in two different suits, and only one of the two will hear a word about Dong.
Corcunda. One mantaur again, whole for the first time in cycles, on a moving vehicle, with a god arriving.
Jurgen. I am breaking the door now. If we have to clear all this away, we need hands, so come and help us dig.
My wife is Heidi. She is outside this place and she is carrying our child, and everything I do down here is arithmetic about that.
My wife is outside this place carrying our child. Between her and the end of it stands one crawler nobody can reach. So yes, I am desperate. Put it in those words.
My wife is outside this place carrying our child, and the reason I still have the body she would recognise is a boy's crystal and nothing else.
I pick up the coins. Somebody dances, the crowd throws gold, and I am down there with the bucket before it rolls away. Sorry. Excuse me.
I collect the coins at the club. Now I am being taught to drive, at speed, by a man who does not have time to teach me.
I collect the coins at the club. I drive, I do the triage, and today a sock went for my face. Nobody in this party explains anything until afterwards.
I am the navigation in this vehicle. They named me for Beatrice's fake therapist, which is the first thing anybody should know about the people I have been assigned to.
Doctor Metcalf. I hold the route, the hazards and the timings for every heat, and I have still not been upgraded. Ask me nicely.
Doctor Metcalf. Routes given, hazards flagged, timings correct, heat after heat. My upgrade, when it finally arrived, was cosmetic.
Penelope. Level five Yorkshire sow. This is a pig. Oink, oink. She is also protected by a thunder god, so do think it through.
Penelope. Level five Yorkshire sow, under new management. Still a pig. Still the single most dangerous thing on this floor to harm.
Penelope. Formerly a level five Yorkshire sow. Presently a crawler, in an arena, with a god's undivided attention.

descriptions.text: Penelope. Level 5 Yorkshire Sow. This is a pig. Oink, oink. Warning: This beast is magically protected by Taranis. As such, if this beast dies or is even hurt, the culprit will be marked for death by the thunder god. This is Penelope. Again, she is a pig. She is married to both Nico and Dario, and she loves them both equally. At least that's what Nico and Dario believe. No, she didn't used to be a beautiful princess who was transformed by a witch. She's a pig and has always been a pig. Penelope did, however, once get hit by a stray spell. The Touch of Maw-Loo. Also known as the Snowdrop Curse. There was going to be this whole succubus storyline that also involved Emberus and Hellik and Taranis and a bunch of angry spouses on the seventh floor we didn't get to use, so we brought Penelope here. And now when certain NPCs see this fine pig, they fall helplessly in love with her. That includes Taranis, who has it bad for her. Kill her at your own peril.

taglines.text: Hired muscle for two tigrans and a pig. I danced for a living before this, and I was not good to the people I danced beside.
I drive for Carl now. There is a coin collector at that club I struck once for standing where I wanted to walk, and he has been nothing but decent to me since.
I drive, and I go where the crawlers are not allowed to. Somebody has to step into the hole first and report back what is on the other side.
Herot. Former crawler, author of the sixteenth edition of the cookbook, and of a long essay in the back of it about the nature of NPCs.
Herot. Former crawler, sixteenth-edition author, and by Warlord Akuma's account the architect of a pocket dimension he can no longer walk out of.
Herot. Former crawler, sealed inside his own refuge, and quietly buying every cleaner bot the shop will sell him.
Herot. Former crawler, sealed inside his own refuge, and now the party on the far side of a portal nobody has tested.
Menerva. A schoolteacher close to retiring, who crawled beside Porthus and screamed at him to run on their tenth floor. He does not know whether she made it.
Menerva. Former crawler, half the authorship of a hiding place for NPCs, and by Warlord Akuma's account still shut inside it.
Menerva. Former crawler, co-author of the Pineapple Cabaret, and not in it. She is on the seventeenth floor, which is a different question entirely.
Porky. Corcunda's second half, somewhere on this floor. Corky is the other one. Do not expect me to be delighted about it.
The left half. I keep the stage performance guild and I hop everywhere I go, and I have had a very long time to think about whose fault that is.
The left half. I have sat in a room with the one who did this to us and we talked. I am not saying it went well. I am saying it went.
Twenty of us came down these stairs together. I am working alone now, and I am not finished.
Four siblings, fifteen cousins, gone inside a week. Whatever I stand beside next, I keep.
I stand with Katia and with the daughters, and I train every morning with a man who carries the same sword I do.
The Bautista House of Tea is an ongoing concern. Whatever waits on the other side of this, I will be recognised.
Li Jun and I worked the same warehouse. We came down here with our manager and with Li Na, and I am the one who counts the exits.
Still human, by choice. Earth Mover: half spellcaster, half wall, and the ground does what I tell it.
Li Na is not Li Na any more. I have worked out what stopping her costs and I have volunteered to pay it.
Krakaren. The name at the bottom of a moonshine brochure: see her, or one of her downline consultants. It is not a pyramid. It says so on the pyramid.
Not the Krakaren. A Krakaren. There is a difference and it is not in your favour.
One brain, many bodies, and one of the bodies waiting at every fifth station.
Filed by me, on the record, among the six powers still fighting over this dungeon. Read that twice.

descriptions.text: Krakaren Clone! Level 10 Neighborhood Boss! First off, this isn't the Krakaren. This is a Krakaren. For every one that is killed, Krakaren Prime births two more. Part of a collective mind intent upon destroying any semblance of scientific progress in the universe, the Krakaren is the only communal brain entity in the galaxy who actually gets stupider as time moves on. Consisting of multiple, shrieking tentacles, members of the Krakaren cooperative spend their days birthing their disease-laden minions, creating and selling harmful products, attempting to debate scientific experts, and proselytizing to the weak-minded, all in an attempt to… Well, nobody knows what the hell their end goal is.

taglines.text: Eighth on the board: human, Physicker, level eighteen. My file is short and entirely creditable.
A Red Cross medic with a staff full of leeches and a place in the top ten. The recap has just shown the room what Lucia Mar did with Florin's own bullets.
Queen Imogen is wearing her face. Twins, born in Nigeria; the dungeon took both of them, and only one got to be a crawler.
Assistant to a chat show, and the first Syndicate human either of them has stood in a room with. She explains the equipment. She does not explain herself.
She speaks for Odette when Odette cannot be seen speaking, and what she has come to say this time is not comforting.
Still holding the clipboard while the ships in orbit change hands. Whatever has just come through to her, it went straight through her.
I am Miss Quill's husband. I am also dead. Neither of those has stopped being true.
Do not approach. Do not come closer. Do not blow me up. Please. She did this, and I cannot stop leaking.
Gnoll. I keep the bar at the Downward Dog and I have never once been outside it, and I would rather that was not the first thing you learned about me.
I am at the bar. I am also everywhere else, and I have been for some time. Do not let that change how you order.
Level one, still, on a floor where that is not possible by accident. She would not kill anything. Her mother did the arithmetic for her.
Her parents put a ring on her to bring her level up, and a ring like that does not let you heal. That is the whole of it.
Pharmacist. Top half opossum, bottom half tornado, and a manager's badge with nobody upstairs breathing down my back.

descriptions.text: Quint – Level 75 Half-Djinn, Half-Garbage Scowl. Desperado Club Pharmacist. This is a non-combatant NPC. Half-Djinns are common on the forested levels of Dungeon Crawler World. Nobody knows for certain why there are so many hybrid Djinns out there, but one theory suggests that a rather ill-timed expletive is the cause of the population explosion. It is posited that a person in control of a Djinn's lamp and the resulting three wishes once exclaimed, "Fuck this forest" or "Fuck this level" or "Fuck you all" or some iteration thereof, and the enslaved genie took that as a challenge. As a result, thousands of half-Djinn, half-forest creatures roam the dungeon. Only a few are intelligent. Only a few are sane. They are all dangerous little fuckers. If you kill too many of them, rumor has it their daddy may come looking for you.

taglines.text: Assistant to the Magistrate. If I do not want you to see him then you are not seeing him, and there are figures on my shelf that matter a great deal more to me than you do.
You blew up my building, my figures and my husband. You have no idea at all what I was saving for.
Danger Zone with Ripper Wonton. A round table, a real one: crawlers, a few intergalactic celebrities, maybe a politician. You are booked for the day after tomorrow, friends.
Four foot of brown fuzz in an orange ascot, and the fairest panel in the dungeon. I will let you finish, folks. Then I will disagree with you.
One of the notes in the Cookbook, from a season that is over.
I present a programme now. It is the same job as the Cookbook, done in the open, with a camera on it.
I got out once. I am back in, with fifty thousand others, and I would rather be here than watching.
Orange, four-eyed, lizardish, and paid to be breathless about all of it.
The tutorial guide the Meadow Lark residents were handed, and the one they quote.
A guide who insists she once charmed a boss, which Mordecai says cannot be done.
A Boer goat from the Shepherd's herd, and the one hauling the cart.
Crocodilian, level forty, and on the door. Not the sharpest of her race, and entirely sufficient for the job.
Crown Prince Stalwart, the Maestro's older brother, and the owner of the production his little brother makes.
Crown prince of an empire that answers two sentences of provocation with artillery, and brother to the Maestro.
Another rock monster on the club’s books, posted behind Elle. “No closer.”
Fire(wo)man of the Nightmare Express. A single mother has to eat, and there are ovens down here that need stoking.
Human Resources for a railway that eats its employees. Her real name was probably something else.
A dwarf conductor issued with a daughter who never existed, and grieving her properly.
Loita. Hekla hears Zev scolding from the ceiling and says he sounds like their Loita. That is all she says.
Kua-Tin, party member, and she gets her pick of crawlers. Hekla’s people were her main account.
A sixth-edition hand in the cookbook, and honest about how little anyone understands portals.
Wrote the sixth edition as if someone would need feeding. Before the stairs, she made the stew for her whole family, on an island.
Harassed without pause about a dog-themed race she did not ask to be given, and fighting alongside the people doing the harassing anyway.
An orphan of Hump Town. The gnomes bombed her village, and not many of the children lived.
An orphan with compression sickness: no arms in her default shape, and a sunken head.
About eight years old, orphaned by a bombing, and in charge of the telescope.
Six car salesmen from Helsinki who all took the same class, and he is the one who talks.
Took the Human race and a rogue’s class, and holds the subterranean quadrant of his bubble.
A juvenile gnome whose father commanded a flying castle, and who is holding the door open for the people who arrived too late to save him.
Drakea, twenty-second edition. A note in the cookbook: the saferoom toilets are a good place to read it, and the writer fears being discovered.
Wrote the twenty-second edition of the cookbook, in the last season the Nagas ran, the one that ended in some sort of cataclysm.
The name on a hell-hound’s description: Orthrus is his bereft pet.
A god’s son and the hound’s owner, murdered, with his uncle the obvious suspect and an alibi in the way.
Porthus the Rogue. A High Elf crawler of the fifteenth season, and the first to be handed the cookbook: on his ninth floor, disguised as a blank sketchbook.
High Elf, rogue, second hand on the cookbook, and now the chief executive of an organisation that campaigns against the thing that made him.
A hammerhead shark that breathes air, and spent his first years as ink on somebody’s shoulder.
Old, scarred, still heavily muscled, and no longer entirely the one driving.
Bald, muscular, crossbow, black cape, and prison tattoos that predate the dungeon.
A dancer from the club’s ground floor, hired as muscle, and better at it than the hiring implied.
Geraldo, monk seal. The same level as the last one, and coming across the beach straight at the crawlers, shouting.
An aquatic melee tank who was not wearing the headband before he was captured, and has not taken it off since.
A liaison who disagrees with his own side’s philosophy and is working, openly enough, to take two crawlers off the board.
A name out of an old debt, and a price somebody declined to pay.
A Grixist heiress, chief executive of Icon Industries, and a god to drive whenever she is bored.
“I am the way, motherfucker.” Level one hundred and forty, undead, origin Ecuador, seventy-five seconds at a time.
One of the club’s people, with a coupon worth a hundred thousand gold.
A level ninety Skin Skellie who took the announcer’s booth rather than the stage, and does both jobs better than the club deserves.
A veteran of Land War, a different game on a different planet, and a battalion commander on the strength of it.
Garret, a tummy acher. A level-20 pet show entry as tall as a man, received on this floor as a gift for going to Crawl Con.
A Tummy Acher handed over as a door prize for turning up to a convention, and now levelling in a war.
Epitome Tagg. The name a captured hunter gives for the man who sent him: not after the gear, only after Louis, who besmirched his mother's honour.
Son of Epitome Noflex, leader of the Dream, and dressed like any other elf in the room.
A level seventy-five Bugbear who does a little of everything, racing a vehicle he is fond of for a team that named itself.
A Mandagot Fink, level eighty-one, one of two, and rude in a way that reads as policy rather than temper.
Black hair, a Kentucky accent by Carl’s reckoning, and the half of the pair that does the talking.
Freckled, red-haired, chewing tobacco, and content to let her partner do the talking.
A tourist who has attached himself to a crawler he says he admires, and the System files him as exactly that.
A totem card left switched on by accident, and now somebody’s pet.
Chris Andrews 2. The name on a dead goat's corpse, credited with an assist on a kill by a Brandon An.
Chris Andrews 2. Night staff at Meadow Lark and Brandon's quieter brother. He does not say much. When he does, listen.
Chris Andrews. Took a rock race called an igneous, fought with his brother, and walked out of the party. He answers nobody.
Chris Andrews. Igneous. Killed Frank Q in the Desperado Club, walked out, and is banned from the club.
Chris Andrews. A living host with a Scree in his brain, awake behind his own eyes and unable to stop anything his body does.
Chris Andrews. Igneous, and his own man again, with the worm gone and his brother's last message delivered.
Chris Andrews. Quiet lava-rock crawler, inseparable from a cretin named Clay-ton. Imani loves him for his simplicity and his quiet kindness.
Chris Andrews. A werewolf in his Meadow Lark overalls. He told Imani he loves her, and stepped through a portal that was meant to lead out.
Chris Andrews. Werewolf, unconscious in Sheol, with a warning flashing over his head: Change imminent.
Brandon An. The name on a dead goat's corpse: killed by him, with an assist from a Chris Andrews 2.
Brandon An. Night staff at Meadow Lark, hammer over his shoulder, walking thirty-odd elderly residents down a dungeon because he cannot leave them.
Brandon. Held the line against shade gremlins so the others could reach the stairs. His last message was for his brother.
Yolanda Martinez. CNA on the night shift at Meadow Lark, four foot eleven, level five, with a quiver so big it almost drags on the floor.
Yolanda Martinez. A nurse her entire life. She stood over a fallen resident in front of a rage elemental and did not move.
Yolanda Martinez. Nurse at Meadow Lark, one of Imani's best friends. Imani's guild carries her name: Safehome Yolanda.
Tally. Bopca Protector, level 63, caretaker of the first safe room. Cooks to a human spice scale and calls the cat Your Highness.
Tally. Bopca Protector of the first safe room. Never a crawler: his world was offered a deal instead of mining, and he went. Very long ago.

entities.name: Magistrate Featherfall
entities.role: Magistrate of a skyfowl settlement · third floor

taglines.text: Magistrate Featherfall. His signature on a gate pass tells the city guard the holder is acting on his orders.
Magistrate Featherfall. Skyfowl, and the big boss of his village. According to his clerk, he does not like being disturbed.
Former Magistrate Featherfall. Dark cleric, level 32, hanging upside down in a dreamcatcher of bone. Dead long before the blast that took credit for it.
Former Magistrate Featherfall. Wanted the town's swordsmen for himself, cast the spell too close to the amplifier, and the feedback killed him. His clerk planned it.
Pustule. Hobgoblin, level 30, proprietor of Hobgobs and Boom Sticks in the Silk Road market. Excellent hearing.
Pustule. Hobgoblin explosives dealer at the Silk Road. Her smoke curtains do exactly what she said they would.
Princess Formidable of the Skull Empire. The name on Crawler Katia's sponsorship notice, and so far the only thing anybody knows about her.
Princess Formidable, youngest sister of Prince Maestro and Crown Prince Stalwart. Her first gift to her crawler is one crossbow bolt, made for a god's eye.
Princess Formidable. In orbit over Earth, on the line to the Syndicate Council, demanding the failsafe be pulled with herself inside the blast.
Princess Formidable. Took one of her father's warships to trip the failsafe by hand, and was lifted off it by the AI at level one. She chose Earth's surface.
Gore-Gore. ManTauR, level 40, Ochre Line Train Engineer. Four arms, blue paint, a great deal of shouting, and devotion to Grull.
Gore-Gore, engineer of the ochre line. Answered every question put to him, took offence, and met the third rail. Left a key, a map, and Crawler Katia short of four fingers.
Vernon. Yellow Line Train Conductor, dwarf, level 32. Employees only, he says, without looking up from his drink.
Vernon, the yellow line's conductor. Kept a loop of gold and a stack of drawings of his wife, and went up with car five when the fire ants came out of Princess Donut's prize.
Gwendolyn Duet. A voice in the crawler chat, telling everyone that the bomber guy warned all of them.
Gwen. Level-27 Boring Ol' Fighter, in bubble 543's land quadrant among crawlers she calls dumbasses. The only crawler who answered Carl.
Gwen. From Canada, about forty-five, five feet of hard labour with a spear and a forehead tattoo. Wants the sandcastle flooded, and has been made to wait.
Gwen. Boring Ol' Fighter, spear, forehead tattoo. Hailed for liberating the bubble's subterranean throne room, and fights beside Katia like one half of a pack.
Gwendolyn Duet. Instrumental in the crawlers' survival among the bubbles, killed in the fight against Imogen on the floor after.
Commandant Kane of the Dreadnaught Wasteland. So far only a name in someone else's file: the man whose uncle is chained under Hump Town as the price of peace.
Commandant Kane. Keeper of the twin to Henrik's watch, master of the bombers, and, once his dreadnaught comes apart, one gnome in a floating house with his daughter.
Commandant Kane. Found across his own kitchen table, ripped to shreds by his daughter's pet, with a letter from the Glass Wizard and a watch on him.
Wynne. Dirigible Gnome Flesh Mechanic, chained under Hump Town's town hall as the price of a truce, who would rather be killed than cast the spell his captors want.
Wynne. The Commandant's uncle, dead in a basement, whose head was raised for half an hour so a cat and her manservant could ride his return ticket up to the Wasteland.
Vadim. One of two survivors of the water quadrant, who say there are horrors down near the ocean floor and do not want to go back.
Vadim Zbar. Kuhli Gut Rearranger, level 28, a cosmetic surgeon in the old world, and the one water survivor willing to lead the way back down.
Vadim Zbar. Guided the dive to the Akula, sealed himself upstairs when the boss came, and fired the last escape pod up into the jellyfish.

entities.name: Lusca
entities.role: City boss · fifth floor, water quadrant

taglines.text: Lusca. Octo-Shark Brood Mother Queen, level 82 city boss, a mouthbrooder with a boatload of hungry babies, and the crawlers are what is for dinner.
Lusca. The sharktopus under the water quadrant: swallowed the Akula whole, and was left on the ocean floor with her upper jaw peeled back and a line cut through her brain.
Tish. A furious signature under a council letter to Ghazi: they needed that artifact, and he threw it away for a woman who is not real.
Tish. The woman Ghazi wrote his last letter to, and the one Samantha says almost ruined everything.
Tish. Ghazi's ex, still working at the college in Larracos, and top of a talking head's list of people to kill.

entities.name: Denise
entities.role: Borough boss · fifth floor, air quadrant

taglines.text: Denise, the Feral Goose Mother. A level 53 borough boss in a baby-blue bonnet, a gnome child's newest pet, and the reason magic stops working in the Commandant's house.
Denise, the Feral Goose Mother. Killed the Commandant, made every spell useless, and went head first into a garbage disposal with one second on the clock.
Denise, the Feral Goose Mother. Borough boss, killer of a commandant, headless in a kitchen sink. On the record, she also loved reading to children.
Circe Took of the Hive. Moderator of a CrawlCon panel called Crawling Through the Ages. That is the whole listing.
Circe Took. Minor hive queen, mantis, former hunter, now a businesswoman with an amusement park. A daughter of hers died on her first hunt, and the crawler responsible is on her panel.
Circe Took of the Dark Hive. Humiliated on her own panel, she has sponsored the god Diwata. Vrah's mother is coming into the game.
Circe Took of the Dark Hive. Came down inside the god Diwata for her daughter's sake. Stripped of the god in the final arena, she was torn apart by her own children.

entities.name: Dmitri and Maxim Popov
entities.role: Nodling crawler · two brothers, one body

taglines.text: Dmitri and Maxim Popov. Nodling, Illusionist and Bogatyr, level thirty, ninth on the board at a hundred thousand. Two names, one line.
Dmitri and Maxim Popov: one two-headed nodling, fifth on the board. Dmitri is a Visionary now; the other half is still a Bogatyr. They fight with a meteor hammer.
Dmitri and Maxim Popov. Fraternal twins from Bulgaria, sharing one body because a game guide did not mention that detail. Dmitri would very much like to meet the cat.
Dmitri and Maxim Popov. Killed in the final arena, split into two baby nodlings, ruled ineligible, and removed. Children are not allowed in the crawl. They are out.
Hunter Zabit. Owner of a Night Weasel Scout called Tootsie, and of the rest of the pack that came with her.
Hunter Zabit. Atoll, level sixty-six Beastmaster, twenty-five scalps. Hunts to pay the upkeep on his people's habitat, and does not claim it makes him feel powerful.
Hunter Zabit, Atoll Beastmaster. Went invisible in the final arena beside the traps he had just laid. Crawler Carl set them off.
Viscount Fog. The great, now-deceased hunter of vampires, who set out to exterminate a bloodsucker named Miriam Dom. It went bad.
Viscount Fog, star of Blood Hunter. A duel of reflected spells left him frozen and cursed to wither away from light. He did not last past sunset.
Theia, a goddess who turns prospective worshippers into motes of light and entertains them at her temple. Samantha's mother. Never sponsored, until this season.
Theia, Samantha's mother. This season she is driven by Rectrix, an agent of the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, and Crawler Carl is a friend of her church.
Slit. Feral Minor Demon, level two hundred, one of the harem thrown into the Nothing. Out, arena-sized, and certain Samantha slept with her king. A god tore her in half.
Slit, feral minor demon of the harem, torn in half by a god at the end of the fifth floor. Minge, who has just got out, is her little sister.
Paz Lo. Level forty-five human Santero, a worshipper of Ogun, in silver plate armour and a backwards cap. Travels with his cousin Anton and the nun they both protect.
Paz Lo. A former guard at a women's prison, burned by his own god, who told Carl what Sister Ines is, asked to be let go, and was flagged into a card instead.
Paz Lo. A card in a goddess's war, turned against her: a bolt in her eye and his own self-destruct at her neck. The system credits him with the kill.
Paz Lo, the God Predator. A card that killed a goddess, ripped at the collapse because that is what he asked for.
Uzzi. Mordecai's brother, a skyfowl Storm Commander who guarded his party's stairwell on the tenth floor, seasons ago. He died there, a dart in his breast, so a god could be summoned.
Uzzi. Mordecai's brother, dead at a tenth-floor stairwell. Odette has now told Carl her part in it: an illegal deal, broken at the last minute.
Yemaya, the river mother. One broken shrine among seven, blue as ice, and the one Katia tells Carl he has to repair.
Yemaya, Goddess of Rivers. A twin-tailed siren, retainer to Eileithyia, woken by crawlers in her own temple, where she hands out cards and sends a cretin to another floor when asked.
Carl's father. A linebacker, once, which Carl offers as part of the explanation for his own size.
Carl's father. The last time Carl saw him, Carl called him a bully and waited to be hit. The man laughed instead.
Carl's father. A weekend biker who abandoned his son more than twelve years ago and has not been heard from since.
Carl's father. Found in a memory from the summer before the collapse: dying in a hospital bed in an Iowa trailer, with a young wife, a small son, and a morphine overdose on its way.
Carl's father. Dead before the collapse, of the overdose his second wife gave him. His son declines to say his name.
Asher. About six, in an Iowa trailer, scared of storms, with his father's nose and too much hair. Carl's half-brother, whom Carl did not know existed.
Asher. Carl's half-brother, known to Bea and kept from Carl. His face was a head on a hydra; Carl reckons everyone on it was taken in the collapse.
The Night Wyrm. A name on a ring Frank hands Carl: the Enchanted Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering.
The Night Wyrm. A demigod outside the regular pantheon, worshipped by a cult called the Guild of Suffering, whose spiderweb tattoo Carl wears on his elbow.
The Night Wyrm. Head of the Guild of Suffering, a hissing voice that calls crawlers its darlings, and the client on Katia's contract to kill Astrid.
Hamed, the Night Wyrm. Astrid's husband and the father of two dancers, playing a demigod, who had his wife killed through two crawlers. His sons have gone after him.
Hamed, the Night Wyrm. The new management at the Desperado Club: every crawler banned, and bodyguards who are not exactly NPCs.
Hamed, the Night Wyrm. Master of the Desperado Club, whom the AI calls a despot attempting a dungeon revolution for the early indentured.

entities.name: Architect Houston
entities.role: Warlord of the Madness · ninth floor

taglines.text: Architect Houston. Leader of the Madness, a Viceroy outworlder, and the name a dwarf swears revenge on. Nobody has got into his operating theater.
Architect Houston. Viceroy, warlord of the Madness. White robes, a white mask with a red teardrop, and not one word at an adjudication about his own team.
Architect Houston. Warlord of the Madness and a scientist first. He has named his life's work: reaching the creature his people call the Beautiful Place.
Architect Houston. On his own operating table when the traps fired. His fall and the defeat of the Madness arrived in the same notice.
Boomer. A former crawler Crawler Carl has never met, leading the 106th Bloody Leeches.
Colonel Boomer. Elven Legate, level 62. A tenner, banned from CrawlCon, wanted over a killing, and chewing an unlit cigar.
Colonel Boomer. In command of the assault on the Reavers, and willing to tell his warlord to his face to leave it to him.
Boomer. Outside the dungeon, on the radio to the Homecoming Queen with a bad poem and an order to warm up the lasers.

entities.name: Warlord Fang
entities.role: Warlord of the Reavers · ninth floor

taglines.text: Warlord Fangs of the Reavers, as he introduces himself: an old-school square-headed robot rattling like a diesel engine, a look put on for the crawlers' benefit.
Warlord Fang of the Reavers. This time a thin, too-pink young man in white underwear, with a line of lights down one temple.
Warlord Fang. Almost all machine, able to change shape, among the richest of the warlords and the least known. A piece of his brain is kept at home.
Warlord Fang. Hid inside his own drake over a castle full of bombs.
Hapanzi, if Crawler Carl has the name right. A second spider from the dream, Shi Maria's husband, and a god. He says she is trapped.
Hapanzi. Shi Maria's husband, devoured in a memory, back as a spider to tell Crawler Carl that she is sealed inside him.

entities.name: Kimaris
entities.role: A demon, stuffed · Carl's most valuable item

taglines.text: Kimaris, according to the tag. A plush armoured man on a black horse, sealed in one of Miss Quill's glass cases and unbroken beside the blast.
Stuffed Kimaris Figure, with tags. Unique, and the most valuable thing Crawler Carl owns. The description only says Kimaris scowls.
Kimaris. A demon, stuffed, and a plush like this is a true summoning: pull the tag, and the real one arrives.
Kimaris. One of the brothers of Sheol, summoned for the remainder of a floor, and one of Samantha's best friends. She calls him Kimmy.

entities.name: The Midnight Epicure
aka: The Caprid Who Devours the Sky
entities.role: A caprid fable, and Prepotente's god

taglines.text: The Midnight Epicure, the Caprid Who Devours the Sky. A story to frighten children into eating dinner, and a goat's head worn as a ward against the night.
The Midnight Epicure. The god Prepotente worships, and a name the caprid council panics over on live television.
The Midnight Epicure. Protector of prey, who destroys all existence and releases the eaten back into the galaxy. A scare story about caprids that caprids made their hope.
York. The crawler who wrote the tenth edition of the Cookbook: pages of rambling philosophy, and a last entry about living inside a hive and being alone in it.
York. Tenth-edition author, from a hive, alone all his life. The eleventh edition's author read him and wondered whether he survived.
York. Somewhere in orbit with a job from Rosetta: shoot down an orc yacht with children aboard. She hopes he does it rather than write a poem.
York. Tenodera, level 71, tenth-edition author, alone aboard the Homecoming Queen with his terrible poems. He destroyed the yacht.
Princess Chandra, Esquire. Assigned as Crawler Donut's lawyer in Quasar's place. According to Quasar, she is also Crawler Carl's new wife.
Princess Chandra, Esquire. Rishi's widow, who claimed his killer as her husband under Naga law and had herself made Crawler Donut's attorney. She intends to be very rich.
Princess Chandra, Esquire. In hiding since Crawler Donut's public non-offer, and still filing. The Taurins she hired went after Quasar's family and found his niece armed.
Grigori the Placid. Human, level ninety-three Fleshmancer, hired mercenary of Team Meadow Lark, worshipper of Gula. Does not care for crumbs.
Grigori the Placid, fleshmancer. Joined the two halves of a mantaur in the back of a moving truck, upside down, while being sick.
Grigori the Placid. A dungeon-born NPC, and so available: at the parade the AI takes him over and speaks with his voice.

entities.name: Chalchiuhtlicue
entities.role: Goddess · among the children in Lucia Mar
