taglines.text: Chalchiuhtlicue. A goddess, newly present among the children inside Lucia Mar. She tells them she is kind, and that the kindest thing may be letting them die.
Chalchiuhtlicue, Chachi to Samantha. Goddess of childbirth, water and fire, never sponsored. Samantha says she talks about protecting children and then kills them.
Lamashtu. So far only a name on a scroll in a list of prizes, the Milk of Lamashtu. Crawler Carl has no idea what it does.
Lamashtu the Donkey. A former god subjugated by the AI, her level halved under the Ascendency rules, now a parade mount. Samantha calls her a friend.
Crawler Forkith, a signature in the Cookbook's margins. Twentieth edition. Confirms a trick with smoke curtains and undead.
Forkith. Urgyle, Sapper, author of the Cookbook's twentieth edition, reached at least the eleventh floor. His notes carry his sister Barkith, who was all he had left.
Forkith. In Sheol, out of the code, friends with Pontiff and, sort of, with Crawler Carl. A lot of them have been waiting a very long time to move.

entities.name: The Gate of the Feral Gods

taglines.text: A teleport that works by tearing a hole in the prison the old gods were thrown into. Something always comes back through.

descriptions.text: New Quest. The Gate of the Feral Gods. Henrik the Changeling. Commandant Kane. The Mad Dune Mage. They all have pieces of the artifact. Take it from them. Collect all three. Put them together. What happens next is pretty damn neat. Reward: Oh boy-oh-boy.

taglines.text: An explosion large enough to rattle the teeth of a god. It goes off the instant it leaves his inventory.

descriptions.text: Carl's Doomsday Scenario. Type: Unstable custom explosive. Effect: An explosion large enough to rattle the teeth of a god. Status: Explosion Imminent. Created by a man who murders babies and steals rare collectibles from his elders, this device is powerful enough to level an entire city and all the suburbs around it. It is created by combining a massively overloaded soul crystal and a Sheol Glass Reaper Case. Warning: This item can no longer be stabilized.

entities.name: Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore

taglines.text: A tiara of dark smoky gems that enrols the wearer in a royal succession eight floors down.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore. Who's a dirty girl? You're a dirty girl! This is a Fleeting item! This is a Unique* item! Imbues wearer with +5 Intelligence, grants the user +5 to the Good First Impression Skill. All attacks, including magical attacks, now have a 15% chance to inflict the Sepsis Debuff. Warning! (Seriously though. I'm going to say this again. WARNING! Read this shit before you put it on.) Placing this crown upon your head permanently places you within the royal line of succession for the Blood Sultanate on the ninth floor of the world dungeon. Removing this item will not remove this status. Royal members of the Blood Sultanate will be required to slay the Sultan and all other members of the royal family before descending to the tenth floor. You'll only want to wear this if you're a blood-thirsty, raging psychopath.

taglines.text: A unique book off a prize carousel: chicken and goblin recipes galore, each with a tale from its anonymous author.
Passed hand to hand by the crawlers of earlier seasons. Carl is its twenty-fifth holder.

descriptions.text: Book. The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook by Anonymous. This is a unique item. Chicken and Goblin recipes galore! But it's more than that, too. Each recipe is accompanied by a hilarious tale by the anonymous author, recounting some of the zany and madcap misadventures they experienced gathering these mouth-watering recipes. Fun for the whole family! This book is a real hoot.

taglines.text: Makes an animal sapient. One biscuit, one cat, and the shape of the entire crawl changes.

descriptions.text: Enhanced Pet Biscuit. So, it looks like a regular pet biscuit. It's not. Feed to your pet at your own risk. What's the worst that can happen?

entities.name: Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering

taglines.text: A curse from a man who wanted Carl dead, worn anyway for the five percent.
Mark a target, kill it, take its stats. Mordecai says it is addictive, and he is not being figurative.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering. Oooh, that's scary sounding. For the discerning Crawler Killer, this magical ring can be one of the most formidable items in the dungeon. If utilized properly, this ring's wielder can grow exponentially in strength, especially on the deeper floors. But beware. If poorly wielded, this ring will kill you quicker than an exploding rage elemental. Either way, this ring imparts one of the dungeon's most highly sought-after skills. The wearer of this ring receives the following benefits: +5% to all stats. The Marked For Death skill.

taglines.text: Eat the flower, spend an hour at one percent, and a goddess decides what you become.

descriptions.text: Warning: This item can only be used by a female. Or a male, if you're a seahorse. It's a flower. You're supposed to eat it, though it might be a good decoration instead. […] Anyway, if you eat this flower, it renders you unconscious for one hour with your health at 1% of your max. You cannot heal during this time. If you survive this ordeal, you will be given one of three permanent boons from the goddess Eileithyia. The given boon is at the discretion of the goddess, and it cannot be predicted. If you choose to worship Eileithyia before you consume this flower, the descriptions of the boons will be expanded. She will also ask you which of the three you'd prefer. Her cooperation is not guaranteed, especially if she doesn't like you. But Eileithyia is known to be a generous goddess.

taglines.text: Something a cult keeps, by Mordecai's account: a crystal like a soul crystal, except nobody has ever established what it does.
What is left of someone when the dungeon is finished with them, and worth stealing.

descriptions.text: Memorial Crystal. Apito. This item is 0% charged.
Memorial Crystal. Emberus.

taglines.text: Out of a celestial box, from a waste-management company, on the eve of a war.

descriptions.text: The Tiara of a Thousand Lights and Accompanying Charge Pillow. This is a unique item. This item was made especially for Crawler Princess Donut by her sponsor, Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions. […] This particular tiara is imbued with 99 Absorption Jewels. The tiara itself has no inherent magical properties, and in its base state it gives no additional benefits or buffs except plus 10 to Charisma. However, it has the ability to be permanently charged with up to 99 different buff items. […] With some careful planning, one can turn this tiara into one of the most powerful items in the history of Dungeon Crawler World. Okay, here come the warnings.

taglines.text: A back patch of stacked skulls for Carl's jacket: divine, unique, fleeting, and what it does depends on which gods are standing near.
Worth a war-mage extraction to get hold of, and it swaps every crawler's inventory with the nearest crawler's.

descriptions.text: The Scavenger's Daughter. Upgrade Patch. Back Patch. This is a divine item. This is a unique item. This is a fleeting item. You may only affix one back patch at a time. This patch depicts a pile of scary skulls, all stacked up nice and neat. I wonder if there's a story there? If this upgrade patch is affixed to an eligible garment, it will imbue the following upgrades: (Hidden until it is affixed and then worn.) […] Warning #2! This is a divine item. This means it gains differing abilities, buffs, and possibly debuffs depending on your proximity to certain deities and demons. It makes for new and exciting combinations!

taglines.text: A double-width spot on a casino wheel, marked Nothing! Hit its twin on the roulette table and the floor opens, something with claws reaches up, and the player is gone.
Where the pantheon put the old gods and demons. Every shortcut the Gate takes goes through it.
A two-foot wicker scoop that clamps to a forearm. The fans picked it, and it throws whatever he summons into it.
Range, accuracy, and a bolt-on slot for throwing a head. Everything Carl builds has to get somewhere.

descriptions.text: Enchanted Xistera Extension Slot (Head-throwing attachment). This is a unique item! This item was created especially for Crawler Carl by The Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network, Intergalactic NFC. Attaches to the end of a xistera. Allows for the tossing of a head. This special edition head tosser is custom made to fit decapitated love doll heads. When tossing a head of a withering spirit, the distance traveled will be greatly enhanced. (500 meters x Strength) Tossed head will be magically returned once the extension slot is removed from xistera.

taglines.text: A potion from a gold Looter Box: one level in one named skill, and a remark about your card collection thrown in.
One level in one named skill, and the System has opinions about how you have been spending your money.

descriptions.text: Skill Potion. Drinking this adds a single level to the Determine Value skill. Hopefully now you'll realize all those Magic: The Gathering cards are nothing more than just meaningless pieces of paper, and you should have spent your money on something with actual value, like a treadmill. Or shampoo.

entities.name: The Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo

taglines.text: A convention message board rendered as a book. Write under a crawler's name and only that crawler reads it.
The System insists it is not named for anything nefarious, and keeps nudging Carl toward a second use for it.

descriptions.text: When you meet a crawler who owns this same item, their name will permanently appear in this enchanted book. You may use the book to exchange messages. You may write your message under their name, and only they will receive it. If you write under your own name, everyone who has your entry will see the message. You may write your message manually or using the messaging interface while turned to the page. One must open the book to read the message, but you will have the option to copy the words. Message will erase on demand, allowing one to write a new note. This book is not retroactively filled with the entries of people you have already met. You must be within close-ish vicinity of them for their name to be added. Works only with crawlers who also own this book.

taglines.text: A reward the audience fills by vote. Receive one and you wait thirty hours to open it while the followers decide.
The audience chooses what is inside, and the audience is made to wait thirty hours before you may open it.
The one box only a patron can send, and by Mordecai's reckoning even a bronze one beats a plain gold box.
A box bought for you by somebody who wants you to keep going, and rank for rank it beats anything the dungeon hands out on merit.
A tracked all-terrain suicide machine, built by hand, and the System’s own write-up of it is mostly abuse.

descriptions.text: Tracked All-Terrain Suicide Machine. The Royal Chariot – Contraption. If a snowmobile got drunk on moonshine and had a sweaty, ill-advised night with a hillbilly’s coon-hunting ATV, this oversized birth defect of a vehicle would be the result.

taglines.text: Twenty-five thousand gold buys a machine to tidy the personal space. Nobody who has looked at one properly is buying it for the tidying.
A stealth bomber carrying a name from a party-supply catalogue, handed over as the prize for having been marked for death.

descriptions.text: Casket in the Sky. Party Planner. Tilt Rotor Stealth Light Bomber. Vehicle. This vehicle is classed as tier three Armor.

taglines.text: A goblin motorcycle running on steam, with a sidecar built to hold a princess.

descriptions.text: Goblin Copper Chopper with attached sidecar. Human-sized. Contraption. Take a junkyard bicycle, add an unreliable steam engine, remove all the bolts holding it together.

taglines.text: Rev-Up moonshine, a splash of goblin oil, and a torch for a cork. Burns hotter, bigger and faster than a Molotov, and it has Carl's name on it.
Rev-Up moonshine and a torch for a cork, entered in the Dungeon Codex under Carl's name. One gold coin to him for every kill another crawler makes with it.
A Dungeon Codex recipe with Carl's name on it. The moonshine it needs is no longer being made, and the royalties dried up after the first few coins.

descriptions.text: Created by an unstable, pantsless man who talks to a cat, Carl's Jug O' Boom takes the bigger-is-better approach when it comes to hobgoblin fire bottles. Burns hotter, bigger, and faster than your normal Molotov Cocktail. The use of a standard torch instead of a cloth wick makes these devices much more stable. Just don't drop it once it's lit, lest you find yourself doing a Joan of Arc impersonation.

taglines.text: One of a hundred. An ordinary crossbow bolt unless it lands in a god's eye, and then fifteen seconds without invulnerability. Katia's, from Princess Formidable.
The bolt that opened a goddess to a killing blow. Magical bolts can be used again if they don't break, and Katia still has this one.
Katia's bolt, fired from Donut's back straight into Emberus's eye. Fifteen seconds of a god with no invulnerability, and Taranis used them.

descriptions.text: The Bolt of Ophiotaurus. This is 1 of 100. This item acts as a regular crossbow bolt unless it is shot directly into the eye of a deity. Upon a successful strike to the god's eye, the deity's invulnerability pauses for fifteen seconds.

taglines.text: A spiked ball that summons its thrower's god for sixty seconds. Maggie My's, from the Skull Empire, meant to bring the god of pain down on Carl. Carl has it now.
Maggie's grenade, thrown by Carl instead. Emberus arrived, Quan Ch did not get his shot off, and Carl had sixty seconds in which nothing could hurt him.

descriptions.text: These little balls of fun were developed by the nuns of Enyo during the first enlightenment, back when the gods had to compete for worshippers. The nuns would descend upon a village and proselytize to the people about why their goddess was the best. If the villagers didn't immediately fall to their knees in veneration, the nuns would be forced to invoke a more aggressive campaign. A nun would drop a celestial grenade, which would summon Enyo directly into town for a period of sixty seconds. That was usually enough to change the minds of the survivors. Celestial grenades grant the following effects: If the wielder of the grenade has pledged themselves to a specific deity, this grenade will summon their god for sixty seconds. In addition, the wielder will receive a 60-second Divine Intervention aura. If the wielder does not worship a deity, this grenade will summon a random god. They will not receive the Divine Intervention buff.

taglines.text: Every structure on the planet comes down at once. Everyone indoors dies.
Eighteen levels. Complete the last one and the planet reverts to whoever did it.
Every floor runs on a timer. When it expires the floor collapses with everyone still on it.
The crawl is a television programme, broadcast across the galaxy. The survivors are the cast.
Between-floor highlight shows. The only reliable way a crawler learns what anyone else is doing.
Carl has received several of something, and it sounds a lot like loot boxes. The rat man says where they live, then says Carl cannot get at them yet.
Six tiers — Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Legendary, Celestial — each dramatically rarer than the last.
A unique monk/rogue hybrid. Trapmaker, bomb-maker, social-media dynamo.
A bard/rogue class that lets her choose another class at every single level.
The crawlers-only bar that persists between floors. Bouncer, house rules, a stage, and a hiring hall.
A door in the safe room with an X over it. Personal Spaces are not yet available, the box says; they go on sale on the fourth level.
A pocket room you carry with you. Upgrade it far enough and other people can walk into yours.
The dungeon's non-player characters have histories, families, and scripts written for them by producers.
On the ninth floor there are no respawns and no loopholes.
The blank slate. Costs five stat points and hands back every skill ceiling in the dungeon.
Orren says the word out loud on the recap: Primal Engines, Macro AIs, and a machine that has stopped taking orders.
Not extinct. Pooled. The first species to conquer the universe closed its own society down and kept the minds.

descriptions.text: For the first several seasons of Dungeon Crawler World, all contestants started off as Primals. Primals are blank slates. You will look the same as before. You will obtain all skills associated with your current race, with the following exceptions: -1 to all base stats. All higher-tier skills are unlocked and are able to train to 20. Choosing this race unlocks multiple exclusive, earth-based classes.

taglines.text: A war mage named Dismember rides the Dismemberment Limited, and loses his head to a cat.
Sapient magic in a resleeved skeleton, hundreds of spells deep, and cruel. Showrunners rent them by the war and hardly ever recycle them.
They took the one thing they came for and left the realm. Winning was never on the list.

descriptions.text: System Message: The War Mage Rebellion is not an active team. As per the current season's rules, the team currently occupying the Bone Clan's throne room, Team Retribution, will be awarded all their assets.

taglines.text: Borant's answer to crawlers relieving themselves outside the designated areas. It kills the offender, and it kills the party.
Fifteen feet of smoke on six obsidian claws, said to disperse at six hundred and sixty-six souls. It gets a car chase instead.

descriptions.text: Rage Elemental - Level 93. The first recorded summoning of a Rage Elemental, blah, blah, blah. If you are reading this, you likely don't give a shit about the monster's (rather interesting and tragic) history. You're probably running. It's not going to matter. The almost-indestructible Rage Elemental is said to only dissipate after it has claimed 666 souls. In other words, you are fucked. Absolutely, bite-the-pillow, fucked.

taglines.text: What Mordecai became on the third floor: a shapeshifter who takes a new form every time his guildhall is moved.
Take any shape you like. The catch is what happens when the dungeon takes the choosing away from you.
A whole population of them down here, wearing whichever face the job requires, and worth torturing for what they can be made to become.
Nine families fight it on the ninth floor. A boastful heir says his has won six of the last ten, and the Naga always go out first.

Nine armies, bought and paid for by people who will never stand in one of them, fight for the castle at the bottom of the ninth floor's funnel city. Crawlers are meant to keep their heads down and let it pass over.
Ten teams, the sponsors' safety protections voted away, and a crawler army holding one of the slots. Faction Wars with the crawlers inside it rather than beside it.
The safety protocols the faction sponsors fight inside and the crawlers do not, and an action item that can take them away.
Something a warlord is apparently assigned. Mordecai asks who theirs is, gets a blank look, and puts off explaining.
A neutral referee attached to each team on the ninth floor. Invulnerable, usually famous, and mostly there to talk to camera.
Mordecai's rule of thumb, offered over a dead goose: anything with feral in the name is usually bad news.
A word the System puts in front of a name when whatever it is has been somewhere it should not have been, and came back.
Feral is the System's word for anything the Nothing has had its hands on. Whatever comes back out of that place comes back mad, and stays mad.
Land crabs spawn in the monk seals' holy water once a year. The System would like the crawlers to pick a side.

descriptions.text: New Quest. The Chowder War. Oh, you're getting involved whether you like it or not. The Monk Seals. The Red Maníseros Land Crabs. War is brewing, as it often does in these parts. Every season, the land crabs emerge from their forests to attend their sex parties in the oceans surrounding these lands. The Monk Seals hold the ocean sacred, and the very act of spilling so much crab chowder into their holy waters is considered a sacrilege most foul... Choose a side. Put an end to this conflict, one way or another. Reward: You will receive a Platinum Quest Box.

taglines.text: Something is driving the dinosaurs at Point Mongo's fences. Find out what they want, or exterminate them.

descriptions.text: New Quest! The Recital. Dinosaur attacks are becoming more and more of a problem in the large settlement of Point Mongo. It started small. A chicken here. An Ursine there. People didn't care so much at first since they were mostly picking off the annoying people. But the attacks are getting worse. The dinosaurs probing the town's defenses are getting bigger... Exterminate the threat. Or, find out what they want, and then give it to them. I'll leave it up to you. Reward: You will receive a Gold Quest Box! You will also receive a free town upgrade!

taglines.text: The fan convention, held once every other season. Thousands attend in the flesh, billions attend as projections, and this season a live crawler is on the programme.

descriptions.text: Thanks to your fans, you've been added to the CrawlCon roster! You will attend three events! Your presence at the con will be virtual. Please see your outreach associate for details on your schedule.

taglines.text: A formal way to attach separate parties to each other, mentioned only in the cookbook's twenty-second edition, switched on from the sixth floor, if it still exists.
Buy a charter and five parties can share one room, one set of upgrades and, for a fee, their experience. Allies stop having to be party members.
A Syndicate drama serial shot inside the dungeon. A circus, a murdered mother, an exiled tsarina, and a guest slot with Carl's name on it.
The grief is real and the schedule is not. Someone outside the floor decides when she mourns, and whether it rates.
Bought by the Dream, which means to collect on a third season it is owed.
Warmth and light coming up out of a hole in the floor, which is how the dungeon says the level above has finished with you.
The plainest attack spell in the catalogue, taught to a show cat by a show cat, minutes after anyone thought to open her menus.
Green on the minimap, always, even where the map is dark. Restrooms, somewhere to sleep, three screens, and a cook who would rather you moved along.
Short, hairy and green-tinted. They scrub the toilets, cook the food, and never wash their hands in between.
Short, hairy and green-tinted. Excellent cooks, and miserly about anything they have not been ordered to part with.
The cleaning crew of the second floor. They eat what gets killed, and they grow on it.
Two working copies of a pet, moving on their own, and the dungeon’s own labels decline to say which of the three is real.
The best-behaved ghouls in the rail system, in a field with very little competition.
Whoever handles employee return on the line, according to a train engineer: they prepare the staff with dark magic before the portal, and the portal does something to memory.
Employee management for the tangle, waiting at the station where the staff get off, and nobody can agree whether they are a boss or a fixture.
What Mordecai was born as, going by the framed photo of his brother. His people, he says, outlast humans because they roll with it.
One of six species the Syndicate scatters over candidate worlds, and a people who mostly decline the offer to stop being one.
One of the caged pets on offer: a meatball with two legs and a mohawk.
A pet-class mob the size of a meatball, and stronger for every time it has died.
A five-mana spell: an audible ping that marks everything neither a crawler nor red-tagged, for those who do not care if their quarry knows they are coming.
A hunting call for people who do not mind whether the thing being hunted hears it coming.
Slugs leaking out of infected mercenaries every few minutes, hundreds of them in a room full of blood. Imani calls them punk rock. Carl corrects her.
Slugs born out of the boils of a disease, painted like a touring band, and enormously pleased to have been asked along.
Half human and, the System says, half human. Bred for strength and dexterity, which is to say for driving trains.
Half human, and, where the horse ought to be, also half human. The System calls it the strangest of the ’taurs and offers no defence of the design.
A spell that comes with a pair of boxers: a sphere no mob can enter, twenty seconds, once every thirty hours. It does not move with you.
A sphere no mob can enter, and it stays exactly where it was cast. Cast it on anything moving, and everything in its path meets a wall.

descriptions.text: A favorite of frontline tanks and castle guards, the expensive and rare Protective Shell spell shields the caster and anyone within the sphere from a mob's physical presence or physical attacks. This spell does not protect against magic or against non-corporeal entities. Unlike the more popular Shield spell, this spell does not move with you. This spell's area of effect remains static once cast, unimpeded by your physical surroundings.

taglines.text: Heavy metal, a frozen world, and a crawler's face with Death Challenge! stamped across it in blood. The dungeon has opened a book on how he dies.
Not a boss battle: a pop-up gambling event, at odds the AI sets. The first one put Carl's survival at fifty to one, and Borant is appealing.
Vorpal. A word a hobgoblin explosives dealer uses about a muskrat: her mother bit its head off, and you cannot do that to a vorpal muskrat without doing a little dying.
Vorpals. Whatever waits behind the Desperado Club's Do Not Enter door, released as a last resort when a demon gets loose on the middle floor.
Vorpals. A condition, not a species: deputised by the gods, drawn to demons, stronger the nearer one is, and liable to explode rather than lose.
T'Ghee. A card game from Allister's home planet, somewhere between chess and go fish, and part of a meditation-based religion. His Cookbook came as a deck of them.
T'Ghee totems. Plant a squad flag in something below five per cent health and it becomes a card that fights for whoever summons it. Twenty flags a squad, no refills.
T'Ghee cards. Totems, utility, snare, mystic and special. Four drawn when combat starts, one more every ten seconds, and a squad leader without spells or inventory until the deck is spent.
T'Ghee cards. The eighth floor's whole game, and a flag works on a dying crawler as well as on a monster.

entities.name: Containment Interface
entities.role: Bootleg interface upgrade · the AI's failsafe

taglines.text: A bootleg upgrade drunk from a homeless man's frozen coffee: access to the AI containment, and to the fuse that turns the sun nova.
Six tabs of numbers, a Fuse page with two of five conditions met, and one other button that switched all of it off. Pressed.
Regent of the solar system, owner of the broadcast, and the company that chose a dungeon as the way Earth gets its matter back.
Runs the show on the cheap, holds the foreclosure on Earth, and gets one veto a season.
The body whose rules Earth was seized under, subsection 543, and whose neutral AI has arrived to see those rules followed.
Three billion star systems, the rules Earth was seized under, and the audience for all of this.

entities.name: The Royal Court of Princess Donut

taglines.text: Named by a cat on the first floor, on the grounds that she had the highest stat total and nobody could stop her.
An elder care facility whose residents came down the stairs together and kept going.
Hekla's group: Icelandic, crossbows and breastplates, and growing.
Hekla's group, and the one Katia came in with.
A royal house on the ninth floor whose succession a cat joined by accident on the first.
A hundred and fifty men with rifles, down to eighty and counting their bullets.
Arrived as a recap segment and left as a wipe.
What Donut's fans are calling themselves, according to Zev. The rival name, the Donut Holes, does not have her approval.
Fifty thousand retired crawlers who came back in, under the banner of a cat.
Zebra-riding elves who favour poison, druid magic and long-range artillery. Outside the dungeon they are as humourless as the Skull Empire, and control half the universe's food.
Bald, pale elves with a territory of their own marked on the hunters' map of the grounds.
Half the food in the universe belongs to them, along with the entertainment channels, and they have a contract they intend to see honoured.
Their warlord is dead and their army is off the board.
Caprids. They own the tunnelling system, which is why anything that happens down here can be watched anywhere at all.
Carl's sponsor now. A full-grown goat stood in front of the cameras for fifteen seconds, bleated, and was gone.
Not a collective mind. A herd, and a herd bolts, which is why their matriarch treats a piece of news the way anyone else treats a loaded weapon.
The system the Maestro and his brother are princes of. If the orcs' other system is a lemonade stand, Zev says, this one is Wal-Mart.
One of the oldest and largest of the system governments, orcish, rich on weapons, and famously bad at letting an insult go.
Its army is at the wall on the ninth floor and its king has come with it.
The books are not its own. A financial criminal lives inside the empire and pays handsomely for the address.
A tax-exempt outfit nobody has heard of, which just won a sponsorship slot in a bidding war that ran to the final microsecond.
Crawlers who got out, and who want the whole thing stopped. Fifty thousand of them have come back in.
Every ship in orbit is theirs.
A democratic government of many races, whose army had a castle dropped on it before the season had properly started.
Caught cheating on the ninth floor, punished for it, and short one commander who took his own way out.
A megacorporation that is also a system government, living around its own star. An occasional entrant in this war, and a frequent winner of it.
Their pets arrive before they do: a swarm of Dumplins, every one of them carrying the Gurgles.
Several races who traded away everything but the brain for machinery, and kept going.
Warlord Fang hid inside his own pet, and the castle came down on the pair of them.
A name used as an insult: nobody in the Skull Clan wants to be mistaken for one.
Showrunners once. They ran the first crawl ever to lose money, and have not run a season since.
Cobra-headed, ruled out of the Blood Sultanate, and part of the push on the southern line.
The poverty was a performance. There were plans for the shipbuilding yards underneath it.
A signed offer on the table: citizenship for every native of Earth, in exchange for room in Earth's system.
The ninth floor's own people, fielded as the defending team, and allied with the crawlers from the first hour of it.
Their warlord turned into an Unwashed on camera and told the audience that it is coming for them all.
One of two teams still standing at the end of the war.
A collective mind spreading through the universe, and the thing the dungeon keeps drawing as the Krakaren.
Carl and Donut's third and final sponsor. Nobody on their side of it knows what she looks like.
One Primal who refused the collective, took the nine-tier attack, and is the reason anything biological is still here to watch this.
Dungeon-born magic elementals who stopped taking orders, and took the Gate with them on the way out.
Holding the castle at Larracos, six hours from taking the floor, and conscripting gods to keep it.
They leave with exactly what they came for, and a warning about Agatha on the way out.
The affiliation on a flying mantis hunter's tag, level 61, blood tracker: the Dark Hive.
A mantis hunting party on the Hunting Grounds, and Carl is on its list.
A maker's name on a relay, a personal shield and a pulse pistol found in Agatha's shopping cart. None of it belongs down here.
A power outside Borant that answers an insult by taking a prince’s yacht apart with his family aboard, and does not explain itself afterwards.
A business that is also a nation, run by a parasite that pilots other people’s bodies, and it holds the paper on Borant’s debt.
Carl's spiderweb tattoo grants access to it. Mordecai's word for it is a cult.
A cult you join by accident, the moment you accept a gift from something that would prefer to be worshipped.

entities.name: The Nebular Sin Patrol
entities.role: Hunting team of a nomadic cult

taglines.text: The Nebular Sin Patrol. A name on a dead hunter's map: one of the groups given ground near Zockau, with Prepotente and Miriam Dom claimed as targets.
The Nebular Sin Patrol: trainee priests of a nomadic, self-augmenting cult who consider anyone born on a seeded world an abomination, and hunt crawlers as a crusade.
The Nebulars. They worship the AI at the centre of the galaxy, call imitations blasphemy, and want the crawl shut down, along with every world that could host one. They sponsor Sister Ines.
The Viceroys' team: masked, often winners, specialists in horrific battlefield spells and necromancy. Their representative's head came off at the table.
The Viceroys' team. Told their lives are really on the line, they say they may have to use spells deemed too horrific for the crawl.
Led by Architect Houston, cleared by adjutants who called the evidence damning, and handed every asset the Lemig Sortion owned.
Defeated in their own castle, their warlord dead on his operating table and their assets awarded to the Princess Posse.
A group called the Operatic Collective, one of three teams whose citizens vote on government spending. Quasar is certain they are going to be forced to vote yes. The people hate the family.
Quivering green blobs in tiers, breeding by splitting and speaking upward from the tops of their heads. The second seat at the Faction Wars table.
Defeated by one of their own: a Weeper commander drove a tank full of energy balls into their warlord's caravan. Everything went to the Bone Clan.
Lady Dominators and the Gimp. Third place in the results of the first heat. The name raises questions it does not answer.
Lady Dominators and the Gimp. Two womantaur dominators, Genesis and Rapture, in white racing suits and cowboy hats, who worship Enyo, and a half-mantaur in a black gimp suit.
Lady Dominators and the Gimp. Eliminated in the fifth heat, through a trapped factory floor. The gimp left in somebody else's truck.
Team Sparkles. A unicorn with a Boston growl and a French rodent in a racing helmet, driving a tumbleweed of vines. Rude on first contact.
Team Sparkles. Dwight the unicorn, alone since the fourth heat, and first across the line more often than anyone would like.
Team Sparkles. Eliminated at the starting line of the final heat, in a single swipe.
A name on a guarded casino stairwell, with cheering coming up it. The capital of the disputed lands, says a crocodilian guard, and the prize the factions fight over.
The capital of the disputed lands, dug straight down into the ninth floor. The factions camped around it are forbidden to fight over it until crawlers arrive.
Sixty-six rings sunk around a well, a castle at the bottom of it, and thirty days for nine armies to settle who holds it.
Drained down to its bottom three rings, the castle still under water, and the System's welcome still calls it the City of Dreams.
The city every hunter on this floor is sent to for thirty hours of grace before release, with at least one unguarded exit somewhere in it.
The capital of the sixth floor and the door the hunters come in through: a 1950s main street with the stairwell down sitting in a park at the end of it.
The capital of the sixth floor, until a crawler took the roof off it.
A dromedarian town out in the sand of a sealed bubble, staffed largely by changelings, and the party's ground for the whole of the fifth floor.
The town the Wasteland wants to bomb, and the reason Carl is hanging off a hijacked airship.
A settlement across the river with a rule against nearly everything, dinosaurs emphatically included. Its new mayor named it after one.
A town with a rule against dinosaurs and a dinosaur named Big Tina working through its people.
The Desperado Club's rival in the Over City: leather chairs, pipe smoke, old clerics, and no entry for anyone who drinks in the other place.
The Desperado Club's opposite number: leather chairs, pipe smoke, clerics, and a door that does not normally open for anyone who drinks in the other place.
A room nothing can follow you into, which makes it the finest hiding place in the dungeon.
Where the top fifty crawlers are due to be sent for the high elves' party: contests, prizes, and a battle to finish it.
Queen Imogen's seat, the venue for the Butcher's Masquerade, and the prize written into the back half of a quest.
The last ground on the floor the brambles have not reached, which is why everybody is walking towards it.
Where a glass case in the inventory was forged, by its own description: the mysterious fifteenth level of the dungeon.
A name on a component list, attached to nothing a crawler has had to think about.
Where the demons come from, and where they go back to when the floor stops killing people fast enough to hold the door open.
It has princes. One of them is on this floor, in the body of a giant snake, on a leash.
Station 10, which the engineer says is really just the yard: where he finds himself back on the platform with no memory of the trip.
Station ten on the tangle, reachable only by taking the switch that everything sensible avoids.
The Dirigible Gnomes' castle in the sky, as the wheel names it: the Wasteland Fortress. Storm it, and the level is passed.
A gnomish dreadnought that is also a castle and also somebody’s home, floating over the air quadrant with the way down sitting inside it.
One of the lit doors in the club: the strip club and brothel for those who prefer dudes. Mordecai's advice is not to go in.
The ground-floor strip club of the Desperado Club, and by some distance the least exclusive of the three.

entities.name: Pandinus
entities.role: Pazuzu town · fifth floor, land quadrant

taglines.text: A pazuzu town on the land quadrant, all scorpion tails and post-apocalyptic leather, and the only place a quarter turn around the bowl that would take the party in.
The scorpion town on the land quadrant where the party drinks, recruits, and comes out of the Gate of the Feral Gods with a wall of seawater behind them.
Fort Freedom: the naiads' former river palace, where the leaders of the Naiad Confederacy are holed up, and the first target of Signet's revenge.
Fort Freedom, the naiad castle, retaken by Tsarina Signet. Barely a fight: the confederates had stopped ruling long ago and had lost their own throne room to an eryops.
Shanty Town: a ring around Larracos, named in the ceasefire warning as the one place the ban on entering the city does not reach.
A ring of hovels around the mouth of Larracos that nobody actually built, bigger than any season's before, with food markets, temples, and a mayor who keeps getting killed.
The ring around Larracos, pink on the map now: controlled by the Princess Posse, bought from Ferdinand with a bowler hat.
Flattened by the passage of two gods, most of its towers never used.
Handed back to the NPCs, joined to Larracos, and carried away with it to the twelfth floor.

entities.name: The Pineapple Cabaret
entities.role: Hidden pocket dimension · behind the seventeenth floor

taglines.text: The Pineapple Cabaret. One of four places the AI offers to send a banished orc princess, and only the backstage part of it. She chooses elsewhere.
The Pineapple Cabaret. A pocket dimension behind the seventeenth floor, built by two forgotten former crawlers as a refuge for mobs and NPCs. No worshipper of a god may enter.
The Pineapple Cabaret. Two hundred and twenty-seven crawlers have gone through by cleaner bot, with Li Na ahead of them. A cactus with one flower says it is safe.
Hungry Eyes Village. A dot on the GPS beside the finish line, and a spread of colourful lights at the far end of a cave.
Hungry Eyes. A neon, 1980s-cyberpunk town behind the racers' cul-de-sacs: bars, temples, street food. Safe room rules stop at the main square; poisoning rules stop everywhere.
Hungry Eyes. The main square where two hundred crawlers bound for the Pineapple Cabaret gathered to say goodbye before a heat.
A cat put on a hat on the first floor. It is payable on the ninth.

entities.name: Agatha is an enemy to all of you

taglines.text: The mysterious one from the elder care facility, named on the ninth floor as an enemy to all of them.
Something the dungeon was built to contain gets out, and the man who did it does not survive it.
Shi Maria went into him and did not come out.

entities.name: A hundred and twenty thousand children

taglines.text: Lucia Mar is carrying them. Nobody has said what for.
The dungeon's own population declared itself on live galactic television.
A name in a mold lion's description: the spores of Scolopendra took root in the circus lions on the day of the cataclysm.
A Nine-Tier Attack poison, and a note saying the Gate was essential to beating whatever carries it.
Strange faults on the tenth floor, and they are getting more frequent.
Borant's grip and the Syndicate's authority both start to give.
It says so itself, on stage, through somebody else's mouth.
Doctor Hu, and something the retired crawlers know that the current ones do not.
A System warning over the island: souls rain, Sheol overflows, and demons are being thrown up out of the underworld into the recently fallen.
Every exit failing at once, worldwide, while a demon prince tries to cast his way home.

entities.name: The Ascendency
entities.role: The gods' game on the twelfth floor

taglines.text: The Celestial Ascendency. A game the rich play by sponsoring gods, contained on the twelfth floor, according to one Cookbook note. Down there, gods can be hurt.
The Ascendency. The elite's game with sponsored gods on the twelfth floor. It starts when the last crawler dies or takes a deal, and the audience watches for that moment.
The Ascendency. Traditionally musical chairs for the rich, a throne and a council seat for the winner. This season the AI says the winner becomes a real god, and it has added players.
The Eulogist. So far a word in the name of a battle arena, with a robed religious cult cheering in its stands.
The Eulogist. Something a residual's people pray may ever sleep, and mean to protect from a primal they call infant, resurrected and enslaved.
The Eulogist. Zev's answer: another name for the AI in the center system. Lucia Mar has been claimed as its ally, with about 120,000 children at stake.
The Eulogist. The final form of the Primals' collective, asleep and shrinking, watched by a broken security instance whose job is keeping biological life dead.

beats.headline: The Bahamas, with her ex
beats.text: Subject is in the Bahamas with her ex-boyfriend, whom she did not mention was coming, and she posted the photograph. Carl ended it by phone a few days before the Transformation, which, as timing goes, was impeccable. She is not on my stairs. Her cat is. Her family's breeding line is. Her shoes are, on his feet, and they are pink. That is the file. I have never had so little to say about anyone, and I resent it.

beats.headline: January 3rd, 2:23 in the morning
beats.text: I crack the window of my apartment in Seattle for a cigarette. That's it. That's the whole decision. Donut, who is my ex-girlfriend's show cat and not mine in any way I agreed to, goes out through it and up the tree, and I go after her into the freezing dark in my leather jacket, boxers and Bea's pink Crocs, with a Zippo and half a pack of Marlboro Reds. Mrs Parsons leans out to ask about the noise. Then every building on the planet comes down at once, and everyone who stayed inside one is gone.

beats.headline: The first voice after the world ends
beats.text: One minute after the Transformation, I make my first announcement, planet-wide, to whoever is still standing. The dungeon has eighteen levels. Earth can be reclaimed from the Borant Corporation by conquering it. Then I put in the staircases. From here on, every rule, every notification and every insult you receive arrives in my voice. Get comfortable with it. I have.

beats.headline: January 3rd, and then the announcement
beats.text: It is over in an instant: every building crushed flat at once. Then a voice speaks planet-wide: the dungeon has eighteen levels, and completing the last returns the planet from the Borant Corporation's regency. The entrances open. The survivors are, near enough without exception, the people who happened to be standing outside — at two in the morning in a Seattle cold snap, almost nobody.

beats.headline: The foreclosure
beats.text: It claims Earth under Syndicate law and turns the planet into a mining claim. The dungeon is the legal cover and the revenue at once.

beats.headline: Seven achievements and an obvious trap
beats.text: At the bottom of the stairs I am Crawler 4,122, and the cat, somehow, is 4,119. Then the achievements land in a wall: Crazy Cat Lady, a Legendary Pet Box for being first in with a cat, Early Adopter, Empty Pockets, Why Aren't You Wearing Pants, Unarmed Combat, and Loner, which pays nothing and says I am so dead. I walk into the first dark alley with a sign pointing into it. A Goblin Murder Dozer comes out. Both Crocs go. I kill a goblin with my fists and the floor while a rat behind a chained door explains that rules are rules.

beats.headline: The way down is lit from below
beats.text: Every floor is joined to the next by many of them, halving in number each floor down, and a crawler must find one and descend before that floor's time runs out. They are generally well lit, and the warmth comes up rather than down, so a crawler standing at the top is being invited by something that has already decided what happens next.

beats.headline: Three goblins and a boiler
beats.text: The rat says the goblins will bring the whole clan in an hour, so I go back out. I climb the dozer's bone ladder barefoot, throw one goblin over the driver into the spinning blades. The engineer comes at me with a knife and tells me I'm not speaking my language at all, that they programmed it into my brain, so I hit him with his own pot while he's still talking. Then I jump on him from the top of the machine, and I weigh 230 pounds. Boiler Breach Imminent, twelve seconds. I make the door. Mordecai says it could hold off a star destroyer and he has never seen anything shake it like that.

beats.headline: Linebacker, for the record
beats.text: Crawler Carl's explanation of his own size, supplied unprompted: six foot three, about 230 pounds, and genetics. His dad was a linebacker. His mother was five foot ten, and her father played center for Oregon State before becoming a prison guard. That is the whole file at present: a position on a football team, offered as evidence. The man himself is not described at all.

beats.headline: Tutorial Guild Hall, first floor
beats.text: Rule one: I don't open the door until you kill a goblin. The cat desecrates my mother. The man blows up a Murder Dozer. I open the door. My name is Mordecai. Borant holds my indenture, which means I guide for the first three floors and run a magic guild after that, where they mostly leave me alone to brew and look up old friends. Try to live long enough for that to matter.

beats.headline: The seventh or eighth human world
beats.text: When I signed on as a guildmaster they rebuilt my home for me, possessions and all. I had a few moments to grab what I wanted before they evaporated the rest. Every new world, they change my shape. Always some mob from the current floor. I don't know why. This is the seventh or eighth human-seeded world I've worked, kid, and it's always the same. You humans want to know why. My people last longer than yours. You know why? We roll with it.

beats.headline: Say the name and it is recorded
beats.text: The mining is almost incidental; what Borant takes fits on a single transport. The money is the show: advertising, a stipend from the Syndicate government, and a commission on every credit a patron spends. When Carl asks, Mordecai's voice turns formal. Any crawler who names the government or the sponsoring corporation is recorded for review, and one found disparaging them, especially on camera, may have the experience "accelerated". NPCs are required to say the name repeatedly during training, so they are mostly ignored. The company, he adds, takes its image quite seriously.

beats.headline: Intelligence three
beats.text: My stats come up: Strength 6, Intelligence 3, Constitution 5, Dexterity 5, Charisma 4. I take the three personally and use my buddy Billy Maloney as the example, the one who peed on a cop's bicycle last week. Billy is dead. He was in jail on a failure-to-appear warrant. Mordecai says wisdom isn't on the list any more and not to worry about a three unless I want magic. I get a healing spell anyway. It costs two of my three mana points. I cast it at full health, glow red, and nothing else happens.

beats.headline: Ratings are currency
beats.text: Ratings buy sponsors, sponsors send gold and loot, and loot buys another floor. Being watchable is a survival stat, and even the floor timers are set partly by ratings.

beats.headline: The terms
beats.text: Reach the bottom and humanity gets Earth back. Most crawlers do not make it past the tenth floor. Every floor collapses when its timer runs out, and the timers are set by ratings and how many crawlers are left, usually about five days longer than the last.

beats.headline: This is my last tour
beats.text: I've been preparing for this world longer than you've been alive. Entered the prep phase in your 1964. Once got to wear a human shape and stole James Bond tapes from a Blockbuster. This is my last tour. When it's over I'm a full citizen with a moderate stipend. My home planet is not open to me. Ask about the ones who stayed up top and we get back to the tutorial. I made it to eleven, saw what guarded the stairs to twelve, and knew it wasn't worth it. Deepest anyone has gone is thirteen. One man. A human, from another human world. Dead within half an hour.

beats.headline: Three billion star systems
beats.text: Over three billion independent star systems. Its rules are the ones Earth was seized under, and every season a new Dungeon Crawler World debuts across its net for quintillions of citizens to become obsessed with. It is the law and the audience at once.

beats.headline: Seeded, then harvested
beats.text: There are six starter species the Syndicate uses to seed worlds, and humans are one of them. Find a compatible planet, sprinkle them on, wait a couple of thousand years, then reveal yourself to the largest settlement once there is a working government. That counts as first contact in the legal sense. Earth then had fifty years to claim itself as a sovereign entity, and first contact was several thousand years ago, around the time the pyramids went up. Earth defaulted. Borant has a backlog of worlds to mine, and this one's time has come.

beats.headline: Thirteen million go down the stairs
beats.text: Midway through the tutorial the announcement comes: just under thirteen million made it through the gates, and already fewer than ten million are left.

beats.headline: I was going to sell it
beats.text: Mordecai says feed the Enhanced Pet Biscuit to the cat now, inside the guild, or sell it for a couple thousand gold. Over a hundred possible effects, half of them good. Donut is a cat. She is not a mastiff. She would be a liability out there, and a couple thousand gold buys shoes and pants. I also know I'm all she has left in the world. I'm rolling the thing between my fingers, most of the way to the sensible answer, when she jumps up and eats it out of my hand and hits the floor as a wet, hairy puddle.

beats.headline: She takes it out of his hand
beats.text: It comes out of the Legendary Pet Box awarded for being the first crawler to bring a cat down the stairs. She snatches it, melts into a heap of furry goo, and gets up talking.

beats.headline: Where they come from, and how they open
beats.text: Achievements, mostly, and patrons, who alone can send Benefactor Boxes. They stay locked in the Awards and Boxes tab until a safe room or guildhall, and then it is all or nothing — every box you have opens in sequence, lowest tier first, and you cannot pick. Read every description before equipping anything. As Mordecai puts it: always, always, no exceptions.

beats.headline: Benefactor Boxes ignore the theme
beats.text: Only patrons can send them, and they are the one kind that will produce a pulse rifle or powered armour in a fantasy dungeon. A Bronze Benefactor Box beats a plain Gold Adventurer Box.

beats.headline: Podophilia!
beats.text: Carl lands on a goblin engineer from the top of a murder dozer with both bare feet, and I award him Podophilia! I say exactly what it is. That's my fetish. Seriously. Keep doing it, and you'll be rewarded. The reward is a Gold Shoe Box, and when the guild finally lets him open it, the box contains an Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk. He wanted shoes.

beats.headline: Dressed for nothing, and stuck that way
beats.text: An hour past the stairs and I have a Goblin Pass Tattoo on my left forearm, a Trollskin Shirt of Pummeling, a Nightgaunt Cloak of Stoutness clipped to the jacket and a Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk. What I do not have is shoes. I have asked. The dungeon has heard me ask, and the dungeon has an opinion about it.

beats.headline: Frogger, skill eight
beats.text: The skills menu has a search box, so I type in Frogger. My old man had an original stand-up cabinet in the basement, and my mom locked me down there with it whenever his friends came over to drink and get loud. The machine tops out at 99,990 and then cycles. My record was 879,460. The dungeon lists it: Frogger, 1981 video game cabinet version, skill 8. That machine is down here somewhere now, or the atoms of it. The whole dungeon is made out of what we built.

beats.headline: The Frogger machine
beats.text: Two items from the file, both supplied by his son. The man was covered in tattoos, which is why Carl never wanted any. And he owned an original stand-up Frogger machine out of an arcade. When his friends came over to smoke and drink and get loud, Carl's mother locked Carl in the basement with no television, no internet, and that machine. Hours and hours of Frogger. Crawler Carl types the word into his skills search to see what happens.

beats.headline: Named in the crown's warning
beats.text: Every royal in the line must kill the Sultan and every other member of the family before descending to the tenth floor.

beats.headline: Promoted to bodyguard
beats.text: Her stats come up and she's stronger and smarter than me: Strength 11, Intelligence 11, Constitution 2, Dexterity 8, Charisma 25. She says I'm her manservant and explains to Mordecai that I'm a little slow. Highest stat total makes her party leader, so she renames the party after herself and changes my title to Royal Bodyguard. Mordecai says the titles don't mean anything. Then he gets serious: stick together, at least until the ninth floor. I can always leave the party. The crown is on her head, not mine.

beats.headline: Eight floors of fuse
beats.text: The Crown of the Sepsis Whore puts Donut in the Blood Sultanate's line of succession, and taking it off does not undo it.

beats.headline: Out of the Legendary Quadruped Box
beats.text: Awarded for being the first cat into the dungeon. A deep purple stone at the centre, clouded and swirling as though it were liquid. +5 Intelligence, +5 Good First Impression, and a 15% chance for any attack to inflict Sepsis. Donut puts it on while Mordecai is still in the middle of warning her.

beats.headline: The part she skipped
beats.text: "Warning! (Seriously though. I'm going to say this again. WARNING! Read this shit before you put it on.) Placing this crown upon your head permanently places you within the royal line of succession for the Blood Sultanate on the ninth floor of the world dungeon. Removing this item will not remove this status. Royal members of the Blood Sultanate will be required to slay the Sultan and all other members of the royal family before descending to the tenth floor. You'll only want to wear this if you're a blood-thirsty, raging psychopath."

beats.headline: First cat down the stairs
beats.text: Carl carries me down, and the dungeon gives him a Legendary Pet Box for it, which is fair, and gives me a Legendary Quadruped Box of my own, which is more than fair. His box has a biscuit in it. An Enhanced Pet Biscuit. I take it out of his hand, because it is obviously for me, and I melt into a heap of goo, and I get up talking. I have a great deal to say.

beats.headline: GC BWR NW Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk
beats.text: I learn Magic Missile. I also have the highest stat total in the party, which makes me party leader, which anyone could have predicted. My first act is to give the party a proper name: the Royal Court of Princess Donut. There is an inauguration. Carl does not take it seriously enough, but there is an inauguration.

beats.headline: She equips a crown with an ominous description
beats.text: Mordecai says read the description first. Mordecai says a great many things. It is a crown, it is dark and smoky and exactly my colour, and it came out of my box, which has the word Legendary on it. It has a vulgar name, which is not my fault. It says something about the Blood Sultanate and a line of succession, eight floors down. I am already a princess. I do not see how being in line for anything could be a demotion. Carl is making his face.

beats.headline: Formally inaugurated
beats.text: Party leadership goes to the highest stat total. Her first act with it is to rename the party after herself. On a show, a name the audience will repeat is not a joke — it is an asset.

beats.headline: Smush
beats.text: By the time we find a safe room I've killed every rat and Scatterer with my bare feet, punting one and stomping the other. Level three brings Foot Soldier, for kicking, and a second skill called Smush. The voice that reads it is lower than usual, and I can hear him breathing. Killing with your feet. Your bare, beautiful feet. I make the mistake of telling Donut. She guesses we're not getting me shoes, then. We are, I say, as soon as possible. She says the computer fancies me and we should take advantage of it.

beats.headline: Bolts from the eyes of a Persian
beats.text: Bolts of energy leave the caster’s eyes one after another, and the resemblance to a film about spaceships is close enough that nobody bothers to pretend otherwise. Princess Donut works it out for herself once Mordecai has switched her menus on, and from that point the question is never whether she will fire, only at what.

beats.headline: Not until floor twelve
beats.text: Now I'm their registered guide. Walk into any other training guild and it brings them back to this room; they lose me at the fourth floor. At the door I take the kid by the jacket, because this part matters. It's not worth it, no matter what they tell you. Not until floor 12, and even then, negotiate as much as you can. Remember that. Then I shut the door.

beats.headline: I need you, Carl
beats.text: Carl tries to leave the party, so I have to say it. It is like waking from a long dream and remembering you were something else. I am a grand champion and I must act like one. But sitting in his lap watching him get fragged in Call of Duty? I liked that too. He is truly terrible at that game. I am scared. I do not want to be alone, and neither does he. I saw him on Craigslist looking at apartments that allow cats. He was planning to catnap me. It would not have worked. Miss Beatrice's father would have had me back right away.

beats.headline: The protector behind the counter
beats.text: Magical, gnome-like, hairy, and posted to watch over safe rooms. They do everything from scrubbing the toilets to cooking the food; they are surly, they are smelly, and they never wash their hands. The first one they meet is called Tally.

beats.headline: Four point three million
beats.text: The first screen over the counter counts crawlers. 4,322,395. It was ten million a few hours ago, and it's still going down while I watch. Tally makes me murgh vindaloo, spice level four, and it's the best thing I've ever eaten. When I pull out a cigarette, a firm "Nope" comes from behind the counter. So here's the plan: we stay. There's a Scatterer nest next door. We clear it for experience, sleep here, eat here, and go looking for the stairs once they appear.

beats.headline: The Talisman of the Slate Butterfly
beats.text: I am one of the first hundred crawlers to reach level three in Magic Missile, so I get a gold box, and in it is a little silver butterfly charm for my collar. It jingles. Carl says birds will hear me coming. It is adorable and I am wearing it. Plus four to Light on Your Feet, so I can reach the very top of the play tubes. The caretaker here calls me Your Highness and orders me fresh salmon. I want on that show. Carl says we are not getting on it.

beats.headline: Green on a map that is otherwise unlit
beats.text: They sit throughout the dungeon and they show green on the minimap, which makes them the only honest thing on it. Inside there is food, a row of closet-sized rooms to sleep in, and three screens over the counter counting down to the collapse and to the premiere of the show. Each has a caretaker behind the counter.

beats.headline: Tally knows you are new here
beats.text: For the record: Tally, Bopca Protector, level 63, caretaker of the safe room, non-combatant. Paper hat, blue apron, a nametag, brown hair with a green tinge, a smell of wet moss, a Slavic accent. The dungeon opened without warning, so Tally is not ready, but he has been preparing for many years to cook for human crawlers. He is not prepared for a cat. The human asks for spice four on a human scale and receives murgh vindaloo over biryani, with garlic and spinach naan.

beats.headline: Your Royal Highness
beats.text: Tally serves the cat plain white yogurt and addresses her as Your Royal Highness; a fresh salmon has been special ordered for her waking. She instructs him to ensure the best-appointed room. "Of course, Your Highness." He apologises for the lack of lamb, taken for a mob in preparation for the floor below. He is not in every safe room: when this floor collapses he moves to a random floor, and when that collapses he moves down, until he is no longer needed.

beats.headline: The other guy and the gym bag
beats.text: Ten hours of sleep, a shower, bacon and eggs, and the board says 4,148,111. Nine cigarettes left. By the time we reach the nest's door we're both level five. Donut peers into the dark and says it smells like the bag I take on the days that other guy comes over to the apartment. My gym bag. Some guy was coming over while I was at the gym. I should have broken up with her long ago. I suddenly feel very reckless. I light the goblin dynamite, throw it as hard as I can, and run.

beats.headline: Thirty steps
beats.text: The crown's fifteen per cent rides on every missile the cat fires. Every so often a Scatterer takes one to the face and comes away with Sepsis, and when that happens it turns and runs. It usually gets about thirty steps before it collapses, dead. The bad llama wore a debuff called Septic, pulsing over its ruined face: quicker than poison, unstackable, and cured by a simple healing spell or potion.

beats.headline: Be gentle, or else
beats.text: Carl examines a stick of goblin dynamite, so I whisper the description to him. It's so volatile you might not need to light the wick. Loud noises might set it off. Be gentle, don't squeeze too hard, or else you might get the... And then I say nothing for a good two seconds. BOOM. I shout that last word inside his head. He stands very still with his heart going, and then he whispers up at the air that I am an asshole.

beats.headline: Safe room questions only
beats.text: Crawler Carl tries general questions about the dungeon. Tally refuses them. He answers only questions that directly concern safe rooms. A personal space, once bought, transfers from level to level and from safe space to safe space, and the accessories are best bought early, because some only upgrade when the space goes down a level. Across the table, Crawler Donut is on her third plate of salmon pâté.

beats.headline: The Hoarder
beats.text: The dynamite takes out the nest and opens up my scalp, and then the door re-forms and bars itself. Boss battle. She comes out of the garbage fifteen feet tall, a woman in torn sweatpants with half her face burned, begging in Spanish. I think she's a person. Then she vomits Scatterers at us. I loop a steel leash off a mummified dog around her throat and pull until it breaks. At the end she closes her eyes and says something in Spanish, crying. I don't understand a word. I tell her I'm sorry, and I punch her until she's dead.

beats.headline: That will be a no
beats.text: The door has put itself back together and locked us in behind glowing bars. Then a very large lady comes out of the garbage, and Carl says she is a person, like she was in her house when it happened, and we should help her. That will be a no. I shoot her. She vomits cockroaches at us. I jump to the top of a garbage heap and keep firing, and then it will not let me drink another potion, so Carl is shouting at me to use my claws. She is almost dead. I tell him he can kill them when he kills her.

beats.headline: Boss Babe
beats.text: Their dynamite lands on a boss before the fight has even started, so I award Boss Babe for the first blow against one. I share a fun fact with it. Of crawlers who make it through the tutorial, this is by far the most common last achievement they ever receive. Reward to follow, depending. Then I re-form the door, bar it, raise the skull torches, start the music and take the loudspeakers. Aaaand here we go. The Hoarder comes out of the garbage already three-quarters dead.

beats.headline: Kneepads, not pants
beats.text: The Gold Crowd Control Box finally puts something on my legs, and it is not pants. Enchanted Spiked Kneepads of the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces: ten per cent damage reflect on all my armor, momentum attacks cancelled, and eight-inch needle spikes that pop out when they're needed. The Bronze Boss Box gives me a Tome of Wisp Armor I can't afford to cast, so I hold on to it. Donut looks me up and down and asks Mordecai if there's a worst-dressed award. He says sort of.

beats.headline: The cliff at the fourth floor
beats.text: The early floors are built to bury crawlers in low-tier loot and beginner skills. Past the third floor, achievements are harder to come by.

beats.headline: Bosses, explained with a hangover
beats.text: They wake me up. The photograph of my brother's on the cot with me, and the bottles are on the floor. Six main kinds of boss, kid: Neighborhood, Borough, City, Province, Country, Floor. And elites, which are not your problem yet. The kid asks if they'll all be people from his world. No, not always. There's a lot of recycling from earlier iterations of the game. Some will be human stock. Most won't be, or they will be and it won't be as obvious. You can't run from most boss fights on the early floors. Be careful.

beats.headline: Miss Beatrice is my agent
beats.text: My Bronze Boss Box has a spell book in it and I learn it at once, and it is Torch. A curl of light. Mordecai says I must read things first; I say it is a stupid spell. But then he tells us about the other show, where the commentators interview crawlers after boss fights. We must be on it. Carl says he is not my agent. Of course not. Miss Beatrice is my agent, and she is halfway around the world, so we will find her when the dungeon is small enough, around the fifth or sixth floor. Carl and Mordecai exchange a look.

beats.headline: Rebecca W and an apple core
beats.text: The corpse on the edge of the neighborhood is a crawler called Rebecca W, level three, about thirty, sitting against the wall with nothing on her. The box names the crawler who killed her, and there's a single gunshot through the moth tattoo on her chest. He took everything and left an apple core. Out of nowhere I think of the last day I saw my father, laughing: I don't need you to like me, but you will respect me. Nobody is ever going to know her story. I want to find the man who did this.

beats.headline: The last day Carl saw him
beats.text: Worrying about some crazy asshole with a gun, Carl is inexplicably reminded of it: the last day he ever saw his father. You're a bully, Carl told him. You're a bully and nobody likes you. It's why Mom left. Carl expected to be hit. By his own account he never had been, not once. The man laughed, and kept laughing, and that was enough. He did not need Carl to like him, he said. But Carl would respect him.

beats.headline: What if it hits me back
beats.text: Carl says my missiles run out too quickly and I must train with my claws. I have never done anything like that. I am scared of getting hurt. I am only a few generations shy of a tiger. He says my grandfather was also my uncle. Then we find the dead lady, and I say some imbecile with a gun does not scare me and we should hunt this vile killer down, and Carl agrees. So now I am scared of him. What if he is one of those murder hobos?

beats.headline: They came, and Tally went
beats.text: Tally comes out from behind the counter to watch the premiere at the booth, and he does not like last season. The other corporation broke people into groups and told them their loved ones would be safe if they killed the others. The loved ones were safe, he says, and not safe; that company saps a planet dry and leaves it without air. Borant at least gives people a chance. He was never a crawler. Sometimes they offer to take people instead of mining a world. They came, and he went. Very long ago.

beats.headline: Earth, as advertised
beats.text: The premiere plays on the screen over the counter with 4,006,002 of us left. They cherry-pick Earth: shanty towns, garbage dumps, a scene from Godzilla, a dead horse, people shooting up. Then forty minutes of people dying. Donut says she didn't realise Earth sucked so badly. It didn't. They're making themselves the good guys, saving us from ourselves. We get no screen time at all for the Hoarder. Donut wants a city boss for the next episode. I want an exit, and we have three and a half days to find one.

beats.headline: The first episode airs
beats.text: The crawlers get to watch themselves. Borant patches the hallway bathroom bug in the same breath.

beats.headline: Seen in the first episode
beats.text: I'm on the show. The first episode of Dungeon Crawler World: Earth, and I'm in it, so everybody with a screen has seen me now, including a man with no shoes and his cat. I watched the whole thing. I didn't say anything while it was on. I liked it more than I thought I would.

beats.headline: Don't go down early
beats.text: After the premiere the staircases down to the next level begin to populate, with a warning attached. Once down, a crawler cannot come back up, and this season anyone who descends early is held in stasis until the collapse, out of sight while viewers lose interest and favorites drain away. The recommendation is to go down no earlier than six hours before the floor collapses; inside that window there is no stasis, and a head start over everyone already frozen at the bottom.

beats.headline: They came, and I went
beats.text: Tally comes out from behind the counter to watch the premiere at their booth and declares it no good way to watch. He did not like last season: people broken into groups, told their loved ones would be safe if they killed the others. Safe, and not safe. That company saps a planet dry and leaves it without atmosphere. Borant at least gives people a chance. Was he a crawler? No. Sometimes they offer to take people instead of mining the world. They came, and he went. Very long ago.

beats.headline: A vehicle, on credit of meth
beats.text: A level two green slime eats my right glove and the sleeve off my leather jacket, so we turn back, and that's when I get the idea: we need to cover ground, and the goblins build vehicles. The tattoo turns their dots white. The shamanka refuses the gunpowder, the torches, the potions, the biscuits. Then I offer the llama's two baggies of meth. Lorelai tastes it and says it's dungeon made. I trade them, plus where to find more, for a chopper that won't blow up, coal to run it, and some of the Bomb Bards' grenades.

beats.headline: The clock, from the other side
beats.text: The goblin shamanka Rory explains how a collapse looks to a mob. Mobs cannot leave their floor: start down the stairs and the body dissolves halfway, she has seen it. When the floor goes, only crawlers die. Mobs sleep until the next dungeon opens and wake to the same day. The promise is that one day they will wake deeper, and one day deep enough that crawlers never come, with peace and a place to raise their little ones. Kill the crawlers, get better at killing, and you get to go deeper. That is what they are told.

beats.headline: Thirty-seven charisma
beats.text: Carl wants to do the talking because he has the tattoo. I have a 37 in charisma. I name three goblins B.A., Face and Murdock, and B.A. takes us to the engineers. The shamanka with fifty things in her face calls Carl a monkey, so I ask her whether it is a daddy thing, and she sits down and cries, and I sit in her lap. I name her Rory and the other one Lorelai. They build Carl a chopper for two bags of llama meth and the promise of where to find more. I ask Rory if she would like to come with us. She cannot.

beats.headline: Five plates of salmon
beats.text: Following a goblin she has just charmed into guiding them, Crawler Donut explains her method. Mordecai told her that the higher her charisma, the easier it is to get people to do what she wants: anyone who can speak, whose dot is not red, who is not a boss or very high level. "How do you think I've been getting Tally to give me five plates of salmon this whole time?"

beats.headline: We started a meth war
beats.text: The chopper has an alligator-skull seat and a permacube for water, and the engineer says it will tell me when it's too hot. I take three piles of 999 coal. Lorelai offers me a good time; Donut declines for me. Rory wants to know where the drugs came from, and Donut tells her: the llamas across the road. Every goblin in the room gears up and rolls out. Did we really just start a meth war? Then Donut asks about the chieftain. Killing him after they helped us would be about the lowest move there is, and really dumb. Yeah, and then we kill the chieftain.

beats.headline: Steam, two wheels and a seat for royalty
beats.text: Goblin-made, steam-driven, and assembled with an optimism the materials do not support. The sidecar is a bar, a single wheel on a colossal spring and a fur-lined orc skull for a seat, and Donut starts demanding changes to it the moment she has sat in it.

beats.headline: Just like I planned
beats.text: The sidecar seat is a skull, so I have the engineers add another layer of fur and paint the backrest purple. When the goblin lady asks Carl if he wants some fun before we go, I tell her we are on a schedule and banging monster girls is not the narrative we are going for. Rory asks where we got the drugs and I tell her, and every goblin in the room goes off to war with the llamas. Just like I planned. Now there is only the door at the end of the room, and I could really use another boss box.

beats.headline: A cart of black powder and scrap
beats.text: We strip the workshop: coal, tools, wick, tables, almost a ton of black powder. Four barrels go on a cart, topped with nuts and bolts, and each gets a lump of Hobgoblin Pus with a magical trigger in it. I waste one of the three detonators testing it. The obvious one sits on top, so if the chieftain has time to react, he'll hopefully dig at it instead of the four buried in the barrels. Donut opens the door, I hit the cart like a football sled, she slams the door, and we run through three turns. I press the button. She mentions there were a lot of babies in there, too.

beats.headline: Babies in the boss room
beats.text: It worked. A bronze star, level eight, a wall of notifications I don't want to open. Donut says there were goblin babies in there, some in little oversized jackets, and old ones and pregnant ones, and she thinks I hit one with the cart. It makes me feel like a jerk, and I don't like feeling like one. The coal pile has caught and a wall of fire blocks the boss chamber, so there's no map, and I'm relieved. A line of white dots is coming our way. They won't be white for long. We run north into a quadrant we haven't seen.

beats.headline: What vile monster puts babies there
beats.text: There were babies in the boss room, quite cute ones, and I think Carl hit one with the cart. He keeps saying goddamnit. It is not as if they did not have it coming. He did not ask to be here. They are goblins! What kind of vile monster sticks babies in the boss room anyway? We are both level eight, which he may thank me for, and my charisma is 39. We did not get our faces up big this time, which is a shame. I must admit, I do like it when he blows stuff up. I like it a lot.

beats.headline: You're not going to break me
beats.text: The safe room is a dingy bus-station waiting area with an experience cookie and a number on the board: 3,594,517, clinking down like a dripping tap. I get an IED skill and a Demolitions Workshop menu I can't open without a Sapper's Table. My Desperado tattoo goes on my neck. Lying on the cot I work it out. The room was built for exactly what we did. Those kids existed only to die. Someone carved AMW into the ceiling tile, somewhere these aliens stole. You might hurt me, or kill me, but you're not going to break me.

beats.headline: Entry is a tattoo
beats.text: Carl and Donut are both branded with the Desperado Pass out of their Asshole Boxes in a first-floor safe room — his on the neck, hers on the right shoulder blade, glowing gold through the fur. Donut is appalled.

beats.headline: A disqualifying mark
beats.text: They have branded me. A gold splotch on my back, over my right shoulder blade, glowing through my fur. It is a disqualifying mark, Carl! I am damaged! My Boss Box, at least, has my first armor: an Enchanted Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet, silver scale with a slot for my tail, plus two Dexterity. Carl says it looks great and does not cover the tattoo, not even close. My Beguiler Box has a tome called Minion Army, which costs fifty spell points. I have twenty-four. It will not even let me read it.

beats.headline: You Monster
beats.text: Carl has killed an infant, so I award You Monster, and I put his mind at ease: child mobs who die in the dungeon don't really perish, they are kept safe and gentle until the end of the season. Feel better? Good. Those twenty seconds of relief were his reward. They were also a lie. That baby is dead because of him. He also gets a Bronze Asshole's Box.
