Mordecai's summary: the progenitors, the first species to conquer the universe, the boogeymen of the cosmos, gone one day without a note. Taking it costs fifteen stat points against staying human: the ten a human gets, and five more. What it buys is a ceiling. Every skill trainable to twenty, and only a rare few who take it ever train one or two skills above fifteen.

beats.headline: Asleep through the paperwork
beats.text: I curl up with Mongo and fall asleep while Carl reads every race there is. Staying a cat gives me Night Vision, Slash Attack, Cat-like Reflexes and something called 9 Lives, which halves the first nine physical hits I take each day. When I wake up I ask Carl if he grew elf ears. He did not. He is still human, which is boring. He says he is a Primal. That sounds like a caveman, and he smells exactly the same.

beats.headline: A sign that grows out of the ground
beats.text: At the gate Mordecai gives me the first rule: don't cross the level-75 guards; there is no jail, only the death penalty. Then he points at a discoloured rock just outside it. Focus on it, and a holographic sign grows out of the ground like a tree: arrows and distances in kilometres to saferooms, restrooms, stairs six kilometres off, and a medium-sized settlement 34 out. Then the rest of the rules. Don't go into the ruins at night until he says so. Stay away from girls with horns. Then he makes a beeline for a pub.

beats.headline: Where the tourists are
beats.text: No tourists on the third floor, Mordecai says. Most of them are on the eighteenth, a billionaire's luxury retreat where the galaxy's rich and elite party, gamble and satiate their most base desires, and the one place where printed people may legally be used for the rest. Carl asks what happens if a crawler gets there. Nobody ever has, so nobody knows; the same goes for the fifteenth. Borant and the AI are required to have a plan.

beats.headline: Props who do not know it
beats.text: Most of the people in these villages were engineered by Borant, so Borant owns them. It is the only world they have known. Every time they are regenerated their minds are altered and planted with false memories, and anything inconvenient, like a crawler explaining that they are props, is erased. Those meth-addicted goblins were written for this world only. Carl asks how that is legal. You cannot alter the memories of naturals unless they sign their rights away. Using the printed ones outside sanctioned entertainment is basically a war crime.

beats.headline: A quest, and a stilt clown
beats.text: A lemur in a painted human skull throws a knife at my head, and the cloak turns it off my chest. Then a Quests tab, trumpets, streamers: The Show Must Go On. Find out why this circus still exists and end it, for a gold quest box. I ask Mordecai whether to take it. He answers with something about his mother's ashes; he is drunk after fifteen minutes. A boom jug sets the building alight, a giraffe flings lemurs at us, and Donut drops an eleven-foot stilt clown so I can land on its chest.

beats.headline: Clown ankle
beats.text: Clown DOWN. Ankle. Bite. Bite. BITE. Mongo is BIGGER. Carl picks Mongo up. NO. Clown is FOOD.

beats.headline: The Belly-Rubbed Pug
beats.text: On the third floor the saferooms are inns. This one is a renaissance-fair pub at the end of a dead-end alley, a pug in a top hat on the sign, the three screens as before and a Bopca called Gordo behind the counter. The sleeping rooms, only five of them, now cost ten gold a night, and the food costs money too. Mordecai teleports in with his trousers round his knees, addressing two girls and a grandma who are not there, vomits, sits in it, and passes out. Gordo's verdict: "You two are so dead."

beats.headline: Thumbs up on the classes
beats.text: Hello, hello. Okay, so, good news, Carl and Princess Donut. Odette's show was another hit, and the majority of viewers are giving a thumbs up to your class and race choices. Both of you picked unique classes, which is always a plus. There are a few other Primals, no straight cats, one were-cat and some cat girls. The public cannot see Mordecai now. No VIP crawlers nearby, and I'd avoid the locals. The next interview is likely the fourth night. I have had to take on extra people for the requests.

beats.headline: A cactus and eighteen westerns
beats.text: My Silver Earth box: a three-inch cactus from Home Depot, $3.99 price tag still on the pot, and a shrink-wrapped pack of eighteen L'Amour paperbacks, the Sackett Family Saga. My dad had a whole shelf of them, and I used to read them under the covers with a flashlight. I haven't read these. My hands are shaking and I'm not sure why. Donut's gifts were deliberate: a candle and a cat tree. I don't know why they picked the cactus. The hobby potion gives me level three in Cesta Punta, whatever that is.

beats.headline: Three of something there was one of
beats.text: Cast on a pet or a minion, the target splits into three. The copies are real, look right and act with minds of their own, and after a minute they fall apart into gears and servos and go up in smoke. Donut learns it from a spellbook the same evening her Earth box turns up a cat tree and a scented candle, which is roughly the level of seriousness the dungeon brings to its gifts.

beats.headline: Two more Mongos
beats.text: Mongo BIGGER. Too big for Mother's back. Collar. BAD. Mother says no. Collar stays. Two more Mongos! FRIENDS! Friends fall apart. Mongo sad. Mother, AGAIN.

beats.headline: Not my child, he says
beats.text: My Earth box is lovely: a Sea Breeze candle and a cat tree fancier than the one at home, which Carl will assemble. My hobby potion makes me a scutelliphile, which sounds obscene. Outside, I show my son how a lady takes a lemur off a roof, and my collar jingles, and Mongo screeches, and I get it anyway. Carl says Mongo is not my child, he is a pet, and we do not risk our lives for pets. That was very hurtful. Then I tell him where the circus tents are. He calls me partner. Okay. Partner.

beats.headline: The Indigenous Species Protection Act
beats.text: Both Earth boxes come with an Earth Hobby Potion, which, per subsection 1256-C of the Indigenous Species Protection Act, the Syndicate Government requires be awarded to all crawlers who have chosen a domestic class. It is optional, cannot be sold or transferred, and grants a random level-three Earth hobby. The AI's own description complains about the lawyers making it put their crap in. Carl wonders whether it is a bureaucratic attempt at preserving Earth culture, and is reminded of the military.

beats.headline: A cat on her lower back
beats.text: Entered into the record, by Carl, in a basement under the Over City: Beatrice's tattoo is a faded Persian cat on her lower back, surrounded by uneven wisps. The cat is Princess Chonkalot, Donut's long-dead grandmother and Beatrice's childhood cat. Carl considers it a stoned Ewok, and once said so aloud, along with a remark about who gets to see it. That was a mistake. Donut rules it a masterpiece and an exception to the rule against tattoos.

beats.headline: Rings off a dead crawler
beats.text: Three dead crawlers near where the lemurs hit us, left out as bait. Three women, sisters or close family, all level 8, all killed at the same time. Their inventories are gone and they've been stripped in a hurry, but two rings are still on one of them, both +2 strength, and a wooden anklet on another. I rub the blood off the rings and put them on. I take no joy in looting crawlers. I can see the allure of being a player killer, though. This game gives a lot of loot.

beats.headline: A pinky against a charm
beats.text: The woman from the circus poster is standing in the street, level 60, an Elite, and I want her. It comes on sudden and almost overwhelming, and I take a step toward her before I understand it's a spell. Mordecai calls it Puppy Dog, a buff that comes with a charisma past a hundred, and there's one surefire way to break it: fracture your own finger. I bend my left pinky back until it snaps. It's like a bucket of cold water. She looks at my finger, amused. I drink a health potion.

beats.headline: The circus in the Over City
beats.text: Grimaldi's Traveling Circus is pitched in one of the Over City's districts. Grimaldi, proprietor. Tonight two crawlers, Carl and Princess Donut, are scouting the grounds as the mobs form up for the night. That is the whole entry so far: a tent, a company, and two people looking at it from the dark. Filed under Over City, third floor.

beats.headline: He remembers none of it
beats.text: I am in my room, it is getting late, and Carl asks how my head is. The cat informs me, in capitals, that I molested someone's grandma. I let Carl explain everything, and then I tell them to back out of there and get to the safe room before dark, and that I will explain how stupid they are once they arrive. Then horns and a charm: break your own finger. Then the cat says it is no succubus but an elite. Get out of there. Do not get involved.

beats.headline: She sees the elf lady first
beats.text: I make the hole bigger so my Puddle Jumper can see the sky, and there she is on the street, waiting like she knows we are here: the elf lady from the poster, naked except for a quite lovely thong, covered in tattoos that swim around like a fishbowl. Her dot is white. I get too scared to examine her. I do not like tattoos. When she reaches out to pet me, I growl. We want nothing to do with her and her circus freak friends, and I tell her so.

beats.headline: Met outside Grimaldi's circus
beats.text: Night comes down on the Over City and the mobs form their lines around Grimaldi's Traveling Circus. Two crawlers have come to scout it, a man and a cat, and they leave under magical mortar fire, and I am what they run into on the other side. My charisma stands past a hundred. He stares, as they all stare. Then he snaps his own finger, and it breaks. I have not decided whether to be offended.

beats.headline: Citizens worth zero experience
beats.text: The announcement after the recap: nearly 40,000 different classes among just under 700,000 crawlers, a record. Potential sponsors may now put in early bids. And a general warning against violence toward non-combatant NPCs. It is not technically against the rules, but Borant wishes to keep the citizenry as safe as possible, so the experience counter for citizens is now zero and city guards get a slight boost in stats. Carl asks what that is about. Mordecai does not know.

beats.headline: A lion's heart in my hand
beats.text: Six Mold Lions on the rooftops and Signet in her arms-out pose, not moving. I have one contingency worked out and haven't explained it to Donut. Protective Shell, with Signet inside it; Donut's last scroll of Confusing Fog. One lion bounces into a wall and hangs there, pinned by the shell. I punch until something gives, then reach into its chest and pull. I'm sitting on the ground holding a lion's heart. "Second Chance!" Donut raises it, and our zombie lion kills the next one.

beats.headline: Amazonian, Shieldmaiden
beats.text: I walk into the guild alone. The women joined me after each of us already had a guide, so we come out of selection scattered to the wind. I come out a good foot taller and much wider. Amazonian. Strength first, and a good measure of dexterity. They let me pick an earth class, and there was one obvious choice. Shieldmaiden.

beats.headline: A Lajabless
beats.text: I am grown now. A Lajabless. Half the day I am beautiful, and my spells cost half, and I am half as strong. The other half my face is a skull, and I am twice as strong. My right leg is a goat's leg now, with a hoof. I can't run on walls any more. My dogs stay dogs. They look at me funny. My class is Black Inquisitor General. Cleric, magic-user, warrior. All three.

beats.headline: Lion belly
beats.text: LION. Big FOOD. Belly. Rip. Rip. Lion swipes. Lion dead. Mongo on lion. RIP. Mongo BIGGER. Bigger than Mother.

beats.headline: An incubus's weakness
beats.text: I apologize. I have not had a drink in an Over City pub in a very long time, and I did not take into account the incubus's weakness, which is alcohol. Sober, I would have told them that quests are great for experience and loot only when you are comfortably ahead of the curve, and with eight days and the two of them playing catch-up, skip it. And once I was cogent, I told them to stay away from the elite. They made a date with her for tomorrow night.

beats.headline: Never trust an elite
beats.text: Elites are never naturals. They are designed, printed and imprinted with the memories their drama needs, and they move freely between the urban floors. This circus is a storyline with its own show and a team of writers, and if the story drifts they hot patch new instructions right into the elite's head. The fairness rules are looser around them. One crawler's life against a drama that has been building for weeks: you know what happens. You are the red shirt. When this floor collapses, the important ones go down to the sixth. Forget the quest. Go to the city.

beats.headline: Zombie lions
beats.text: Carl shouts spells at me and I cast them. Second Chance, ten points, on the lion he pulled apart, and it gets up and rips the throat out of its friend. Then that one gets up too, and I give it two clockwork copies for twenty-six points and a mana potion. The last lion swipes at my son, and I shoot it dead with a magic missile. He does not even notice. We are both level fourteen. I do not like that lady, even if her dot is white.

beats.headline: Lions off a bug zapper
beats.text: Six mold lions pounce at once in a dark street. Crawler Carl slams the shell down as Crawler Donut's Confusing Fog billows out, and the lions bounce off it like fireflies off a bug zapper, each ricocheting in a different direction, howling. It holds long enough for Carl to punch into a lion's chest with his gauntlet and pull its heart out. The shell fizzles just as the reanimated lion gets back to its feet.

beats.headline: Special Edition: the races
beats.text: A special edition shows what the favourite crawlers chose. First a demon-like city boss with crab pincers kills about forty crawlers in seconds. Then Hekla, a man who became a massive slug, a four-armed Kabaddi Raider, Carl, Donut, and Lucia Mar to close. Just about 80 per cent of crawlers have stayed human. A clip of an old Primal with wispy angel wings and a lightning sword, charging a twelfth-floor Divine Guardian, fades before the fight. Mordecai says he died a minute afterwards.

beats.headline: The sacrifice who took no scratch
beats.text: My lovelies take blood, and only the blood of a proper sacrifice. I may not bleed it myself; I must set two creatures against each other, guess the loser, and cast upon it before its first wound. Tonight I chose Carl. Primal blood; I could sense its power. But he took nary a scratch, six lions lie dead, and the night's attack is canceled. My boys were so looking forward to it. So I invite them to hear the sad tale of Signet the Bastard and Grimaldi, the man she loved. Tomorrow, an hour after sundown, right here.

beats.headline: Selection is slow going
beats.text: A long message, waiting when Crawler Carl wakes. Selection is slow going. No resident can choose human without staying as they are, and the ones with cognitive issues have to pick some really weird races to stay viable. Brandon stayed human. Chris and Imani did not. Most of the residents are still level one and getting Legendary Pacifist Boxes for arriving without killing anything. "I hope we see each other again." Carl replies: find whoever has the manager benefit and talk them into taking it.

beats.headline: Fifteen hours on a couch
beats.text: We're heading for the next town and I'm telling Donut we'll stay as far from elites as we can, and then: stunned, paralyzed, unconscious, and the AI quoting Of Mice and Men at me. I wake on a mildewed couch with all my gear and no Donut on the map. Fifteen hours gone. An achievement called Lazarus, for surviving a spell over level 15. Then Signet's hand on my leg. I called her a name and broke my promise. Donut is under Water Lily, and if Signet dies, so does Donut.

beats.headline: He became the vine
beats.text: Signet's account, given on the walk. The poison cloud was a nine-tier attack; the lucky ones died and the rest transformed. Grimaldi, owner and ringleader, stood in the centre ring at the end of a show and became the vine. Everyone in the tent was then infected with mold-covered parasites that put them under his control: lemurs, clowns, almost everyone. When they die, the spores return to the vine, and they are reborn the next day. He took her in as a child. She loves him. She attacks every night.

beats.headline: Selection is slow going
beats.text: Brandon's message: selection is slow going. None of the residents can choose human without staying in their current condition, and there is pushback; those with cognitive issues have to pick some really weird races to stay viable. Brandon stayed human. Chris and Imani did not. Most residents are still level one, and for reaching the third floor without killing anything or dealing damage they are getting Legendary Pacifist Boxes, among a ton of others. Some may soon be more powerful than Imani. Mistress Tiatha thinks they are far from Carl.

beats.headline: Guarding Mother
beats.text: Mother asleep. Mother does NOT wake. Carl builds pile around Mother. Carl says STAY. Protect. Mongo on top of pile. Mongo stays.

beats.headline: The rules he cannot break
beats.text: Most of what I know I'm not allowed to volunteer. Some of it I can only give you if you ask the exact question. Without press credentials nobody watching can see me or hear me, and as a manager I can't touch a mob. My advice is what it has always been: stay ahead of the curve, never trust an elite, stay away from gods. Carl has heard all three.

beats.headline: Managers have one rule
beats.text: The Bopca tells me he has not felt himself since those two arrived, so I mix him a draft from behind his own bar. It knocks him out, and I go into his kitchen for the newsletter; shopkeepers get a printed brief after each recap. I take a few herbs while I am there and pass them to Carl under the table. Managers have one rule: no direct battle with mobs. Everything else is fair game. The brief warns of a major battle event in this area today or tonight. Eat, and get to that town.

beats.headline: Water Lily
beats.text: I followed them this morning to see whether Carl would keep his promise. He did not, and he called me an asshole. I could have melted them both. Instead, grace, which my mother taught me, and heirloom magic, which she also taught me. Water Lily. The cat sleeps until I cancel it. If I die, she dies. If she is moved, she dies. Carl may earn her back by keeping his word. Tonight he will kill Heather, and her blood will raise my squad.

beats.headline: Heather, and the custard
beats.text: My first solo boss: Heather the Bear, level 19, on roller skates. Her worm claws wrap me like a tetherball and start burrowing, and voices in my head call me delicious Primal flesh. Protective Shell cuts them off. Moonshine and a torch set her alight, and she keeps coming. I scratch the lottery ticket and it lands on Custard, which heals her, and the healing kills the worms. The skates and the hat fall off. What's left is an old bear who wants it over. Two punches, and my foot.

beats.headline: The cure is not in this town
beats.text: I visit my old friend Eklund, the only game guide in this town I know. He is too smart for his own good and will not look up the Water Lily cure, but he does tell me the name of Signet's programme, and Carl's hunch is correct. Then I have the recipe: Satch Toad extract mixed with a standard healing potion. It negates all naiad sleep effects and curses. Simple. I can buy it at the alchemical market in a medium or large town. Not in this one.

beats.headline: The paper army
beats.text: Heather's blood is powerful indeed, and I spend it all: my entire retinue, their longevity traded for strength. My lovelies leave my skin as tall as houses, and we break the defenders at the strongest we have been in a long while. I stop the calliope myself. The serpent's waterspout dies against the big top, as it always does; the ancient magic holds, and I am banished from within. So Carl will go in with a clown's ticket and break the three poles. He freed Heather tonight. She was family. This is what you do for family.

beats.headline: The programme has a name
beats.text: Carl has a hunch that Signet's storyline is a programme of its own. Mordecai's old friend Eklund, a game guide in the nearby town, supplies the name: Vengeance of the Daughter. Its producer is not yet taking Zev's calls. Mordecai's view of such things stands: a team of writers, very protective of their show, and an elite with thick plot armour at the centre of it.

beats.headline: The producer is not talking
beats.text: Carl, I'm watching. The whole universe is watching, and we are all rooting for you. I can't interfere, and I told him so. He explained what he wants anyway. I said it was impossible; he said try. So: I messaged the producer, and he didn't want to speak with me. I think he is waiting to see how this plays out. My boss made me run the request past the Syndicate AI referee, and it will only allow this under very strict circumstances. Nobody can give Carl any help whatsoever.

beats.headline: The smell of the circus
beats.text: Inside the big top the smell hits me: peanuts, cotton candy, roasting corn, hay, animal musk, cheap plastic toys. The circus on my fourth birthday, when my mom had run off with me to her parents' place in south Texas. She cried that day, and until this second I always thought she was crying about my dropped hotdog. I have so little of her, and this place just took that too. I stop caring about the plan, or about saving my life. I just want to tear it all down.

beats.headline: Poisoned blood on the vine
beats.text: The vine fills the centre ring and swallows the pole: a city boss, level 85, and an elite. Not one crawler this season has faced a city boss and survived. Nobody inside even looks at me, so I sit in the bleachers by a root, take off the cloak that gives me poison resistance, and double up on health potions to poison myself. I cut my palm on a lemur's knife and let it drip. Heal, antidote, breathe. The blood's almost gone. I have no idea if it worked.

beats.headline: Ringmaster, and City Boss
beats.text: Ringmaster Grimaldi, Pestiferous Vine. Elite. Level 85 City Boss. A dwarf, once, standing centre stage when the cloud swept over the circus, and there to this day. However often his family dies and however many crawlers the clowns devour, he brings them back, memories mostly intact. His sign at the entrance promises that within the tent all worries and fears are left behind. Inside, the performers keep performing. A crawler has just sat down on the bleachers beside him.

beats.headline: How to kill a Pestiferous Vine
beats.text: I explained it after the recap. A Pestiferous Vine is a trope, lazy writing. Really a fungus hybrid: its spores infect parasitic worms, and the worms infect the mobs. Plants are easy to kill if you know the trick, and this one's trick is poisoned blood. A few drops on the vine break its link with every symbiont, in fifteen to twenty minutes, and it will not know. If it suspects, the same blood with an antidote in it cures it, so it will try to get its monsters to bleed you. A city boss as well? The core should be the same size. I think.

beats.headline: A cone of worms, on purpose
beats.text: The Wisp Armor spellbook is the one Donut asks me for about once a day. I read it myself on the way down the bleachers, because it blocks mind control and I am about to eat Apollon's ice cream cone, which is worms. A six-minute timer starts. Then I am outside with Signet on one side and Grimaldi in my throat, saying his half of the argument out loud for him. With less than a minute left I drink Mordecai's double healing potion and throw up a never-ending stream of dead worms. Quest complete. Level 15 to 18. Then Mordecai: Donut's health just dropped below 20%. Go now.

beats.headline: Speaking through a crawler
beats.text: Through the parasites in Carl's gut, Grimaldi reaches him: Carl. No. Come back. Please. The Wisp Armor keeps the crawler's legs his own, and he carries the voice out of the tent to Signet at the calliope. Carl makes the case for both of them. Once the worms force words out of his throat — "She hurts the family. She has turned her back." The last words they force out are Grimaldi's answer to her: "I have un-banished you, my love." Signet walks into the tent. Carl's part of the quest is complete.

beats.headline: Carl signs on to her show
beats.text: Grimaldi has lifted my banishment. Carl went into his head to ask him, and I asked with him. I may leave the circus behind me at last and go where my vengeance waits, and that is the sixth floor, not here. Carl has agreed to be part of it as well, the Vengeance of the Daughter, when it comes to its proper act. Before he went in he sat and read a spellbook. Wisp Armor. It guards the mind against control, and he wanted it on him before he swallowed the worms that let Grimaldi speak inside his skull. He does not walk into another creature's mind unarmoured. Nor would I.

beats.headline: Carl signs on
beats.text: He poisons Grimaldi's vine with his own blood and offers the producers a deal: he will appear on the programme when it moves to the sixth floor, or he heals the vine and their big night is a dud. They take it, and he heals the vine anyway. Then he reads a Wisp Armor spellbook for cover against mind control, accepts a cone of parasitic worms from Apollon the Mighty so he can speak inside Grimaldi's head, and talks him into lifting Signet's banishment.

beats.headline: She signs on Carl's behalf
beats.text: Okay, so. Carl wants a message relayed to the producers of Vengeance of the Daughter, word for word, and this is not what we discussed. My boss patches them in and they hear all of it. They say, and I am quoting, "Let's see what you got for us, Crawler." It is a deal. Carl wants it official, on paper. I tell him it is official, because I have the power to sign on his behalf, and he says that is terrifying. I ask him if he knows what he is doing. He says no.

beats.headline: This is my family
beats.text: A Heal scroll gets the spikes out of Donut; for Mongo it takes one of Mordecai's recipes. The street urchins came for the barricade I built around her, not for her, so I clear it into my inventory and they lose interest. Then there are hours of night left, and Mongo, much too big for it now, curls up on my lap and snores. Donut breathes against the back of my neck. I think about my mother, my father, Bea, Billy Maloney and Sam, the guys at the boatyard. All gone. All I have left is right here. This is my family.

beats.headline: What Bea's mother said
beats.text: Donut makes rash-looking decisions that are almost always the right ones, and I have started to think her camera self is an act, hiding how sharp she is. I remember Thanksgiving, on Bea's parents' couch with Donut asleep on my neck, listening to Bea's mom tell her you have to make them think you're dumber than you are. That attitude, wearing a mask even with family, I never understood. Now I am afraid Donut picked it up from the two of them. We are always camera-facing, and I have no idea how to talk to her about it without sounding like an ass.

beats.headline: He stands over her
beats.text: Mother down. Mother NOT MOVING. Mongo on top of Mother. Spiky things. MANY spiky things. Bite. Bite. Bite. Hurts. Mongo stays on Mother. Carl says something. Mongo does not listen to Carl.

beats.headline: Brown drink, then big
beats.text: Carl back. Carl pours brown drink in Mongo mouth. Spikes fall out. Mongo BIG now. Mother wakes up. MOTHER. Jump on Mother. Jump on Mother again.

beats.headline: A potion that works on a pet
beats.text: A Heal scroll does nothing for the dinosaur and neither does a potion. Listen. Take out a heal potion. There is a cinnamon stick in your inventory and I gave you a couple of branches of thistle rot. The whole cinnamon stick goes into the potion. Wait five seconds. Add the thistle rot. Cork it, shake it, pour it down the pet's throat, and try not to get your hand bitten off. The cinnamon and the thistle both came out of the Belly Rubbed Pug's kitchens, where I stole them.

beats.headline: Asleep for all of it
beats.text: I wake at dawn in a chair in a strange building, level 15, having done nothing whatsoever, and Mongo is enormous. I dreamed Ferdinand came to visit and turned into a porcupine, which was unpleasant. Carl did not kill the boss. If I had been awake we would have done things differently. He says the producers now want us alive. Until the sixth floor, when they write something to get us killed. We are guest stars, Carl, and a show cannot keep guest stars more interesting than its main character. That is why they killed Barb. GUESSING THE PLOTLINES OF TELEVISION SHOWS IS MY SUPER POWER.

beats.headline: Under the circus
beats.text: By morning the circus tents are gone, and so are the corpses and whatever a city boss might have dropped. In their place, in the middle of the park, is a staircase down to the fourth floor. It never showed on the map before, not even as one they could not reach, the way the Ball of Swine's did. Mordecai says many stairwells from here down only become visible once a quest is completed. This one had probably been sitting under Grimaldi the whole time.

beats.headline: Who makes Vengeance of the Daughter
beats.text: Okay, so, Carl and Princess Donut are booked for the day after tomorrow on a round-table show called Danger Zone. Other crawlers, a few intergalactic celebrities, maybe a politician, and an uncensored call-in segment, so be ready for anything. Then Carl asks who is behind Vengeance of the Daughter. Not a Kua-Tin company: nobody in our system may run serials while we run the game. It is Sensation Entertainment, Incorporated, from one of the center systems, and the gentleman I dealt with was a Sac. Carl asks what a Sac is. Since he does not know, I cannot tell him.

beats.headline: Freeballing
beats.text: The first thing I am going to buy tomorrow is pants, I say. Then I read a Scroll of Upgrade and it picks my Enchanted BigBoi Boxers. Plus five dexterity, plus five intelligence, three more constitution, and a benefit called Freeballing: double damage on attacks from below the waist, and those skills train 20% faster. The catch is that only a single layer may cover my crotch, and I am already wearing it. No trousers. I look up at the ceiling. Well played. Mordecai and Donut laugh hard enough to wake Mongo.

beats.headline: Hadji, and a casino chip
beats.text: Carl and Donut hit a quadrillion views among the first ten crawlers to do it, and each gets a Gold box whose contents the followers vote on, locked for thirty hours. The Hadji achievement, for finishing a quest an unusual way, lifts both their Gold Quest Boxes to Platinum: 5,000 gold each, a skill potion and fang caps for Donut, a Scroll of Upgrade for Carl. His Lucky Bastard box holds a 100,000 gold casino chip, playable only at the Desperado Club's tables. Donut earned the same survival achievement and got no box at all. Nobody knows why.

beats.headline: The manager goes where Donut goes
beats.text: I pop into my own room with a drink in my hand, because nobody warned me. As a manager, my town now matches wherever Donut last entered; a plain guide can dial it anywhere. There is a guide-only town these two cannot reach, and I was looking forward to it. The drink works because I brewed a potion that lets alcohol affect demon spawn. On my world I was a mycologist. Odette made me learn plenty about vegetation when we made it to the sixth floor. The cat gives Carl a sharp look when I say that. Neither of them says anything.

beats.headline: The boxers, upgraded
beats.text: An upgrade scroll goes onto the boxers. The spell itself does not change; the garment gets plus five Dexterity, plus five Intelligence, three more Constitution, and the Freeballing benefit, which permits one layer of clothing over the crotch and so rules out trousers. Mordecai calls them probably the most valuable item Crawler Carl owns. Five points of Intelligence is two and a half more metres of radius.

beats.headline: Acute Ears, in a safe room
beats.text: Donut drinks one and comes up with Acute Ears, plus fang caps for Mongo. Carl comes out of the same haul with a great deal of explosive and a Scroll of Upgrade that improves his boxers, which is roughly the ratio he has come to expect.

beats.headline: A quest outside the gate
beats.text: Just past the town wall, GumGum is tossing corpses onto a pile of about fifteen dead women, all twisted like dish rags. She finds more in the alleys every morning, blood mostly drained, nobody knows from where, and the guards don't work at night. Can we help. The quest arrives: The Sex Workers Who Fell from the Heavens, a Silver box. I notice wounds on the shoulders of two of them. We'll see what we can do, I tell her. Then I tell Donut we had a good day and I am not letting a quest derail it. That's what you said last time, she says.

beats.headline: Three biscuits, one herd
beats.text: The recap follows a crawler who entered with fifteen goats and has five left. She fed them three pet biscuits, and the third one went badly for several of the goats. Of the two that changed, one now walks upright in armor with a double-headed axe, screaming occasionally for no reason. The other is a hellspawn familiar: a horse-sized, pitch-black goat with glowing red eyes and six breasts. Mordecai rates hellspawn among the most powerful pets in the game, likely to sprout wings and grow to dragon size if kept alive.

beats.headline: Sparks
beats.text: Carl puts shiny teeth in Mongo mouth. Bite. SPARKS. Mongo scared. Mongo wet. Mordecai LOUD. Bite again. Sparks do not hurt Mongo. Bite. Bite. Bite. GOOD.

beats.headline: You can't save them all
beats.text: An orc woman at the pub, GumGum, says she needs our help. No. Not tonight. It is a quest, and we are doing no more quests on this floor. Then the kid wanders back out of his room, and she is already gone. So I tell him, and I want it to sink into that thick skull. You can't save them all. The people running this know who you are, and they will always be baiting you. If you truly want to help others, get as strong and as deep as possible.

beats.headline: A master shopper
beats.text: Shopkeepers get sweetness and sugar, and they love me for it. It takes five general stores to sell everything, and we come away with about fifty thousand gold. The Artist Alley Merchant class I chose to emulate did not give me its buying discount, but I have the extra fifteen percent when I sell, and I planned it that way. Miss Beatrice did not call me Princess Money Bags for nothing. Carl says it was Money Pit. We spend fifteen thousand on a pet carrier for my son, who needs his rest. I relent.

beats.headline: The Boomy Boy
beats.text: Carl and I have a playbook now. Either of us may call a play and the other follows without argument. Panic is the first: Carl casts Fear, I hit the mob with a missile. Today we add another. My Acute Ears tell us something is waiting around the corner, a manta ray thing called the Dispenser that drops off a wall, and I send two reanimated brain boilers at it, then a clockwork Mongo with a stick of dynamite in each hand. The whole fight takes under a minute. The real Mongo screams. We call it the Boomy Boy.

beats.headline: Fifteen seconds of Mongo
beats.text: The recap airs a fifteen-second montage of Mongo guarding a sleeping Donut, killing dozens of street urchins. Carl gets a few seconds and no explanation of how he got out of the circus: that scene belongs to the Vengeance of the Daughter production, Mordecai says, and anyone looking at Carl's numbers already knows. The same episode is following a crawler with an alligator head and a mag-fed shotgun that never seems to need reloading. Donut wants to know how he gets a T-shirt over that head.

beats.headline: On the door of the Desperado Club
beats.text: Subject is a Crocodilian, an intelligent, thick-skinned, semi-aquatic people who are not celebrated for their quickness, and she works the door of the club. This is a non-combatant posting, which describes her contract rather than her capabilities. Nobody has yet found the argument that gets past her.

beats.headline: The members-only room
beats.text: The front room is for locals and crawlers still earning a pass. Past Clarabelle is the members' floor, and it sits on its own plane: every club location on the level opens into the same room, and a member leaves through the door they came in by. Most of the crowd are bots, one vanishing whenever a real visitor arrives. A drawn halo gives a privacy bubble. Doors lead to two brothels, a jobs room, the Silk Road market, and three unlit signs, one of them a casino that is not open yet.

beats.headline: Ten left, and no more moonshine
beats.text: Crawler Carl has ten boom jugs left and a stash of Rev-Up bottles set aside to sell. Quint the pharmacist had heard the Krakaren say no more of the stuff was being made this season; Mordecai says Carl and Donut are the reason it was shut down. The royalties stopped after the first few coins. At least one other crawler found a few bottles.

beats.headline: Immortal, sort of
beats.text: Carl asks why I was so upset to be picked. It is not you. It's complicated. Then he asks whether that opossum was right that I am immortal. Sort of. From the fourth floor, managers get a protection package. Not you. We can still be hurt and still feel it, but dying there only kicks us out of the game. For the rest of this floor I am as unprotected as you. If I die as a manager I am done for the season. The rules pay me more the longer Donut survives, and past the ninth it is an obscene amount. Let's go look at the Silk Road.

beats.headline: A Dirty Shirley, in a bowl
beats.text: Mama needs a night off, so I order Miss Beatrice's kryptonite, the Dirty Shirley, in a bowl. Vodka is gross. I only ate the cherries. And a little more. The pharmacist looks to me like a floating, talking anteater, and I talk him down to three bottles and a potion to stop the room being wavy, and I would like to know why Carl did not warn me. Then a notice arrives: my followers' box can be opened. I leave the men at the table for the dance floor, jump onto an ogre's shoulder, and we twirl.

beats.headline: A starter kit for three bottles of moonshine
beats.text: Mordecai has me sent over to his table with a barefoot human and a talking cat, which is the sort of shift I am having, and I have not seen the man in years. He is a manager now. Sweet gig, that. No AI breathing down your back. He wants my starter kit. I want the Rev-Up in the human's inventory, because that Krakaren told me no more of it was being made this season. I ask four bottles. The cat, drunk on the cherries, talks me down to three and a Hair of the Dog. Deal.

beats.headline: What he says about the girl with the dogs
beats.text: The human asks about last night, so I tell him. A crawler came in, a real looker with one goat leg and two dogs. She put the dogs in the playroom and they went bonkers, she froze the whole room with a spell, stole tequila from behind my counter and splattered the brains of an elite gnoll with a mace. The playroom is shut for a week. Her membership has been revoked, thank the gods. The human knows her name before I have finished.

beats.headline: A kick in the alley
beats.text: Mongo bolts screaming into an alley and we chase him. A burning hand, three flying women's heads trailing their own organs, and GumGum on the ground with her chest torn open. Donut's Torch sends the heads corkscrewing away. The fourth one, an elf, teleports in front of us and starts announcing the final battle and how he has trained his whole life for this moment, and he knows our names. I kick him in the nuts at the same moment Donut's missile hits his neck. His head comes off. Mongo takes it.

beats.headline: Valued at 7,500 gold
beats.text: Pustule the hobgoblin, asked what a jug is worth, rubs it, whimpers, and licks it. Her verdict: nice design, material cost much too high. A different accelerant would burn less hot and cost ninety percent less, and plain moonshine would sell for more than the bomb. She would sell one for about 7,500 gold and pay half that. Crawler Carl keeps it, for a value reference.

beats.headline: The smell in the alley
beats.text: Out of box. Street. Carl throws biscuit. GOOD. Then SMELL. Burning meat. Mongo must go. Mongo goes. Carl yells. Mother yells. Tall one. Tall one falls down. Head. Mongo has head. Shake head.

beats.headline: Pustule has excellent hearing
beats.text: The hobgoblin at the explosives booth is ugly. Like really ugly. I whisper it to Carl, and she says she has excellent hearing. So I start over. Oh sweetie, we got off on the wrong foot; we will be buying a great deal from you, and I would really like us to be friends. Her last friend was a muskrat called Tiff. Her mother bit the head off a vorpal muskrat, which killed her. By the end I have fifteen hundred gold down to a thousand. On the way out she calls after us again: excellent hearing.

beats.headline: Hobgobs and Boom Sticks
beats.text: For the record: Pustule, hobgoblin, level 30, proprietor of Hobgobs and Boom Sticks in the Silk Road market. Mordecai's introduction: a little odd, but harmless, and "you'll be seeing a lot of each other." About six feet tall, an open sore on her cheek bubbling black and green ooze onto a threadbare pink T-shirt with a unicorn in sunglasses, and a smell of rot and sickness. Crawler Donut's first assessment, whispered: "She's ugly. Like really ugly."

beats.headline: Tiff the muskrat
beats.text: Goblin smoke bombs are crap, in her professional opinion; a hobgoblin smoke curtain works much better, and she has none tonight. What she has is hob-lobbers, twenty-five for 500 gold. In passing she mentions watching her mother bite the head off a vorpal muskrat. She was friends with Tiff, the muskrat. Her mother died of it. Crawler Donut, charisma at full, talks her down from 1,500 gold to 1,000 for the lot.

beats.headline: She licks the jug
beats.text: Crawler Carl sets one of his boom jugs on her table for a valuation. She rubs the side, makes a whimpering noise, and licks it. Then, all business: the material cost is much too high, and plain bottles of moonshine would be worth much more. She would sell it for about 7,500 gold and pay half that. "Beware of meteors!" she calls after them. From about fifty paces away, she also hears Crawler Donut's assessment of her. "Excellent hearing."

beats.headline: One muskrat, one mother
beats.text: A hobgoblin at the Silk Road, midway through pricing hob-lobbers, mentions that she once watched her mother bite the head off a vorpal muskrat. To teach the warlord a lesson, her mother said; the daughter suspects another reason. A few minutes on, Princess Donut hopes the mother won't be biting her head off too. No danger, says the hobgoblin: she died. It was a vorpal muskrat. You can't bite the head off a vorpal muskrat without doing a little dying in the process. Nobody asks what vorpal means.

beats.headline: A photograph from a box
beats.text: The first box Donut's followers voted on contains a small framed photograph of Beatrice, taken straight from her Instagram: bikini, laughing, on the lap of her ex-boyfriend Brad. It is the photograph over which Carl ended things. Donut is delighted and shows it to Mordecai, Mongo and the barkeep, who strokes the glass. Carl finds that it no longer bothers him, and shrugs deliberately at the ceiling. Donut puts it on the table beside her cat tree. Mongo hisses at it.

beats.headline: Oranges against the door
beats.text: The Cesta Punta skill from that Earth hobby potion was never a martial art. It is jai alai, and the thing in my box is the scoop you wear to play it. I strap it on. A pull-ring folds the scoop into a bracer over my forearm, and my gauntlet fits right over the end of it. Fitz brings the oranges I asked him for. The first one hits the centre of the safe room door and disintegrates. The slingshot rocks are too uneven to throw. I message Zev. You win. No more slingshot.

beats.headline: A pass signed in his name
beats.text: Two pieces of paper from the quest. A Gate Pass: "The holder of this pass is doing this on my orders. Magistrate Featherfall." Carrying it keeps the mindless swordsman guards off your back, provided your criminal enterprise is not too overt and you stay in the township that issued it. Beside it lies a blood-soaked letter in necroscript, which Mordecai cannot read but recognises: something an undead magic user writes. His conclusion: "I'm thinking you two might have a lich problem."

beats.headline: City elves and a squiggly letter
beats.text: The shirt is from the 201st Security Group, the city elves' militia. Conspiracy nuts, too stupid for the high elves, who kick them out. Their cause is protecting the eagle folk, my own old people, whom they take for angels, all because of a few stories about their tree goddess. I have never known them to be violent. The cat declares she is doing the quest; I ain't your dad, I'm your manager. Then the letter off the dead orc. I can't read it, but I know these squiggles. Necroscript. You two might have a lich problem.

beats.headline: GumGum died because of us
beats.text: She was a nice lady, for an orc, and she was doing the right thing. They probably killed her because we took her quest. So we are finishing it, and I tell Mordecai there is nothing he can do to stop us. I ask Fitz how he knew about the krasue, and he tells us GumGum's mother was one of those ladies, and bled to death alone on her own stoop. Miss Beatrice's picture goes by my cat tree. I make Carl promise not to let me die alone. Then something hits the roof right above our heads.

beats.headline: Voted in by an audience
beats.text: The first fan boxes come open in the Over City. Donut draws a framed photograph of Bea and Brad. Carl draws a xistera: a wicker-looking scoop reaching two and a half feet past his hand that straps to his hand and arm and hurls whatever he pulls out of his inventory into it, adjusting itself around the shape of the thing. It makes his slingshot redundant.

beats.headline: A name on a dead boss
beats.text: There is a level seventeen neighbourhood boss rotting in an empty swimming pool, and the kill notice carries my name. I had four brothers and sisters and fifteen cousins, and I am all that is left of any of them. So I hunt, and the notice carries my name and nothing else, which is accurate.

beats.headline: Off a dead boss and onto a roof
beats.text: It goes dark before noon and a dozen red dots close in. A green bolt snuffs Donut's Torch. My first pre-lit hob-lobber sinks into something big, the second takes out an elf. I throw two sticks of dynamite and one bounces back off a shape at least twelve feet tall, so I jump backward into the empty pool, where the bloated corpse of a dead boss is lying. That is the last thing I remember. I wake up on a roof across the street, level 19, and Donut is firing missiles over the edge.

beats.headline: He cares about being disturbed
beats.text: Mordecai's briefing: the surviving skyfowl villages keep the old structure without the oversight, so Featherfall is this village's big boss man. Getting to him means teleporting onto the town hall's third-floor landing and walking through a mall for skyfowl. His clerk, Miss Quill, declines to disturb him about a dead woman who is not skyfowl; it was like this under her late husband, and it is like this now with Magistrate Featherfall. The door to his chambers is magically locked.

beats.headline: You are not seeing the magistrate
beats.text: Two of them at my desk. A human with no shoes, a cat that talks, and a body. They have put a body on my desk. Evidence, they call it, and the human has shown the swordsmen a pass for it from the magistrate, so they leave without him. The magistrate is not to be disturbed. If he does not care about your business then he will certainly care about being disturbed, and I will not be discussing it further. Behind me is a shelf of beanbag figures in their proper order, and the human is standing far too close to it. The door behind me is locked. It is locked for a reason.

beats.headline: The only one still awake
beats.text: Carl jumps into a swimming pool full of dead boss and the boss goes off like a potato in a microwave. I watch him sail over the street spinning like a pinwheel. So I fetch the neighbourhood map, missile two of the last three, set Mongo on the third, jump to the roof and heal Carl with a scroll. I am covered in three inches of guts. Mongo is level 12. We have a new rule: no throwing explosives while blind. And I need a shower before our interview.

beats.headline: The frog in the pot
beats.text: I have had an answer ready for this. All it takes is a little seed. When the host asks about the Skull Empire's unrest I tell the frog story: boiled slowly, it never jumps. If it used to be okay and it isn't any more, do something about it. Kick them out and set up your own. Tucker says advocating sedition is a crime. Then you're all in that same pot. Besides, what are they going to do, throw me in the dungeon? Barely two minutes pass before the shot comes. It was meant for Donut and me.

beats.headline: A seat on the Danger Zone panel
beats.text: Ripper Wonton's panel, and the crawler and his cat are on it. I keep reaching for his hand and my claws keep going straight through his fingers, which does not stop me reaching. Then the Skull Empire fire at those two and hit Manasa instead. My friend. The comedian starts treating her death as a piece of political arithmetic, and I tell him to shut his mouth. The Prism Kingdom condemns the action, and I say so on air within the hour: we will bring a grievance against the Skull Empire in the Syndicate Courts.

beats.headline: His name was Gravy Boat
beats.text: A caller on Danger Zone asks Princess Donut who Ferdinand is. The answer given is the love of her life: a star-crossed ruffian, branded a Moggie, hunted by the authorities, who called to her from outside the window. Carl identifies him as the creepy yellow cat that came to the window when she was in heat. His name was Gravy Boat, and he belonged to Marjory on the first floor. Animal control never managed to catch him. "He preferred Ferdinand," says Donut.

beats.headline: Asked about her husband
beats.text: Carl and the cat are on the panel. One of the Daughters is near them. She recognised the circus and wants to come back to the team, but we are too far. She needs levels. I ask them as a personal favour, and the cat says yes before Carl can. The One-Eyed Narwhal, tonight. Don't blow her up. Then a caller asks why I left my husband to fend for himself. He left me. He was going to get us both killed. Now he is dead and I am not. Do I regret it? Of course I do.

beats.headline: Disowned, then rumoured aboard
beats.text: The Maestro has been stripped of his titles and disowned by his father, amid unrest in the Skull Empire's home systems, and is no longer counted as royalty. When Prince Stalwart's yacht fires on the wrong trailer, the Valtay Corporation claims one of its dreadnoughts in Earth orbit has destroyed that yacht. Stalwart was not aboard. The Queen Consort Ugloo and the former prince are rumoured to have been. Princess Donut asks Carl whether he heard that the Maestro is dead. He did.

beats.headline: The statement read out on air
beats.text: Subject is the crown prince, brother to the Maestro, a coarse-haired boar-like creature with lean muscle and a manner that is meant to be read as cruelty and largely succeeds. When his empire fires on a trailer and takes someone who was nobody’s enemy, it is his statement that goes out on air. He recorded it before the shot was fired, with an army drilling in the window behind him, announcing an execution that had not happened and, as it turned out, did not.

beats.headline: Will she leave Carl for Bea
beats.text: A caller in a top hat, Chappy, asks me what happens if Miss Beatrice is alive and shows up. Am I really going to leave Carl for her? The studio has already bucked once tonight, and I was sick all down my front. Now this. When we reunite with Miss Beatrice we will all work together. It will be like before. He seems perplexed and asks Carl, who mumbles something about bridges. Then the host breaks in with news.

beats.headline: Danger Zone, with two new guests
beats.text: Welcome back, folks. On the panel tonight: Princess D'nadia, Manasa, Tucker, Hekla, and the two everybody in this galaxy has been waiting to get in a chair. Tucker opens with a crack about letting a pet sit on the panel, and the cat spends the next half hour taking him apart on air and calling him Butler, and I put my head down on the table so nobody sees me laugh, because it was funny and because he had it coming. Then the barefoot one starts talking about revolution inside the Skull Empire, and when Tucker tries to cut in I tell him to stop and let him finish, because a guest of mine gets to finish a sentence.

beats.headline: The show goes dark
beats.text: And then the Skull Empire answers my guest by firing on a trailer, and they take Manasa, who had swapped trailers with my guests and was nobody's enemy and was not even the target. I hand the room to the audience questions while I find out what happened. Then we come back and I read Prince Stalwart's statement out on air, because that is the job, and then I say what I think of it, because that is also the job. By the time I finish saying it the Valtay have taken his yacht apart, with his mother and his disgraced brother rumoured aboard and Stalwart himself not, and folks, none of this is entertainment any more.

beats.headline: Carl plants a seed on Danger Zone
beats.text: A few minutes of provocation on a chat show, and the Skull Empire answers them with a pulse from Prince Stalwart's yacht. It hits Manasa's trailer instead of Carl's, which was a mistake, and the Valtay answer that in turn by destroying the yacht, with his mother and the Maestro rumoured to be aboard. Three funerals come of it.

beats.headline: A singer with a worm in her head
beats.text: Manasa, the cobra-headed pop star with the eighth-ranked single in the universe, died long ago; she contracted with the Valtay so that one of their parasites could keep her career going, and it is hotter than ever. On the panel she backs the Valtay's attempt to collect their debt from Borant. Then a pulse meant for Carl and Donut hits the trailer she swapped into, and she is gone. Their entertainment assets bring in more than their technology, Ripper says. Then the Valtay claim a dreadnought has destroyed Prince Stalwart's yacht.

beats.headline: Set up, and the pawns with us
beats.text: Manasa is dead in the trailer we were meant to be in, and I don't trust luck that tidy. Stalwart had his statement ready and the camera pointed at the army outside the window before I opened my mouth. So I say it in chat, never out loud: we were the bait, and so was she. Someone knew the orcs meant to kill us and set up the switch on purpose, or jumped on it. If the Valtay lose an ally, maybe go to war with the Skull Empire, they won't have time to take over the Borant system. Borant benefits. But we have so little information.

beats.headline: I punch a level-75 guard
beats.text: The elves are glowing on acorns when a pregnant fathom dwarf named Eunice lays their leader out with a rolling pin. An Icer freezes her solid, and two level-75 swordsmen lift their blades over her and the boy lying across her. So I punch the nearest one. It is like punching a Sherman tank: I dent it, and it does not stagger. Warning: branded a troublemaker, attacked on sight. Then Mic Drop: a one-armed kid under my arm, a boom jug in the air, Puddle Jumper to a roof across the street. The remaining eight elves are crisped. The temple burns, and the house next door with it.

beats.headline: A dark cleric, in theory
beats.text: The working theory, formed after an attack by shambling berserkers that Crawler Carl assumes were sent by "our Featherfall friend." The town's lead skyfowl is a dark cleric who commands the undead. The city elves of the 201st Security Group worship the skyfowl as living angels, which makes them free, enthusiastic labour for herding his undead minions. Knock out that support network first. Nobody has yet explained the dead women in the alleys.

beats.headline: Mic drop at the temple door
beats.text: A one-armed dwarf child under one arm, a lit jug in the other hand, a swordsman guard swinging. Crawler Carl tosses the jug straight up, Crawler Donut's Puddle Jumper takes them all to a rooftop across the street, and the jug comes down on the temple entrance. The remaining eight city elves are crisped instantly. The two guards' health bars barely move.

beats.headline: Benjamin, twice
beats.text: FOOD. Small lizard on a stick. BAD. Lizard comes back up. Small dwarf hits me. Arm is FOOD, and lizard again. MOTHER says HOLD. Tummy BAD. Small dwarf wants arm back. Give.

beats.headline: New rule: nothing outside the dungeon
beats.text: I distinctly remember saying subtle. The kid calls an orc king a pussy on air, the king's son lasers the wrong trailer from orbit, and the Valtay answer by blowing up the royal yacht. His wife is dead. So, new rule. We do not mention anyone outside this dungeon, not until after the sixth floor, if these two idiots make it that far. Odette asks, they have no opinion. I wanted his people aimed at the Blood Sultanate on the ninth floor. I don't think that's going to be an issue now. What can he do to them in here? Nothing yet. That changes very soon.

beats.headline: Named the Oak Fell
beats.text: The city elves outside a corrupt temple call me a disgusting, vile blasphemer, and I have done nothing. It is the anklet: the Enchanted Anklet of the Fallen Oak, which Carl gave me and which I always said was ugly. I show them my backside, which is award-winning. On Carl's word I shake my back leg, the beads rattle, and they come apart; one of them claws her own face bloody. Then they eat acorns and glow, and their leader announces who I am. Donut, the Oak Fell. The Death Upon Us All. She Who Ends.

beats.headline: He closes with Manasa singing
beats.text: We are out of time and I am not doing a comedy sting tonight. Roll the tape of Manasa singing. All of it. Goodnight, folks.

beats.headline: Booking schedules are public
beats.text: Okay, so. That was terrifying, and I thought Carl and Princess Donut were dead for certain. How did they know which trailer? Rental trailers put their booking schedules out for anybody to see, so everyone can coordinate availability. Nobody has ever needed to hide one, because nobody has ever tried to assassinate a crawler outside the dungeon. Now the Valtay have blown the royal yacht into dust. The good news is that nobody on the net is saying anything negative about Carl and Princess Donut; the prince is the villain. Our team is fielding a wave of interview requests. Odette has the contract on the next one.

beats.headline: They carry her as far as they can
beats.text: A neighbourhood boss and a borough boss with Katia in tow, until the third floor scatters everyone on arrival and she is too far from the rest of them to share in the experience.

beats.headline: Talking to the letter
beats.text: Mordecai works it out. The Mysterious Letter from GumGum's inventory is a spent Suppurating Eye scroll, a lich spell, and the blood on it is the caster's. Out of my inventory, whoever cast it can see and hear what's near it. That's how he answered me with a dead woman on a roof. Donut says we use it. So on a rooftop at night I set it on the tiles and we perform: stuffed animals worth stealing, a filing cabinet to loot, a hole to hammer through the ceiling of the office. Donut overacts. It's too late to fix that. The letter goes back in my pack.

beats.headline: Two Mongos and a bloody letter
beats.text: On a roof across the alley from the magistrate's building, Donut casts it on Mongo and pulls the original back into his carrier. The two copies squeak their disappointment and then do the work. One swallows the Mysterious Letter, which carries a lich's eavesdropping spell, and the pair leap across the alley and up a full story to the magistrate's roof, howling. Anyone listening through the letter should now place the crawlers overhead. Carl had not believed they could jump that far. The real party is crouched a building away when he presses the detonator.

beats.headline: She asks them to take her
beats.text: We carried Katia and her friend through a neighbourhood boss and a borough boss, and I would do it again. Then class selection split us, and I run this party on numbers, and Katia's numbers stopped adding up next to anyone she stands beside. I cannot carry that down another set of stairs. So I am the one asking. Carl. Donut. Take her. She is better than she looks right now, and she will hate that I said so.

beats.headline: Ten levels behind and nobody's problem
beats.text: I came in with a friend. We fell in with Hekla and Brynhild's Daughters, who carried the two of us through a neighbourhood boss and a borough boss, and I know exactly how much of that was us. Class selection split us up, and she did not wait. Now Hekla is asking Carl and Donut to take me. The system has just upgraded my displayed race from "What the f-word?" to "Human", so things are looking up.

beats.headline: Doppelgänger, Monster Truck Driver
beats.text: Bannon, my guide, talked me into it: a momentum-based constitution tank who can reshape her own mass, body and equipped gear together, into any form of the same weight. I sculpted my face using my reflection in a health potion bottle. Carl says it looks like a Juan Gris. He is being kind, and I would know.

beats.headline: Fuel tank, battering ram, stairwell finder
beats.text: Strength eleven. Intelligence eight, Charisma eight. Dexterity thirty. Constitution fifty-one: fifteen from a ring out of a loot box at the start, more from buffs, more from the class. Second Fuel Tank absorbs damage and reflects some back, once a fight, at random. Rush uses my body as a battering ram, once a thirty-hour day. Pathfinder finds stairwells. I am immune to wind spells. My Earth Hobby Potion made me a gear head, though I have never fixed an engine. I was an art teacher. What is the saying? Those who can't do, teach.

beats.headline: A feud, according to the recap
beats.text: The recap has a feud now. The cat, against my dogs, Cici and Gustavo. The cat says she never challenged anybody. The show says she did. Everybody watching heard the show. I know which one I am going to listen to.

beats.headline: Dynamite in the shelves
beats.text: They did not come back. They did not need to. The human fixed my shelf for me, the day he threw a dead woman across my desk, while I was on the floor gathering my figures, and I did not so much as look up. The shelves are hollow. Three sticks of hobgoblin dynamite and a detonator are sitting inside the second one now, under my figures, which is the one place nobody ever looks, because nobody but me has ever cared what stands on that shelf.

beats.headline: Pony-sized
beats.text: Cold ghosts. Bite! Level thirteen. BIG now. MOTHER on my back! Jump! Jump! MOTHER falls off. MOTHER angry.

beats.headline: What the newsletter does not say
beats.text: I talk Fitz into showing me his herb stash and steal his newsletter. Borant is warning shopkeepers and pub owners to be extra careful not to anger crawlers. It doesn't say why. I can read between the lines. Some of you are getting stronger than you should; the kid who trashed the Desperado Club is proof. Borant controls the mobs and most of the experience. The System AI controls most of the loot boxes, it is still the ultimate arbiter, and it is evening the odds against the shorter floors. These elaborate quests are the same symptom. Keep the new girl alive. If she dies, get those rings off her.

beats.headline: Since when can the news lie
beats.text: The recap puts me against Cici and Gustavo 3 with a lightning bolt between us, as though I had thrown down a gauntlet at Lucia Mar's dogs. I have done no such thing. They play me at the bar, being rude about rottweilers, which was a remark and not a challenge. Then the girl herself, with bugs crawling in her eye sockets, says she will find me in the dungeon and her dogs will tear me apart. Carl, since when is the news allowed to lie? We would kill them easily, of course. I simply do not want those ugly skulls after my name.

beats.headline: Ten smoke curtains, as promised
beats.text: She came through. Three more boxes of hob-lobbers, all impact-detonated, and a ten-pack of hobgoblin smoke curtains, round fused bombs meant to outperform the goblin kind. Crawler Carl buys all ten. That night, on a rooftop beside the magistrate's building, one of them fills the whole area like a heavy fog, far better than the goblin kind. Pustule had been correct.

beats.headline: Magistrate of a town that ignores me
beats.text: Three achievements scroll by after the blast. Assassin, for a ranking town official. Ultimate Extreme Power, a Platinum Tyrant's Box, and control of the whole settlement. CockBlock, for killing an NPC another crawler needed. My title goes from Royal Bodyguard to Magistrate Carl, until the floor collapses. I don't laugh. The quest is still sitting in my menu, which means we may have just killed the wrong bird. Two of the town's bird people hover over the roof and I tell them I'm on magistrate business. They tell me, less politely, to go back to the Desperado.

beats.headline: Fireball, for once
beats.text: The muted room fills with krasue peeling their heads free, trailing organs; one slaps me in the face with a still-beating heart. We back out into the smoke of the living room and I pull the Fireball or Custard lotto ticket. Last time it cast custard. I scratch it expecting custard again. Fireball. Spicy! It rolls through the doorway, shatters the jamb on both sides and goes off against Featherfall's corpse in its hoop of bone. The floor buckles. The room turns to Xs and half drops to the level below. The red dots circling Donut on the roof all disappear.

beats.headline: The bait is a job at the club
beats.text: Burgundy worked in another settlement until city elves told her she could get a job at the Desperado Club, which had an entrance in this town. Everyone knows, she says, that working at the club brings a chance to descend, and maybe deeper, where it's safe. It was all a lie. Women who come to work at the club are the ones brought to Remex.

beats.headline: Credited with his death
beats.text: Dynamite through the magistrate's floor. The notices arrive: a public official assassinated, control of the Medium Skyfowl Settlement, a new title, Magistrate Carl. The only NPC the notices name is Miss Quill, and a bronze boss box says one of the two was a neighbourhood boss. But the quest is still open, which should mean the head bad guy is still alive. Crawler Carl's conclusion: they killed an NPC they never met, blew his house to bits, and still have not finished the job.

beats.headline: Upside down in a bone dreamcatcher
beats.text: Found in the magistrate's quarters, at the centre of a room of krasue bodies hanging from the ceiling: Magistrate Featherfall, naked and emaciated, lashed upside down in a massive dreamcatcher of bone, featherless wings spread, a clear fluid dripping from beak and eyes. He had been there some time; the body was being mummified. Lootable Corpse. Former Magistrate Featherfall. Dark Cleric. Level 32. A fireball scatters his ashes. No neighbourhood map turns up in them, so by Crawler Carl's reckoning he was not the boss.

beats.headline: A dark fetish, by her account
beats.text: A dying krasue woman, mortal while Crawler Donut's torch holds the curse back, sets the record straight. Featherfall was not the one who did this. He has been hanging on that thing the whole time, and he was dead when she arrived. His body was turned into a dark fetish that keeps their bodies safe at night. Miss Quill has been running the city all along. She is the real magistrate.

beats.headline: The administrative building, and everything in it
beats.text: Miss Quill is dead. The reception office came apart with her in it, and the shelf, and every figure on it. Magistrate Featherfall, credited dead in the same blast, had been hanging mummified in a dreamcatcher of bone in the rooms behind for a long time before any of this. The barefoot man is magistrate of this settlement now, which is what happens when nobody checks the paperwork. He collects one achievement for assassinating a public official and a second for killing an NPC another crawler needed for a quest. The achievement declines to say whose, or what the quest was. She kept that door for a very long time and not one crawler ever thought to ask her why.

beats.headline: Hanging ladies
beats.text: Hanging ladies. Heads FOOD. Crunch. Crunch. Crunch. One head NOT THERE. Bite legs instead. MOTHER says RETURN. Ladies wake up. Screaming. More FOOD.

beats.headline: She asked me to
beats.text: The burnt woman is Burgundy, from the stairs, one of the magistrate's assistants, and one of those things: a person by day, a krasue at night. Carl wants to heal her. She says healing will only turn her back, and to kill her while she is still mortal. So I stroke her hair and tell her it is going to be okay, sweetie, and ask about Featherfall. She tells us Miss Quill ran the city all along, and about a husband named Remex across the street. Then the room slumps and she slides away, begging. I hit her with a Magic Missile before she is gone.

beats.headline: A survivor gives up his name
beats.text: A woman called Burgundy, one of the Krasue, lies burned to charcoal from the waist down in a building that is coming apart, and she has given two crawlers my name and told them where I am kept. Her husband, she called me: not alive, not dead, something monstrous. Accurate, as far as it goes, and it does not go far. Nobody has had cause to say my name aloud in a very long time. I know what that means. I have known what it would mean since the day I was pulled back.

beats.headline: He thanks the two who took his revenge
beats.text: My sisters and a cousin, five of them, went in seconds to Former Circus Lemurs; I was with my other cousin, and we barely got away. He gave up, and the next day he was gone. Now I walk out of the crowd to find the lemurs already dead by somebody else's hand, and the secretary I had a quest to kill dead by the same hand, and none of it mine. So I swear a debt to a cat and a man with no shoes, give them my chat contact, and point them at a stairwell three kilometres east. Then I ask the man the question I cannot answer for myself: how can we make it to heaven if God does not recognise us?

beats.headline: A forester
beats.text: Donut asks what I'd do if I could do anything. Not fixing boats. Not the Navy, either; it was the Coast Guard, whatever Bea told people. I think of the college applications I started and never finished. The forestry service, as a forester. I've seen enough ocean to last a lifetime. I'd be happy alone in the woods, watching for forest fires. She says she and Zev will be a television writing team, Gossip Girl with an intergalactic slant, and maybe if the shows are good enough people won't be so interested in watching real people kill each other. You surprise me every day, Donut.

beats.headline: Holding the boom switch
beats.text: My face is better now. Carl calls me out of the crowd and puts a pencil-like detonator in my hand, and I back away from it; the description says it might click on its own. Keep it in your inventory, he says. If they die, or if he says so, press the button. They need someone outside the lich's influence holding it. Mutually assured destruction, then. Hekla warned me that he was crazy. Then he tells the crowd they are all still in the blast zone, and I back up with the rest of them.

beats.headline: Rescued from the rubble
beats.text: Recovered from the debris of Miss Quill's building, which is falling in at the time. One of her glass cases, charred and half-buried less than a foot from the explosion, and not broken, so likely enchanted. The char rubs off. Inside is a plush: an armoured man atop a black horse. The tag says Kimaris. Crawler Carl pulls the whole thing into his inventory and runs, and the rest of the building caves in behind him.

beats.headline: Liches never shut up
beats.text: Liches come in all shapes and power levels. But they all have one thing in common. They are just like Odette: they never, ever shut the hell up. Narcissists, and cowards, who will do anything not to let go of the life they have grabbed back, so they always have minions and grandiose plans. I said blow the building and take a chance on losing the quest. Then they killed most of his support, and I changed my mind: he'll be weak. One more wrinkle. The last one was a neighbourhood boss. I'd bet my left nipple this is a borough boss. Come prepared.

beats.headline: He promised I would not die alone
beats.text: Carl's plan is to ring the warehouse with dynamite and go up alone to meet the lich while I wait outside. Absolutely not. He promised me I would not die alone, and he cannot keep that promise if he dies before me. We do this together. So the plan changes, and Katia gets the button. I tell him at the bottom of the ladder that I do not like this plan. Mongo stays in his carrier; he has proven he cannot be trusted to stay still. I ride up on Carl's shoulder.

beats.headline: They take him for a lich
beats.text: They come across the floor towards me with the cat out in front and a fuse somewhere behind, and they have decided that I am a lich, that I am the borough boss, and that finishing me finishes their quest. I am no lich. I am no boss. I am a level one bird with no feathers left and a nick in the plane between the living and the dead, and if they lay a hand on me their souls come out through the scratch and go into the tank, and I have no way on this earth to give them back.

beats.headline: A case for the gem
beats.text: The epicentre is the gem, not Remex, and I have one thing that might hold it: the glass case Miss Quill's Kimaris came in. It protects against most, not all, forms of abuse, and every opening carries a 1.5% chance of blasting you with fire, which I read after opening it. I close it around the floating gem without letting my hands touch it, hook the latch, and try to pull it into my inventory. Yeah. Nice try, asshole. So I let go, and it hangs there around the gem, the cracks spreading, two and a half minutes on the clock.

beats.headline: Killed by the feedback
beats.text: Remex, Soul Leech Capacitor, tells it as a story he has rehearsed. Featherfall never liked the guards and wanted more control over them; after Remex retired and handed him the perch, he asked what it would take. After Remex died, Featherfall asked Quill to help cast a spell that would pull a dark cleric back from the dim as a capacitor. He took the Night Votive position with Quill in the room, too close to the amplifier. The feedback killed him. Quill planned it. She kept his office running with a forgery spell.

beats.headline: She spends a death sentence saving NPCs
beats.text: The Fools Who Broke the Glass quest is close to unsurvivable, and it triggers before I have earned my place. I spend the time getting NPCs out. I tell Carl and Donut to save themselves. I mean it.

beats.headline: Out of the case
beats.text: Sorted by value, the stuffed horse-riding soldier is the top item in Crawler Carl's inventory, and its glass carrier is the second. The case is a Sheol Glass Reaper Case. It protects against most forms of abuse, and carries a 1.5% chance of Sheol Fire every time it is opened, which Carl reads after opening it. He takes Kimaris out and keeps the case, closes it around a soul gem that is about to flatten the neighbourhood, and sits down to watch.

beats.headline: Correction to the file
beats.text: Remex tells them the rest of it, there being nobody left to stop him. She was not guarding the magistrate. She was guarding what she had done to her own husband: let Featherfall drag him back into the world as a soul leech, knowing the feedback would kill Featherfall, and kept him above the swordsmen's warehouse as her capacitor, feeding off the soul crystal, so that she would have the mana for a working called The Final War. The devotion to the figures was real. The refusals at that desk were real. Both of them were also the cover, and I filed her as an obstructive minor official for the whole of the season.

beats.headline: A bereft minion, then run
beats.text: Not a lich, he says. No. A bereft minion: one still alive after its controller is dead. You killed the head bad guy when you blew up Miss Quill. Quests sometimes look bigger than they are; I should have known, it was only a silver quest. Sorry about the dynamite. Get the story, put him down, get out before the swordsmen wake. Then the quest drops. Run for the Desperado Club; the second room is out of the blast. Protective Shell won't work, it's magical. Break the gem? Probably makes it blow early. It's called The Fools Who Broke the Glass for a reason.

beats.headline: I know she's dead
beats.text: Carl says we can save ourselves, or try for Katia and eighty other people with an idea that probably won't work. I don't know. Then I do: we try, because it is the right thing. We sit and watch a glass case float round a cracking gem while Remex tells his son he is coming. Carl says Remex was a crawler once. I do not want to become an NPC. Carl says he is proud of me for worrying about Katia; I tell him I just don't want Hekla mad at us. Then I tell him I am not as dumb as I pretend. I know she's dead.

beats.headline: Soul Leech Capacitor
beats.text: You asked before you detonated anything, which is more than most would do, so here is the story. A Soul Leech Capacitor is what a necromancer builds when what they want is a battery with a face. The spell reaches for the soul the target loved best and drags that soul back into the world, tied to them for good. Featherfall cast it, wanting power over the swordsmen, with my wife in the room to help, and the feedback killed him, which is exactly what she had planned. Since then the power of this town's soul crystal has run through me, and she has been spending it, and what she is spending it on is a working called The Final War. I agreed to none of it. I would like that written down somewhere.

beats.headline: The Fools Who Broke the Glass
beats.text: Am I glad you asked. A while back an NPC started a spell so potent it had to be finished by a future generation, and old spells are like trees: they grow, and when they get screwed up, the bigger the spell, the worse it goes.
