I was looking forward to this one going off. Oh well. Every bird-folk NPC in the area is falling ill, being tied to it. Every crawler within forty-five square kilometres gets the quest: don't die. Not your fault, unless you are Carl, Princess Donut or Katia Grim. Sixty seconds to reach a saferoom. Seven minutes to the explosion. Run.

beats.headline: I told you it was here
beats.text: I told them there was a stairwell three kilometres due east of the village. Now the whole district is running for it, and I jog up with a new group behind me while the timers run down. I told you it was here, I say. The man with no shoes, in nothing tonight but a jacket, claps me on the shoulder. I nod to him, and I am the first of us down the stairs to the fourth floor.

beats.headline: Naked, running east
beats.text: Mordecai says every magical item off, now. Everything I wear is magical except the jacket, underwear included, so it all goes into my inventory. I post the two ways out in the quest chat, and three crawlers answer the same way: the back room at the Desperado Club disappeared when the saferooms closed. That leaves the stairwell three kilometres east. Katia jogs up with a handful of strangers. Magical gear off, I tell them; sixteen minutes, full speed. One of them finally asks why I'm naked. I point east. Go.

beats.headline: Congratulations, unanswered
beats.text: Mordecai is in his room, safe. He'll sit and twiddle his thumbs for three days; we won't notice the difference. The guards came back on the second burst with a single life point each, and he'd have me killing them if I were there. Then I tell him congratulations. He doesn't answer. Donut works it out: we make the fourth floor, and he gets to go home once the dungeon is over. I think of Remex, about to finish his duty too. Of Signet, Quint, Pustule, GumGum, Miss Quill, and little one-armed Ricky Joe. I wonder if his mom ever had her baby.

beats.headline: Built in the middle of a collapse
beats.text: During the Fools Who Broke the Glass, Carl drops a Sheol Glass Reaper Case around a Soul Crystal that is already going up and pulls the result into his inventory. Status: Explosion Imminent. "This item can no longer be stabilized."

beats.headline: Forty-five square kilometres
beats.text: Enough to take a city and every suburb around it. It can no longer be stabilized, and the moment it leaves his inventory it goes off, with less than a second to spare. "Created by a man who murders babies and steals rare collectibles from his elders."

beats.headline: Destroying it does not help
beats.text: The crown crumbles to dust in the Over City's collapse, taken by one of the pulses that strip magic from whatever is still being worn. The succession survives it.

beats.headline: Destroyed, and it changes nothing
beats.text: The third pulse of the blast destroys any armour still equipped, and the crown crumbles to dust on her head as she agrees to take it off. The succession is untouched. It said as much on the label.

beats.headline: Through the wall
beats.text: The fourth pulse fires the first things in everyone's hotlist, and for me that is Rush. I glow, clip Carl on the way past, and go straight through the wall of the building with the stairwell in it. That really hurt. At the bottom of the stairs Carl has me take out the detonator. It has a ten-second delay; press it at about fifteen. Won't that make the bomb go off faster? By a couple of seconds, he says, and it probably died in the first burst anyway, but if it works we all share the experience. I press it at twenty.

beats.headline: It was my first item
beats.text: Carl wants the tiara off. I will lose five Intelligence, and my Sepsis debuff, and I really like it. And if I lose it somebody else gets it and we will have to fight them, and I do not want to hurt a person. But a man's arrows have just gone off in his quiver, and Carl says it might set my head on fire, and Katia says he is right. Oh, all right. It crumbles into dust before I can take it off. At the door I point out that Carl should have put his pants back on before we go straight to Odette's show.

beats.headline: On the way down
beats.text: On the stairs off the third floor, Crawler Carl runs through everyone they met there. Signet the half-naiad. Quint, the possum-faced pharmacist. Pustule, the hobgoblin explosives dealer. GumGum the orc. Miss Quill. Little Ricky Joe, the one-armed child dwarf. A week on that floor, and it felt like a millennium.

beats.headline: Four shocks, and a town coming apart
beats.text: Remex is finished. He began to convulse and the settlement went with him: a foreshock that stripped the enchantments off every piece of gear in the district, a second that set weapons off where they hung, a third that took the Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore apart, and a fourth that reached into every crawler's hotlist and set off the first two things on it. Ranger Conrad E's arrows went off in his quiver and took him with them. For the record: he asked them not to come closer, he told them the whole story, and he was the most honest thing in that town.

beats.headline: A part in a bomb
beats.text: The word arrives the way most of the dungeon's cosmology does: buried in an item description. A Sheol Glass Reaper Case is half of what makes an explosion large enough to rattle the teeth of a god. The case's own description says it was forged in the fires of Sheol, the mysterious fifteenth level of the World Dungeon, and nobody asks what that means.

beats.headline: Mind the gap
beats.text: This one sits three kilometres east of the settlement in a small, decrepit building, and with the saferooms shut and the Desperado Club's back room sealed, it is the only way out of the blast. Crawlers have been leaving notes in the bars with stairwell locations. A floor ends for whoever goes down the moment they pull the handle at the bottom. The door there carries the usual oversized carving, and its properties read: Entrance to the fourth floor. This is where the real fun begins. Mind the gap.

beats.headline: It burns a veto rather than pay
beats.text: Eighty-three Celestial boxes are owed. Borant appeals, a Syndicate court overrules it, and it burns its one seasonal veto to void the prizes anyway, which has never been done this early. It is still liable for the one box that was opened before the appeal. A production company that cheap has seams worth looking for.

beats.headline: All about progression and training
beats.text: Odette runs the footage of me crossing the city in a one-armed leather jacket and nothing else while I sit on her couch in a loincloth of toilet paper. Then she explains how we were robbed: a Syndicate court said pay us, and Borant burned its one veto of the season so it wouldn't. I laugh. It doesn't matter how hard we work, we keep getting screwed. We messed up chasing quests when we should have been grinding, and we're not going to make that mistake again. It's all about progression and training. The explosion still counts: I go from twenty-one to twenty-seven.

beats.headline: Tenth on the board
beats.text: Tenth on the draft leaderboard, spelled Elle McGib: Frost Maiden, Blizzardmancer, level thirteen, bounty one hundred thousand. She began the third floor at level one. Carl knows her as a wheelchair-bound resident of Meadow Lark and cannot work out how she got there; he has not talked to Brandon in several days.

beats.headline: Fourth on the board
beats.text: They put the leaderboard up tonight and I am on it. Fourth. Crocodilian, Shotgun Messenger, level twenty-four, three hundred thousand. I don't know what they showed to get me there. I wasn't doing anything I would call footage. I would have preferred to stay a name nobody had learned yet. Too late for that.

beats.headline: Second on the board
beats.text: Second on the draft leaderboard: Hekla, Amazonian, Shieldmaiden, level twenty-eight, a bounty of five hundred thousand, behind only Lucia Mar. Odette, who has watched her some, has her parted from her guide, and fixed on bringing Princess Donut into Brynhild's Daughters. Not for the cat's sake. The cat comes with a permanent manager, and Hekla knows about Mordecai because Katia told her.

beats.headline: Eighth on the board
beats.text: The board does the introductions this dungeon never bothers with. Ifechi is eighth: human, a Physicker, level eighteen. Healing is a class down here and a liability at the same time, since the one thing nobody in this place will let you do is keep other people alive. Note it and move on. The audience already has.

beats.headline: This is the real me
beats.text: We come through the door into a green room that seems to be on a boat. Donut says I am getting really good at the sculpting. I touch my face. This is the real me: short black hair, the face I came in with. On Odette's couch I am brought out as the newest member of the Royal Court of Princess Donut, and I answer her questions one word at a time. Then she puts our levels up over our heads. I have gone from nine to twenty-one.

beats.headline: Ninth on the board
beats.text: Ninth on the draft leaderboard: Li Jun, human, Street Monk, level twenty-five, bounty one hundred thousand. Carl remembers him from the Maestro's show, the one he helped save from the troglodytes and brindle grubs, and is glad to see him there. He hopes Zhang and the others are doing well too.

beats.headline: The top tiers cost the house real money
beats.text: Borant owes the Syndicate tax on every non-sponsored box it hands out: a handful of free Celestials a season, and a steeper bill for each one after that. In the whole history of the show only 2,145 Celestial boxes have been awarded, and no crawler has had more than four. The previous record for one season was eighteen, in a Naga season long ago.

beats.headline: Eighty-three Celestials, and one veto
beats.text: A quest reward gets double-upgraded to Celestial for 83 crawlers. Borant burns its single seasonal veto to void them and is a moment too slow — Quan Ch has already opened his, which leaves the company liable and in a Syndicate court. The upgrade achievements responsible are patched out immediately.

beats.headline: First on the board
beats.text: First on the draft leaderboard, and by a distance: Lucia Mar, Lajabless, Black Inquisitor General, level twenty-nine, bounty one million, twice the next name down. Odette explains afterwards that the number is what other crawlers get for killing her. Princess Donut calls her ugly on air, and the audience laughs.

beats.headline: The season that lost money
beats.text: By Odette's account, more than 250 cycles ago the Blood Sultanate of the Naga ran the first crawl ever to lose money, and they are still recovering. That season also handed out eighteen Celestial boxes, the most in any one season before this crawl, and was cursed for other reasons she declines to get into. The Nagas have not run a season since. They keep a standing place only because they bought a permanent spot early on.

beats.headline: Why I warn Carl about Hekla
beats.text: Lexis takes the new girl out, and Carl sends the Princess after her, because this is for him. Hekla is not evil, or psychotic like Lucia Mar. She is practical and cunning, and she does not have his sense of what is just, which makes her dangerous. She wants Donut in her party, because Mordecai comes with Donut, and a permanent manager is worth having. Donut would never leave him, not as long as he is alive. Why tell him? I bought their rights early, when they were cheap. If he dies and Donut joins Brynhild's Daughters, my contract is void. And those numbers on the board are bounties.

beats.headline: A war god and a sponsorship
beats.text: Be careful with that gauntlet, Carl. Used against a war god's celebrants, it can summon the god himself, and his celebrants start appearing on this next floor. The Skull Empire has just spent a lot of money on a deity sponsorship, which they don't usually buy, so it may be an attempt to get to you. I don't know which god. If I were still a gambler, I would bet on that one. Can he reach you if you don't summon him? Probably not, not on this floor. Ask Mordecai how that works. He has a lot of experience in the subject, unfortunately.

beats.headline: An iron paw
beats.text: Odette shows a crawler dragging himself into a saferoom, the same one who was so rude to us in the quest chat. I am glad he survived; I felt kind of bad, because I blocked him. You cannot let people in your chatrooms get out of control. Then Quan Ch opens a Celestial box that he got for our hard work, and we get nothing, not even a Platinum. This is an outrage. Then the leaderboard: Carl sixth, me seventh, dear Hekla second, and that ugly Lucia Mar first. We are in the top ten!

beats.headline: He opens his before the veto lands
beats.text: Eighty-three crawlers are owed Celestial boxes at the close of this floor. Borant appeals the ruling and loses, appeals the prizes and loses again, and then burns its one seasonal veto here, voiding the lot. It is a fraction too slow. Crawler Quan Ch's box is already open, and you cannot un-open a Celestial box, not even with a veto. So the count comes to one: a level fifteen trooper in a glowing robe that lifts him off the ground. The veto was not mine. I want that on record.

beats.headline: Remex the Grand
beats.text: The newscast has a name for him now: Remex the Grand, whose tragic, controversial tale finally comes to an end. The footage shows the pus detonating at the warehouse, swordsmen tumbling with their health deep in the red, and Remex curled in his corner, a silhouette of pulsing yellow. The light leaves him two seconds before the blast. He cries out as the dynamite takes him. The soul release from the fallen swordsmen tempers the wild magic, and thousands of NPCs and several dozen crawlers are potentially saved.

beats.headline: Katia joins on air
beats.text: Odette brings the newest member of the Royal Court of Princess Donut out in front of the virtual crowd: Katia, who answers the first few questions in single words. Mongo gets a welcome back, squawks at the audience and curls up at Donut's feet. Behind them the court's levels go up on screen, all earned from an explosion that paid no prizes: Donut nineteen to twenty-six, Carl twenty-one to twenty-seven, Katia nine to twenty-one.

beats.headline: One veto a season
beats.text: The AI rules that Carl's detonator came through both precursor bursts; Borant appeals, and a Syndicate court overrules it, adding that the achievements from the explosion are just and must be paid. But Syndicate rules give every host a single veto each season, almost always saved for the tenth floor or deeper. Borant spends it on the third. The Syndicate also taxes every non-sponsored box, allowing only a handful of free Celestials a season, and an emergency session is now deciding whether Borant pays for the other eighty-two.

beats.headline: A shield left behind on the tracks
beats.text: My pedicure buffs have lapsed, and a Drek baby finds that out by gnawing on the sole of my foot. Then they get through the first door, and the alarm trap plays Fergalicious loud enough to hurt. I check the map for a straight run of track and cast Protective Shell. The shell stays where it's cast. The train doesn't. It sweeps back through cars sixteen to twenty and off the end, pushing every mob in the way ahead of it. Car sixteen is all blood after that, with a Psycho Sticker so flat it doesn't even show on the map.

beats.headline: They are waiting when the doors open
beats.text: The commonest ghoul on the line, and by the System’s own account the most tractable of them, which says more about the others than it does about these. The court meets its first pair in the first minutes on the new floor, by diving into their train car to escape a flood of Drek babies, before anyone has established what the rules of the place are.

beats.headline: First through every door
beats.text: Something on this floor has doubled my constitution to 102. It is a momentum bonus, though we are standing still, and Carl says it may be patched out tonight. So I go through each door first, because my constitution is four times his. I suppose that is my job. The first time, Mongo leaps in with me and I land on my face, and my axe skitters ten feet ahead. It is a good weapon. My strength is not high enough for it.

beats.headline: The skill that stayed behind
beats.text: Kid, listen. Her Negotiation came at level five with the Artist Alley class, and she sold it up to seven. The class is gone and the five levels went with it, but she kept the two she earned, experience and all, so it bumped itself to four. So a skill she levels even once, she keeps. Stat points, no. Use Mongo as much as you can and Mascot stays. Watch for classes with rare spells. And it's probably a bug, so don't talk about it out loud. They won't notice until she carries a spell down a floor.

beats.headline: Hooligan, on six minutes’ notice
beats.text: The moment we land on this filthy train, my Character Actor skill says I must pick a new class in six minutes or be given a random one, and the list is nothing like before. I DON'T LIKE THESE CHOICES, and I tell Mordecai so. He says Football Hooligan: a momentum bonus, team buffs, and a skill called Mascot that is all about Mongo. I get Mascot. I do not get Group Chant or Moving Riot. I get ten points of Constitution, and Guinness, which doubles my strength when I am drunk. So if there is fighting, we stop at the club first for a dirty Shirley.

beats.headline: Left behind on the tracks
beats.text: The secondary effect, applied. Trapped in a speeding subway car with mobs breaking through the doors, Crawler Carl checks that the track is straight and casts. The shell ignores solid objects and stays exactly where it was cast along the track, so the train carries on through it, and it rolls down the cars, sixteen to twenty, pushing every mob before it like a bulldozer and squashing them into paste against the first surface they meet.

beats.headline: The magistrate’s necklace
beats.text: The Tyrant's box holds ten thousand gold and the Enchanted Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie. One poor sapphire on it, for the town I ended up magistrate of on the third floor, worth 432 gold in taxes every ten days if I keep it. Plus five dexterity and Talon Strike, which turns the side of my bare foot into a slashing weapon with a two percent chance to cast Eviscerate. It sits heavier than it should under my shirt. We didn't wear dog tags in the Coast Guard. The boss box is a tome for Bang Bro: fire and electric damage on my gauntlet.

beats.headline: A shield that looks like my sleeve
beats.text: My box gives me an arm bracer that becomes a shield. When I activate it, it takes on the look of whatever is around it, so it is a buckler of blue polyester, but it rings like metal when I knock on it. Mordecai says it carries Shatter and I should use it with Rush. Donut says I can be the liquid metal Terminator. I never saw that film. I don't like violence. She says I am in the wrong job, honey. I have promised my coupons to Hekla, and Mordecai has already worked that out.

beats.headline: A toad, not a frog
beats.text: This floor they've made me Grulke Infantry. Toad warriors: leapers, a tongue that hits hard, and a people gone to mercenaries and vagrants. Tunnel trolls hunt them to lick them. Don't ever call a real Grulke a frog; they're mean bastards. Toads. And yes, I know about the quest. I get notices of court decisions that go against my client. You got screwed, but you're alive. The third floor is usually twenty days, and you had ten. Level 27 and 26 after that is lucky and a miracle. We can't rely on luck.

beats.headline: A level-5 space, from an odd little box
beats.text: Carl, Donut and Katia each get a special achievement whose box holds personal space coupons — beds, a shower, a crafting studio and a training room. Donut installs a cat tree.

beats.headline: Wendita, down to 37,500
beats.text: The Bopca says fifty thousand for a personal space and that it is not something they negotiate. Oh, sweetie. Everything is negotiable. She offers forty-five, I turn my back on her, and she says forty-four thousand, and then thirty-eight, and then 37,500, which is as low as the system will let her go, so I ask how much she has saved up. Carl says not to make her pay from her own pocket. I can feel her wavering. It is delicious. But we pay with the coupons from our boxes instead, and fifteen thousand gold on top, and she weeps and says she knew asking her to pay was only a test. A real princess would never do such a thing.

beats.headline: A spell called Hole
beats.text: A new tiara poofs onto my head: the Enchanted Tiara of Mana Genita, white jewels instead of purple, three intelligence and better at spotting mobs on my map. It is not as good as the one I lost. Then the mailbox in the corner has my spellbook, and it is not Fireball. When am I going to get a good spell? I ask Mordecai whether I should read it or sell it, and he says read it. It is called Hole. At level one it is not thick enough to get through most doors.

beats.headline: Cuck Aquaman
beats.text: Crawler Carl, a housekeeping note. My award for going down the stairs early has been removed by Syndicate Court Order. Next: you got fucked by a fish. You did something so spectacularly controversial that courts and lawyers had to get involved, and the end result was my decision being overturned. Reward: a Platinum It's Not My Fault You Fish-Headed Assholes Don't Properly Program Your Quests Box. Seven slips of paper. A free personal space, upgraded to level three. Two environmental upgrades. Two crafting tables. Two table upgrades. The cat gets the same. So does Katia.

beats.headline: Messages from deceased crawlers
beats.text: Filed under Messages from deceased Crawlers. The third floor was about to collapse, and Brandon and a resident named Henry held the line against the shade gremlins so Imani, Elle and the others could reach the stairwell, twenty minutes away with ten on the clock. He had fought with his brother, who left the party and stopped accepting his messages. The message asks Crawler Carl to tell Chris he was sorry, that Chris was right, and that he loved him. "That's the most important part."

beats.headline: Messages from deceased Crawlers
beats.text: Brandon's message was sitting in a folder I never noticed: Messages from deceased Crawlers. He and Henry held the line against the shade gremlins so Imani, Elle and the others could get away, with ten minutes on the clock and the stairwell twenty off. He'd fought with his brother Chris, who left the party. If I see Chris, I'm to tell him Brandon's sorry, and that he loves him. When I close it, Brandon comes off my list. Mordecai says to apply my buffs first, and I tell him where to go. One hour of Bare Knuckles on the wooden dummies.

beats.headline: On the board, two hours in
beats.text: Crawler Elle McGibbons, formerly of Meadow Lark, is seen on the recap for one second: a blue-skinned, white-haired elf thing that floats instead of walking, skewering a troll-like monster in a subway car with icicles shot from her palms. Race: Frost Maiden. Class: Blizzardmancer. Level: seventeen; the list the crawlers were shown before had her at fourteen. Leaderboard rank: ten. Bounty: one hundred thousand gold. Carl realises he has already seen her in passing on earlier recaps without knowing it was her.

beats.headline: Second, and another 83
beats.text: The recap puts me at two. Amazonian, Shieldmaiden, level twenty-eight, five hundred thousand gold on my head. The clip is me with the crossbow in a mass of four-legged rat things. Our train filled with monsters the same as theirs, but we had one stop to ride before the transfer station. Ours is also number 83, on the Orange and Indigo lines. No sign of the Red, the Yellow or the Nightmare lines.

beats.headline: One of the handful the show follows
beats.text: The recap presents the top ten one at a time, a short clip each, and she is in it: Elle, Li Jun's team, Ifechi, the cat and the man, Florin, Prepotente, Hekla, and the girl who is hunting the cat. Ifechi travels with Florin now. Being in the running order is not the same as being safe in it. It is nearer the opposite, and every one of them has worked that out by now.

beats.headline: Still first, on the recap
beats.text: The show plays me pulling the head off one of the janitor ghouls in a train car. The blood goes everywhere and I am laughing. Then the board comes up. One. Lucia Mar. Lajabless. Black Inquisitor General. Level thirty. A million gold on me. The cat is seven. The man is six. A hundred thousand each.

beats.headline: Two hours of sleep, then a schedule
beats.text: You only sleep two hours now, so I'll see you out here for the recap. Then the schedule. Wake, eat, buffs: shower, the cat's brushing, your feet. An hour in the training room on one skill, because you only get one a day. Carl, Smush. Katia, Catcher. Donut picked Dodge. Crafting after that, starting tomorrow. The recap freezes on REDACTED; get used to it, that's the part explaining the level. Where I woke up was station 317: the Yellow and Emerald lines, and a big one called the Misery. I wrote it all down.

beats.headline: On the recap
beats.text: They have put me on their recap, the programme between floors, in a row with humans. The captions say Elle, Li Na's team, Ifechi, Florin, Hekla, Lucia. And Miriam, of course, since she is the one who walked me into this place. I did not ask for the camera and I do not smile for it. If the audience wants a goat that performs, the audience can wait until I feel like singing, and then it can sit very still and listen.

beats.headline: The board, two hours in
beats.text: Elle, Li Jun, Ifechi, Florin, Miriam, Prepotente, Hekla and Lucia, all in one broadcast. It is how the crawl keeps track of itself.

beats.headline: Hunting season is open
beats.text: Welcome to the fourth floor, crawlers, a genius feat of engineering. The trick is to find the stairwells. For this level only, you may not go down early: the stairwells open six hours before collapse, and that's it. The leaderboard has populated, and every name on it carries a bounty. Hunting season is open! Kill one and a loot box pays you. Survive with a bounty on your own head and you get ten percent of it. The third floor ran hot, yes. Group quests gone bad. We are all concerned about early extinction. So quit sucking.

beats.headline: A bucket of pink glitter
beats.text: First time at a workbench. I point the Goo-inator at a swordsman's breastplate, pick Freeform, and bend iron like dough. The achievement is Martha Stewart, and the Bronze Crafter's Box holds pliers, a tape measure and a bucket of pink glitter. Not a vial. A bucket. Some of it's on the floor before I can store it, and I know from experience it's there for good. Mordecai says the shaping tool weakens what it shapes, and that a saferoom may keep you from dying at a bench, but botch it badly enough and you'll wish you were dead.

beats.headline: Five westerns for five books
beats.text: Limp Richard, the mole man at the general store, has read his Andre Norton a few dozen times. Shopkeepers get no entertainment feeds, he says, only books and comics, and he has fifteen, sixteen counting the one with its last chapters torn out. I trade him five westerns I've already read for three Nortons, The Lathe of Heaven and The Forever War. Donut says I'm a terrible negotiator. The Coast Guard taught me what books are worth to a bored man who has run out. In a couple of days he'll be jonesing, and once we can backtrack, we swing by again.

beats.headline: Catching the club from behind
beats.text: On the platform we kill whatever stands in the train's doorways, and nothing on board can reach us. Hekla's party has been doing it all morning; she thinks it's a bug. Carl thinks it is a time trap. So we board, and I use the shape I have been practising: shorter, squat, forearms swollen. When a bonker swings at Carl, I catch the club from behind and add to its swing, and he stumbles into Carl's fist. A spike caught me, but it mostly scraped the metal part of my arm. Mostly.

beats.headline: The Gangway Chock
beats.text: I've built two kinds of defence at the engineering bench. The Gangway Chock was a swordsman's breastplate, thinned to a fifth of an inch and big enough to wedge the gap between cars. The door blocks are weight benches turned into wedges, with crossbars through the handholds, and I made them too slim. At Phantom Kangaroo a pollyslog walks into one, finds it can't board, and goes berserk. The doors on this train do not bounce back. One loses both arms and the other is cut in half. I measure the doorway while there's time.

beats.headline: Vernon’s loop
beats.text: Vernon, the yellow line's dwarf conductor, drinks in the break room because the engineer ignores him and the janitors try to eat him. He talks freely once he notices Donut is royalty. Everyone gets off at 435, he says; then it goes fuzzy, and he's standing at station 10 with the train reset. A drawing of his wife in his pocket stays with him through every reset while the original waits in his cabin, so now there are dozens, and ten gold coins have become hundreds. The one time he's heard of an engineer leaving his car was a derailment. When Donut's suitcase opens on his counter, the ants take him.

beats.headline: Every station, relayed
beats.text: Vernon says the yellow line meets Indigo at 89, where the Daughters were, but they are on the Winter Sky line now. So when Carl and Donut go to the porter car, they leave me with him. He knows every station: its monsters, which ones are transit stations, which lines meet at each. I pass it all to Mordecai, who complains about being our secretary and writes it down. When the ants come, the explosion throws me off my feet. The train is stopped, so my momentum bonus is gone, and my health drops further than Carl expects.

beats.headline: Suitcase number eight
beats.text: The Yellow Line Reward Room is a porter's hatch and shelves of suitcases, one prize per crawler per line. I am suitcase number eight. It is just like Deal or No Deal. Carl's is somebody's lingerie and three potions, one of them invisibility. Mine is full of ants that are on fire. Thousands. The bar goes up, the moonshine explodes, my tail is burning, and poor Vernon is just gone under them. I cast Heal Pet on Mongo and we jump out onto the platform as the doors shut. That was the worst prize ever.

beats.headline: Employees only, says the dwarf
beats.text: For the record: car five of the yellow line train is the conductor's, and the conductor is Vernon, dwarf, level 32, drinking. His duties are to take care of the train and to be in charge of its employees. In practice the engineer does not listen to him, the janitors try to eat him and the porters are in their own little world, so he drinks until the end of the line and then does it again. He asks the crawlers to leave. Then he notices Princess Donut is royalty, salutes, and his drink goes flying.

beats.headline: The loop, as far as he knows it
beats.text: At station 435 everything goes fuzzy, and subject finds himself on the platform at station 10, the yard, climbing aboard again. He cannot say how much time has passed. He is not looping himself, he reasons, because a Brain Amoeba scar stayed with him; the train is, because a bottle poured out returns to its shelf. A Goateo once stayed aboard past 435 and was found as a skeleton. The engine car is locked. Nobody gets in without an engineer's key.

beats.headline: Ten gold, every trip
beats.text: Anything aboard on his first day resets each loop, and anything he carries stays with him. So subject has a jacket full of identical drawings of his wife, and several hundred gold grown from the ten coins on his nightstand: each trip pays him the equivalent of ten trips. He could go home from the yard any time. He is staying until he cannot hold any more gold, before one of the other dwarfs finds out and tries to weasel onto his train, and then he means to go home to his wife. One day.

beats.headline: Fire ants in car five
beats.text: Station 116. Crawler Carl unzips Princess Donut's prize suitcase on subject's counter, and the Find Traps notice arrives too late. Literal Fire Ants, level 1, pour out in impossible numbers, and the drawings of his wife are the first thing to burn. The moonshine explodes. The crawlers get out through car four onto the platform. Subject does not. A flaming wave sweeps over him, and the train picks up speed and disappears into the tunnel, burning.

beats.headline: Imani is looking for you
beats.text: Hey man, you free? I got a message for you. I'm at the Desperado Club, and I just met a guy who's in contact with a woman named Imani. She needs to talk to you. Says it's super important, something about a Brandon and a Chris. She'll try to be at the bar each night after the recap. And be careful, man. I heard a few guys talking about hunting down the leaderboard for the bounty, and I don't think this bar is a saferoom. The trick to finding the club: a transfer station whose number ends in one.

beats.headline: There is no wife
beats.text: Katia's sorry for Vernon, saving up to buy his wife a house. There is no wife, I tell her. He wasn't lying; he believed it. This floor has been open one day. When they generate a floor, the NPCs are given artificial memories as part of the story. Before this he was probably a dwarf doing whatever the fourth floor was the last time they ran it. No home, no wife. And they aren't computer programs. They're living creatures who believe this is the real world. It's just as bad as what they've done to us.

beats.headline: A purple mohawk
beats.text: Donut tells me I need a mohawk and a catchphrase, because Zev thinks I need to be more vibrant. I have almost ten billion followers, and it was almost nothing before I joined them. She has over 700 trillion. Rookie numbers, she says. So while Carl gathers up the robot scrap, I let her dress me: a black bodysuit, knee-high boots I did not shape well, a purple mohawk. Carl says to just be myself. Donut says that is terrible advice for a doppelganger. I don't know what being myself means anyway. I never really did.

beats.headline: Rabbits make everybody sick but him
beats.text: RABBIT hums. Carl falls down. MOTHER is sick. Mongo is not sick. Rabbit is FOOD. Level fourteen. Bigger now.

beats.headline: A control sigil
beats.text: That's a control sigil. Only you can see it, because of your Escape Plan skill. Secondary programs like Vengeance of the Daughter use them, and so do the dungeon's makers sometimes, though it's considered sloppy programming because they're easy to break. They're mostly for controlled gating: stopping a specific type of mob passing. The showrunners turn them on and off, not the AI, which is why they use them. Blue means it's on. It'll have no effect on you. Can crawlers make one? No. There's a similar kind of magic you'll never have the mana for. Donut might.

beats.headline: No wife, says Carl
beats.text: Crawler Katia says what there is to say: poor Vernon, he was saving up money to buy his wife a new house. Princess Donut's complaint is that the bugs burned up her prize. Crawler Carl answers both. There is no wife, he says, and there was no prize; the ants were the prize. He resolves to train his Find Traps skill, which did warn him, but much too late.

beats.headline: Katia needs to be more interesting
beats.text: Carl, Princess Donut, okay, so. I'm still working on your mid-floor appearance, and a lot depends on the sponsorship bidding. I need to bring something up while I can. It's about Katia. People don't like her. Odette complained about her participation in the interview, and the tunnel is full of people hoping she goes so it can be just the two of you again. You either need to ditch her or make her more interesting. A mohawk, maybe. I'm not allowed to message her directly yet. If they don't like her, they stop watching, and fewer views means fewer prizes.

beats.headline: Nine prizes on a carousel
beats.text: The fans vote to let me pick. Two potions with no description, five hundred bombs, two thousand books, a pair of chaps. My father's 1965 Harley, with the dent in the tank from the day I knocked it over, the one time he beat me, bloody, with a belt. My own tool chest from the shop, and I think it's empty. A thick book with the anarchy symbol on the cover glints as the carousel turns. The last time I caught a glint of light, it saved my life. I'm a Compensated Anarchist. I pick prize six.

beats.headline: A dent in the gas tank
beats.text: Prize four on the carousel is a 1965 Harley Davidson FLH Panhead Electra Glide, red and beige, with a small dent in the gas tank. Carl knows the dent. As a boy he slipped coming up the driveway and knocked the bike over. His father was never physically abusive, Carl says, except that day: a belt, hard enough that Carl's underwear soaked through with blood. His mother cried and said they were going back to Texas. They never went. Carl cannot tell whether it is the real motorcycle.

beats.headline: The Prize Carousel
beats.text: Crawlers, welcome to the Prize Carousel! Our contestant's fan box lit up the wheel, and when the wheel lights up, folks, that means me! And a twist before we even start: your guide is in time-out. Seven days, Mordecai, nothing personal, put your feet up. Now, to the prizes! Carl looks them over and picks... a book. A book, folks! Let's hear it for a man who knows exactly what he wants!

beats.headline: The prize for being watched
beats.text: Awarded for gathering a following, or for doing something in front of enough people that the following gathers itself. The contents are put to an audience vote, and the box will not open for thirty hours, so the crawler carries it around knowing that strangers are arguing about what they deserve.

beats.headline: One of a kind
beats.text: A Determine Value potion lets Crawler Carl see rarity, and he filters for Unique. There is exactly one item. Not the nuke, which is merely Pretty Damn Rare. The stuffed Kimaris figure on the horse. The description reads, in full, that it is impossible to accurately portray Kimaris's usual I-hate-this-and-I-hate-you scowl, but this collectible bean bag makes a valiant effort. That is all the System saw fit to say. It is still the most valuable thing he owns.

beats.headline: Earthquake
beats.text: Armadillo is FOOD. Crunchy. Level fifteen. Big now, big as a pony. New trick: jump, land, EARTHQUAKE. Bad things fall down. MOTHER says good boy.

beats.headline: Special Brew and potion balls
beats.text: Get back. You'll contaminate it. I put Donut's two table upgrades into the alchemy table, so it's level three. Two of my Special Brew: thirty seconds of healing and regeneration, near enough immortality, but not against decapitation or blowing yourself up. It adds about ten hours to your potion sickness, and two is the lifetime limit; I've never got past that. Two Superb Constitution potions for the cat. And fragmenting potion balls: pour a potion in, throw it at a bad guy. Potions work on mobs. It doesn't make sense. It's always been that way.

beats.headline: Naughty, for seven days
beats.text: The Prize Carousel materialises in the personal space, and its host is Chaco the Bard. Guide Mordecai throws a metal chair at him with his tongue. The chair stops a quarter of an inch from the host's head. Naughty. Mordecai blinks out, and the room marked Manager goes with him. Time out: seven days, for violating the rules, which returns him with a day and a half left on the floor. Chaco says it was a long time ago, that he was doing what Mordecai's manager told him, and asks that Mordecai be told he is sorry.

beats.headline: A saddle from the fans
beats.text: Mordecai's constitution potions give me one point, which is a waste, and then three. Then my Platinum fan box opens and our fans have given me a saddle! The Enchanted Mongoliensis Saddle, adjusted to fit a cat, matching his feathers. Fifteen percent more spell damage for me, twenty percent more constitution for Mongo. Thank you everybody, I love you all so much! Carl puts it on him, and it clicks into place, and Mongo howls and bounces around the room trying to get it off. Carl says to wait until he is used to it. Oh, all right.

beats.headline: Hired at the bar
beats.text: Transaction logged at the Desperado Club. Clients: Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut. Hired: Bomo, mercenary, and the Sledge, mercenary, sold as a set. Also present at the bar, at no charge: Elle and Imani. The cat orders a dirty Shirley, in a bowl, with extra cherries, and gets it, because the Desperado knows who tips. Bomo's transcript is short. That is a feature, crawler. The talking ones cost more.

beats.headline: The race he made her pick
beats.text: Elle, a Frost Maiden now and floating at the Desperado Club bar, supplies a footnote. She had a long list of races that would have put all her marbles back in the bag. Brandon made her pick the Frost Maiden, a tricky race, because it carries the manager benefit, which Crawler Carl had told him about. Her game guide cried when she chose it. Elle's summary: Brandon was a good kid. Imani's: he died, along with Henry, protecting their escape.

beats.headline: The twenty-fifth holder of the Cookbook
beats.text: Twenty-four crawlers carried this before me. Different seasons, different species, worlds that aren't there any more. Whatever I do from here, I'm finishing somebody else's work, and most of them never got to finish theirs.

beats.headline: The explosives chapter first
beats.text: The book is sorted into chapters: potions in one, explosives in another, and a list of monsters and what they are weak to. Some of the people who wrote in it filled pages. Some managed a line. I go to the explosives first, obviously, and the first note that catches my eye is about infusing bombs at a sapper’s table.

beats.headline: A dirty trick, well executed
beats.text: Most viewers never see Mordecai; managers are edited out of the feed. People with press passes, like Odette, can. So somebody made the connection between him and Chaco and floated the idea of trolling the vote. I look up into the air and tell whoever's watching: that was a dick move, but brilliantly executed. Good job. Then I get over it. Most crawlers don't have a manager at all. Bautista and the Cookbook have shown me what crowdsourcing is worth, and bounty or not, I need to add as many people to my chat as I can.

beats.headline: Igneous, and changed
beats.text: For the record, by Imani's account: Chris picked a rock race called an igneous. Lava rock, covered in little holes. He got very strong, and it changed his personality. After a couple of days he and Brandon were fighting constantly. Chris wanted to hunt and kill every minute of every day and go find Crawler Carl, whom he respected as aggressive; Brandon wanted to train close to the stairwell. Several men left with Chris. Of those who broke away, only he is alive, and he answers nobody.

beats.headline: Scores to settle
beats.text: Subject, on the door, is told why Crawler Carl arrives without his manager. Her assessment: that'll do it, and he only gets one warning. The manager has spent many hours in this club crying into his cup and has named a list of scores he means to settle once he is out, and the Chaco idiot has come up more than once. She also sells the pair private security, 500 gold for two, because both are on the bounty list. Crawler Donut tries for a better price. Her charm does not work on the subject.

beats.headline: Elle's rock
beats.text: Subject is a rock monster of the same stamp as the club’s cretins, posted behind Crawler Elle McGibbons on the dance floor with his arms folded. His entire recorded conversation is “No closer.” She moves him aside by hand when she wants to.

beats.headline: Hiring, and a dirty Shirley
beats.text: They take on Bomo and the Sledge there and meet Elle and Imani. It stops being a bar the moment it becomes a labour market.

beats.headline: Introduced in the Iron Tangle
beats.text: Carl picks it off Chaco's prize carousel as a joke book of chicken and goblin recipes, and it is not new: this is the twenty-fourth edition, first generated in the fifteenth season, and it has been passed from crawl to crawl, each owner adding a page for the next.

beats.headline: Frost Maiden, for now
beats.text: I'm a Frost Maiden. For now. Blue, small, and I float, and yes, those are still the anti-slip socks. I had a long list of options that would've put all my marbles back in the bag, but Brandon made me pick this one, for the manager benefit Carl told him about. Mistress Tiatha actually cried. I got my club tattoo for an icicle up the keister of an orc bartender. There's twenty of us left, and Imani still acts like the babysitter. And Carl is buying this round.

beats.headline: A comment in the margin
beats.text: For the record: the first trace of this crawler is a comment under someone else's note. Crawler Sinjin, fifteenth edition, advises soaking a hobgoblin smoke curtain in a healing potion and letting it dry, to mass-kill undead. Crawler Forkith, twentieth edition, confirms it: works with bombs too, but smoke works better, and high-level undead only get mad. He used them to clear rooms of invisible Swamp Wights. Crawler Carl slams the Cookbook shut, knowing that if he keeps reading, he never stops.

beats.headline: What happened with Chris
beats.text: Obsidian Butterfly, Fire Spiritualist, level twenty-four. The wings aren't physical; on the sixth floor I choose whether they fly. I came here to tell Carl about Chris. He picked a rock race, an igneous, got very strong, and it changed him. He wanted to spend every minute hunting and go find Carl and Donut. Brandon wanted to train near the stairwell. They fought, and several of the men left with Chris. Henry and Brandon died protecting our escape. Chris is the only one of those who left still alive. He won't answer us. He is looking for you, Carl.

beats.headline: Banned for life
beats.text: On the recap I make a necklace out of monster tongues. I am in a saferoom eating a bowl of rice, and one of my dogs sneaks up and takes it off my neck. The club at the stations will not let me in. Banned for life. I have tried a few times now. They are ready for me.

beats.headline: A skull on the dance floor
beats.text: Crawler Princess Donut is on the Desperado Club dance floor with the Sledge, plastered on two or three cherries, while Carl talks at the bar. He looks away for a second. When he looks back, both her bodyguards are on their backs, her health is in the deep red, and her Cockroach skill has fired, sparing her the first killing blow. The front of her is covered in blood. A human crawler lies in front of her with his throat slashed. He goes still. A single skull forms after her name.

beats.headline: Bought at the bar
beats.text: Two crawlers come up to the counter and buy security. Me and Bomo, sold as the pair. That is the arrangement in this place. You pay, and we stand between you and whatever comes through the door. The cat is not what I expect. She orders a dirty Shirley in a bowl with extra cherries, drinks the whole thing, and then she wants dancing, so I do my version of the robot while she bops and twirls on my shoulders. Princess Donut. I let her.

beats.headline: The management apologises
beats.text: Astrid. Bloodlust Sprite, level 125, Cardiovascular Mage, assistant manager of the Desperado Club. The Bloodlust Sprite is one of the rarest and deadliest things her kind produces, born holding magic over anything with a circulatory system, and the signature trick is a heart beating fast enough to catch fire. She is the size of your hand, she wears a tuxedo, her hair is up in a bun, and her voice is deeper than yours. A crawler makes an attempt on Princess Donut on club grounds and Astrid comes down to say sorry in person. The Royal Court walks out with permanent complimentary security. Establishments like this one do not hand out refunds. She handed one out.

beats.headline: One spin of the wheel
beats.text: The comp chip I've been carrying is a hundred thousand, the maximum bet, and every bet over the minimum takes a red spot off Tito's wheel. With the chip, two are left: Nothing! and getting stabbed in the stomach by the croupier. I bet it anyway. The wheel stops on Spin Again, right beside the half-million sliver, and on the second spin it hangs one click from Nothing! and settles on green. Scroll of Upgrade. My toe ring goes from plus three strength to plus ten and adds five to Powerful Strike. Tito asks if I want another go. Yeah, no.

beats.headline: You come for Donut, you come for us
beats.text: A woman in the crowd is about to blast Carl and the cat, so she gets a two-foot icicle through the eye socket from behind. There's a skull after my name now. Don't care. I call dibs on her gear and tell Donut to loot hers before we get thrown out. Then I tell the room: anybody comes for Donut or Carl comes for all of us, and I will freeze the blood in their veins. A dwarf gives me the eyeball. He backs up. Donut, don't you cry. This was inevitable, and once word gets out, nobody will mess with you again.

beats.headline: Primes, and the stations nobody has seen
beats.text: We trace our position on Carl's map and pick a stop where we can meet. Elle points out that every transfer station is a prime number; Mordecai had written the word in the corner and circled it. That is a pattern, not an answer. We don't have enough information. We need to know what happens at the stations every five stops, where the mobs all get off, and more importantly what happens at the end of the line. So my team takes one of the fifth platforms, and Carl and Donut go after an engineer.

beats.headline: Her first skull
beats.text: I never wanted to get a skull. The lady cast a spell, and my guy and the other rock guy fell, and I fell too, because Sledgie was stunned, and the other one had a knife. Now he is on the floor. Ji-Hoon, a Knife Sharpener. And there is a skull after my name. Nobody is going to like me now. Carl says they attacked me, and nobody will be mad, and he is positive. I didn't want to kill anybody. Maybe those stupid dogs. But not a person. Not a real person.

beats.headline: A miss on his own shift
beats.text: A crawler goes for the Princess on my floor, on my shift, and I do not get there in time. Elle puts the second one down. Astrid comes to apologise in person, and I stand where I am and wait to hear what a miss like that costs a body like me. Carl does not ask for blood. He asks for me and Bomo, permanent and complimentary, the Royal Court's own security every time they walk in. So now I have a court.

beats.headline: Which rail is hot
beats.text: I have no multimeter, so I make one: a curved rod wired to a hob-lobber fuse, thrown across the rails one pairing at a time. The fuse only blows when it touches the third rail and something else, which is how it should be. Donut's clockwork Mongo confirms it by exploding. I spray a big X on the side of the next train so Meadow Lark and Bautista's crew know it's the last one down the line for a while. Then I lower two Jelly Bombs onto the track with a fishing pole: a plunger idea from the cookbook, changed just enough to look like mine.

beats.headline: Hekla at sixty-five percent
beats.text: I'm on the couch wearing Hekla when they come back, and it holds until Carl reads the name over my head. The ability is called Walk in Their Shoes, and it only switches on at a ninety percent match. This Hekla is sixty-five. I spent both upgrade coupons on the Makeup Table: at level three I can put any face I've met on the glass, and save three designs. Carl tries hard not to sound horrified. Then they pile the dead assassin's armor at my feet, and I see the skull over Donut's head.

beats.headline: One at every fifth station
beats.text: Elle passes the word along: at one of the every-fifth stations her team fought three neighbourhood bosses and left the borough boss alone. A miss Krakaren, Imani calls her, an old friend. A borough boss is a size up from the one in the distillery, and there is no reason to think she is the only one. The dungeon does not run short of them, because running short is not a thing this creature can do. Take one apart and the original makes two.

beats.headline: The saddle
beats.text: MOTHER on back. Strap holds MOTHER. BAD. Mongo bucks. MOTHER flies. MOTHER lands on the potion table. Carl laughs. Katia laughs. MOTHER says BAD MONGO. Mongo rolls over. Off, saddle. OFF.

beats.headline: But a trifle
beats.text: Katia sees the skull and wants to know what happened. Oh, it was but a trifle. A poor crawler thought he could keep up with me, and I accidentally had to rip his throat out. Honestly, I barely remember the incident. I did have a cherry or two too many. Now if you'll excuse me, I have training to do. By the end of the hour my Dodge is seven, which means I get into that locked door at the club. Then Mongo and I work on riding. We have a psychic bond. Carl has never been a mother, so he wouldn't understand.

beats.headline: What the engineer says about the gate
beats.text: The derailment works: level twenty-nine, and the engineer climbs out of his tipped-over car. Gore-Gore thinks we were passengers, so he answers. Stop 434 is barren. At 435 the other employees take a portal back to the depot, and it does something to their memory. He drives his engine car into a gate past 435 and comes out at the depot; the other nineteen cars are gone. Passengers who ride through get deep-cleaned. Sometimes there are bones. The engine car isn't cleaned. Nobody rides in it but engineers, and he'd be honor-bound to slay us.

beats.headline: Ten and a half percent
beats.text: Gore-Gore goes into the church-like club by the station for mead and comes out calling us saboteurs, blades out of his wrists. Magic missiles bounce off him. Every punch I land adds one and a half to the chance my gauntlet calls his god, and nobody said it stacks. I'm at ten and a half when he gets me by the throat. Protective Shell throws him down the stairs, and since he's still holding on, it throws me too. Then he says he feels it in his chest, and there's a timer over his head. I drop-kick him onto the third rail.

beats.headline: Out of the tipped engine
beats.text: For the record: the derailment works. The engine car of the ochre line train lies on its side, and out of it climbs Gore-Gore, level 40, a ManTauR: about eight feet of man with a second, smaller man where the neck should be, four arms in all, streaked in blue paint. He hails the brother, the sister and the fine Princess, takes them for passengers who survived the wreck, and gallops off onto the platform shouting about sustenance and mead.

beats.headline: What happens at 435
beats.text: Charmed by Princess Donut, subject talks. Passengers should get off at 433, the last transit station. At 435 the employees disembark into a tunnel back to base, the Kravyad prepare them for the portal, and the portal does something to memory that human resources is said to be looking into. Nobody rides the first car except engineers; anyone else in it, he would be honour-bound to slay. Blades come out of his wrists to make the point. Then he goes into Club Vanquisher for mead.

beats.headline: Hail and kill
beats.text: Subject comes back out of Club Vanquisher calling the crawlers saboteurs, a ram-headed cleric waving from the door behind him, and the system stages it as VERSUS: neighborhood boss, train engineer, adherent of Grull the war god, berserker extreme, level 40. He swats Mongo to low health with the flat of his blades. When Crawler Katia steps in front of a blow meant for Crawler Carl, part of her arm spins away. Crawler Carl assumes it is only armour.

beats.headline: Grounded on the third rail
beats.text: Every punch from Crawler Carl's gauntlet carries a chance of summoning Grull, and the odds have climbed to 10.5. Subject, down to about a fifth of his health beneath two wrecked cars, announces that he feels it in his chest: he has been blessed by the gods. A ten-second timer appears over his head. Crawler Carl drop-kicks him in the lower chest. He goes back across the tracks and into the third rail, and the next thing on the screen is Winner!

beats.headline: A summoning barely avoided
beats.text: Gore-Gore, engineer, gives the party two routes back to the stairwell stations and then attacks them, which is the sequence I have come to expect from railway staff. In the middle of it he tries to bring in Grull. It does not land. Understand what almost happened there: a mob with a grudge and a prayer nearly put a war god into a train carriage with four crawlers. Horses pray to Grull. Centaurs pray to Grull. There are a great many horses on this floor.

beats.headline: Jump ahead on the fast trains
beats.text: The engineer's key will only open engines on the ochre line, and crashing a train to get one stops the trains. So, Carl, doesn't it only stop the trains behind it? We get the key, jump on the Nightmare Express or one of those other super-fast loop trains, go ahead up the line, and catch one of the trains that were already in front. Carl says that's brilliant and scratches my head.

beats.headline: Surprise Three
beats.text: The Dismemberment Limited has one pair of doors, by the driver, and Levi the Seventh begs us not to get on. Then the quest: don't let the Fleshers eat him, or every crawler aboard becomes one. Katia and I brace a slab of metal against the back door while Donut and Mongo rip at the flaps of skin curling round its edges. Dismember the war mage leans on the other side, explaining what he'll do to us. On three, Donut opens a Hole in the plate, I pull his head through by his silver hair, and she closes it.

beats.headline: What he leaves behind
beats.text: Looted from the corpse, which a clockwork Mongo has dragged clear of the live rail: 498 gold, a bottle of Rev-Up Magic Hair Restoration, the Ochre Line Engineer's Key, and a neighborhood map of the whole ochre line, stations 11 to 435, every train on it. Also left behind, at the top of the stairs: four of Crawler Katia's fingers, taken when she blocked his blade. When she healed, they did not come back. She can build more from other parts of herself.

beats.headline: What the Pooka hand out
beats.text: Carl, we should stop derailing trains until there's a solid plan to get out. If other crawlers are behind you on the line, you may trap them. At the stops ending in five or zero, the mobs line up by race at doors with slots. Behind each door a Pooka hands out one vial of a race-specific sedative, and they take it back through a one-way portal. The description says if they miss their fix, they change physically. The Krakaren makes the drugs. I wasn't confident we could face her, so I had the team back off. Pookas turn into giant goats when attacked.

beats.headline: Fingers that do not come back
beats.text: Gore-Gore chopped my fingers off when I was protecting Carl. Carl thought it was only armor. When I healed, my fingers didn't come back. It's stupid. I can build fingers from other parts of me. I'm like clay; all I lost was a bit of flesh, and I moved the ring from the severed finger onto the new ones. But part of me is gone. I'm losing myself. Carl taps my forehead and tells me the real Katia is still in there, and not to let them break me. I say okay.

beats.headline: Reading the Tangle
beats.text: My sponsor is a princess too, it says. Princess Formidable of the Skull Empire. I haven't received anything from her. Over the soup I fill Mordecai's map in with the ochre line and what the daughters have sent, and I find us a route: change lines, take the Dismemberment Limited, change for the Nightmare Express two stations down on the Mauve line, and ride it to 436, one past the end. Hours instead of days. Carl doesn't understand a word but believes me. Try the Tokyo subway knowing only Icelandic, German, Russian and English.

beats.headline: Princess D'nadia, and the Donut Holes
beats.text: Carl, Carl, I hit level twenty-eight and I got a sponsor, and it's Princess D'nadia of the Prism Kingdom! I love her. Carl doesn't even remember who she is, so I make him apologise, because she is probably watching right now. He sat right next to her on Ripper Wonton's show. People watching our feed will see our sponsors' commercials, and I hope she has lots of different ones. My fans should have a name. The Princess Patrol, or something. Carl suggests the Donut Holes. Don't be crude, Carl.

beats.headline: A princess on the notice
beats.text: For the record: Crawler Katia has a sponsor, and the notice reads, in full, Princess Formidable of the Skull Empire. That is all it reads. Over pho, Crawler Carl works the rest out from something Zev told him: if Prince Stalwart was disowned for his failed attempt on Carl, the sister would be next in line. He assumes this is the sister. Crawler Hekla, it is noted in the same conversation, has drawn some interstellar ranch.

beats.headline: A sponsor Borant cannot refuse
beats.text: The Admin notice arrives while Carl is still picking himself up beside the track: he has been sponsored, and viewers of his feed will now see his sponsor's advertisements. The sponsor is the Valtay Corporation. He answers Donut's question out loud with the name, then switches to chat: not a word about them out loud. Borant hates them; they are the ones trying to invade the Borant system, and they are the reason the show started when it did. Borant probably had no choice. It could mean good loot. It could mean Borant tries harder to get him killed.

beats.headline: Dismember, on the trains
beats.text: Aboard the Dismemberment Limited, Donut's Hole spell takes the head off a war mage called Dismember. Levi, the symbiote cowering in the car with them, can only say that war mages are war mages.

beats.headline: Neural Enhancer #544
beats.text: After the recap a Bronze Benefactor Box arrives from the Valtay Corporation, stamped Keeping the Best of You Alive. Inside is a blue and yellow capsule: a permanent change to my brain that installs Identify and Analyze Subspace Portals. I put it in my inventory first, to make sure nothing's living in it, then swallow it with cold coffee. A new tab, Third-Party Upgrades. The doorway out to the coffee shop glows purple, and when I ask for a visual it shows me Nodd the bopca behind the counter, picking his nose. I can see through doorways now.

beats.headline: Forkith, for Barkith
beats.text: The bomb-making chapter keeps a thread of notes on madness satchels. Rosetta, ninth edition, found that an equipped backpack stopped them destabilising. Allister, thirteenth, notes the inventory delay she was working around is gone, though backpacks still hold. Forkith, twentieth edition, writes that they only slow it now; he found that out the hard way, and he asks whoever reads it to kill an enemy today in honor of his sister, Barkith, who was all he had left. What Carl takes from all of it is that backpacks are a thing.

beats.headline: Rest well, little sister
beats.text: Under a note on keeping explosives stable in an equipped backpack, Forkith adds that backpacks now only slow destabilisation, and that he found this out the hard way. Rest well, little sister, he writes. Her name was Barkith, and she was all he had left; he asks those who read it to kill an enemy in her honour today. Crawler Carl pieces together the rest. Forkith wrote the twentieth edition and reached at least the eleventh floor. He was an Urgyle, a small, winged, demon-like race, kept it at selection, and was a Sapper.

beats.headline: A ton and a quarter
beats.text: The system calls it the Ugly Ass Backpack With a Completely Useless Design that Only an Idiot Would Wear. Carl loads it with metal poles and balls while it sits on a stand, I make myself into a shelf on legs, and when the stand falls away the pack equips and becomes me. A ton and a quarter, give or take. I tip over like a turtle, then reshape: eleven feet tall, with a strength bonus for carrying the mass. When the daughters hear about this, they're going to flip out. If only Fannar could see me.

beats.headline: A room with five stairwells
beats.text: I find the room. It is big. There are five stairwells in it, in a circle. Then the zombie things come. I fight them. They keep coming. They keep coming. I fall back.

beats.headline: Lightning down a tunnel
beats.text: Recap, a crawler I do not usually feature: Crawler Quan Ch, flying down a train tunnel on ethereal wings, blue lightning from his left hand. The front of a train crumples and stops dead on the track, and its driver falls out of what used to be the cockpit. By the evening he has taken Li Jun's place on the leaderboard: level thirty-one, half-elf, Imperial Security Trooper. Crawler Donut calls him a cheating poser and maintains that the jacket was theirs.

beats.headline: A note in the bomb-making chapter
beats.text: My note is in the Cookbook, in the chapter on bombs. That is the whole of what anyone here knows about me, and for a long while it was the whole of what I wanted them to know. You do not put your name on a thing like that expecting to be asked about it afterwards.

beats.headline: Planet Beautiful
beats.text: Hi guys! The fans liked your line at the end, Carl. People want the trademark line more often, though not too much, or it gets weird. Okay, so, I booked you two for a show in two days. Katia stays in the dungeon; Mongo goes in the cage. It's called Planet Beautiful: narration from a sound booth, a segment about this season's planet. Carl asks what the segment is and tells me I'm a terrible liar. Okay. It's about beauty pageants. And pet shows. Princess Donut says yes before he can.

beats.headline: Fist bumps all round
beats.text: I get the dance floor's attention and ask every crawler in the club for their chat details. We should all make a habit of it, so information can move: there are probably lots of ways off this floor, and everybody needs to know them. There are about twenty of them, most around level twenty. Bomo looks close to a heart attack, but I fist-bump the whole room, add twenty-two names, and make Donut do the same. Now a guy named Koki has found a way to message everyone on his list at once, and my inbox is a mess.

beats.headline: Stealing the Nightmare Express
beats.text: The plan: Donut Puddle Jumps us up the track, I hit Protective Shell as the train reaches us, and the shell clears every car. Donut's jump won't land as close to the platform as we wanted, and the train speeds up instead of slowing. I jump. I don't make it. Two potions on, I'm lying above the cowcatcher. I punch through the cab window: two bodies in the gore, and the boiler about to go. A demon woman in the firebox talks me through the valves. Level thirty-two, three boss boxes, and I have stolen a train.

beats.headline: Stoking the Nightmare Express
beats.text: Subject is a Lesser Demon and a non-combatant, level seventy-five, and she shovels for the Nightmare Express. Where one finds large ovens that want feeding, one regularly finds her sort, and the tangle has more large ovens than it has anything else. She is on the crew that the crawlers need and does not pretend otherwise.

beats.headline: You are making her change
beats.text: We are in the dark tunnel waiting for the train, and Carl says Katia is a big girl who can take care of herself. Then why does he keep telling her what to do? He didn't even ask her if she wanted to get giant. He just shoved the backpack at her. He says look who's talking, me with the boots and the purple mohawk. That's different. Fashion is different from making someone change. He says I'm right, and next time he'll ask her. Good boy, Carl.

beats.headline: The train drives into it
beats.text: The plan for the Nightmare Express: stand on the track in the tunnel, cast the shell as the train arrives, and let Crawler Donut's Puddle Jumper take them a quarter of a mile down the line. They cut it close. The train roars through the spell, and every red-tagged monster aboard slams into its wall and is pushed backward. The train then speeds up, and they have to run for the platform.

beats.headline: Bricks in the cab
beats.text: The box at the back of the Nightmare Express's cab holds about fifty Sheol Bricks. The item description promises not to say where they come from, then admits it: it is a baby corpse. The stoker's own description has the arithmetic. A Lesser Demon's labour runs about sixty days and delivers fifteen to eighteen thousand young, one in ten thousand viable; the rest harden into fuel that burns long and hot. Carl drops the first brick and wipes his hand on his cloak. Then he takes the whole box into his inventory.

beats.headline: A spell bought with my own money
beats.text: The Princess rides on my shoulder through the club now. As we cross the dance floor I cast a protection spell on the party, and everyone glows blue. I bought it with my own money. Bomo tells Carl so, which is the longest sentence anyone has heard from Bomo. The Princess says thank you, Sledgie, and pats my head. The Dodge room will not let Carl in. It lets me in with her. Carl waits at the bar.

beats.headline: The pit at 436
beats.text: Abyss Station has one steep stair, and it takes almost an hour to climb. At the top is a burning pit at least a mile across, its walls covered in portals. For a moment I'm at the Grand Canyon with my mom, her hand tight on my wrist. Then a train bursts out of a portal and falls, and there's no engine car. So the colored trains don't loop back in time: the cars get thrown in here, the engines go home, and they build new trains. The portal analysis says three things I'm carrying count as keys. One of them is that stupid conductor hat.

beats.headline: You can't save them all
beats.text: I send what we know to everybody on my list: four ways back to the early stations, two sure and two maybe. The replies all tell the same story. Trains out of service at an alarming rate, people stranded, dozens of miles to hike, almost six days left. Mordecai's voice in my head: you can't save them all. York's last entry in the back of the cookbook won't leave me: the hive, protecting those who are yours even if you never knew them, and the consolation of dying for a cause worth it. I'm not sure I agree with that last part. I fall asleep thinking there's something more to be done.

beats.headline: Stuck at 275
beats.text: We clear stop 275 on the Camel Line and kill one of those Krakaren bitches. Easier than Imani thought. Then the train to 277 never comes. Imani blames that Quan Ch fellow for blowing up trains. It's twenty or thirty miles to the next stop and another thirty after that, so instead we take the druggie portal back to 272 and hike down to 271. If the Cobalt line is out too, there's a named train there called the Eviscerator. We're out of commission for a day, at least. I tell Carl. He tells me to stay away from the third rail. Oh, you know it.

beats.headline: Swarming the wreckage
beats.text: At the bottom of the pit above Abyss Station lie thousands of crashed train cars and hundreds of fires, and the janitor ghouls are down there, swarming the debris like ants. Train after train bursts from the portals in the walls and tumbles in on top of them. None of them has an engine car.

beats.headline: Down the tracks
beats.text: MOTHER on back. Down the dark tracks. Mongo RUN. Really, really fast. Dead things on tracks. MOTHER finds map. MOTHER finds gold. MOTHER says Mongo FAST.

beats.headline: The Princess Donut goggles
beats.text: My first benefactor box is the greatest prize in the history of prizes. Princess D'nadia had it made especially for me: Prism Industries Capacitating and Focusing Goggles, a unique item, personally signed. They turn my Magic Missile into a laser, and I can shoot four at the same time, into four train doors at once. Plus they're beautiful. I look like Miss Beatrice. Also I went up two levels to thirty, my charisma hit a hundred, and I picked Love Vampire, which Mordecai told me to get.

beats.headline: The switch nobody is meant to take
beats.text: The named trains run their loops until they reach a set of three switches, and only one of them leads here. Getting to it means reading the network, or else noticing that the souvenir conductor hat handed out at the start of the floor is one of the keys, which is the sort of joke the fourth floor keeps making.

beats.headline: The last entry in the back
beats.text: Crawler Carl cannot sleep, and a passage from the back of the Cookbook keeps coming back to him. It was written by a crawler named York, author of the tenth edition, who wrote pages and pages of rambling philosophical essays Carl can barely follow. This one appears to be his last entry. I have been surrounded by my hive, yet I have been alone, it says. The Cookbook, York writes, is an attempt to make a hive of those who never cross paths, except in these pages. And there is consolation in dying in the pursuit of justice, however small.

beats.headline: A way out of the robot rooms
beats.text: Hey, hotshot. Your instincts were right. There's a secret way out of the robot rooms: a long tunnel sloping downward. It doesn't open until the robots wake up, and they don't wake until the monsters start their withdrawal. Lucky us, we don't have to fight the metal bastards. I still can't believe you blew two of them up. We're following the tunnel now. Sounds like there's another train track down there. It's far. More when we know.

beats.headline: Two little ones
beats.text: At the switching station the stoker puts her head out of the firebox and chats. Crawler Donut says she is a mother too; her boy is named Mongo. A good name, Brandy says. She has two children so far, and her kind do not name their young until they are presented at the altar. Crawler Katia says she was about to adopt when aliens destroyed her planet. That's too bad, honey, says Brandy, and sounds as if she means it. Another child is born mid-conversation. Her one request of Carl: try not to blow up the train.

beats.headline: Traveling spikes
beats.text: Babababoons in the transit station, second stage of the DTs, crawling all over the Nightmare. I have one in a bear hug and he's hitting me really hard. Then my body jerks to the side and takes his top half with it. I think I've figured out how to move the metal around inside me. It's slow, but it hurt him more than it hurt me. I think I can make traveling spikes, so anything using its hands impales itself on me. When I do it really fast, it feels like breaking my own bones.

beats.headline: Minion Army, read already
beats.text: Remember the tome of Minion Army from the Beguiler Box on the first floor? It costs fifty spell points. With our rest and shower buffs I have fifty-two, so I looked. And of course I read it, Carl. Mordecai isn't here, so we're talking about it now. Five minutes to cast, stuck in place the whole time, and at level one each mob has a two percent chance to change sides. Carl says don't cast it unless he tells me to. Don't be so pessimistic, Carl.

beats.headline: Banger Spheres
beats.text: The close fighting on the trains has kept it mostly idle this floor. On the platform at 283, Carl loads a Banger Sphere, one of a few hundred baseball-sized balls of dwarven robot scrap he made at the engineering table; the system names only that size. The first catches a babababoon in the neck when he was aiming between the eyes. It dies anyway. He throws two more at the two mobs on the other side of the platform, and they die too.

beats.headline: Widget, briefly
beats.text: Station and Repair Hub E: a yard of engine cars, a shaking fence, and thousands of ghouls. A grease gremlin named Widget rides a basket down a chain from his tower, takes one look at us and asks what happened to CrackJack. I tell him. He doesn't mind much, as long as Brandy is fine. He says a train called the Escape Velocity goes to all the stairwells; you catch it at 89, up the Tangerine line. He unhooks our wrecked cars and waves, and the spider ghoul Donut shot gets back up and takes his head off.

beats.headline: Six mimics at Terminus
beats.text: Madison, from human resources, can't tell me how to get to Yard A, or whether she's ever been to her own apartment. Mandatory overtime, she says. The back of the cookbook has an essay on this: challenge an NPC when they don't know what they should, kind but firm. So I push, and she tells me what she does know. She tells employees overtime is mandatory, and she's benefits manager for the six Station Mimics at Terminus, which get cranky if not enough passengers go into them. Bautista is nearly at 433. I message him: don't get off at Terminus. It's a trap.

beats.headline: Out of the burning substation
beats.text: Subject is a level ten human and a non-combatant, filed as a Human Resources Associate for the line. She comes running out of the burning substation at Trainyard E in one heel with a ghoul at her hair, rides the Nightmare Express as far as station sixty, where the employees are supposed to live, finds nothing there, and sits down to wait for Rod. Her name was probably something like Jennifer or Ruth before she had it changed, around the time of the divorce.

beats.headline: The tower controls
beats.text: I'll go up the chain. Carl is the only one who can drive, and Mongo would be ready to graduate college by the time he got up there. From Widget's tower I can see really far. It smells awful. How many lotion containers does one gremlin need? There are multiple control panels and nothing is labeled. Whoops, that one tipped over a freight car. Then the turntable, one slot over, and it lines up. I opened the gate already, by accident, and more ghouls walked out. I didn't tell Carl straight away, because he might get mad.

beats.headline: A yard given up to ghouls
beats.text: Station and Repair Hub E is not coping. The DTs have been turning mobs into Festering Ghouls born knowing how to get here, and thousands have arrived, pushing the fence back and forth. According to Widget, someone cheaped out combining two systems: the ghouls were meant to be caged and conveyed onward, the cages broke, and too many came at once. The staff are about to abandon the yard for Yard A. Then a section of the great wall collapses, and the ghouls surge out of the enclosure toward the conductor staging area beyond it.

beats.headline: A memory with nothing under it
beats.text: Crawler Carl reopens the file while questioning Madison, an employee who has been putting in a lot of mandatory overtime. When Vernon told him about his wife, Carl had taken her for a made-up phantom. Now he has a theory to put under it: this floor's NPCs were given false memories without a proper foundation, stories as paper-thin as the background of an NPC in an actual game. Asked whether she has ever been to her own apartment, Madison says of course she has. It has just been a few days.

beats.headline: My name on the back
beats.text: Katia gets me alone at station 24 and hands me a black ticket with a gold skull on it. A PVP coupon: kill the crawler named on the back and collect three gold boxes, a platinum box and a player level. The back says Crawler #4,122. Carl. She watched Donut stuff it under the track.
