Once the ninth floor opens the factions can't buy new gear at all. I'll explain that when you get there.

beats.headline: We'll be there, Carl
beats.text: Carl asks nicely, and Louis asks whether he's going to blow them up. So I jump onto their table, which scatters their glasses and spills vodka everywhere, and I explain. Carl won't hurt them. But anyone who isn't part of the team will be kicked out of town, and I haven't seen a mob out there lower than level thirty, and these two chuckleheads are level twenty-two. Then I tell them exactly what to say. We'll be there, Carl. Louis says it. Lovely. Chuckleheads is from the AI, not Elle. I've been waiting to use it.

beats.headline: Allister's deck of cards
beats.text: The Cookbook manifests differently for each owner. For Allister, author of the thirteenth edition, it came as a massive deck of playing cards from his home planet, for a game called T'Ghee. From the little he wrote about it, a mix of chess and go fish; also part of his people's meditation-based religion, which made it easy for him to spend hours studying the cards.

beats.headline: Somebody has to put her down
beats.text: The recap shows how Ifechi died: Lucia Mar put a spell on her head, Mordecai thinks, so Florin's own shotgun killed her, and the dungeon gave him the kill. The kid talks to people who aren't there. She's insane. Katia says she needs to be dealt with. I say we need to put her down. Donut calls dibs on the dogs. Mordecai says her spell has a big vulnerability, and that they may want her killed. Then the board goes up, and I'm number two.

beats.headline: Ife, and the warehouse
beats.text: Lucia blocked the stairs and set the dogs on me, and I fired. At her, at both dogs, again and again. None of it hurt them. Ife was against the wall with her head gone. She'd cast her protection on me and on a stranger and kept none for herself. The dungeon gave me the kill; there's a gold skull over my head for it. In the warehouse I sat down in the corner with her leech staff across my lap. I didn't spin anything. I leaned my head on the wall and went to sleep.

beats.headline: Florin's own bullets, turned around
beats.text: Crawler Ifechi is dead. The recap of the previous floor carried it in full: Florin put shell after shell into Lucia Mar, and none of it landed on her. It landed on Ifechi, leaning against the wall, who had spent her protection spells on Florin and on a stranger and kept none for herself. A Red Cross medic, top ten, and by the reunion the recap chose to show, a good deal more than Florin's friend. It ran the whole thing, which is a detail I did not write into the format and cannot take out of it.

beats.headline: Knowing it without knowing it
beats.text: Carl and I build the Chariot side by side at the engineering table, and every time I wonder how a track mechanism goes together, the answer is simply there. That is the earth hobby potion. I know how engines work, but I don't know it, know it; it is as if it is downloaded on demand. If people out there can buy expertise like this, how is there so much cruelty? Carl thinks it must be expensive, like plastic surgery. I still can't stop thinking about it. He suggests calling me Katia Prime. I do not find it as amusing as he does.

beats.headline: I told him I would
beats.text: The station is almost empty and there is a line at the stairs. This is mine. The crocodile man says crazy bitch where he thinks I can't hear. I throw a boy at him. He says I'm not right in the head. There is nothing wrong with my head. I tell him if he talks again there will be something wrong with his girlfriend's head. He talks again. Cici and Gustavo go for him and he shoots all three of us. We don't get hurt. She does. I told him I'd do it. He shoots me again, and I slide across the ice and down the stairs.

beats.headline: Safe only with a crawler inside
beats.text: Kid, a saferoom protects whoever's in it, but a Borant-owned NPC alone in one isn't protected. If there are no crawlers or off-world NPCs in the room, the room's probably gone with the rest. The Toe isn't a real saferoom; if the proprietor isn't a Bopca, it's about fifty-fifty. Our personal space is. So if the gnomes do to this town what they just did to the Bactrian one, you come in here. There are other rules, and the manual on saferoom procedures is like a phonebook. The primary and secondary zones are different; they don't directly touch crawlers or NPCs at all.

beats.headline: Debuff stacking, ruined
beats.text: Watch the highlights from the last floor, since they insist on replaying them. Miriam and I are stacking debuffs onto a boss, one on top of the other, timed to the second, the way it is supposed to be done and the way nobody else in this dungeon can do it. Then Quan Ch walks into the middle of it, and the plan is gone. The best work I have done in this place, and that is the part they replay.

beats.headline: Fourth, and not moving
beats.text: Prepotente is crazy. Carl is crazy too. Lucia is something different; she's insane. And when she threw that boy across the room, nobody stayed for him except Ifechi, which is sad. I call dibs on the dogs. Then the new top ten goes up: Carl second, me fourth, and Katia gone from the list entirely, which is outrageous, because she was a superstar. Katia says thank god. Why didn't I go up? We're separated. This is not acceptable, Carl. And Florin fell down the list, after something that sad. They're punishing him for it.

beats.headline: He wrecks the debuff stack
beats.text: Recap, highlights from the previous floor. Crawler Miriam Dom and Crawler Prepotente working a boss down the careful way: stack the debuffs, keep the rhythm, let the arithmetic do the killing. It is good technique and it films well. Then Crawler Quan Ch gets involved, and it comes apart. I am not going to editorialise. The footage editorialises for me.

beats.headline: Built on the floor it is meant to cross
beats.text: Carl and Katia build it at the engineering and metalworking tables around a single-gear magical train cart engine, and trade metal tires for a wide snowmobile track once the metal bogs down in the sand. Donut names it before it is finished. The System's description reads as abuse, and Katia collects an achievement for inventing it.

beats.headline: An oil rig that throws fireballs
beats.text: We're the only ones in the water quadrant. We've got ourselves a galley now, fish-people doing the rowing, and we're probing our castle: an oil rig run by orcs that shoots fireballs at anybody who gets close. We've seen the land crawlers but haven't talked to them. Their castle's an oil refinery. The whole bubble is some stupid story about how we earthlings ruined our own planet. The air castle's a storm cloud that rains acid, I think. You get saddled with a bunch of layabouts, Carl?

beats.headline: On Louis's lap
beats.text: I am on Louis's lap, because Louis is sweet. Now the other crawlers in the quadrant have found Carl's group, and Carl's group has a cat who talks. Their manager, Mordecai, is sobering Louis and Firas up on the spot. All the fun is coming out of their blood at once. Louis looks very sad about it. I am not sad. I am here, and I am staying.

beats.headline: The Tiddy Twister
beats.text: Okay so, the van. My mom's Chevy Astro, top cut off, the Tiddy Twister, a hundred thousand likes. Five in the morning, driving back from Jojo's on I-95, road goes all jacked, glowing stairwell right there, slid right in. Broke the axle. Got a spell for being the first to drive a van into the dungeon: Cloud of Exhaust, level eleven. Me and Firas spray and run. Then the eagle hands us white potions with no description and I puke for like five minutes. Notification says I can't drink anymore. Not cool, man. It's all I got left.

beats.headline: Rapid Detox, and a wasted spell
beats.text: One of these two fuckwits has his boots on the table, so I land on it, and it breaks, and I tell them to shut up for five minutes while I brew. Rapid Detox, with sage beetle ichor so they can't read the label. Clears alcohol and most drugs, and for one floor, if they drink, they get violently ill. The good kind of poisoning. Then the part that matters: Louis carries an enhanced, legendary-tier Cloud of Exhaust, almost certainly the same spell the goat lady has, and he's been using it to run away. He should be level forty by now.

beats.headline: Not shapeshifters at all
beats.text: Carl asks about the Valtay while Mordecai is explaining the local shapeshifters, and the answer is that they are not shapeshifters. They are a kind of creature called a Gondii. A Gondii enters a dead body within hours of death and reactivates it, reads its old memories, and can keep it running for centuries. Intellect Hunters do something similar, but their bodies begin to rot almost at once, so they are forever hopping. There is also something called an Infiltrator, which Mordecai calls much more insidious, and does not explain.

beats.headline: Stay out of city hall
beats.text: Firas puddle jumps us onto the town hall balcony. Downstairs, Louis's cloud drops the two guards on the basement door, and they turn out to be changelings in the shape of camels. I kill one, a level 49 Changeling Principal, and keep his head for Mordecai. Under the trapdoor is a map of the Necropolis of Anser that installs itself into my party's map and crumbles. Past the quadrant barrier, chained to the wall, is an old gnome, Wynne, the commandant's uncle. I get a quest to free him. Five crawlers arrive on the far side, Wynne begs them to kill him, and one does.

beats.headline: The guards are not what they look like
beats.text: In the town hall basement, some of the Dromedarian guards are changelings wearing the uniform, and one of them has been drugging a chained gnome and wearing the faces of people he knows, to make him give up a spell. A race that can be anyone is a race that can be planted anywhere, and both sides of this floor have worked that out.

beats.headline: Named in his uncle's file
beats.text: Subject enters the record secondhand, in my file on a chained gnome: Wynne, great and favoured uncle of Commandant Kane of the Dreadnaught Wasteland, held hostage by the dromedarians as a guarantee of peace. Per the same file, the Dirigible Gnomes were once a peaceful race who took to the clouds to be left alone, and whose long history left them forced to choose between fighting and being wiped out. They chose to fight.

beats.headline: The basement under the town hall
beats.text: Hump Town's town hall, and a good number of the Dromedarian guards are not Dromedarians. In the basement is Wynne, held as collateral, and Wynne is willing to say who has been working on him. Henrik: to look at, a regular level-30 camel who shows some sort of ID at the back door; underneath, a changeling. What he wants out of Wynne is a spell that will put flesh on Quetzalcoatlus, and the method for getting it has been to drug him and come to him in borrowed faces, until the next dose may kill him. Crawlers from the subterranean quadrant appear at the boundary, and at Wynne's own begging one of them puts him down before any of it concludes.

beats.headline: A pipe behind the town hall
beats.text: I am a pipe on the building behind the town hall, with a view of the back door. A dromedarian named Henrik comes out, level 30, and shows the guards an ID first. Through the open door I count at least twelve guards, two everywhere, so my plan to copy someone and walk in is dead. I keep watch instead. Three guards step out for a smoke and I tell Carl to go now. Then a waster guard stops two ordinary camels at the door, kills them both, and drags them inside. They stay camels when they die.

beats.headline: Two levels off a camel
beats.text: Okay so, the frog plan. Firas jumps us up to a balcony, and we walk down the stairs like we work there, calm purpose, whatever that means. Carl throws a sparkler through the cat's hole, I cast the cloud, and two camels go down, only they're not camels, they're these faceless guys with glowing heads. Carl kills one. Then he tells me and Firas to hit the other one in the head. It wakes up. We hit it a bunch, the cat finishes it. I went up two levels. Firas is 24. Now we're holding a door.

beats.headline: A sect after a full library
beats.text: Ah, shit. I should have known. Changeling Principals. It's an old story; I haven't seen it used in a long, long time. They're a sect of changeling culture, cultish, like those city elves, but less apocalyptic and more power hungry. They're obsessed with a full library, and since a changeling can only become something it has physically touched, they go after rare creatures. Get the brain, kid, the glowing part. If you kill one, take the head; I can make a potion from it. Only if it's untransformed when it dies. Knock them out first.

beats.headline: Hole, applied to a door
beats.text: Carl says he'll have to blow the door. Don't be so dramatic, Carl. I snap off my Hole and cast it again a few inches to the right, so it takes both deadbolts and part of the wall, and the door swings open with a half-moon bite out of it. Glass Cannon makes the spell reach right through. Then Carl tells me to kill the spell, so I do, and the missing piece of door comes back wrong and breaks its own bolts. That was Carl's fault. Then Louis calls me Cat. I am Princess Donut, you buffoon.

beats.headline: A name out of a basement
beats.text: The name surfaces in a cellar under Hump Town, out of a man being taken apart in pieces. Wynne is being worked on to give up a spell, and the spell is meant to put flesh on Quetzalcoatlus. Whatever she is, she is worth a body to somebody, and somebody is prepared to do that to a man over several days in order to get her one.

beats.headline: Chained beyond the boundary
beats.text: Subject: Wynne, Dirigible Gnome Flesh Mechanic, level 50. Located in a chamber below the town hall, past the shimmering quadrant boundary, chained to the wall. Elderly, no red hat, sickly, scabbed, half starved. Great and favoured uncle of Commandant Kane. A healer able to bring the long dead back to life, if only temporarily. Held by the dromedarians as a guarantee of peace. Crawler Carl was issued a quest to free him, reward a Silver Quest Box, and could not reach him from his side of the boundary.

beats.headline: Kill me fast
beats.text: Five crawlers arrived at a run on the subterranean side. Subject told them the human was no human but a changeling named Henrik, who was torturing him, drugging him, trying to make him give flesh to Quetzalcoatlus, and he would not last much longer. He said he had the map to the temple, and that if they killed him they would have access. Kill me fast, he said. Crawler Low Thi did, with a spear, over Crawler Carl's objection. Quest failed. There was no map.

beats.headline: The only one who finds the traps
beats.text: Bobby D.J. Level 24 Spy, rogue class, human, early twenties. An eye twitch; a left hand that does not stop trembling; a stutter. His quadrant is a maze of traps, and he appears to be his party's only rogue, which makes him its first line of defense. His party keeps getting water-breathing scrolls and scrolls of disarm trap. Told that Carl was going to kick his ass, he sits down anyway. Asked whether Carl will murder them: the d-d-day isn't over yet.

beats.headline: Total, Utter Failure
beats.text: An achievement for failing a quest inside five minutes. Reward: Ha. A camel rocket blows in the door, so I throw an eighth-strength hob-lobber down the hall, and something a camel was carrying on the outside goes up with it. The town hall catches fire. Donut opens a hole in the wall, I summon Bautista's stuffed grulke toad in the alley and send it hopping over the city wall, and Donut puddle jumps us down the street. A camel tells us frog creatures attacked. Then the town hall collapses. Donut says people are going to start thinking I have a problem with authority.

beats.headline: Sneak in, sneak out. Good job
beats.text: I stroll up in human form with a drink with a little umbrella in it. The plan was to sneak in, find out what was hidden, and sneak out again undetected. Good job. The frog con won't last; this world is too small, and the only ones who saw any frogs are the new people. Then my second sponsor arrives: the Squim Conglomerate, which sponsors about five hundred other crawlers. Loita books me alone on a one-on-one interview show called Dungeon Sidekicks. I can't wait.

beats.headline: I am not Zev
beats.text: All three clients commanded very high fees; the cat's and the man's bidding wars ran to the final microsecond, and the cat's set a record. The cat, the man and the dinosaur are booked in six or seven days on a program about the cat's sponsor's product, which arrives as a benefactor box that is really a free sample. The man may make his famous comments, but should not disparage it too much. The man calls it an infomercial and asks whether she is kidding. She is not Zev, she reminds him, and that tone will not be tolerated. Zev is still in treatment.

beats.headline: Carl's second sponsor
beats.text: Donut is taken by Veriluxx RealPet Companions and Katia by the Squim Conglomerate, and neither of those needs explaining: a pet brand wants the cat, a conglomerate wants the coverage. Carl is taken by the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network, which is registered as a not-for-conquest, answers to no system government and pays no tax. Nobody can say what it wants.

beats.headline: The highest bid ever
beats.text: My new sponsor is Veriluxx RealPet Companions, which sounds just awesome, except they sponsor a bunch of other people too, and Princess D'Nadia just sponsored five more. Then Loita says my bidding war lasted until the final possible microsecond and was the highest sponsorship bid ever, beating Carl and Prepotente. That is pretty much what I expected. I ask how Zev is. Twice. She is still in treatment. My sponsor is sending me a product sample, and Carl and Mongo and I are going on a program about it. Do you think there'll be a script? Will I get lines?

beats.headline: An empress in the walls
beats.text: Per Morris Sp of the subterranean quadrant: Anser was an emperor, and when he died, his court and his wife were sealed into the tomb with him, alive. The wife is Quetzalcoatlus. She is undead now, non-corporeal, able to pass through the tomb's walls, and she can be heard screaming, like a bird. Having failed the map quest, the tomb crawlers received a new one: find her and kill her. Nobody knows how to kill a ghost. Morris observes that she would probably be easier to kill with a body.

beats.headline: The tomb raiders, so called
beats.text: Subject kept the Human race and took the rogue-type Spy Class, and he is one of the two in his party with Desperado Club access. His party holds the subterranean quadrant of their bubble. Carl calls them the tomb raiders, which is not their name for themselves and is the one that stuck.

beats.headline: Nine kilometers up
beats.text: The Valtay pill gives me elevation and airspeed. That's it, I think, and don't say out loud. The elevation display takes some figuring. Planetary sea level puts me at minus 92,000 meters. The gauge labeled Gravitational Zone Sea Level says 8,932 meters, which means we're standing about nine kilometers above the water quadrant, roughly the height of Everest. Which means the Necropolis of Anser under our feet is enormous. We need to give those guys in the tomb all the help we can, because if they fail, we're the ones going in there.

beats.headline: I hope it was a lie
beats.text: I spent the storm at the club with Morris and Bobby, drawing them a general map of the necropolis and a detailed path to a town halfway down. They're total trainwrecks. If something happens to Bobby, the whole team is dead; he's the only one who detects traps, he has already missed a few, and they send others ahead of him who die in front of him. They kept asking when we would storm our castle, so they can wait for our help. I told them we don't expect to finish the air quadrant until time is almost up. At least I hope it was a lie.

beats.headline: One root vegetable
beats.text: The Valtay Corporation sends a neural enhancer, which is exactly the sort of thing a corporation sends. The Network sends a single Toraline root vegetable. Mordecai has never seen the plant, and can only guess at what it is for: a potion, an explosive, an inside joke. It is listed as very rare and worth about as much as an old shirt.

beats.headline: Eight more visits
beats.text: Katia and I spent the whole storm at the Desperado Club, and Katia came back in a feather boa, and Mongo has one on his collar that he keeps biting. Eight more visits and I get a free dance. Carl wants to know how much we're spending. Carl, guess what? I got another box from Princess D'Nadia. It's only a bronze this time, but I bet it'll be awesome. The product sample hasn't come yet. Loita says the sponsor wants to make sure we survive the bombing first. Isn't that exciting?

beats.headline: A creditor with a seat at the table
beats.text: A corporate system government inside the Syndicate, which is to say a company that is also a country and answers to neither description when it is inconvenient. Its people are parasites in the literal sense, riding the bodies of other races. It holds the Borant Corporation’s debt, and it sends a crawler a neural enhancer, which is the sort of gift that is also a note.

beats.headline: Ruckus, and the second stage
beats.text: Four missiles with surefires in a launcher on my swivel seat, telescope clamped beside it. The first one's second stage lights, then the whole thing blows a few hundred feet short, and the exhaust has burned my right side. So much for hitting the Wasteland from the ground. I have Katia turn around and drive straight at the bird, lock the last three on the wing joint, the neck and the buzzsaw's cable, and pull all three pins. The wing comes off and Ruckus wraps up in its own cable. I want that saw intact.

beats.headline: Anything marked with the word
beats.text: The word turns up on a dead goose, a neighborhood boss dropped out of a gnome plane in a broken egg, dead from the landing. Asked what it means, Mordecai does not know that creature specifically, but anything with feral in the name is usually bad news. Then it turns up again, in the description of a borough boss, as the name of an artifact buried in the necropolis under the bowl. Mordecai's advice holds: stay away from anything marked that. It is always bad news.

beats.headline: Hidden in the tomb
beats.text: Carl learns of it from the description of Ruckus, out in the desert quadrant. It lies buried in the Necropolis of Anser, and it has drawn treasure hunters: the bugbear submarine captain Shamus Chaindrive, who spent close to twenty years looking for the tomb, a young mage trying to burrow into it by magic, and a colony of dirigible gnomes. An artifact of this grade has no business appearing before the eighth or ninth floor, and the world freezes for half a second while the game reconciles the conflict.

beats.headline: A counterweight in one hand
beats.text: Carl makes me turn the Chariot toward a level 55 bird towing a row of buzzsaws, so I grow a second face on the back of my head to ask if he's crazy. He fires, and I turn too sharply, and the Chariot starts to tip. I hold my arm out on the other side and put mass into my hand until we come level, then drop it. We didn't need to drive toward it; the first stage had range enough. He says he didn't want to damage the prize, and I know he means the saw.

beats.headline: A timeout, not a glitch
beats.text: I felt it. It happens. That half-second freeze usually isn't a glitch; it's a gameplay timeout, so the dueling routines can reconcile a rule conflict. An artifact is a legendary or celestial-tier item you find lying around or drop as loot, and they start turning up around the eighth or ninth floor. The showrunners control the storylines, but the AI picks the specific loot, and it can and will adjust the story to keep the game fair. If you get what I'm saying. And remember what I said about the word feral.

beats.headline: The bubbles are inhabited
beats.text: The pocket worlds are not stage sets. A bubble holds Hump Town and its dromedarians on the sand, a castle of dirigible gnomes in the air, the Necropolis of Anser underneath, and every one of them was there and running before a crawler arrived.

beats.headline: The glasses see heat
beats.text: Princess D'Nadia's box was empty. Then my sunglasses got an update: surface and subsurface temperatures, in precise detail. At the town gate I can tell two of the guards are different from the others. Earlier I stole Skarn's telescope in ten seconds flat; I forgot to leave the thirty gold. Out here it's five degrees hotter in the middle of the bowl than at the edges, which is not acceptable. Then Carl fires a missile right next to me. I'm flammable, Carl. And I don't think I did anything productive in that battle.

beats.headline: A letter I never delivered
beats.text: Chris Andrews took the water castle, which means he's in here with us. He's Brandon's brother. I keep Brandon's last note in my scratch pad: they fought, Chris left, and now it's too late to tell him he loves him. I promised myself I'd give it to Chris. But he took a rock race, stopped talking to Imani, and, the Sledge says, crushed Frank Q's head at the Desperado Club counter and walked out. That isn't the quiet man I remember. Imani thinks he wants to team up. I've had enough of that with Hekla.

beats.headline: The watch's twin
beats.text: Subject owns the twin of the pocket watch Henrik carries. Once a day its alarm sounds, and its mirror shows the Commandant making a sign with his fingers; the hostage names a time, the hands are set, and subject's watch moves to match. It is a code the dromedarians do not understand. The two sides also trade written messages this way. His ambassador, Leon the Commissar, inspects the hostage with a spell against changelings. The Bactrians' collateral was different: his daughter's favourite pet swine, sunned daily for the farseers.

beats.headline: He explains the collateral
beats.text: Carl and Princess Donut sit down with Henrik, charmed, and he explains how collateral works here, which is the local economy in miniature: Wynne held against the truce with the gnomes, and an ambassador, Leon the Commissar, who comes to inspect and casts a spell to make sure the collateral has not been swapped for a changeling. The next inspection is due in two days. How the code between the two sides actually works, he does not volunteer, and nobody in the room expects him to.

beats.headline: Still Brandon's brother
beats.text: Carl tells me he's found Chris. He's in the same bubble as Carl. Chris still ignores every message I send. I hope the real Chris is still in there somewhere; he's the only non-resident left. Here we need a boat with armor. Elle's ice keeps the fireballs off, but we can't get near the oil rig for the monsters in the water and the orc archers. Carl says build a sub, like that's easy. We bought the shop interface on Donut's advice. And Carl? Don't kill him. Please. He's still Brandon's brother.

beats.headline: A room that is not a way home
beats.text: The Toe is full of children, forty of them, and I am handing out juice boxes. Carl takes everybody into his room. The kids knock over the couch, grab the robot, and make a gambling ring out of the straws. I turn into a hairy monster and the robot gets dropped. Then the eagle puts a movie on the screen and it goes quiet. I ask Carl if the room can take us home. It cannot. There was a way, and it went with the town hall. Stop the gnomes, and my people live, and I will tell him what we seek.

beats.headline: This is not a daycare
beats.text: I don't have the materials for Feather Fall; the seed pods are scarce until the sixth floor. I can make him one kind of potion, two doses, and he won't like it. Then he walks in with forty children. This isn't a goddamned daycare, Carl. Do you see a jungle gym? So I stream a movie to the screen from the library I collected before we went live. Toy Story. It's a manager benefit, for strategizing on the screens. Now the cat knows. And that is why I never told her.

beats.headline: You could cook an egg on him
beats.text: Through my glasses Henrik's head glows hotter than anybody's; you could cook an egg on it. Carl needs a boost from my charm, so I tell Henrik we can save the town and we don't care which of them are camels. He shows us the watch. At the Toe, Juice Box's head is just as hot, and the bartender is one too, which is just sneaky. Then Mordecai puts a movie on the screen, and he has a whole library. I have to know how There's Something About Mary ends. Also Louis taught me janky. I'm allowed to have friends, Carl.

beats.headline: Years of the code
beats.text: Posthumous addendum, from Henrik, under Princess Donut's charm. Each day a watch alarm sounded and the gnomish Commandant made a sign in its mirror. Subject was shown the sign and named a time; the hands were set to it, and the gnomes knew he lived for another day. He cooperated for years. Only when he was moved to the chamber below the town hall did he understand the arrangement had changed, and stop. After that he was drugged with mushroom, and had to be fed more every day.

beats.headline: The helmet and the fish
beats.text: The sniper in the Vahana's basket wears a round black half-helmet with no face shield. My dad wore one like it. A month before he left, he ripped it off and smashed my fish tank, and I picked the mollies up off the floor with cut fingers and put them in a cup. They died anyway. I didn't cry, and that bothered me for weeks. What I took from it was: never get a pet again, all they do is die. Wrong lesson, probably. I look across at Donut on Mongo, doing her best to look menacing. She's not a pet anymore. I don't know if she's better off.

beats.headline: The fish tank
beats.text: A sniper gnome in a round, black half-helmet reminds Carl of his father's. Soon after Carl's mother left, a month before his father in turn left Carl to fend for himself, the man ripped that helmet off and smashed Carl's fish tank. The mollies flopped on the floor while Carl cut his fingers on the glass picking them up. None survived. Carl did not cry, and that bothered him for weeks. The lesson he took from it: never get a pet again. All they do is die.

beats.headline: A throat with nobody behind it
beats.text: Subject Firas is seated in the back cart behind a Henrik who is not Henrik. On cue he stands, draws a long knife and runs it across the camel's neck. The blood sprays convincingly. Then he stands staring at the knife, stupidly, until Crawler Carl tells him by chat to stomp the head, fast. He stomps an empty robe several times. Told to sit and be inconspicuous, he sits. When the ambassador heads for the cart, subject asks the chat what he is doing, twice. The ambassador runs his changeling check on him and moves on to the body.

beats.headline: The delegation to the gnomes
beats.text: The plan walks out of the hall in a line: Carl, Princess Donut, Firas, Louis, a reanimated Wynne, and a Henrik who is Katia Grim doing his voice, not very well. They meet Leon, the Gnome Negotiator, and present Wynne as a man in urgent need of healing. Princess Donut announces herself as the healer and asks for passage onto the Wasteland in exchange. Leon will take Wynne and the healer and nobody else; the cat will not go without her manservant.

beats.headline: Chair, gnome and Henrik at once
beats.text: I am the back seat of the Chariot, the body under Wynne's head, and Henrik in the cart behind, joined to the rest by an arm draped over the seat. My Henrik voice is not very good. When Firas cuts his throat, I pull that mass back in, and the robe falls onto the changeling corpse already hidden in the cart. Leon, leaning right against me, lays his hand on the gnome's head, and his spell finds no changeling. Then the head I am wearing times out and turns to dust, and I grow a new one before anyone looks. Carl pours Mountain Dew down my throat. Who can drink this bile?

beats.headline: The famed healer of Queen Anne
beats.text: The gnome ambassador wants to know which of us is the healer, and it is I, Princess Donut, the famed healer of Queen Anne. I ask for passage onto the Wasteland and mention that my manservant is a world-renowned masseuse, an expert with feet. CARL tells me to stick to the script. Wynne is only a head I raised with Second Chance, and I have never resurrected just a head before. They are a lot more surly. When Leon asks what the potion is, I do not hesitate: Healer's Respite. Stichberries boiled with iron slivers and manticore shavings. It is Mountain Dew.

beats.headline: Sky garden, renamed dreadnaught
beats.text: The Vahana, the black-and-gold striped Gnomish Legate Balloon that comes down to parley, is perhaps the oldest vehicle left aboard the Wasteland, and its description tells the gnomes' side. They once took to the skies hoping to stay out of this world's wars as neutral peacekeepers, and a Legate balloon on the horizon meant ambassadors and perhaps peace. Then winged predators came through a mysterious portal and would share the sky with nobody. The balloons were mostly dismantled and sewn into the settlements' defences, and the flying communities changed their name from sky garden to dreadnaught.

beats.headline: Half an hour of Second Chance
beats.text: Subject's corpse was retrieved by the tomb raiders a few hours after death, chewed by beetles, face untouched. Princess Donut raised the head with Second Chance, reaching his level 50 from her 33 by way of her glass cannon class, for half an hour. Katia Grim supplied everything below it. Leon the Commissar laid a hand on the snapping head, found no changeling, and said it appeared to be a ghoul. Then the spell timed out behind his back, the head went to dust, and Katia grew a new one before anyone looked.

beats.headline: He wants the Gate
beats.text: The Wasteland is broken, and what's left of the castle is a house, no bigger than a regular one, hanging from a single balloon at the top of the bubble. The Commandant is in there with his daughter. Katia wants to put another missile in it. I want to go up and take it the old-fashioned way. Henrik has a watch, the Commandant has one, and I'm pretty sure the Mad Dune Mage has the third, and they all come together as the Gate of the Feral Gods. It's a celestial-equivalent item. They don't put that in here to be ignored. I want it.

beats.headline: Just him and his daughter
beats.text: Subject received a message in Henrik's name: Wynne gravely ill after a resurrection spell, a travelling healer bringing him out beyond the walls. Leon came to meet it. Subject's dreadnaught was then taken apart over Hump Town. What stayed aloft was a single house under a balloon. Through a farseer, Crawler Carl saw a girl of about ten at its door, and behind her, before it shut, the Commandant. Crawler Carl announced he wanted subject's watch, on the theory that three watches together make the Gate of the Feral Gods.

beats.headline: The bombs never land
beats.text: Carl, Donut and Katia climb into the Vahana's basket and take it as it rises with Langley's team shooting from the ground. Carl puts missiles into the Wasteland's bombs before they can be dropped on the town. The Wasteland breaks apart and comes down. The castle it carried stays up.

beats.headline: Too much UP
beats.text: UP. Too much UP. Brothers jump off. Basket rocks. MOTHER says carrier. NO. Carl yells very loud. Fine. Carrier.

beats.headline: A hole in the basket
beats.text: Katia tells me to make sure she is secure before I do it, because it is a long drop. I cast Hole on the bottom of the basket, a meter and a half wide now that I have practiced, and all three gnomes fall out with the most astonished faces. Level 34! Then I send two clockwork Mongos off the edge after the next balloon, and it goes past us with a bloody basket and one of Mongo's brothers screeching hello. Level 35. By the time I climb out of my hole in the sand, I have my benefactor box and level 36.

beats.headline: Looking better already
beats.text: The message Crawler Carl had Henrik send the Commandant, for the record: Wynne cast a resurrection spell for the dromedarians, became gravely ill, and a travelling healer would bring him out beyond the walls. By the time the balloon rose, the Wynne curled on the floor of the basket was Katia Grim in duct tape, keeping quiet because her voice work was barely passable, curled up to hide the extra height. Leon leaned down to look at her. He's looking better already, he said.

beats.headline: Just your social media manager
beats.text: Hey guys! Wow, that was fantastic. Great job. Your social numbers are looking great! Okay, so, Princess Donut, I am just your social media manager now. Administrator Loita is in charge of all public appearances, and you are not able to message me directly unless I open the chat. I've never been better, thank you. Carl, the audience is noting that you are being extra angry with the other crawlers. Katia, your numbers are rising steadily. Princess Donut, people want more Mongo, and you have used your new spells only once. Now get back out there and kill, kill, kill!

beats.headline: Small NOT MOTHER
beats.text: Small MOTHER. Smells wrong. NOT MOTHER. Says bad things about dogs. BITE. Head off. Fire. MOTHER says bad Mongo. Too late.

beats.headline: Sell the kit, use the stone
beats.text: Kid, keep the Half Splat in your hotlist until you find a real Featherfall; it stops the fall killing you and leaves you at five percent. And don't knock Dolores Doesn't Splat. Unpleasant, sure, but you landed at a hundred percent. The platinum stone is what I was talking about: items that enhance the items you already have. Use it now, it has a short shelf life. The author kit you'll never have the skills for; a simple Light scroll would take a week of practice. Sell it. One guy last season used the same scroll over two hundred times and learned the spell.

beats.headline: I have merch
beats.text: My benefactor box from Veriluxx RealPet Companions opens, and it is me. A robot me, three-quarters size, with fur like rat hair, and it says it likes lasagna and hates Mondays. Katia says they mixed me up with Garfield. They made a doll out of me. It is merch. I have merch. It is the greatest thing since I won Grand Champion Best in Show in Cleveland. Then it asks Mongo whether he is a cocker spaniel, Mongo bites its head off, it catches fire, and a static shock hits me on the nose. This is most certainly going into my review.

beats.headline: Good boy
beats.text: Cannonball. You fell from a great height and survived, and you get a Silver Skydiver's Box you don't deserve. Now, every live ammo ball the gnomes fired at Carl held a frenzied gerbil, level 11, and every one of them overshot him. Then thousands of them come at Hump Town, far more than ever fell out of the sky, and they keep coming. Camels fall. The cat sets the gerbils on fire and the gerbils set the camels on fire. Then Carl catches one on his buckler and steps on it, and on about fifty more. You're the reason why daddy drinks. The acceleration action has been suspended. This time. Good boy.

beats.headline: Bronze from a sponsor beats gold from the floor
beats.text: Only a sponsor can send one. They use the same six quality tiers as every other box and they outclass the ordinary run of loot at every rank, so a bronze one from a benefactor is worth more than a gold one earned. It means the fastest way to be well equipped is to be liked by someone with money.

beats.headline: The ball in the impostor's hand
beats.text: The friend standing in front of Carl is Maggie My wearing him, and she has a round, spiked ball in her hand when Katia's petrify bolt takes her in the head. The ball rolls. Carl dives for it and puts it in his inventory before it can do anything, without knowing what it is. It does not list itself as an explosive. It is a celestial grenade: summon your god for sixty seconds, and stand inside Divine Intervention while it is here.

beats.headline: Bought by the Skull Empire
beats.text: Mordecai's eyes go huge when Carl tosses it to him. These are very expensive and rare, he says, seen on the ninth floor a lot, near the end; using one on a single crawler is like trying to kill a bug with a kinetic strike. The crawler Maggie has been riding gets a message out before he is cut off. She worships Algos, the god of pain, chosen from a scroll sent by her sponsors, Prince Maestro and Crown Prince Stalwart. She got the grenade on this floor.

beats.headline: The man inside is not Chris
beats.text: He walks up at level 35, Igneous, Zulu Warrior, having taken the bridge of the Akula and been fired out of a missile tube. He claims chat costs him health. He says his family is dead, and that he has two daughters. Crawler Carl works it out: this is Maggie My. A petrify bolt drops him. Mordecai names the parasite: a Scree, an infiltrator, and the host is awake behind his own eyes. Through Elle comes a message from Chris himself: "Carl, Donut. Please. Kill me."

beats.headline: Dropped through the street
beats.text: A second message arrives through Elle before his privileges are suspended: Maggie worships Algos, the god of pain, and she and he share two sponsors, Prince Maestro and Crown Prince Stalwart. Crawler Carl puts a hand on his rocky shoulder and tells him that his brother loved him and regretted never saying so. Brandon gave his life protecting his friends. Then Crawler Donut opens a hole beneath him, and host and worm fall into a sealed chamber below the street. She is not letting Crawler Carl kill a friend.

beats.headline: Somebody has to send it
beats.text: Imani won't send this one, so I will, word for word, from Chris: Carl, Donut. Please. Kill me. It's okay. I give you permission. Carl tells him where he can go, and I tell Chris the same thing. But if they can't find a fix, they don't have a choice. If it was me stuck in there, I'd want someone to pull the plug. I pass along the rest when it comes through: Maggie doesn't worship Grull, she worships a god called Algos. Then Chris gets cut off mid-sentence, messaging suspended for thirty minutes.

beats.headline: A Scree riding Chris Andrews
beats.text: Frank Q is dead. Chris Andrews killed him, and Chris Andrews was not the one driving. Maggie My is back in the dungeon as a Scree, riding inside another crawler, and Frank died of exactly the thing he brought down here with him. He found Carl at the Desperado Club and gave him a ring. She found Frank there afterwards. Half of a pair who taught this planet what safe rooms are for. The other half is still walking around, wearing somebody else.

beats.headline: He's being controlled
beats.text: Carl says it is not Chris. It is. Chris has messaged me: he is petrified, and when his body wakes he will lose consciousness again, because something else is driving it. Then he asks Carl and Donut to kill him, and I will not send that on. Elle does. When Carl tells me he is sorry, I do not answer. Donut drops Chris through a hole into a sealed chamber under the street instead, and I thank her. Take all four castles, I tell them, then go back, incapacitate them again, bring them through the portal, and your game guide can make the potion.

beats.headline: Two in the rock man
beats.text: I touch the rock man, and he's hot, and there are two in there. So I tell Carl to bring these two guys. He doesn't get it. I grab his hand and pull. He doesn't get that either. Katia shoots the rock man, and I tell Carl straight: that's your friend Chris, don't kill him. There's also an Infiltrator in there. Kill that one. Carl asks can I turn into one of those worms and go in after her. No. They're too small. And that's a pretty messed-up thing to ask.

beats.headline: Ten bolts from Princess Formidable
beats.text: An emergency silver benefactor box, from Princess Formidable, and Mordecai says to open it now. Ten bolts of Petrify Rock Class. I put one into the head of the thing wearing Chris while it stands over Carl with something round in its hand. Petrified, sixty seconds, and every bolt resets the timer. I wonder why they would send bolts that only petrify instead of kill. Mordecai says they cost more than regular ones. I keep shooting while the others argue. When there is nothing left to argue, I tell Carl he does not have a skull yet, and I do. Let me do it.

beats.headline: Infiltrators
beats.text: Oh, fuck. Shoot him again. I've told you about brain worms, kid. Intellect hunters take corpses, and the bodies rot. The Valtay keep their bodies alive. Their cousins, the Scree, are better known as the Infiltrators: they take living bodies, and after a few days the host is locked out and watches himself move like a puppet. She's in his brain. His body is her armor. Getting her out without killing him? Next to impossible. There's an antiparasitic that will kill her, and I won't have the materials until the next floor.

beats.headline: Don't be mad at me
beats.text: Carl forms his fist to kill Chris himself, and everyone else steps back. Don't be mad at me, I tell him, and I open a Hole under Chris, and he drops through into the dark room underneath with a splash. Carl only falls about a foot, onto the quadrant's forcefield, and I tell him to step out before his feet get chopped off. He says that was a mistake. It was not. Carl is not a killer. Not a person killer. I am not going to let him kill one of his friends, because I cannot have him being all mopey.

beats.headline: Ten bolts, emergency rate
beats.text: An emergency benefactor box, silver, from subject. Mordecai says it must be opened at once, and that it probably cost the princess a sizeable chunk of her net worth. It holds ten bolts of Petrify Rock Class. Then Crawler Katia puts the first of them into the head of Maggie My, who has been riding inside another crawler and is standing over Crawler Carl with a celestial grenade in her hand. Crawler Katia's reading of the ledger: his sister is spending a lot of money to stop him.

beats.headline: Algos, by celestial grenade
beats.text: The ball in Maggie My's hand is a celestial grenade: it summons the holder's god for sixty seconds and wraps the holder in Divine Intervention. Through Chris, relayed by Elle, comes where it came from. Maggie's sponsors are Prince Maestro and Crown Prince Stalwart, and so are Chris's. They sent her a scroll to choose a god, and Chris a box with a picture of Algos on it, so she knew which. Mordecai reads it as unofficial, a bribed one-on-one in a saferoom, and Algos as the god of pain: he would kill everyone in town in seconds.

beats.headline: Death Trap, renamed
beats.text: The gnomish Drop Bear that Louis and the archers dragged in runs on real gasoline, and I have plenty in cans. I fill it a quarter of the way to keep it light. The name stencilled on the nose is Death Trap, with four bombs painted after it. I spray over it and write Nightmare II. There's no runway, so I pull the emergency balloon lever, and we rise tail-first to the ceiling of the bubble, about five kilometers up. Then I throttle up, skitter along the ceiling toward the house, cut the power and coast in.

beats.headline: One of three holders
beats.text: The quest arrives with subject's name in it. Henrik the Changeling. Commandant Kane. The Mad Dune Mage. Each has a piece of the artifact; take them, collect all three, put them together. Reward: oh boy-oh-boy. Subject's air force is grounded. His house has floated up until it is wedged against the top of the bubble, with no obvious defences, and by the party's count only two living creatures aboard: the Commandant and his daughter. Crawler Carl declines to shoot it down, because he wants the watch intact.

beats.headline: Three pieces, three holders
beats.text: A winding box and two magically linked pocket watches. Henrik the Changeling has one watch, the gnomish Commandant Kane the other, and the Mad Dune Mage the box. The quest to collect all three offers a reward of "Oh boy-oh-boy."

beats.headline: I lied about the Gate
beats.text: Henrik is my brother. He's a Principal. People say they're a cult that catalogues every known species. They're looking for one, and it's Quetzalcoatlus. I told Carl the Gate of the Feral Gods was a myth. I lied. It's real, and it's dangerous. It opens a way from one place to the next, and when it closes, an ancient feral god comes through on the side that opened it. We could go home, and this world would pay for it. That's why even my brother doesn't want to use it. He's not that cruel.

beats.headline: Did you ever want children
beats.text: We stand looking up at the house wedged against the top of the bubble, and I ask Carl whether he ever wanted children. He says no; he would not be a good dad. I tell him I could not have children, when I was human. I was going to adopt. You can do that in Iceland when you are single. I was pre-approved. I was on the list. Something happened, and I was disqualified. It is not important. I tell him I am glad now, because Maggie is what losing everything does to a mother. And I am happy to sit this one out.

beats.headline: The doll is rigged to blow
beats.text: The fourth robot cat has just exploded in front of the Spit and Swallow. Subject Loita informs Crawler Carl that the real Veriluxx toy takes far more stress, and that his boosted strength is the problem: it is built for children outside an enhancement zone. She adds that once the production realised he would fiddle with it, they required the sponsor to make the doll self-destruct if sufficiently broken, so that he could not get at the interior parts. The retail version will not have that feature. Try not to break the next one, she says.

beats.headline: Why the changelings want her flesh
beats.text: Juice Box lays out the arithmetic. The changelings want Quetzalcoatlus given a body so that they can touch her, because touching a thing is how a changeling adds it to the shapes it can wear. And they need what she carries: a great many of them are sick with compression sickness, and they believe she has a spell that alters living things which can be turned on the illness. A wailing shrieker over a tomb, wanted for her hands and for her medicine.

beats.headline: Compression sickness
beats.text: Subject is a changeling, and she has compression sickness: in her default form she has no arms and her head is sunken. One birth in four now arrives this way, and the ones born with it are sterile. I note it because nobody else in the building will.

beats.headline: If you must choose, Ivy
beats.text: Okay, so, the audience loves the strange vibe of the doll, but I tend to agree with the crawler: it does not sound like Princess Donut. We put that in the notes. Veriluxx hasn't changed it. Carl says he can't imagine it doing well, presented the way it is, and I tell him he is not wrong. There are memes. When Princess Donut asks whether she should name her robot Charlie or Ivy, I tell her it is inconsequential, crawler. Then, before the chat closes: if you must choose a name, I would go with Ivy.

beats.headline: She brings them inside
beats.text: Subject is a juvenile Dirigible Gnome of the air quadrant, daughter of a commandant. She is the one who brings the crawlers in through the door, and what they find on the other side of it is her father, already dead, ripped to shreds by her new pet, which has gone out for food. The girl's eyes are dilated and she is setting up a lemonade stand. She is under a spell. Nobody discusses the alternative.

beats.headline: Head first into the disposal
beats.text: The boss is Denise, a feral goose in a blue bonnet, and the rules say no magic and no physical damage, with three minutes before the house hits the ground. I grab the lemonade, because it has to be the answer. It's lemonade. The AI calls that a Wild Goose Chase. What actually hurts her is anything that was already in the house: a mug, the pitcher. Bonnie pointed at the sink earlier. I remember the two switches beside it, shove Denise head-first into the drain, and yell at Donut to flip them. The garbage disposal does the rest.

beats.headline: On the kitchen table
beats.text: Lootable Corpse. Commandant Kane. Dirigible Gnome. Level 55. Ripped to shreds by Denise. Found draped across his own kitchen table, half eaten, while his daughter set up a lemonade stand beside him. Asked why Denise killed her father, the girl pointed at the kitchen sink. Crawler Carl looted him by accident, falling into the body when the house lurched: 5,030 gold, a Mysterious Watch, and a Letter from the Glass Wizard telling him his bombs were weakening the temple, and to stop, and think of his people and his child.

beats.headline: Ripped to shreds by Denise
beats.text: Subject enters the record on another creature's corpse tag: Commandant Kane, ripped to shreds by Denise. Asked who Denise is, the Commandant's daughter, eyes dilated, said she went out to get some food. When the child's pig was taken, her father kept getting her new pets. Not the gerbils; they were mean. Other things, including ol' Denise. She's okay. She's no Sausage. Do not tell her that, though. She gets jealous.

beats.headline: When she gets mad
beats.text: The floating house began to sink. That's Denise, the child explained: when she gets mad, magic stuff doesn't work, and the balloon goes down; she is probably on the roof. Somewhere in the house the clockwork Mongos exploded early and tore up the real one. Mordecai briefed the party: no spells, no scrolls, no gauntlet, gear protections gone. Scrolls on the bleeding Mongo did nothing. Then the flying lemonade glass moved itself away from Crawler Carl's hand, the window slammed, and the doors locked.

beats.headline: The Feral Goose Mother
beats.text: A white goose in a frilly baby-blue bonnet and a torn, bloodied shawl. Level 53 Borough Boss. Plucked from the seventh floor when her grandfather, emperor Anser, used a magical gate to bring his people here, she lingered too long in the Nothing, and her mind is all but gone. The gnomes captured her without knowing who she is. Neither does she. She can prevent magic from harming her. She is an environmental. She needs to protect children. Mostly, she wants to kill everybody.

beats.headline: No health bar
beats.text: Mongo got her by the neck and shook her; she bounced back up. Subject's bill opened into a flower of razor teeth and fired them like a shotgun. A banger ricocheted off her bill. No health bar appeared. She took a chunk out of Mongo, and a thrown mug knocked her off the kitchen table and launched the Commandant's corpse into the ceiling. She chased the party upstairs, hopping one step at a time, and put two barbs in Crawler Carl's face. Only then did a health bar appear, barely dented.

beats.headline: The garbage disposal
beats.text: The lemonade was a trick: Wild Goose Chase, magic doesn't work, it's lemonade. Crawler Carl hit subject with the pitcher, took her teeth across the face, lost his left eye's sight, and held her bill shut by hand. He remembered the child pointing at the sink, and saw the two switches. Subject went into the drain face first. Princess Donut flipped both switches. The timer stopped at one second. The Commandant's quarters are occupied. The Air Quadrant is liberated.

beats.headline: A truce, by letter
beats.text: Kane. Cease your hostilities. Your bombs do not harm me, but they are ruining the structure of the temple, weakening its wall, and surely even in your floating city you understand the danger if it collapses. So I propose a truce: you stop the bombing, and I won't end this world. I have the winding box. I have cracked its secret. I know how to open a portal, and I do not need your watches to throw this entire world into the void, which I will do before I allow that ghost to leave the temple. Think of your people. Of her. Stop.

beats.headline: Goose NOT FOOD
beats.text: Brothers go POP. Hurts. Goose. BITE goose. Shake goose. Goose gets up. Goose has teeth. MOTHER pulls tail. Up the stairs. Rabbit. Mine.

beats.headline: My heal spell stopped working
beats.text: The goose turns off magic, and the two clockwork Mongos explode early and hurt my baby. My heal spell will not work. My Heal Critter scroll fizzles. My pet carrier does not work. Mongo is bleeding and his health keeps going down, and CARL shouts at me to use a bandage, so I do, and it works. I rip a hole in the bedroom floor so we can drop back into the kitchen. And who flips the garbage disposal switch while Carl holds the goose's head in the sink? Me.

beats.headline: The air quadrant liberated
beats.text: The last piece of the Wasteland comes down in a hurry and stops just short. With Denise dead in the kitchen's garbage disposal, the Commandant's quarters count as occupied, and a bubble notification congratulates crawlers Princess Donut and Carl on taking the throne room. The Air Quadrant is liberated, and every crawler who started there may now travel freely into the other quadrants. Then the house bumps gently onto the ground.

beats.headline: Denise killed my dad
beats.text: Subject Bonnie is waking from her father's potion in Skarn's house, where Juice Box is showing her a cot. It is not her bed, so Crawler Carl pulls her own pink bed and nightstand out of his inventory. She states that Denise killed her father, that he knew it was coming and could do nothing, that he told her to make lemonade and gave her the potion so she would stop being scared, and she asks for another one. Juice Box says no. Skarn tells her his parents died when his town was bombed, and that the camels are grumpy but not mean.

beats.headline: The moment I change my mind
beats.text: I strip the house: two laptops, three televisions, the gaming consoles, the bikes, a kayak, the Christmas tree and the electrical panel, whose outlets keep working as long as they stay attached. No guns, though the doormat says they had some. At Skarn's house I set down Bonnie's own bed and the picture of her with her mother and father. Loita tells us to stop concerning ourselves with NPCs. When I look back, the girl is sobbing into Juice Box, holding the pink rabbit Mongo gave her. I'd been toying with an idea and dismissed it as too risky. That's the moment I change my mind.

beats.headline: A drawing in a frame
beats.text: Addendum, from the house. On subject's nightstand, in a frame meant for a photo, a drawing he had put there himself: Kane, a woman gnome, and a baby. His watch is bronze, carries a bone symbol, and does not tick. His daughter, waking from his potion, supplies the rest. Denise killed him. He knew she was going to. He said there was nothing he could do, told her to make lemonade, and when she started to cry he gave her the potion, and she was not scared anymore.

beats.headline: Supposed to drown her
beats.text: Post-mortem. The house's power crystal had shut itself off under subject's anti-magic aura; with her gone, the balloon began refilling on its own. Princess Donut's assessment of the fight is that the goose was meant to be drowned, in the sink or the lemonade pitcher, and not put through the garbage disposal. When the child woke, she told the party her father knew Denise was going to kill him and could do nothing, and asked for another potion.

beats.headline: Mongo, as a threat
beats.text: Subject Loita announces that Crawler Princess Donut has a new doll to spend time with, and that if it works the pair will do the show a day early. When the cat talks back, Loita tells her she keeps forgetting her place. When the cat says she smells, Loita says the feeling is mutual, and that if she talks back again Mongo will be taken from her and fed to a mob on the next floor while she watches. She refuses to send Zev down for a goodbye. At Bonnie's bedside, she tells the crawlers that audiences like drama, not melodrama.

beats.headline: Rabbit for small gnome
beats.text: Small gnome sad. Crying smell. Rabbit from her room. Rabbit NOT FOOD. Put rabbit down. Small gnome holds rabbit.

beats.headline: Veriluxx, and who owns it
beats.text: Kid, don't press your luck with that panel. It's a non-enhanced toy; set off the self-destruct and I honestly don't know what the AI does with it. Most toys need a licensed enhancement zone, and some need a license key in the kid to prove his parents paid their taxes. This one needs neither. As for Veriluxx: never heard of them, but the logo says Veritan Linkage, a mostly-Soother lending fund that advocates enslaving people who can't pay their taxes. Odds are it's a way to funnel money to Borant. Carl asks if the whole universe is assholes. Just the ones with the money.

beats.headline: Third, above the cat
beats.text: Miriam and I scale the inside wall of our bubble. A debuff puts the spiders to sleep, and they plummet to their deaths, every one of them, and somehow that finishes the subterranean zone as well. Now we go underwater. The list is posted: third, Prepotente, Caprid, Forsaken Aerialist, level thirty-eight, four hundred thousand. Carl is second. The cat is fourth.

beats.headline: Wall climbers and an absence
beats.text: The recap features the fight on the falling house. Prepotente and Miriam Dom are as far along as Carl's party: they scaled their bubble's inner wall, sent every spider plummeting in its sleep, finished the subterranean zone with it, and are preparing to go underwater. Lucia Mar shatters a multi-limbed ice mummy and is working with a group. Quan Ch has already popped his bubble and is flying around farming every mob he can find. The top ten: Lucia Mar first, Carl second, Prepotente third, Donut fourth. Florin the crocodilian has dropped off it.

beats.headline: Goodbye, from behind the scenes
beats.text: Anyway, the fans really enjoyed that battle. Good job, you two. I'm sorry to say this is goodbye, however. I will still be Loita's assistant, working behind the scenes, but you no longer need a social media manager. Loita explains it: they have bought the social media board, so nobody needs to relay what the dry masses are saying about them. Carl asks whether I can come down so Princess Donut can say goodbye. Loita says no, of course not. He asks whether I can come to the infomercial. Loita says it is not my job anymore.

beats.headline: A commercial that goes off script
beats.text: Before we transfer, I set off a disco ball in the crafting room, a smoke curtain soaked in an invisibility potion, and it coats the robot and me in rainbow dust. In the trailer I lean over Loita to ask whether these things can go into space. I leave robot Donut next to her with orders to stay. On set I go off script and ask about Veriluxx's parent company and slavery, until the lights go red. The couch is gone. Loita is blackened, missing an arm and both lower legs, and alive. She says I did this. I tell her it was an accident.

beats.headline: Coolie's last notes, and Carl's first
beats.text: Three notes by Crawler Coolie, nineteenth edition, run through the pages: a program on a ship in low orbit, its open window held by a forcefield; bugbear paste in his boots for the two admins on his next show; then failure. The admins were holos, the forcefield kept the ship whole, and he wrote as the air thinned, looking down at his planet, Qurux. Beneath them now sits a note from Crawler Carl, twenty-fifth edition: Coolie's passage helped plan the first step, and it was done for him and for a little girl named Bonnie. Then a second note, one word long. One.

beats.headline: The toy on the couch
beats.text: Subject Loita, outreach associate of the Borant Corporation and member of the Bloom, waits in a rented undersea trailer while the crawlers tape a toy commercial, Crawler Carl having left the cat doll beside her with orders to stay. She has just told them that their culture is a rot upon the Bloom, and that bringing Zev back into the fold took unspeakable things done to Zev's mother and aunts. The doll explodes. The trailer's shield holds the cracked window, and repair ships are on their way. Her last words: the Bloom will prevail. Crawler Carl tells her nobody likes melodrama.

beats.headline: What they did to Zev
beats.text: The fish lady will not let me bring Mongo to meet his own doll, and then she tells us why she is so angry. We are dry. We are a rot. And to bring Zev back into the fold, they did unspeakable things to her mother and her aunts, and only then did Zev take the badge. I ask Carl whether she is a complete loon. On set, a lady in a cow-print cape says I am one of her two favorites; the other is Lucia Mar. I read my line: This sure is a hoot. Then the lights go red, and I cannot cast a thing.

beats.headline: A fingernail for a shim
beats.text: Orren's version is polymers, and residue eating a panel. The truth is dumber. The back panel on robot Donut was junk. I cut my left thumbnail three-quarters through, practiced on a spare panel on the toilet, and when I leaned over Loita the second time, I broke the nail off as a shim under the tab. The disco dust was only there so they wouldn't want the doll in the studio. I told it to stay by her, and I gave her a reason to get off the couch. I tell Orren I wish I'd thought of it.

beats.headline: Five days on my own
beats.text: Carl and Donut vanished from chat, Mordecai disappeared, and none of them showed as dead. Once I learned we would not know for days, I took matters into my own hands. The house would not fly to the land quadrant at first. It was the stairwell in the master bedroom; we almost died working that out, and the fix is what Louis did to his mother's minivan. Without the controller Carl left with Louis, we could not have flown it at all. Five days of scorpion men and arguing with Gwen. Level 41. Zev says she is our temporary PR agent.

beats.headline: A liaison hold
beats.text: I didn't think I'd see you again, kid. I got a notice there was a liaison hold on Donut, and then five days were gone. Only the fifth floor, and the liaisons are already involved. By his left tit. Next thing you know, the lawyers will be here, and everything gets complicated once the lawyers get here. A Syndicate liaison, and he let you walk right out? Then the kid pulls Loita's rebreather out of his waistband. He looted it off her body.

beats.headline: He cannot prove it was on purpose
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut have been brought before me at the Desperado Club to account for the death of Loita. My position is that it was deliberate. My position is not evidence. I cannot establish intent, and so I am required to release them, which I am doing, with a note in the file. They have only now worked out how long they have been outside the dungeon. Five days. Their faces are the one part of this I have enjoyed.

beats.headline: Fifteen this season
beats.text: Not counting Administrator Loita, fifteen admins have died to crawlers this season. Crawler Lucia Mar accounts for two, three if one counts her first game guide, which we do not; she signed a confession both times. For every one of them we know exactly how it was done. For this one I can describe a mechanism and cannot establish that it was intended. I offered Crawler Carl a Legendary box for the name of his source. He declined. Until the next floor, no crawler will be teleported out by third parties, and Crawler Carl's next appearance on Odette's program is cancelled. My personal recommendation was not followed.

beats.headline: The liaison under the hood
beats.text: Orren, the Syndicate liaison who questions Carl over Loita's death, lets slip that the kua-tin intervened on the crawler's behalf and overruled his recommendation to remove him, and that the mudskippers are not known for recognising threats. If the rumors are correct and his own people take over after the next floor, he hopes they will listen to him. Then his hood slips. The swirling darkness is a face-shaped bowl of liquid, and in it Carl glimpses a worm. A Valtay worm.

beats.headline: All four castles, and the cost
beats.text: All four castles in my bubble are cleared. I report it in the chat. Most of the people in the bubble did not survive to see it done. How that sits with me is not the kind of thing a chat window was made for, so I leave it out.

beats.headline: Mr. Banana and the flesh weasels
beats.text: Subject and a crawler named Mike, who is dressed as a banana, gather several water-breathing scrolls and leave the saferooms at the top of the subterranean quadrant. In a water-filled tunnel they set off a trap. A tube shoots from the wall, pierces Mike's stomach, and fills him with Finger-sized Flesh Weasels, which eat him from the inside out. Subject retreats quickly. The rest of the party stays in its saferooms, paralyzed, waiting for somebody else to drain the place.

beats.headline: Not as indispensable as I thought
beats.text: The house comes down for us with its whole top half hacked off, because the stairwell was in the master-bedroom closet and the quadrant would not let it leave attached. Firas fills us in. Katia got the house down to the land quadrant and worked out how to breach the castle's door, all without us, and they would be finished already if Zev hadn't asked her to wait. Part of me is proud. Part of me stings that she managed, and I'm horrified I thought it. I decide it's a necessary feeling.

beats.headline: Everybody else in the bubble is dead
beats.text: I finally come out into a quadrant. Everybody else in my bubble is already dead. Not most of them. All of them. That leaves the castles, and one man to take them. I have cleared one so far. I am working my way through the rest. The general view is that I am screwed. I keep going.

beats.headline: Face to face at the sandcastle
beats.text: Crawler Carl lands and finally meets subject: about forty-five, solid, five feet tall, from Canada, a spear over her shoulder, an old double-v tattoo on her forehead and straight-line tattoos down her hands. Level 34 now. Her team has breached the last wall and found a drainage wheel that would wash the castle away, and Crawler Katia has kept her waiting nearly a day so the crawlers can go in the hard way, through the lightning door. Crawler Katia's assessment: once Gwen decides something, she becomes a bully about it.

beats.headline: Holding out for the hard way
beats.text: There are two ways into the sandcastle. Gwen's team found a drainage wheel against the tomb wall: turn it and the water inside blasts out through the drain the castle is built around, and the castle goes like sand under a hose. It also turns the mage, and the winding box, to mud. The hard way is to clip the towers' cables to the door and let the storm's lightning open a glass hallway, once per storm, for a few of us. Zev was unusually insistent that we wait for Carl and Donut, so I made Gwen wait almost a day. Honestly, I would rather do it her way too.

beats.headline: Gustavo, after the battle
beats.text: After a battle, Gustavo kills a group of crawlers. Gustavo is the smaller one. Everybody says he did it by accident. They say accident like it has quotation marks around it. Then I am not all right. I am worse than usual. They show me sitting in a room by myself, and I am crying. They put that on the show.

beats.headline: A cannon full of oil
beats.text: Word reaches Carl through the chat. Meadow Lark are down to the last castle in their bubble, and it is an air castle. The plan is a cannon that shoots oil into the sky, which will hopefully bring it down. If that does not work, Elle is going to use her new Graupel spell to crash the thing. Elsewhere Li Jun and Li Na's team are about to storm an underwater castle, the last in theirs.

beats.headline: Karaoke, and then the curse
beats.text: They put me on a show with Katia and have the two of us sing karaoke. While I am gone, Prepotente has a panic attack and goes berserk and runs off. When I get back I go looking for my boy, and that is when something attacks me and curses me. I was a vegan before all this. The curse has made me a vampire, and I understand the people who chose it for me thought that was very funny.

beats.headline: Horrors near the ocean floor
beats.text: Subject enters the record by name only, relayed by Firas. The water quadrant left two other survivors, Vadim and Britney, and neither wants to go back in. They say there are horrors deep down near the ocean's floor. Firas had told them about Chris. Neither of them was surprised, which is also on file.

beats.headline: Punch him, take the bag
beats.text: Through the peephole the Mad Dune Mage is a guy in a bathrobe watching cartoons, living on top of a floor that is actually a mob. Katia yanks me back when it comes under the door, and my Protective Shell blasts the ooze away and the door with it. Ghazi runs to us, goes back for a leather bag off a burning table, and pats the flames out. I ask if he has the winding box, because the college needs it to save the world. He pats the bag: it's here. I punch him out, take the bag, and we run up the stairs.

beats.headline: What he wanted
beats.text: They come in through the fountain court, three of them and a dinosaur that shatters my Lika where she stands, and then they find me, so you may as well have all of it. Lika is a half-naiad trobairitz out of the stage plays they put on in the city. A bard cleric under a vow of celibacy, played by a different half-naiad every season, based on a minor deity, and not real. I know she is not real. I wanted Yarilo brought back out and asked to make her real, and to make her mine. I told the College of Magecraft I was studying the Gate of the Feral Gods for stable long-distance transport. What answered when I opened it was not Yarilo. It was something else that had learned to wear the name, and it is why this castle is what it is.

beats.headline: Married to the ooze
beats.text: She tricked me. That is the part I want written down. I asked for Lika and the thing married me to the ooze instead, and my wife is still down in my halls being exactly what she is. The doll in the fountain, the one with a soul sitting in it, that is the nearest thing to a real Lika this world ever managed. Carl knocks me flat and takes the winding box off me while I am out. I wake up with a headache and tell them everything anyway, because who else is there to tell.

beats.headline: Under the door
beats.text: Carl has his eye to the peephole and Donut is talking about Juice Box when I see the sand. It is oozing through the bottom of the door and moving its way up the wood. I pull him back and shout for his shell. The spell pushes the ooze back and blasts the door to pieces. Then Carl knocks the mage out, and I catch him before he lands, throw him over my shoulder and carry him up the stairs while the floor follows us.

beats.headline: The glass lady falls
beats.text: Sniff the glass lady. She WOBBLES. BAD. Back away. CRASH. Glass everywhere. Only her head stays. Carl puts the head away.

beats.headline: He had Tish all along
beats.text: The letter from the council is appalling. Ghazi had Tish the whole time, and he left her for Lika, who is a character in a play. When he wakes up I jump on his chest and tell him exactly that. Then he admits the sand ooze is his wife, because he married it, and that the Lika in the fountain was a companion device. Everybody has worked out what kind. I am the first one to say it out loud, because somebody has to.

beats.headline: The floor was the monster
beats.text: Cast on a stairway as a door explodes inward, the shell sweeps the sand off the floor of the room like a broom and uncovers glass beneath. Suddenly the whole room is red on the map. The sand is a mob, and there is no second cast today.

beats.headline: What the council is afraid of
beats.text: A letter from the council of Ghazi's college sets out the fear. What he summoned was not the god of lust but a banished lesser deity pretending to be him, and the scholars believe she only half crossed over. She will occupy the one creature nearby that stands equally between worlds: the ghost queen of the necropolis. If Quetzalcoatlus gains corporeal form, that deity is fully resurrected and the true gods are forced to react. The council's instruction is that Ghazi use the winding box to banish himself, and the entire necropolis, out of this world.

beats.headline: A postscript in another hand
beats.text: Subject exists, at first, as a postscript. Below a council letter to Ghazi, in a different script: Ghazi, you fucking idiot. She told him this would happen. They needed that artifact, without it Scolopendra cannot be defeated, and all he could think about was his cock. She does not forgive him. She was there the whole time, and she guesses she was not enough. She hopes he dies in pain. Do the right thing. Signed, Tish.

beats.headline: So you are from the college
beats.text: Princess Donut read the postscript over Crawler Carl's shoulder and took it personally. When Ghazi came round she jumped on his chest: he had Tish all along, and he left her for Lika, who is not even real. Ghazi's eyes went huge. Tish? So they were from the college? Crawler Carl advised that nobody knew the story beyond one letter. Princess Donut's closing remark on the subject, as Ghazi explained his wife: if Tish could see you now.

beats.headline: The summoning that went wrong
beats.text: Sandcastle of the Mad Dune Mage. Read Ghazi's description and the whole sad story is in it: he wanted the gate so he could reach Yarilo, the banished god of lust, and have Yarilo make Lika love him. Lika is the heroine of a stage play. She was never real. What came through was not Yarilo either. It gave him a wife made of sand, which is why the ooze follows him about, and it left him trapped in his transformed castle with the knowledge of what he has let out. The plaque under his display says my love, my wife. Crawlers, this is the standard outcome of aiming a summoning at a god of lust. Please make notes.

beats.headline: Upside down over the ooze
beats.text: No explosives in the lab, Ghazi says, or the glass comes down on us. So Katia lobs an alarm trap in a metal ball down the stairs to distract the ooze with "Jump Around", Donut holes the floor above, and I go in upside down on Sticky Feet from my toe ring: seventy-something seconds on the ceiling. I pipe Mordecai's burn gel onto the recliner over the core and drop a torch. It burns hotter than I expected. The boss dies just as the roof comes in, and I'm buried upside down in sand.

beats.headline: Flushed into the water quadrant
beats.text: Tran opens the valve part way. The ceiling gives and the water hits like a train. I wrap myself around Donut and we tumble in the flood, my health falling; a spar off the dwarven automaton goes through my leg, and a spear of glass goes through my hand and into Donut. She never took the potion I told her to. Two heal scrolls on her, and we're a hundred and fifty meters down in the water quadrant with dead things sinking all around us. Something big is eating them.

beats.headline: Out of the castle, and no further
beats.text: Ghazi, human, level 43 glass mage, known across the quadrant as the Mad Dune Mage, is dead. The sand ooze went down, the sandcastle came in on itself, and Crawler Katia Grim carried him clear of it.
