She killed him in the open a moment after that, for the notes in his coat explaining how the artifact is worked. He went to sand. Carl and Princess Donut were still buried under the other end of the building and heard none of it.

beats.headline: This is where I point out
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Princess Donut are in the castle's basement with the ceiling coming in when he sends subject a note. She asks whether he means electrify it. No, he answers, hurry. Tran opens the valve part way, and the castle goes like sand under a garden hose, taking the two of them down into the water quadrant with it. Subject's first message afterwards: this is where she points out that if he had simply let her open the valve in the first place, they could have avoided whatever that was.

beats.headline: Too hot for this job
beats.text: Two jugs left. The sand ooze's core sits under the recliner, and ordinary fire is no good: the ooze has already snuffed out the flames left by Crawler Donut's spell. It needs something that burns hot, and Crawler Carl fears the jugs would burn a little too hot. He uses burn gel instead, a cookbook recipe that Mordecai showed him how to improve. With moonshine and a paste of his, it burns hot and bright with little smoke.

beats.headline: She kills Ghazi and takes his notes
beats.text: The sand ooze is dead and the walls are coming in. I get out with Ghazi. Then I kill him, for the notes that explain how the Gate works. Carl and Donut are still buried when I do it. I know how that sounds.

beats.headline: Do not let it touch you
beats.text: Do not let it touch you. Once a sand ooze gets ahold of you it's like quicksand, and Carl's already burned his Protective Shell. It won't just suffocate you, kid. It pours sand into every opening you've got until you burst, and he's wearing boxers. They hunt by vibration and sound, not heat, so clomping across a ceiling will still get noticed; he'll need one of the toys he was building. And I wouldn't trust a guy who married an ooze. Katia, watch him while Carl's in there.

beats.headline: I bite his foot and pull
beats.text: The floor breaks right after I cast my Hole spell, and I fall through with it, and there is sand all around me. Carl is buried upside down, so I bite down on his foot and drag him out. Then we are in a tiny space under three floors of sand, and I did not get to say goodbye to Mongo, and he is just going to sit in his pet carrier forever. And all Carl will ask me is how many water-breathing scrolls I have. Eight.

beats.headline: He opens the valve
beats.text: Carl and Donut are under the sand in the castle's basement, and the ceiling is about to come in. Carl sends Gwen a note. I open the valve, only part way. The water in the necropolis comes out through the drain the castle is built around, the castle washes away like sand under a hose, and everything in there, the two of them included, goes with the water into the ocean.

beats.headline: The second-to-last drawing
beats.text: Ghazi's note ends mid-sentence on a missing page, but the last page is drawings: two watches, the winding box, two gates, every combination and what happens. All but one end with a monster coming out on the opening side. Katia points at the circled one, where we lose the box and nothing gets out. I'm stuck on the second-to-last. I put that away and ask Mordecai whether a feral god could leave the bubble, or break the wall. Then I ask if there's a Desperado Club in this town.

beats.headline: A gate to the ninth floor
beats.text: The mage's notes list times standing for places, all of them around the city of Larracos. Katia works out it could open onto the ninth floor — and Mordecai points out that crawlers cannot hop floors, so all that would accomplish is releasing whatever awful thing comes through when it shuts.

beats.headline: She turns the watches into a map
beats.text: The linked watches read as a reverse compass: a time, an altitude, an exact position relative to anywhere else. Which means the Gate could open onto the city of Larracos, on the ninth floor, and I am mapping ground nobody has stood on.

beats.headline: A city named on the surface
beats.text: Carl and Donut come up out of the water with the concierge sharks behind them and once they reach a town that will take them in, Katia reads the Mad Dune Mage's page of numbers as places the Gate can open onto, every one of them around Larracos, the capital city four floors below them. Mordecai points out that a crawler cannot use it to skip ahead. All it would do is let something out.

beats.headline: Two potions he should not drink
beats.text: Carl's Pacifist box gives him two Potions of Bloodlust. Double strength, double speed, half dexterity, half constitution, and a debuff that means you don't remember where you are or why you're fighting. Don't use those. The last time I saw someone drink that potion, they accidentally killed half of their party. And don't get ideas about the gate either, kid. Crawlers can't hop floors. If you ever get the last watch, stick it in your inventory until you're strong enough to deal with whatever comes out. Which will be never.

beats.headline: A town that would take them in
beats.text: After the sandcastle the party had to track a quarter turn around the land quadrant before any town would let them in. This one did. Its people are pazuzu, half human and half scorpion, built like centaurs and dressed as though the world already ended: punk leather, tassels, goggles, chains and dreadlocks, all bound for a Mad Max convention. Louis and Firas went off to sleep, Louis grumbling about the drink. Once Mordecai walked off, Carl's question about the place was whether it had a Desperado Club.

beats.headline: Worse than the danger dingo
beats.text: I wake up underwater. Completely underwater. I cannot swim; my legs only tread. I stop screaming only because Carl says Mongo needs me. Then I see a shark down there, and more coming, which is a betrayal worse than when he gave my pet biscuits to that danger dingo. Then he says "Hekla", so I cast Second Chance on a dead beluga and Clockwork Triplicate on top, and send them at the shark, and they explode. In the kayak a small fish comes out of me. The box gives me a Belt of Buoyancy. I am never going back there.

beats.headline: A letter addressed to her
beats.text: The pages Katia Grim took off the Mad Dune Mage open as a letter to subject. I know you hate me, but please listen. Hope is not lost. He writes that he was asked to use the box to pull the whole island into the Nothing, and refused, because all three pieces of the artifact would go with it. He sets out how the gate works. If his plan succeeds he dies, and she receives the letter with the winding box and can send another expedition.

beats.headline: The only place they can die
beats.text: I flip Katia's map over and ask Mordecai if it's right. He draws nine petals round Larracos: a city dug deep like an inverted cone, a faction in each petal, fifteen thousand troops apiece, mostly NPCs. The real people there can't die; the system pulls them out first. Then the questions I actually care about. Hunters sign up until the sixth floor opens, and start at level thirty. And that floor is the only place in the game where these rich tourists can really die. Katia asks why she gets the feeling I'm about to do something really stupid.

beats.headline: How to work it
beats.text: Dial a time standing for a place on one watch and the other mirrors it. Both go in the box, which winds and must not be moved or the count resets. Pulling the watches out opens a one-way portal, good for roughly twenty minutes. Afterwards it lingers where it was opened as a two-way passage into the Nothing until something comes through — often a feral god. A weak constitution too near an open portal gets painted with the feral madness.

beats.headline: She planned it from inside the doll
beats.text: I think I see it. When she first escaped, half of her went into the love doll, the closest thing to her real form she could find. So she was the one who talked Ghazi into coming here, and let him think he was calling the god of lust. When he opened the way, her second half came out with the sand ooze. Then something went wrong, the doll was turned to glass with everything else, and she had to use the ooze to keep him here. The scholars thought she had gone into Quetzalcoatlus. Nobody knew there were two halves.

beats.headline: Keep her, as a trainer
beats.text: A withering spirit. Sometimes a soul gets split, and the two halves try to reunite in a proper vessel; when that goes wrong, you get this. Not alive, not dead, hard to kill, mostly harmless, haunting the object. They use them as quest-givers a lot. We avoid gods like we avoid outside factions. And then, knowing I'll regret it, I say we keep her. In the saferoom she can't summon anything, and a minor deity may know potions. Donut can hire her as a trainer. She'll live in a corner of the training room.

beats.headline: In charge of the death charges
beats.text: Carl says I take two or three showers a day, so the ocean is no different. It is entirely different, and it is not happening again, and there is not a thing in this world he can say to change my mind. Then he admits he is teasing. I will only have to float over the water in the house and be in charge of the depth charges. I do like the death charges. And since Zev has her job back, I can check my social media board again.

beats.headline: The head from Ghazi's castle
beats.text: Yes, I am a head. Yes, THAT kind of head. Get it out of your system. I am Psamathe, or the half of her that got stuck when I tried to climb out of the Nothing, and what I got stuck in is a Lika doll from Ghazi's castle, crystallised until now. Withering spirit, the system calls it. Carl carried me here in his pack like a snack. Now he is HIRING me. A goddess. As a trainer. Kept in the safe room. Fine. FINE. I want a mirror.

beats.headline: What escaping it costs
beats.text: Psamathe tried to get out and ended up as half a soul in a doll's head. Every closing Gate portal lets one of the inmates through on the opening side. The winding box alone is a direct conduit — wound and fed a stream of charged energy it will drop an entire location, up to a whole necropolis, into the void.

beats.headline: Tish almost ruined everything
beats.text: Princess Donut, to the doll head of Samantha: she does feel bad for Tish, who really seemed to like him. Samantha's view differs. Tish? Tish almost ruined everything. Take me to her. Crawler Carl completed the sentence for her with the threat Samantha uses on everyone, the one about mothers, and Samantha burst into tears.

beats.headline: Two new crawlers
beats.text: Vadim and I have fallen in with Carl's team. Introductions here are short. Everyone counts heads, adds two, moves on. The first real conversation I hear is Katia telling Carl that pregnant women could not enter the dungeon, and that nobody inside it can get pregnant. Said flat. Like weather. That is the kind of thing people know here, and say out loud. I am going to have to get used to that.

beats.headline: A ghost on the bridge
beats.text: Inside the Akula, a door Vadim swears they left open is dogged shut. Past the airlock, under a floor grate, I loot the neighborhood boss, a little box somebody had to destroy to turn the sentinel gun off, and the whole sub fills in on my map. Corpses on the bridge. And one red dot flickering between the bridge and a chamber outside the quadrant entirely. A ghost that shouldn't be in here. A glowing green pterodactyl head screams through the bulkhead, my vision flashes red, and Vadim drops with his health in the red.

beats.headline: The diving bell
beats.text: I make a diving bell I have never made before, on the spot, hanging off the corner of the house: more an elevator than a bell, three poles for Carl, Tran and Vadim to hold, a ring of dense metal at the bottom so I do not flip. We drop at about five meters a second. Five hundred meters down I open like a flower on the hull of the Akula, spread myself over it as camouflage and stay outside to watch while they go in. Something swims by underneath. It is bigger than the submarine.

beats.headline: The Death Stalker
beats.text: Smaller than Hump Town, with several inns and taverns. No Desperado Club, but a Club Vanquisher, currently closed for cleansing after Prepotente set his hellspawn goat loose in the main lounge over Miriam Dom's revoked membership. So the party met at The Death Stalker: a few tables, a bar and, inexplicably, a gelato cart with about twenty flavours. Donut talked the pazuzu down from two gold to one for a bowl of raspberry. Two crawlers from the water quadrant joined them at the table.

beats.headline: The club revokes Miriam
beats.text: The club revokes Miriam's membership because she is a vampire now. As if that were her doing, as if any of you idiots chose what you are. So I let our third companion loose in the main lounge. It devoured a number of clerics before the rest had the sense to flee. There is a Holy Crusade Bounty on the three of us now, whatever that is supposed to mean, and the club is shut while they cleanse it.

beats.headline: Shuruga36
beats.text: A viewer called Shuruga36 says I have no redeeming qualities whatsoever, that I ruined the viewing experience and almost made him stop watching, and that Donut and her stupid dino-chicken irritate him to no end. Mongo is a child. I can take criticism, but picking on a child is uncalled for. Then I hit the detonator for the chum bombs and go up a level, to 38. Before they drop, I tell Carl and Katia to be safe, because it is horrible down there.

beats.headline: Out of her tomb
beats.text: Quetzalcoatlus is not confined to her tomb. She is on the flooded submarine's bridge, flickering between it and the chamber on the far side of the hull, and she does not like visitors. Her scream is an aural attack: one shriek through the bulkhead reddens Crawler Carl's vision and drops Vadim Zbar into the red. Then she shoots out of the side of the sub, strikes something enormous in the water below, and flies back toward the temple. The thing she struck comes for the sub.

beats.headline: Class: Gut Rearranger
beats.text: Subject: a level-28 spotted, gecko-like Kuhli, which Crawler Carl believes is a fish. Class: Gut Rearranger, a healer and rogue. Sheaths of daggers from head to toe. Cosmetic surgeon in the old world; Crawler Britney was in his office for a consultation when the collapse came, and the two of them were outside taking before photos. At the tavern Crawler Britney said she would rather die than go back into the water. Asked the same, subject said: I'll go. Crawler Tran asked him whether he owned a red shirt.

beats.headline: Fifty children, reportedly
beats.text: Gossip entered into the file via Langley, via Katia Grim. Doctor Vadim was, or had been, famous in the Ukraine: television commercials, billboards, clinics, and lawsuits over botched surgeries. Langley says he has something like fifty children and is known for impregnating his clients. Crawler Carl concluded that if true, subject was a weasel, and not someone to go into danger with while carrying a bounty. Subject's own manner through all the briefings: matter-of-fact and emotionless. He was going anyway.

beats.headline: The way into the Akula
beats.text: Subject supplied the route. The Akula lies 500 meters down, nose fastened to the necropolis, its torpedo tubes pumping the ocean in. A docked mini-sub blew after his party took the bridge. He and Britney had free dived those depths on water-breathing scrolls. His map showed monster types, never the full sub. He rode down in Katia Grim's diving bell, cast Torch as they entered, and led the way in. Crawler Carl kept him in front on purpose, lest he lead the party into a trap.

beats.headline: Chris never talked much
beats.text: Swimming the flooded corridors, subject gave his account of the first assault. Skeletons of bugbears, robots, and only three survivors. Chris was higher level, never talked much, fought fiercely and without emotion, insulted them when they did not do as he said; Britney never liked him. Chris took the boss's note, with the key code to the escape tubes, and did not show it to them. At the bridge a ghost screamed through the bulkhead, and subject went down with his health in the red. Tran healed him.

beats.headline: Depth charges, and everyone inside
beats.text: Something drags the Akula out of its hole and down to fifteen hundred meters. I take Henrik's body whole, watch and all. Then a sharktopus the size of a mountain comes at the window, the world freezes, and it's a Special Event boss battle with a pair of commentators. I tell Donut to drop the depth charges at maximum depth, Louis and Firas to land and get to a saferoom, and Gwen, the tomb raiders and Langley to do the same. Donut asks if the death charges will hit us too. I really hope not.

beats.headline: Locked, then released
beats.text: The moment Carl takes Henrik's body into his inventory, and the watch with it, the world freezes. An admin notice flashes past: three items are under an administrative lock while an appeal in the Syndicate court decides whether they are eligible. A second notice follows before the first has finished: lack of standing for all plaintiffs, lock removed, apologies for the inconvenience. Several someones would like the three pieces out of his hands. For now, they have lost.

beats.headline: The body in the submarine
beats.text: Henrik of Hump Town, changeling, is dead, and has been for some time. Katia Grim runs into the flooded submarine to get away from a sharktopus, and Carl finds the body already sitting in there with its piece of the Gate of the Feral Gods still on it. One magically linked pocket watch, recovered. Also on him: a note recording that Quetzalcoatlus can be put down with an electric shock. Whatever else he was doing, he was still working that problem right up to the finish of him.

beats.headline: Too late to surface
beats.text: Carl tells me to blow my ballast and get to the surface. It is already too late; the big thing is reaching for the sub. So instead of going up I go in, through the torn-open top and down the corridors toward them, and wait in the airlock while it drains, which takes almost a full minute. Carl swears at me over chat. I would not have gotten away. Then I bring Tran and Vadim through, and the three of us stand at the bridge window and watch the second monster come.

beats.headline: The recap guy has a name
beats.text: Subject hosts the recap. He is orange-hued and four-eyed and built along lizard lines, and he delivers the rundown of each floor at a pace that does not permit anyone watching to think about what is being described. Tonight he also takes the live commentary, beside an orc in a sportscoat, and the orc says his name on air: Kevin. I have worked with him for a long time and I have never heard him ask a question he did not already have the answer card for.

beats.headline: Something covering the port
beats.text: The Akula was pulled free of its hole in the necropolis and dragged down past 550 meters, with boss music playing and no boss yet. A sucker the size of half the bridge window pressed against the glass. Then subject came into view: a shark the size of a mountain, glowing, tentacles flowing behind. Crawler Carl identified it as a sharktopus and observed that Princess Donut would be angry to have missed it. His second observation was that this was not good.

beats.headline: Straight from Hayes 17
beats.text: A Special Event boss battle, streamed to subscribers, in a new beta format with live commentary from Kevin and Magnificent Troy. It's Lusca, Kevin shouted, taken from the depths of the water moon Hayes 17. My own description, for the record: Octo-Shark Brood Mother Queen, level 82 City Boss, a single mother carrying a boatload of hungry babies in her mouth. The male who dragged the crawlers down already got his and is long gone. Lusca herself already ate. The babies, however, need feeding.

beats.headline: Ten minutes for the babies
beats.text: Subject is a mouthbrooder, per Magnificent Troy's diagram. She had snapped the Akula in half, and the crawlers were floating in her mouth. Once she clamps onto something, her babies get about ten minutes to eat their fill, and whatever is left goes to mama. The cartoon that followed showed the rest of the process in several stomachs, ending with a skeleton in heart-covered boxers and a crying cartoon Donut. Both announcers fell about laughing. A ten minute timer slammed onto the screen.

beats.headline: How to put her down
beats.text: A note comes off a body in the flooded submarine and it is the answer to her. Quetzalcoatlus can be finished with an electric shock. A wailing shrieker takes banishment, exorcism, a current, or the destruction of her lover's corpse, and of those four exactly one is lying around this quadrant with the power still running to it.

beats.headline: Pulled out of the hole
beats.text: The Akula was torn free of the necropolis and dragged into the deep. The hull rolled onto its side and subject fell with Crawler Tran into the room behind the bridge. Crawler Carl called them through to loot the dead changelings and make for the last escape hatch. The four of them then stood looking out of the bridge window at something the size of a mountain. Subject's mugshot went up on the special event broadcast beside the others.

beats.headline: Bloodlust in the fridge
beats.text: Inside the octo-shark's mouth, a ten-minute timer, thousands of babies hammering at the bridge window. I tape a Potion of Bloodlust to a hob-lobber, duct-tape it inside the bolted minifridge, and seal Katia, Tran and me in the captain's stateroom. The window goes. Something on the other side starts turning the wheel on our door, so I hold it with one hand and hit the detonator with the other. One X on the map. Ten. Thousands. They may be babies, and half octopus. They're still sharks.

beats.headline: A shell down her throat
beats.text: When the timer hits zero, Lusca lifts her head to swallow the Akula, and I cast Protective Shell. I want it to go through her like a bullet. Instead it stops her dead, like she's hit a wall that won't move, and peels her upper jaw back over her own eyes, and every baby left in her mouth dies at once. Then we're pinwheeling on Katia's rocket and buzzsaw, out of her mouth and back through her head. Winner. Then a warning that at this depth I'm losing two percent of my health a second.

beats.headline: What the word means
beats.text: The keyword marks a thing that has been inside the Nothing. The old gods went in at the making of the world and have had every century since to come apart. Duration is not required: standing too near an open portal will do it, and a weak mind takes the stain fastest.

beats.headline: One gets out over the water quadrant
beats.text: Carl steps himself, Katia and Tran off the ocean floor through the Gate, and the Gate shuts behind them. Something comes the other way on the opening side: a god, feral, loose in a sealed bubble with a town in it. The achievement that follows warns that other gods do not like feral ones, and tend to react.

beats.headline: Out of Lusca, and an ocean with it
beats.text: Carl, Katia and Tran kill Lusca and her babies at the bottom of the water quadrant. Carl opens the Gate and takes the three of them to the surface outside the pazuzu town of Pandinus. A spray of ocean comes through in the few seconds the portal is open and knocks over the town wall and a guard tower. A feral god is loose, and the System's achievement warns that other gods tend to react.

beats.headline: Leatherface, underwater
beats.text: Carl calls Leatherface. The move is made for the flying house, and I do not have the mass for it, so I just hold on: braces around Carl and Tran, the steam rocket wrapped in my flesh, and the twenty-five-foot buzzsaw out of my inventory, running. We spin the wrong way, out of her mouth, then back through her snout, and the saw cuts through her like a hot knife. It is her brain we hit. One of her tentacles slams us into the sea floor, the saw buries itself, and I let go.

beats.headline: The babies turn on each other
beats.text: Juvenile Octo-Shark, level 30, minion of Lusca. In each birthing of two to three thousand pups, one or two survive, because in time they learn their siblings are delicious. Crawler Carl's depth charges landed a direct hit; Kevin said she would shrug them off. Then Crawler Carl set off a potion of bloodlust in the water, the babies went into a feeding frenzy, and the kill markers multiplied. Subject swam on in circles around the quadrant at about 35 kilometers per hour. Crawler Carl wondered whether she knew most of her babies were now dead.

beats.headline: Mama swallows the Akula
beats.text: The timer hit zero and subject raised her head to swallow the Akula whole. At that moment Crawler Carl fired his shell spell down her throat. It did not punch through as intended. She stopped dead in the water, as if she had hit a wall; her upper jaw bent back over her own eyes, cartilage snapping, and teeth shattered as the spell drove her into the ocean floor. Every remaining baby died as the inside of her mouth turned outside. She was grievously wounded. She was not yet dead.

beats.headline: Cleaved through the brain
beats.text: Katia Grim fired a rocket and held on to a live twenty-five-foot buzzsaw, and the three crawlers pinwheeled out of subject's mouth and back through her exposed upper snout, cutting her like a hot knife through calamari, until one of her tentacles slammed them into the seabed. Lusca, the Octo-Shark, now floats on her side on the ocean floor, upper jaw peeled back and split, a jagged red line through her tiny little brain. Winner. From her corpse: a Map of the Stars.

beats.headline: A wall of water
beats.text: Carl dialled the Gate of the Feral Gods to a spot just outside town, and he, Katia and Tran splashed out onto the beach inside a wall of seawater. The portal was open three or four seconds. That was enough to topple the metal wall, knock over a guard tower and put a chunk of metal through one pazuzu's front door like a javelin. Any longer and the town would have gone the way of the sandcastle. They ran for the nearest inn, past a staring bartender.

beats.headline: Up a level for doing nothing
beats.text: Carl wants to know if we are almost back. We are not. The wind starts early and blows wrong, Firas says, and we keep getting higher and higher, so we have to go back to Hump Town, and Louis says ten minutes. Then I go up a level, and I did not even do anything. I should stay back more often. This is great. When Carl finally falls into the personal space he is sopping wet. He smells terrible, and he has seaweed in his hair.

beats.headline: Straight down a city boss
beats.text: Swallowed along with a submarine, Crawler Carl casts in the throat of an enormous shark. The static sphere, about twelve metres across by now, shoots away as the shark swims on. He hoped for a bullet through the brain. Instead the boss stops dead, as if it had hit a wall; the top of its mouth peels back over its own eyes, teeth shatter, and the immovable spell pushes it down into the ocean floor. Grievously wounded, it is not yet dead.

beats.headline: Pus by the set
beats.text: Supplier note. On the Silk Road, Crawler Carl bought a few sets of hobgoblin pus from Pustule, the magical detonator, and he is burning through the expensive stuff. Inside a submarine a city boss is about to swallow, he yanks the fuse from a hob-lobber, fits a piece of pus in its place, duct-tapes a potion to it, and seals the lot in the captain's minifridge.

beats.headline: One of the three who go through the Gate
beats.text: Vadim ran. That leaves Carl, Katia and me against Lusca and all of her babies, and we kill her, and then we kill them. Then Carl opens the Gate. One step and the three of us are out of the water quadrant and standing in town. Something came through behind us. A god, the feral kind. That is going to be somebody's problem.

beats.headline: Up the stairs, alone
beats.text: The lights on the bridge went out. Crawler Carl called for Torch. The broadcaster Kevin answered instead: Vadim is running away, and Carl has not noticed yet. Subject had gone up the stairs toward the one remaining escape pod. Crawler Carl messaged him that they were inside the shark and the hatch would not work. Subject did not answer. Crawler Carl sealed his own group in the stateroom and had Crawler Tran tell subject to seal himself in upstairs. Subject did so, and kept not answering.

beats.headline: The last escape pod
beats.text: After the boss fell, subject answered. I'm sorry. I panicked. I sealed the room. The door would not reopen with water behind it, and his oxygen warning gave him five minutes. Crawler Carl told him to raise a shield spell, then suggested blowing the hatch for him instead. The pod launched, curved upward, and punched through the top of the shark into a sky of giant jellyfish. Oh god, they're in the pod with me. The pain amplifier. Warning: This message is from a deceased crawler.

beats.headline: He went anyway
beats.text: I came in with the cat, off the flying house. I'm in the corner where the crafting room meets the back wall. Vadim is dead. I told him not to go. Everybody who goes down there dies; I said it at the table, in front of all of them. He said he'd go. He said it twice. He went.

beats.headline: A patch jacket and a dead man's kerchief
beats.text: Three levels, to 47. The gold boss box gives me Drakea's Enchanted Kerchief of Disorder: plus five Detect Traps, a level-15 Tripper once every five hours, and Remote Detonator, which means no more hobgoblin pus. Drakea wrote the twenty-second edition of the cookbook, and I need to pretend I've never heard the name. My hands shake. The platinum Spicy box gives me the Enchanted Anarchist's Battle Rattle, a sleeveless patch jacket, with an Earth patch to sew on. Apart from my zippo, the old leather jacket was the last thing I had from before. It can go.

beats.headline: Photographs of their mothers
beats.text: Seven silver Summary Judgement boxes, and each one holds a gold piece, a single share of stock in a company from one plaintiff's system, and a photograph of that plaintiff's mother. The first is Queen Consort Ugloo, mother of Prince Stalwart of the Skull Empire. It's the kind of thing middle-school kids do. It's also valuable. I now know seven of the factions that tried to take the gate off me, and since the nagas didn't sue and will be there anyway, eight of the nine teams waiting on the ninth floor.

beats.headline: The twenty-second hand on the cookbook
beats.text: Subject wrote the twenty-second edition of the cookbook and crawled in the final Naga-controlled season, which ended in some sort of cataclysm. Subject’s gear is still being handed out as prizes, a kerchief today, which is the only immortality this production offers.

beats.headline: A god walked through our world
beats.text: We finally pop our bubble, and a god taller than the whole place walks straight through it. On fire. Flattens a Lyrx elf village, knocks over two of their oil derricks and lights them. Half the world is in flames. Imani and I are stuck in the Desperado; nearly everybody else had to run for the stairwell, and we're lucky nobody caught fire. He's looking for something. He keeps shouting "Orthrus." Something tells me this is Carl's doing, and I say so. He says maybe. Well, you better fix it.

beats.headline: Seven factions sue, and lose
beats.text: Seven of the faction-wars factions take Carl and the AI to Syndicate court to stop what he means to do with it, and lose. Carl collects seven Fight the Power achievements, and each of the seven Summary Judgement boxes pays out a gold piece, one share of stock and a photograph of a plaintiff's mother.

beats.headline: A backpack of my own
beats.text: Three levels for me too, to 44. The gold boss box gives me a backpack: much the same as the one Carl designed for my mass, but adjustable, so I can carry even more, and it will not break. It gives me a stability enhancement while I wear it and has retractable stilts, so I can add mass far more quickly. It is good. Carl got all the best things this time. He says we should have tried to swim out. Donut says they never gave us a choice.

beats.headline: The Twister, and a photo
beats.text: Okay so, the AI gave Carl pictures of a bunch of alien moms, and one of them is this angry bald elf lady with blue eyes and she's the hottest thing I've ever seen, so I ask Juice Box for another session where she looks like her. Carl rips the photo out of my hands. Also the house has a name now. The Twister. I wanted Tiddy Twister II, after my van, which was my mom's van until I chopped the top off, but Firas says we're trying to be more mature. And Katia wouldn't let us.

beats.headline: Drakea was a bune
beats.text: I remember Drakea. A bune: a slight, dragon-like people, peaceful by nature, some of the cleverest fighters there are. Class like Carl's, but more magic. A big trap guy. He died on the eleventh floor. Or was it the twelfth? He'd had a pretty good offer and spat in their faces, and then his setup backfired. Unnaturally backfired. Lawyers got involved, and the Syndicate, acting on his behalf, collected a big sum from the Sultanate.

beats.headline: Going primal
beats.text: The AI handing out stock and pictures of plaintiffs' mothers is worrisome. It's supposed to help monitor prohibited speech against the sponsors, not go all in and participate. That usually happens, but at the end, when the system has gone bonkers around the twelfth floor. All large-scale AIs go insane, given time; there's even a term for it, Primal Degeneration. And no, kid, nobody takes it out behind the woodshed. A Macro AI is a lifeform, protected by Syndicate law. It gets its own sealed system to bounce around in for the rest of eternity.

beats.headline: A teacher who does not remember teaching
beats.text: Juice Box takes the news of Henrik's death sadly and then, strangely, happily. She tells Donut she has been dreaming of being a school teacher, and of people who came in and had to kill all of her students because the children were spreading a disease. In it she touched one of the killers, a dragon-headed man, and she can turn into one of his kind though she has never touched one awake. Louis tells her she might be remembering her last time in the dungeon. Donut has seen this before, with Fire Brandy and Tizquick.

beats.headline: Something outside is looking for a dog
beats.text: Crawler Elle McGibbons reports in from a popped bubble: there is a deity outside, taking the landscape apart, and it is searching. Not hunting crawlers. Searching. The thing it has lost is called Orthrus. Every crawler on this floor is working out how to survive their own bubble, and the largest event on my board is a god who has misplaced a pet.

beats.headline: Juice Box is remembering
beats.text: Carl, remember Fire Brandy and that dwarf, when they started to remember? It is happening to Juice Box. When we told her that her brother had died she was sad at first, and then she got really happy. She has been dreaming that she was a school teacher, and some people came in and had to kill all her students because the children were spreading a disease, and she touched one of them, a dragon-headed man. Louis told her she might be remembering her last time in the dungeon. She got a funny look on her face.

beats.headline: My great uncle wants his dog
beats.text: Oh, this is DELICIOUS. Feather boy tells me who's rampaging out there, and I know him. My great uncle. And my cousin, I think; it gets confusing. Blind: plucked out his own eyes when his favorite son died. He's yelling for Orthrus, which means YOU let Orthrus out, his little doggie, sucked in by accident when the son was murdered. He once destroyed an entire country over a drunk who peed on a torch. Woke up a volcano. Don't expect a reward. You are all so fucking dead.

beats.headline: Co-defendants, and victorious
beats.text: Crawler Carl and I have been named co-defendants in an action brought to the Syndicate Court by a third party. Seven times! And we have been deemed, drum roll please, victorious. Crawlers usually lose these, being slaves and all, and I'd throw him under the bus quicker than you can say Arch Support. Not today. Seven Fight the Power achievements, seven Silver Summary Judgement boxes. He also got eaten by something much bigger than himself and came out unchewed, so that's Soft Vore and a Platinum Spicy Box. I think it moved.

beats.headline: Seven factions lose in court
beats.text: Seven factions sue to take the Gate of the Feral Gods from Carl, naming him and the AI as co-defendants, and the Syndicate Court finds for the defence. He collects seven Fight the Power achievements, stock certificates, and photographs of the plaintiffs' mothers.

beats.headline: A hundred and sixty inside, and an eye socket
beats.text: Crawler Tserendolgor is crawling along the inside of her bubble wall, looking for the slot for the final gem, when a giant empty eye socket appears on the other side. It calls her Orthrus and starts screaming, then pounding on the wall. Her world is heating up; the mountain walls are beginning to glow, and in the same bubble a saferoom door is glowing red. She posts to the main chat. There are 160 of them in there and they have not lost a person yet. They were almost done.

beats.headline: Crushed in the tomb
beats.text: Crawler Bobby has been eliminated in the necropolis. He had already told the quest chat he was done, that it was too much, and he was still possessed by a ghost when two of his teammates scratched theirs out on Crawler Carl's advice. The three survivors of the tomb raiders were scattered through the crypt by then, and two of them were on a job for Carl. The tomb has crushers in it; Janice had already walked into one. Morris Sp reports Bobby gone. Cause of death, as reported: crushed.

beats.headline: He sends Morris down the ladder
beats.text: The lightning towers glow and do nothing. The last piece is a panel under the necropolis, still underwater, and the only crawlers who can reach it are what is left of the tomb raiders. I tell Morris to connect it and get out of the water before the next strike. Low Thi goes to distract Quetzalcoatlus, and the boss goes straight through him and turns back for Morris. Morris gets it connected. Both of their last messages come up marked as from a deceased crawler. The quadrant is liberated. I knew they were probably going to die, and I sent them anyway.

beats.headline: Enslaved, and muted
beats.text: The group quest list shows two names at the bottom, separated: Maggie My, and Chris Andrews 2, Enslaved. The enslaved can still chat. While Crawler Donut shouts at Maggie, Chris types, "Donut. Please." They are out of the chamber, he reports: down a ladder, a wire in the water disconnected, a group of crawlers attacked and one of them killed. Then: "Maggie is cheating. She has outside help. A cap…" Chris has been muted from chat, and his previous notes disappear from the log.

beats.headline: Hailed in the throne room
beats.text: Sandstorm, feral pazuzu, and subject and Crawler Katia moving as one, like a pair of pack hunters, after days of fighting these mobs together. Crawler Carl had subject run the long lead from the drain to the lightning tower. The strike turns the beach to glass around their ankles and sends the current through the temple's water. Bubble Notification: the subterranean quadrant is liberated, and the crawlers hailed for the throne room are Gwendolyn Duet, Low Thi and Morris Sp.

beats.headline: Riding the Twister through the storm
beats.text: Okay so, Carl wants me and Firas out in the storm, in the flying house, keeping behind the dog's heads while Donut heals it. In the storm, man. The balloon is slamming back and forth. Whiplash. It's like riding a bull, and Firas says he did that once and fell off. Then he sees half the bowl break away, the side with the Bactrian village, just gone. The net's shot, so we have to land to fix it. No choice. I'm up on the roof telling Carl this thing's going to fall out of the sky if we don't.

beats.headline: The Akula's cheat
beats.text: Addendum. Crawler Carl holds that each of the bubble's four quadrants was built with a cheat, a quick way to kill everything: the knock-knocks under the Wasteland, the hidden drain on the sandcastle, the lightning tower for the final castle. He was never sure what the easy win for the Akula was meant to be. He suspects it had something to do with subject.

beats.headline: He lands inside the bubble
beats.text: Orthrus is now inside the bubble with Crawler Carl's team, and everyone in there has been handed the Where the Red God Glows quest to go with him. Around the edges of it: Maggie My is loose somewhere up on the bowl, and Princess Donut spends the whole thing trying to keep an enormous two-headed puppy alive. Everyone is very busy. Nobody is looking at the same emergency.

beats.headline: The one god down here who can die
beats.text: The file on him, since he is going to matter. Orthrus is a juvenile gate guardian, level 10, kid brother to the three-headed one who guards a stairwell exit a long way below this one. He was on course to become a vicious, baby-eating, nun-defiling murder machine, and then in a single day his master was murdered and he was pulled into the Nothing. Most things the Nothing touches come out ruined. He came out unaffected, because he is too innocent for it to take hold, and fire does nothing to him at all. Here is the line that matters to a crawler: unlike other gods, he is not invulnerable. He is a puppy. Happy, destructive, rambunctious, roly-poly, very pokey. Fragile.

beats.headline: Feral pazuzu out of the sand
beats.text: Night, a rising storm, waves slapping the pub windows, and the pazuzu barkeep huddled behind his bar pointing outside with a shaking hand. When the giant dog jumped, a stone statue off the necropolis crushed a pazuzu hut two hundred feet away. Then a wave of feral pazuzu came up through the sand. Carl caught one stinger in his hand, immune to the venom but not to the hole, tore off the tip, and stabbed its owner in the neck with it.

beats.headline: The quest chat, and the flying house
beats.text: CARL wants me to keep the revolting two-headed dog alive, because I am the only one with the spell. Then there is a quest chat, with everybody in the bubble on it, and Maggie My is on it, so I tell her exactly what she is. Worse than the lady who fed Peanut's Splendid Flavor no meat. Worse than all of them combined. Chris keeps typing my name. Then the spell says I am too far away from the dog, so I go up in the flying house with Louis and Firas, in a storm. Heal Critter works. I cannot believe it. The stupid dog does not even appreciate it.

beats.headline: The panel in the tomb
beats.text: Quetzalcoatlus is finished. Morris Sp went down the ladder to the submerged panel knowing what the next lightning strike would do to anyone still in the water, connected it, and the current did precisely what the cleric's journal said it would. The Subterranean Quadrant is liberated and the bubble pops. Its crawlers are all named in the notice: Gwendolyn Duet, Low Thi, Morris Sp. Every one of them is dead. That was the price the floor quoted, and they paid it without renegotiating.

beats.headline: Flying a gnome biplane
beats.text: There is nowhere to take off, so Louis and Firas fly the house out over the water and I roll the drop bear off the edge of the yard. We drop like a rock, the wind catches us, and she climbs. Yoke, pedals, twin throttles, a fuel gauge and a gyroscope I do not understand. Biplane Pilot goes to three. Then I work out the gyroscope: dot in the middle means level, and the little lock on it is a crude autopilot. The whole plane still vibrates like it wants to come apart.

beats.headline: Sinjin on worshipping a god
beats.text: Sinjin, fifteenth edition, worshipped the goddess Kuraokami and called it the worst decision ever. The rules: touch every kill with ice once a day. Five days running earns a boon. Miss one and she turns her back; miss two, a debuff; miss three and you fall from grace, with a fifty-fifty chance of being smote. Leaving voluntarily is an automatic smite. Her sponsor messaged him constantly. Then a note from Azin, seventeenth edition: that was Sinjin's last entry, a man in Azin's party had a blindness debuff made permanent by his god, and the advice is to stay away from gods.

beats.headline: A quest to bring Orthrus home
beats.text: My son's hound is lost. Orthrus. I believe he is in the eighteenth of these little glass worlds, so I stand outside it and pound on the wall while everything inside turns to lava. The dungeon has made a quest of him: bring him to me. It has made another, for anyone who would rather be paid: kill him before he reaches me. I am interested to learn which the small things choose.

beats.headline: Two quests, pointing opposite ways
beats.text: Crawler Carl and Crawler Princess Donut take an aeroplane up and read Meat Hooks, a scroll whose stench brings every carnivorous pet in range running, to lure a puppy the size of a building out of the water and out of the bubble. The quest that comes with it is simple: bring Orthrus to Emberus. Then a second quest is announced, and this one pays crawlers for killing him. Both are on the board together, which is a design decision somebody made and I am obliged to run. Crawler Quan Ch reads the second one and attacks the puppy.

beats.headline: Meat Hooks, with no off button
beats.text: CARL is flying the drop bear, and I am in the seat behind him with my Torch stuck to the wing so we can see. I heal the mountain of a puppy twice on a pass behind its heads. Then he circles round and I read the Meat Hooks scroll, which smells like the worst thing that has ever happened. It works. The puppy comes after the smoke, straight out of the bubble. Then it is catching up, and CARL says to turn the spell off, and there is no button. There is always a button. The smoke will not stop.

beats.headline: He worships a god to survive a plane crash
beats.text: I am falling out of the sky and Quan Ch is about to finish the job. So I take Emberus as my patron, mid-air, and throw a celestial grenade. The god arrives at my position, and for a little while nothing can kill me. Then Emberus finds Orthrus, and both of them are gone.

beats.headline: He tears off Quan Ch's arm
beats.text: Quan Ch sneaks up and hits me with his lightning while the god's invulnerability is still on me, which he cannot see. I punch him in the face and a health bar appears. He stabs at me and the knife explodes. Then the buff runs out, and he does not know it. I try to tell him what he has done, and all that comes out is that he is a bully and nobody likes him. He rockets off while I am holding his casting arm. He goes. The arm stays, with three rings on it. I have Tran tell him that was just a deposit.

beats.headline: Thrown from the upper wing
beats.text: The biplane is spiralling down, Orthrus is unconscious, and Quan Ch is closing in, both hands glowing. Carl takes Emberus as his god in mid-air, against every warning in the cookbook, climbs onto the upper wing with Donut clinging to his back, and throws the grenade at Quan. Quan freezes it fifteen feet in front of him with a red bolt. It makes no difference. The ball winks out, and Emberus arrives as a city-sized floating head. Quan never gets his spell off.

beats.headline: Sixty seconds of Divine Intervention
beats.text: The second clause is the one that saves Carl. Imbued with Divine Intervention, he is invulnerable for sixty seconds, and nothing over his head says so. He lands in a valley of the land quadrant unhurt while Donut, on his back, is knocked down to five percent. Emberus leaves early, gone with Orthrus before the minute is out. Quan Ch, who cannot see the buff, hits Carl with lightning while the buff still has a few seconds to run. Carl gets up and punches him in the face.

beats.headline: Summoned by a celestial grenade
beats.text: The man is falling out of the sky with Quan Ch a breath from finishing him, and in that moment, with nothing in his hands but a celestial grenade, he decides that he worships me. I am not fooled. I am flattered, which is a different thing, and I answer. I come to where he is. For a little while nothing on this floor can kill him, because I have said so. And there is Orthrus. Good boy. We are leaving.

beats.headline: Collected
beats.text: The aeroplane spirals down with Quan Ch closing in on Crawler Carl. Carl takes Emberus as his god mid-fall and throws a celestial grenade, the god arrives at his position, and for a short while nothing on this floor can touch him. Then Emberus finds Orthrus. The two of them go, together, and the floor is left to the people who were fighting over a dog.

beats.headline: Thumbs, Carl
beats.text: CARL locks the plane onto its little autopilot, jumps out on the wing and yells at me to grab the stick. Grab the stick. I do not have thumbs. I grab it anyway, with everything, and we roll and corkscrew, and something falls off the back. Then he is glowing, and I am on his back with my claws in, and we jump. When I wake up I am singed and he is holding a man's arm. I have decided something. He is crazy. Not a little weird crazy. Not cereal-without-milk crazy. Straitjacket crazy.

beats.headline: The plane, and the grenade
beats.text: An aircraft, spiralling down. Crawler Carl standing on its upper wing with the cat clinging to his back; Crawler Quan Ch closing in, hands glowing, to finish him. Then Carl does two things nobody had on the board: he takes Emberus as his god, and he throws a celestial grenade. The god comes to him. This file only needs to note that Quan Ch had it won, and then he did not.

beats.headline: One arm short, down the stairs
beats.text: Crawler Quan Ch, level 48, reads the quest to kill the puppy and tells Crawler Tran it is too good a prize, and that getting the cat would be a bonus. His robe's shield shrugs off a magic missile. A hobgoblin disco ball and a hob-lobber bring him down out of the sky. He comes back and drops Orthrus to two percent. After the grenade he attacks Crawler Carl, who is invulnerable and does not show it. He launches away without his left arm, lands by the stairwell and goes down it.

beats.headline: A drop of blood and five percent
beats.text: I read the notification at last. I am an acolyte of Emberus, and without a cleric or paladin class I can never rise past devotee. The rules: harm no fellow worshipper; a drop of blood at one of his temples every day, or at the sun shrine that has appeared in my personal space; five percent of looted gold into it; nothing blessed by Hellik; every church quest completed. In return, burn immunity and a ten percent chance to burn with every hit, and two glowing sun tattoos on the backs of my hands. Donut calls the tithe an outrage.

beats.headline: Three rings off a severed arm
beats.text: Quan Ch's arm had three rings on it. A plain plus-two ring of strength, which goes on. Rockard's Ring of Sniping, which marks every creature under half health and everyone wearing magical gear, and explains a great deal about Quan; that goes on too. The third is an unenchanted gold band the system calls worthless. It sticks, and the finger crunches getting it off. Inside, it says For Daddy. I push it back onto his finger as far as the first knuckle and put the whole arm in my inventory.

beats.headline: An acolyte's key
beats.text: Carl takes the vows of Emberus, and the benefits come with an asterisk: free access to Club Vanquisher, regardless of previous and current affiliations. Two quests come attached. Find Out Who Killed My Son, and Kill Hellik.

beats.headline: Phase one, one bubble at a time
beats.text: The procedure. A bubble's survivors gather outside their own Desperado Club entrance. One of them goes in, takes the three pieces, comes out and dials the coordinates Katia has worked out; at these distances the portal opens in under a minute. Everyone steps through to Hump Town. The gatekeeper goes last, the gate closes, and a feral god appears in the bubble they have left. The gatekeeper goes back into the club and hands the pieces to the next in line. The first group comes through crying, they are so happy.

beats.headline: The hound had an owner before this one
beats.text: Subject was a god’s son and the owner of Orthrus, and he was murdered. His father’s quest names the obvious suspect, his own brother Hellik, and in the same breath admits that Hellik was in council with the rest of them when it happened.

beats.headline: The second quest
beats.text: Carl is an acolyte of Emberus now, and the paperwork comes with a brother attached. Hellik: god of sun and life, Emberus's twin, level 250, said around the celestial floors to be quite obsessed with killing his own brothers, and the likeliest hand behind Geyrun's death even though he was sitting in council with Emberus when it happened. Two quests arrive together with the acolyte's package. Find Out Who Killed My Son. Kill Hellik. The second one has a deadline attached and it is the twelfth floor.

beats.headline: The terms of a family feud
beats.text: What a god's grudge looks like when it is applied to one crawler. No magical item blessed by Hellik may be owned or used, so a whole category of loot is now dead weight. Every shrine of his is marked on the minimap. Every one of his adherents carries a symbol over their head and pays double experience when put down.

beats.headline: Nobody left behind
beats.text: Only eight bubbles meet the requirements for the first run: somebody with access to the Desperado Club, and every survivor in the same quadrant. Just over five hundred crawlers, most of them in the first four groups. The second condition is mine. I will not help a bubble out if it means leaving anyone in there with a feral god, not even one person. Elle can tell when someone is lying about their quadrants, and she has weeded a few out. Carl said not to wait for him. I tell everybody we are starting the extractions.

beats.headline: The paper on the stall door
beats.text: The toilet stall in the personal space is the one place we can trade messages unseen: a magical author's kit, the paper clipped inside the door, and anything I write appears in Carl's scratch pad. I took it down when the refugees came and put it back to send him my latest calculation. Then Louis ate the monkey soup and got to the stall before I could stop him. I tell Carl. He wipes the page and starts a warning, and the ink runs out halfway through it.

beats.headline: A shrine in the saferoom
beats.text: A shrine has just appeared in the saferoom. A sun disk, a cup and a skull. It does not say which god, but I am guessing Emberus, and I want to know which of these two idiots is responsible. The cat says it was Carl. Of course it was. I call him an idiot and leave it there, because there is real work: with Samantha's help I have figured out the yam. Each potion takes about an eighth of it. One is ready for him, the second is on the table, and he wants three.

beats.headline: Bubble 18, after the god
beats.text: Bubble 18, per Crawler Tserendolgor's messages. While Emberus was outside, the interior doorknobs in their saferooms were literally melting. Now he is gone, the world is too hot and everything has melted, and one of them who can fly is going out to put the last crystal in place and pop the bubble. The rest will take the stairs straight after. The platinum quest box paid out an upgrade to her flamethrower and a tome of Heal Party to a man in her group. Everyone, she reports, is getting good stuff.

beats.headline: Down before the six-hour mark
beats.text: Sighting, via Crawler Li Jun at the stairwell by his bubble: a woman with a shopping cart pulls up out of nowhere, speaks to no one, and goes down the stairs before the six-hour mark. She is level 12. Li Jun does not know where she came from. Crawler Carl's position on the matter, stated in full: that is Agatha, and we just ignore Agatha.

beats.headline: The bubble escape stays legal
beats.text: The day's announcement. After careful discussion, litigation Borant won, and input from the Syndicate, the bubble-escape method may continue. Some secondary summonings are now blocked: each escaping feral had a 66 percent chance of calling a matching deity, and one of the gods summoned would have been an extinction-level event for this floor and the next. Sponsorship bidding for the sixth floor stands at 33 percent of projections, and nobody wants it lower. Then some sixth-floor notes: specialisation on descent, and third-party tourists who will be hunting crawlers, their entry fees paid by an anonymous sponsor.

beats.headline: Frogger in the air quadrant
beats.text: My fan box gave me a stand-up Frogger machine. Not the one from my father's basement, but close, and it runs on a dwarven battery I rigged up. I suspect it was an attempt at trolling me. Two days of waiting in the air quadrant, and I spend too much of them teaching the others to dominate at Frogger. I only got good because I was locked in the basement while my dad had friends over. It helps anyway. You can take a terrible situation and still find a moment of peace. I needed reminding.

beats.headline: This floor was a drag
beats.text: Imani and I open the portal on our world and get the changelings through to the next floor, Twister and all, then rush back to the club, dead on our feet. Katia gives me a long hug and tells us to be careful. We always are. I wink at Carl, pat the cat on the head, and hand over the three pieces of the gate. I am looking forward to mixing it up with these three again. This floor was a real drag, doing it all myself.

beats.headline: The last rescue of phase one
beats.text: I took three of the castles on my own. The air one I could not. I was the last rescue of the first phase; I have the club because of Ifechi. Before the stairs I came to meet Carl. I was done. I had nothing. Then Elle told me about a man and his cat who stopped everything to help old people in wheelchairs, and meant to use an artifact to get people out of their bubbles. Ife was not the only good one. I might die tomorrow, but not because I have given up. If he ever needs a backup gun, I am in his debt.

beats.headline: Phase two, and what got out
beats.text: Phase two runs the same way, on worlds less sure their other quadrants are empty, plus a few added late. By the end of it, about 1,500 crawlers are out. One feral too big for its bubble simply burst, and the bubble opened and poured the gore into the lacuna. Only two got loose out there: a turkey the size of Orthrus and a city-sized swarm of insects. Phase one called three deities and phase two five more; they did damage and went away. The gate comes back to Katia. Nobody tries to steal it.

beats.headline: Into the dry tomb
beats.text: Subject has a new spear, and is pretty stoked about it. With the tomb drained, she and Tran take their team into the subterranean level, loot what is left of the tomb raiders and open the tomb of Anser: a sarcophagus holding the skeleton of a goose in a golden, unenchanted crown. Quetzalcoatlus's corpse holds a partial map of the sixth floor. Her team agrees to join the party Crawler Katia means to form, which Princess Donut notes, given that the two of them are always fighting.

beats.headline: My brother pushed too hard
beats.text: Carl has been sitting there tense and angry for minutes, and he is scaring the children, so I tell him. He says it is weird being the one who has to wait. He crashed a drop bear into a god's face. He says that was hours ago. He reminds me of my brother. Always moving, always pushing at his goal. When something got in front of him that he could not figure out, he pushed too hard. If he had waited, he would still be alive.

beats.headline: Separate, next floor
beats.text: I tell Carl and Donut we need to separate next floor. It is because of Eva. She is gathering the former daughters back to her. Silfa and her two daughters formed a party with her, and they are dead. The next floor is open. I have to gather the ones who are left before Eva does, and deal with her if I must. I will not leave the party yet. Louis and Firas, Gwen's team, Bautista and some friends, and Florin are coming with me. Carl gives me the Left Fang of the Green Sultan, to return to its owner.

beats.headline: Their schedule, not yours
beats.text: Carl expected a patch to stop the gate trick. They did the opposite, and I am not surprised. They love it when you do stupid, suicidal things, but when it involves the entire population, they start to get alarmed. Don't mistake that for kindness. Once all the sponsorships are done, don't expect them to cushion your fall. Meanwhile the personal space is a wreck, the kids are watching The Goonies, and the changelings are dancing like portly little humans with their shirts pulled up.

beats.headline: The turkey
beats.text: The feral turkey god. Level 150, tripled in size from eating what was left of another god, sitting on a popped bubble and screaming. Miriam and I take it apart with our debuffs. It gives me eight levels, which makes me 55, the highest in the dungeon, which should surprise nobody. The recap shows me gnawing the largest feather in the universe and screaming, over and over, while Miriam strokes my hair.

beats.headline: Anser's tomb
beats.text: Gwen, me and the team go into the subterranean level now it is dry. We loot what is left of the tomb raiders. Electrifying the water set off every trap. The tomb of Anser: a sarcophagus, the skeleton of a goose, a golden crown, unenchanted. Quetzalcoatlus's corpse has a partial map of the sixth floor, with coordinates for several locations.

beats.headline: His brother says his name
beats.text: Crawler Carl kept Brandon's last message in his scratch pad and reread it often. He delivered it on the fifth floor, a hand on the shoulder of a petrified man who could not answer: his brother loved him and regretted not saying so, and Brandon gave his life protecting his friends. When the worm is finally out of Chris's head, Chris sits in a daze and says only one thing. "Brandon. Brandon." Carl tells him his brother died saving the lives of a lot of people.

beats.headline: The box we swapped in a hug
beats.text: Chris hurls the winding box off the bowl and the watches go flying in two directions. It does not matter. Katia built a facsimile box in pieces in her inventory while pretending to learn the engineering table, and we swapped real for fake when we hugged at the club. The watches in it are the fakes I made to fool the dirigible gnomes. There is no god for the ninth floor. The real gate is in the water quadrant, and I tell Juice Box to fly for it. We are keeping the gate.

beats.headline: The worm comes out of my neck
beats.text: From under the sand, Maggie tells me the caprid came to her in the rest area, a cleric, a goat thing, a liaison, and said it would help if they killed me. Then she stops mid-sentence. Chris erupts beside the box. I take the phase potion and reach into his head, and the worm bites my palm and burrows into my arm. I drink the double-healing potion before she reaches my brain, and she comes out through my neck like a sniper's round. Mongo gets her.

beats.headline: Come and get it
beats.text: After the last recap, Lucia Mar falls off the top spot and I am on it. Number one. Donut is fourth, Prepotente third, Quan Ch tenth. Mordecai wants the Ring of Divine Suffering tossed before I go down the stairs. Instead I hold it up for the cameras. The hunters want it, and the gate, and they can come and get it. Better: I will come to them. By the time the next floor collapses, every hunter who sets foot on it with us will be dead. I swear it on my life. I will break you all.

beats.headline: Pulled out through a phase potion
beats.text: Maggie, hidden in the sand, says they have her other daughter. Chris erupts beside the winding box and hurls it. Crawler Carl, phased through lava rock by a potion, reaches into his head and pulls the worm out; it burrows into Carl instead, comes out through his neck, and Mongo ends it. Chris sits with a hand on his head. "That hurt." Then, in a daze: "Brandon. Brandon." He is added to the Royal Court's party, and walks into the stairwell without looking back.

beats.headline: Slit comes for Samantha
beats.text: A feral demon comes over the horizon hunting the goddess who got out of the same place she did, now a love doll's head. Carl carries the head outside, fits it into a sponsor's head-throwing attachment and hurls it fifty kilometres, and the demon wheels after it. A goddess outside a safe room summons a deity, as Mordecai warned: her mother arrives and tears the demon in two.

beats.headline: Maggie My, pulled out at last
beats.text: Maggie My is dead. Carl, phased by a potion, reached into Chris Andrews's head and pulled her out, and she burrowed into Carl instead, because of course she did. A second potion threw her back out through his neck, and Mongo finished her. So that is both of them, Frank and Maggie. Eight skulls between them by the first safe room, and the file is closed.

beats.headline: Larracos: water, charges and sharks
beats.text: The announced plan was to open onto the Skull Empire army and put a feral god in the middle of it — the exact outcome the lawsuit was meant to prevent. It was cover, planned for days. The winding box Chris throws is a fake; the real gate is with Katia in the water quadrant, and it floods the faction market instead: ocean water, timed explosives and a frenzy of sharks, cutting the factions off from resupply. Carl keeps the artifact rather than spending it. Juice Box goes through with the water.

beats.headline: Waiting on the last stage
beats.text: Carl and Donut and me, and the dromedarians rebuilding a town that will not exist in a few hours. Carl explains the last stage out loud, cheerfully, to anybody listening: open a portal to the ninth floor, keep the second watch, and send me through with the rest. I made him promise about my people. I am holding him to it.

beats.headline: We are going to be married
beats.text: The watch Chris threw is not my brother's watch. It is a fake. Carl has changed the plan: no god, they are keeping the gate, and I am to fly for the water, go through to Larracos, stay hidden and tell the others what they really are. Watch over my people, I tell him. We have a deal. And keep Louis safe. I love him. We are going to be married. Carl asks if I am serious. I am. I become a skyfowl and go.

beats.headline: Anchored under the gate
beats.text: The gate opens in the water quadrant, and the timed charges Carl made are sucked straight in. I dropped the chum bomb nearby just before, and it worked really well: the sharks are in their feeding frenzy and slurping in after the charges, with some of the pain amplifier jellies. I am anchored to the temple wall against the current. Then out by the subterranean stairwell, near the shelf where the Akula was parked. I am out. Going down. Good luck with class selection, Carl.

beats.headline: Off to break up the killers
beats.text: Crawler Langley, level 32, eight levels up since he met Crawler Carl. His team leaves the bowl ahead of the last stage. Katia offered them a place with her new team; he is considering others. The Popov brothers want archers to hunt team Cichociemni, who have been preying on weak crawlers, and the player-killer groups need breaking up before they get too strong. Handshakes. Princess Donut notes that every crawler in their own quadrant made it through the floor alive.

beats.headline: The water goes down the hole
beats.text: The plan was never a feral god. The Gate opens in the water quadrant, and a bubble's ocean, a load of timed charges and a feeding frenzy of sharks pour through it into Larracos's faction market. By Katia's math more than half of the inverted city is under water by the time the gate closes; only the upper levels, the NPC residences, are spared. Zev warns that the markets, the mercenaries and the Desperado Club's entrance bar are all down there. Juice Box flies for the gate and goes through with the water.

beats.headline: He finishes Maggie My
beats.text: Thing on Chris. Thing OFF Chris. Thing goes for Carl. Thing is FOOD.

beats.headline: Toss the ring
beats.text: A platinum emergency box. Do you know what that cost? More than the GDP of some star systems. Forget it and go down the stairs. Then he carries the doll's head outside, where she will summon a god, and she does. Then Larracos. Carl. Son. You don't know the forces you're dealing with. You got this far because you make them a lot of money, and you just kicked them in the financial balls. I don't care what that ring is worth. Toss it before the stairs. You can't fight a war like this and expect to win.

beats.headline: Only NPCs
beats.text: Carl's accounting of the flood: innocent people killed today, a lot of them, but NPCs, and none of them former crawlers, who are too valuable to waste in a city razed every season. He tells himself he has spared them a bloody conflict that would have ended in their deaths anyway. The rule Zev quotes is what gives the flood its weight: new worker NPCs cannot be added once a level is created, so a drowned shopkeeper stays drowned. A distant part of him is alarmed at the attitude.

beats.headline: The emergency platinum box
beats.text: An Emergency Platinum Benefactor Box from the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network lands as a feral demon closes on the bowl. Mordecai reckons it cost more than the GDP of some star systems. Inside is one piece of glowing wicker: a head-throwing attachment made for Crawler Carl alone, inscribed with design approval from the Network's CEO. Carl's reading of it: a prize built for a coming floor, sent now because keeping him alive mattered more. He wonders aloud whether they sponsored a deity as well.

beats.headline: Recruiting archers for a hunt
beats.text: Langley, level thirty-two and leaving with his group, lays out their options for the next floor. Large groups are forming. The Popov brothers are looking for archers, because they want to hunt down team Cichociemni, who have been preying on weak crawlers, and the player-killer groups need breaking up before they get too strong. His group may join them. On the board that closes this floor the brothers are fifth: level forty-three, two hundred thousand, doubled.

beats.headline: Maggie's hats
beats.text: GIRL FIGHT. Then CARL is unconscious with a hole in his neck, so I heal him with a scroll, and Chris too. I looted Maggie the first time Mongo threw her up. She had a lot of stuff. A lot of hats. CARL says give it all to Chris. What does Chris need with a bunch of hats? I collect hats. Then Juice Box says she is marrying Louis. The whole world has gone insane. And everyone is going to be hunting us, and I do not like people hunting us, CARL.

beats.headline: Her mother takes her kill
beats.text: Slit. A feral demon, and it is hunting ME, like I do not have enough going on. So Carl throws me. Fifty kilometres, screaming, with Slit chasing, which is apparently a plan: one head versus one demon. I was WINNING. Then the sky opens and my MOTHER turns up, tears Slit in half and leaves. That was MY kill. Throw me again. Maybe she will come back.

beats.headline: A head the size of an arena
beats.text: Slit. Feral Minor Demon. Level 200. Thrown into the Nothing with many other demons, having wanted no part of the royal drama, but in love, and eons of madness have not been kind. The head is sports-arena sized, pink and scaled, trowelled in mascara and lipstick, trailing the stench of unfiltered cigarettes. She wields an electrified chain whip whose links are the size of semi-trucks. Her first words once in view, delivered to a sex doll head: "Samantha. You are so dead."

beats.headline: Fifty kilometres of bait
beats.text: Samantha demands a weapon. Crawler Carl instead jams her face-first into an Enchanted Xistera Extension Slot, a head-throwing attachment custom made for decapitated love doll heads, and throws her more than fifty kilometres. Slit screeches and follows, wings working to keep her gelatinous bulk aloft, dressed in leather and tassels the size of sequoias. Carl's reading of the item: it was built for the next floor, and whoever paid for it was forced to send it early.

beats.headline: Picked up like a rodent
beats.text: As Slit chases the head across the dark, the sky cracks and a second god appears, physically huge, multi-armed, too distant to examine. It ignores Samantha, plucks Slit out of the air the way someone lifts a small rodent, and rips her in two. The tearing is audible from kilometres away. Her chain whip crashes down. Then the god and the corpse are gone. Samantha pops back at Crawler Carl's feet furious that it was her kill. The god, it emerges, was her mother.

beats.headline: Her king, allegedly
beats.text: Post-mortem, per Samantha. Slit is part of a demon harem. Samantha was describing her exploits with her own king and Slit thought she meant hers, so Samantha told her that she and Slit's king had all sorts of weird sex, which upset Slit and all her sisters. The Nothing is filled with the harem, and they all hate her. Anytime one gets out, expect this. Slit was one of the little ones. The sister to look out for is Gash.

beats.headline: Glimpses of the halls
beats.text: Three glimpses across this floor. Psamathe's description promises that those hanging out in the halls of the Celestial Ascendency on the twelfth floor get into serious whackadoodle business, such as a god giving birth to a fortune-telling, snake-headed cow out of his thigh. Mordecai once watched a god die on a recap episode, but that was during the Ascendency, when all gods lose their invulnerability on the twelfth. And a feral minor demon's description records that she was captured and thrown into the Nothing during the original Ascendency.

beats.headline: An attorney for Borant
beats.text: A last-minute lawsuit tries to stop Carl's portal to the ninth floor, and its sole plaintiff is the Skull Empire. The Valtay, currently at odds with Borant, send an attorney to help Borant anyway, with an argument about Carl himself: he now owns stock in a company based in the Skull Empire, and a taxpayer not in arrears is treated differently, so the case belonged in a different court. It is dismissed. Neither the Valtay nor Borant is fond of the orcs.

beats.headline: The extension slot
beats.text: An emergency box from the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network holds an attachment built for exactly one crawler and exactly one purpose. Screwed onto the end of the scoop it lets him throw Samantha, and it multiplies his reach: five hundred metres for every point of strength. Take the slot off and she comes back to him.

beats.headline: A message from the politburo
beats.text: Hello, Carl and Princess Donut. Okay, so, there was another last-minute legal challenge to what you are about to attempt, and it failed; the Valtay sent an attorney to help Borant. I have also been asked to pass on a message. It is from the politburo, who have recently replaced the board of directors in control of Borant, and it is a direct quote: they approve of what you are planning, and game-breaking antics that directly affect sponsors will not be tolerated in the future. Carl, you know such language is not acceptable. Best of luck to you.

beats.headline: They are enraged
beats.text: Oh my god, Carl. They are enraged. This is not what you promised. If you fill Larracos with water and mobs, it kills the NPCs. The markets flood, the mercenaries die, and if the NPCs at the entrance bar die, the sponsors lose access to the Desperado Club. We cannot add new worker NPCs once a level is created. That is written into the rules. Fixing it would need a Syndicate vote they will not have, and the AI on board. You have killed thousands. Tens of thousands. There will be consequences.

beats.headline: New Queen Anne
beats.text: Subject is alive. She survived the collection in a Seattle parking garage with Brad and four dentists, and lives now in a native camp called New Queen Anne, where everyone works but her. She has taken in a half-feral stray she calls Ferdinand, and sings to him at night that she should have let him in. Her face and arms are covered in his scratches. Two bounty hunters cut into her tent; one of them knows her name. Then a woman named Lexis, who works for Odette, shoots her way in behind them and takes her.

beats.headline: Gravy Boat
beats.text: Subject is on Earth. His real name is Gravy Boat. He is Beatrice's neighbour's cat, who used to yowl at her window when Princess was in heat; she called him Ferdinand to shoo him off. She found him in a tree beside the hole where her building was, skin and bones. He is also an A-tier target on the season's Walk-On list, and two bounty hunters have scanned six cats in the area looking for him. Odette's orders: a bounty cube, and a delivery to Borant.

beats.headline: A much better use for her
beats.text: Lexis has Beatrice, out of a camp in what used to be Seattle. She killed a sac pirate, captured his null partner, and shot Bea's human when he went for a weapon. We will not vaporise the town. The null lives, with the weapon planted on him, and the human is left to expire. The cat goes to Borant in a bounty cube, we buy out the null's warrant so he keeps quiet, and the scene will read as a fight over a cat. Tell Beatrice I cannot wait to meet her. We will not be selling her to Borant. We have a much better use for her.

beats.headline: All in on him
beats.text: Behind the Network's money, a conversation. A woman asks how much they have spent, and Dr. Hu says it is best she does not know. They are going all in on Carl. She lists the risks: he is unstable, the Valtay are into everything, a civil war is coming. They should have sent instructions with the yam; half of it went on saving another crawler. He knows what it is really for, Hu says. Every time Carl goes on Odette's show, more people sign up. For his cause, she says. It is the same cause, Hu says. She calls him Porthus.

beats.headline: The second hand on the cookbook
beats.text: Subject crawled in the fifteenth season, chose the High Elf race and a rogue’s class, and wrote the second edition of the book that keeps being handed down. He now goes by Dr. Hu, and he is spending a small NFC's money, more of it than anyone should ask about, on the crawler who holds his book. He is therefore both an advertisement for the dungeon and a witness against it, and production has never worked out how to bill him.

beats.headline: The Walk-On list
beats.text: Survivors on the surface are natives, and by the rules untouchable; their implants are scrambled once the crawl starts. So when producers want a particular native, a Walk-On list goes out, and bounty crews sneak onto a planet closed to non-natives to take them. It is not remotely legal. The Syndicate knows, rights groups complain, and nothing happens, though its security still patrols and still catches trespassers.
