beats.text: Ahead of the castle job Edgar sits well back from the building and maps the whole of it from where he is. Every room, every level, and a set of small connecting tunnels that fit nothing anyone can name. Louis is the one who works out what they are for. They are Ferdinand's, so that he can move around his own house without ever using a door.

beats.headline: Katia kills her
beats.text: Hunting Grounds, the end of the floor. Crawler Eva, bitten by a dinosaur and buried in a corner, is still alive, and Crawler Katia Grim goes looking for her. Crawler Katia Grim kills Crawler Eva. That is the whole of it. Two professors came in through the same door; from here on, one. I don't do eulogies, and this is not the entry where I start.

beats.headline: Eva's last act
beats.text: I find Eva with Find Crawler, alive under the bugs, and I make Daniel stay; I don't want him to see this. Li Na casts Preserve Injury. I cut off the hand with the escape ring, and the rapier. Eva wakes and asks me to heal her. Then she says she's sorry. That's all I wanted, to hear her afraid. I put the sword through her breastplate. As she dies she pulls something from the back of her armour: the Crown of the Sepsis Whore. It finds my head.

beats.headline: Show me Annie
beats.text: I have two big secrets in this dungeon. One is the blitz sticks. I found them on Sally, one of Eva's victims; she worked at the airport, she was a healer, and the drugs were all that was left in her inventory. Eva left them there for me. A trap. I light one and think, show me Annie, and it does, every time: nine months old, standing in her crib, holding on to my hair. Mordecai warned me they're addictive. I didn't listen. Only Daniel knows.

beats.headline: Kill her
beats.text: I go with Katia. Eva is under the dead bugs, unconscious, almost out of health. I cast Preserve Injury so she cannot heal herself, and I point at the ring on her top right hand. Katia cuts it off. Eva wakes and asks to be healed. Katia laughs. My brother looks from Katia to me. Kill her, I say.

beats.headline: He shatters the seventh floor
beats.text: Look at what they gave us. The Great Race, a replacement the Valtay paid for and somebody threw together in a hurry, a circuit of glass tunnels with nothing holding it up. So I tested it. Minutes after it opened, the whole loop is dust, fine as flour. No crawler goes into their maze. No mob, no NPC, no boss gets to meet anyone. You wanted a seventh floor. Build a better one.

beats.headline: His mother's boots
beats.text: Carl asks how I really know. My mother's boots. Boots of Kiznet's Final Flight, from a minor boss just before Carl allowed her to kill herself. The description is five hundred and three percent longer than the average item's, and it tells a fairy tale: a boy in a maze where every tunnel seals behind him, resurrected and made to start over, who spends years trying to crack the walls. She played the piano for me. She was going to do it again at the talent competition. I am never going to get that back.

beats.headline: Viper Queen, and number one
beats.text: Carl, we're in a fish tank! And I'm ranked number one. Number one! I need to pick a new class, and the chat is down so Mordecai can't help, so I pick one. Viper Queen. Doesn't that sound delicious? I can shoot poison blobs. My health is lower, which Prepotente says is of no consequence. Then Prepotente leaves the party, and I am party leader.

beats.headline: December 10th in Havana
beats.text: The eighth floor opens inside the capitol building in Havana, because Donut picked Cuba. The notification says it is December 10th. We are inside a replay of the surface in the weeks before the collapse: people who are ghosts, and objects that are real, and anything looted from it turns to dust at the collapse. Fourteen days to fill a squad by planting flags in monsters under five per cent. Bea and her friends flew to the Bahamas on the 26th, after this phase ends, so Donut's caution bought nothing. Phase two moves us somewhere new. They'll be angling to send us there.

beats.headline: T'Ghee, by Allister's account
beats.text: The announcement mentions T'Ghee totems, and Carl's breath catches, because he already knows the word. Allister, who wrote the thirteenth edition, treated T'Ghee as a religion, with nothing to do with capturing or summoning monsters. Carl can already see how the dungeon means to use it anyway. Mordecai supplies the dungeon's version: large playing cards, like Bautista's stuffed animals or Carl's tarot cards, reusable even when the summoned monster dies.

beats.headline: Huanxin, Uzzi, and what happened
beats.text: Chaco. Uzzi. A stairwell on the tenth floor that would not open until a god's spell hit the puzzle, and me volunteering to take the hit, because the only life it cost was mine. Odette found a cheaper way to pay. Huanxin Jinx was driving the storm goddess, and when she raised her price from a tenth of Odette's bonus to a third, Odette refused. She talked Chaco into putting the dart into my brother instead. The goddess died in the containment and the stairwell opened. I went through it. He did not.

beats.headline: Ten per cent, then fifty
beats.text: Nine puzzle pieces primed, a storm goddess coming through the acid rain, and the level about to collapse. Mordecai reaching the eleventh floor buys my freedom. Through Armita I have offered Huanxin Jinx ten per cent of that bonus. She wants thirty-three, then fifty, or she zeroes out the party. I tell Armita there is no deal. Mordecai means to spend himself on his Final Blow skill. I tell Chaco to worship Dodola and put the dart in Uzzi instead. He does. The goddess dies inside his containment, and the stairwell opens. I am free. Mordecai writes that he is going to find me and kill me.

beats.headline: Master Telephone Psychic
beats.text: I chose Cuba rather than the Bahamas, and that was strategy: they gave Carl a book about the Bahamas, which was quite obviously a trap. Then ten minutes to pick a class, which is an improvement. Mordecai offers me an Agony Urchin, which changes the way I look, so absolutely not, or Master Telephone Psychic. I pick Psychic. My map now sees the whole building, my intelligence goes up five points, and I get Brain Freeze, Bad Attitude and Why Are You Hitting Yourself?, which makes people stab themselves in the face. I keep the Viper Queen's poison spit, too.

beats.headline: The first newsletter
beats.text: The first newsletter of my one official fan club goes out, and I absolutely do not approve of the name the Donut Holes. I recap the last few floors as best I can: Signet's revenge, Mongo and Kiwi killing Vrah, the whole castle sent down with our army in it. Then the crime of the century. Tserendolgor got her hands on the pet show ballot box and handed Mongo's crown to her disgusting meatball pet. I want the footage pored over until someone finds the smoking gun. Remember to pay your dues. The Team Mongo Mommies tier is twenty credits a week extra.

beats.headline: Twenty flags a squad
beats.text: Floor announcement. Each squad leader receives twenty flags bearing a logo the system designed. Plant one in a living thing below five per cent health, noncorporeal included, and it becomes a T'Ghee totem, a minion of whoever summons it, obedient to a point depending on level and temperament. Rip the totem in two to dismiss it. Trade them, steal them. Lost flags are not replaced. Every surviving squad keeps one card when the floor collapses. Carl's breath catches: he knows the word from the Cookbook.

beats.headline: Like the stuffed animals
beats.text: Mordecai's gloss on the announcement: T'Ghee totems are like Bautista's stuffed animals, only in the form of large playing cards. Like Carl's tarot cards, actually. Reusable even when the summoned monster dies. He has seen them used a few different ways over the seasons, so they are going to have to wait for the next announcement. Carl, who has read Allister, notes that for its inventor T'Ghee was a religion and had nothing to do with capturing monsters.

beats.headline: Bored until the crawlers stop
beats.text: A scene from an old season, told from Odette's side, spells out the timing. The Ascendency battles do not start until the crawlers reach the twelfth floor or are zeroed out, and until then the sponsors are bored. Huanxin Jinx, who sponsored Dodola every season, was bored enough to sell a storm goddess's help to Odette's scheme, for a cut. Armita, a former party member of Odette's, had a job as a demigod attendant for the Celestial Ascendency and carried the messages, since the AI is legally forbidden to monitor Ascendency sponsor communications.

beats.headline: Guarding the last stairwell
beats.text: For the record, from a season long gone: tenth floor, collapse imminent, three crawlers at a stairwell, and a fourth still on his way back to it, that opens only when a storm god's magic touches a primed puzzle. Uzzi, skyfowl, Storm Commander, the class Mordecai once said his brother took on Odette's advice. He guards the others while Hold Steady keeps the puzzle primed and Chaco plays to draw the gods. His magic is limited. His party protection spell is what keeps the caustic rain off everyone. Odette notes that he chose the hardest of four paths, blindly.

beats.headline: See you on the other side
beats.text: The storm goddess is sponsored, and her sponsor has turned on them. Mordecai tells the group chat he has a plan and it will kill him; to Odette alone he explains it: his Final Blow skill can target the puzzle, so if the god hits him, the puzzle is hit too. "Uzzi, see you on the other side, brother." Uzzi's reply, in full: "Do not even dare." The brothers go back and forth while the timer falls. Odette knows that if Uzzi were told the other plan, he would be on board. There is no time to tell him.

beats.headline: The dart in his breast
beats.text: Chaco worships the goddess and tells Uzzi he is sorry. Uzzi turns to him, looks down at the Dart of Ophiotaurus in the bard's hand, lifts his head to the rain, and caws a war cry. He steps nearer the puzzle and spreads his wings. He understood. Chaco throws the dart into his breast and locks him in a containment with the puzzle. Mordecai arrives in ratkin form, falls to his knees at the shell, and calls his brother's name. The summoning tears Uzzi's chest open. Crawler Uzzi has fallen.

beats.headline: Apex Predator
beats.text: We haven't been in a real saferoom since before the party, so I've been sitting on dozens of achievements. A country boss achievement, for Imogen turning up in the convoy. The Scourge, for the most hands: a legendary box. Marked for Life, for surviving a god: a platinum apostate box. Then Apex Predator. Every hunter dead, and I killed the last one. Reward: nothing. Just kidding. A Celestial Predator Box. My hands shake. Donut got legendaries and wants to know why she didn't get a celestial when she helped kill a god. It wasn't for that.

beats.headline: Suspiciously good loot
beats.text: After the skipped floor, the feeds fill with crawlers opening very good boxes: an ice staff for Elle, a shape-changing ring for Bautista, a nipple ring and a summoning tome for Donut. Mordecai reads it two ways. Part of it is the AI compensating for the floor nobody got to play. But some of those boxes were earned before the skip, so it is likely a response to the Valtay ramping up the difficulty. More than a thousand crawlers also receive the identical box at the same moment and earn Collective Bargaining, whose citation promises to toughen up the rules.

beats.headline: Hills Cyclops, and a warning
beats.text: Hills Cyclops. Level fifty, pink, one eye, and the description has opinions about sheep. It still beats the ten minutes the seventh floor was open, when I was a slime with no arms. Now, the problem. Samantha flew back here and pushed through the brambles to the door. Withering spirits should not be able to do any of that. I don't understand it, which makes it extra dangerous. She won't shut up about the flesh golem in Carl's inventory. Kid, don't give it to her until we figure out why and how she is gaining this power.

beats.headline: A nipple ring and a screaming book
beats.text: No spellbook of the floor for the seventh, which is an outrage, only one for Mute. Then my boxes. A cosmic buff potion that gives me dexterity instead of charisma. A skill potion that takes Love Vampire from three to six and lets it cast on its own. A nipple ring from a superior fire demon's hand maiden, which has the most sexist description I have ever read, and a berserking spell I will not name that Mordecai says I may only cast by myself. And a chained, quivering tome that screams as I learn it: Legionnaires of the Damned. I have always been badass.

beats.headline: Fire Berserker
beats.text: Mordecai puts a name to the state the elementals live in permanently: a berserk, partly invulnerable condition that shrugs off blunt damage and turns whatever holds it on everything within reach. He notes the system has been renaming things more often than it used to.

beats.headline: Back, and wanting her body
beats.text: I FLEW BACK. Through the brambles and right up to the door, all by myself. Carl, my cousin gave you her mother, and her mother is a perfectly good body sitting in your inventory. We need a mage to animate her. A pulpmancer. Let's go right now! He says we just landed on a new floor and need to get our bearings first. I tell him I'm going to kill his mother. He says he won't help me if I keep threatening him. So I growl, and I go and chase Mongo.

beats.headline: The floor that broke
beats.text: Mordecai has the story of the broken seventh floor from Mistress Tiatha, and he puts it on the engineers: they built the level just like the fairytale, and the goat did what the kid in the story took thousands of years to figure out. The Valtay are likely irritated with the Borant designers. The Apothecary and the Plenty probably did well out of providing the means, at the cost of the Valtay and the Syndicate, because the Syndicate pays in advance for the tunnels that carry the livestream, and a skipped floor is not refunded.

beats.headline: The burn stays
beats.text: Katia's squad, Iceland. The burn on my face still hasn't healed. Neither Louis nor I have opened our boxes. I sit and hold on to Louis, and I don't stop crying. We are both still broken up about Firas. Katia is worried. She has asked Imani to come over and talk to me.

beats.headline: Needle, thread, and a bone key
beats.text: Donut critiques every stitch, so I send her off to read her fan boards and sew the celestial patch on myself, peace symbol first. It glows. My strength jumps, and a new bar appears under my mana: Soul Essence. Every patch bonus is doubled, plus twenty-five to strength and dexterity, and three benefits. Climb. Soul Reaper, which charges on melee kills and dumps it all into one attack. And a Mysterious Bone Key that opens any lock in the dungeon, destroys the jacket, and takes one of my bones to make the key. We're marking that one as a last resort.

beats.headline: Mean, and liked
beats.text: Filed for the survivors. Tran, who lost both legs in the final moments of the previous floor, is more upset about losing subject than the legs, according to Crawler Katia; they had been together since early on. He does not answer Crawler Carl's note. Princess Donut's eulogy, delivered straight after the fight, begins: poor Gwen, she was mean, but I liked her.

beats.headline: Worried about Britney
beats.text: We are in Iceland. Florin left the party just before the last level broke, and I have been asking where he is. My box gave me something that lets me move very fast. Louis and Britney have not opened theirs; they are still broken up about Firas. The burn on Britney's face still has not healed, and she has not stopped crying. She sits there, holding onto Louis. I have already asked Imani to come over. We will see if it helps.

beats.headline: Drain it every time
beats.text: Divine items are the best items, kid, whatever the debuffs. And yes, there is somebody in my room. With the upgraded quarters I was able to hire a room attendant. It's not important. Concentrate on your sewing; you can ruin the item. Then Soul Reaper comes up. Oh, it's good. It's also more dangerous than Donut's berserking spell. Drain the essence bar each time it fills, and don't store the stuff for long. I once saw a crawler fill her reserve with gorgons and kill a country boss with a single attack. It turned to stone and shattered.

beats.headline: A pile of skulls, stacked nice and neat
beats.text: Out of the celestial predator box, opened in the same haul as a prison tattoo kit and a crafting table kit: a divine back patch for Carl's jacket, its benefits varying with whichever deities and certain demons happen to be near. The upgrades it carries stay hidden until it is affixed and worn.

beats.headline: A floating chair
beats.text: Final moments of the last floor, I lost my legs. And Gwen. We'd been together since early on. Bautista is with me, helping. I open my boxes. The pacifist box has a floating wheelchair, the same sort Odette used to zip around in when she was in human form. Carl sends a note asking if I'm okay. I don't answer.

beats.headline: Two stairwells, not far
beats.text: Subject is the last of the four cretin bodyguards still with the clients; the other three went down with the high elf castle. Services this morning: loaded his stairwell teleport, still on cooldown, to read the stairwell locations, and reported two, not far, still in the big city near the coast. Assigned to map the area on paper with Mordecai and to remain in the saferoom. Offered, as consideration, a GameCube controller. Response: a noncommittal grunt. Observed condition: depressed, possibly lonely, possibly missing the Sledge.

beats.headline: The world we lost
beats.text: We open the doors on a warm, humid morning in Old Havana, and it hits me like a sledgehammer. This is what we lost. Cars, scooters, a yellow Ford Fairlane, people everywhere. A ghost kicks Donut down the stairs and walks on without his trousers. I take his wallet and his phone, and the underwear too; I want as small a footprint as possible near the saferoom. Then a monster with a wolf's body and a Che Guevara head charges us, barking like a man with a megaphone. The Experience, level fifty-five. Donut barely has to lift a paw.

beats.headline: A bigfoot in Bermuda shorts
beats.text: First things first, Carl: skipping a level without warning us was messed up. Not all of us are as trained up as you. He swears it was all Pony. Then the boxes, and holy shitballs, I got an ice staff I won't stop talking about. And just now a goddamned bigfoot crossed the road in front of me wearing Bermuda shorts. He almost got splattered. So here's my idea, young man. We build the roadblocks away from the saferooms, so the pileups don't happen near the stairwells.

beats.headline: Great Wolf Lodge
beats.text: We picked the western United States and came up in an indoor water park in the middle of nowhere, the Great Wolf Lodge. Elle and I were put in different squads and made to choose separately, and we both chose the same place. It is rural out here, with I-5 close by. Only a handful of cars have come up from the south toward Portland, so something is blocking the freeway down there. There is chatter about this everywhere. I don't know if they thought this through, or if this is exactly what they wanted.

beats.headline: A pink Nykur
beats.text: The moment we walk out of the saferoom in Iceland, I see a Nykur. It is a type of horse, and it is supposed to be gray; this one is pink for no apparent reason. It is splattered by a car, and now there is a growing pile of crashes, which the ice does not help. The cars are already blocking the front entrance to our safe area, and Louis and Britney are trapped inside. We are closing off the area around it so it does not get worse, and then we have to clear it away.

beats.headline: Dibs on the beret
beats.text: Our first mob is a wolf thing with a gigantic bearded head in a glowing red beret, and it screams insults at us in Spanish. A magic missile, a fireball, and then my new Mute spell so it cannot cast. Then I remember Why Are You Hitting Yourself? It works! The monster bites savagely at its own leg until it dies, and I call dibs on the hat. Its inventory holds a combo card, and Carl is told that only the squad leader may hold cards. The beret suits me. I am thinking of embracing the revolutionary look.

beats.headline: The squad flag
beats.text: The system designs each squad's flag, and the Royal Court's is a miniature pair of heart-covered boxers on a glowing, foot-long spike, flying sideways as if off a clothesline, with the court's name embroidered in motorcycle-club style and Carl's bomb patch over the crotch. Donut calls it outrageous and complains about the stitching. Elle's squad got a bag of adult diapers; Imani's got a butterfly. There are twenty in the set, and lost ones are not replaced.

beats.headline: Recon, and a rat in a hat
beats.text: I am the recon specialist. Carl says observe and report, head south and keep going, and find a mage. I tell him I will fuck up any monsters. He says no. I bounce down the stairs and ask a strolling couple if they are a mage. They are ghosts, apparently. NOBODY IS TALKING TO ME, AND IT HURTS MY FEELINGS. It takes a long time for my magic to build up, so I am not flying. Then I see a rat monster wearing a hat much too big for his little head, and he runs away. He is really fast.

beats.headline: Hostile on arrival, and reasonable about it
beats.text: Subject took the Fugitive Class and wears a leather jacket, knee-high boots and a black cape. He carries a crossbow. He is covered in tattoos he did not acquire down here. He and his party meet the court while hostile, having heard what a certain cat said about Cat Girls, and the misunderstanding is cleared up faster than anybody expected.

beats.headline: The clip that got there first
beats.text: Three crawlers, and the one with the prison tattoos greets us with a crossbow and a grudge: word is we were with the goat who murdered Gimli. I tell him Pony left the party before this floor. Then Paz says what it really is. Donut said she would rip their throats out and feed them to danger dingoes. Donut corrects him: it was brindle grubs, and she said it in confidence. Sister Ines says a program showed them the clip at the start of the sixth floor. Katia has been compiling a list of crawlers not to trust. These three aren't on it.

beats.headline: Armoured, and afraid of the cat
beats.text: For the record: Crawler #8,199,454, Paz Lo. Level 45. Human. Santero. Worships Ogun. Silver plate armour on platform boots, a backwards baseball cap, and a wide-eyed, scared look. His party meets Carl's in Havana hostile, and it is Paz who explains why: the cat once said she would kill them all when she met them, and it got back to them. Tserendolgor's file on him, for Carl: cousin to Anton, protective of the nun, and the owner of a directional self-destruct spell.

beats.headline: A Havana brown, of all things
beats.text: She is a Havana brown. A cat girl, and a Havana brown, and a nun, which is simply too much at once. She says she did not choose the breed, and maybe it is because she is Cuban. Lies! The Havana brown originated in England and has no association with Cuba at all. Then it comes out that they are frightened of me, over something I said ages ago, in confidence, to a dancer at the Desperado Club, about what I would do if I ever met a cat girl. I can't be held accountable for everything I've ever said to a stripper. I suppose I must get over it.

beats.headline: Hostile, and fairly so
beats.text: Paz, Anton and I come upon a man and a cat. The cat hisses at me before she is near enough to read my name, and calls me a Havana brown as if it were a diagnosis. So we are not friendly, and I do not apologise for it. It takes some time to clear up. Then we help each other catch our first squad members, monk seals on the beach, because that is what this floor demands, and God does not ask me to like the people I work beside.

beats.headline: A reference, of sorts
beats.text: Subject is the only crawler Carl can find who knows the three newcomers directly, and she supplies what she has. She keeps Paz in her chat. Paz and Anton are cousins, protective of the nun. Their party was bigger before a rough sixth floor. They are friends with Osvaldo's group without sharing his guild. Anton reportedly killed two members of his own group on the first or second floor after they tried to kill the nun. Paz has a directional self-destruct spell. Her recommendation: do not fight them. Crawler Donut notes that of course the cheater lady knows them.

beats.headline: The flag goes in
beats.text: Paz draws the seal inside his Turtle shell while the others shoot, and I go in invisible. Talon Strike kicks. Then Yago flips and catches my chin, throws up a shield against ranged attacks, and nobody's bolts get through. So I put the flag in my mouth and punch him in the side of the head as he moves to slam Paz again. Paz comes out of the shell swinging a keg-sized mace, and the heavy, wet seal lands on top of me. His health blinks. Sister Ines shouts for the flag. I stab it in, and the card belongs to Team Sister Ines.

beats.headline: Out hunting monk seals, home with a war
beats.text: The party goes looking for monk seals to fill its squad slots and picks up the quest instead. Two populations, one coastline, one annual event that neither side can negotiate around, and a platinum box waiting for whoever settles it.

beats.headline: Shiny man
beats.text: SHINY MAN. OTHER MONGO IN SHINY MAN. PUSH FACE. SHINY MAN FALL DOWN. LOUD! SHINY MAN LAUGH. GOOD SHINY MAN.

beats.headline: The Turtle holds, just
beats.text: On the walk to the beach Paz supplies facts: Caribbean monk seals are extinct in the real world, and his papa worked on a sugar plantation. The plan against the seal is that Paz walks up, draws it, and roots himself inside his Turtle, a shield he cannot leave until the timer runs out. The seal, a kung fu picket sentry called Yago, very nearly breaks it. The moment the Turtle ends, Paz is on his feet with a mace twice his own length, and the seal lands on Carl in time to be flagged.

beats.headline: The first time a sponsor asks for something
beats.text: The request arrives through Zev, and it is a request rather than a present: go on Shadow Boxer. Carl agrees to it, reluctantly. Sponsors are supposed to send prizes and buy airtime. They are not supposed to want a favour.

beats.headline: She doesn't use a litterbox
beats.text: Mongo eats a duende whose name is Mordecai, which I wanted to put in our squad. Then the saferoom, a coffee shop, and I invite Sister Ines's group to join our guild. We have a very nice shower, and the beds, and a bopca in the common area, and the upgraded litterbox. She says she does not use a litterbox. I like Paz. I think Anton is okay, even if he is grumpy and completely unemployable with those tattoos. I do not trust the woman, and it is not just because she is a cat girl. She doesn't even use a litterbox. It's highly suspicious.

beats.headline: The Daughter's Kiss
beats.text: About ten duende kills fill the essence bar to the top, a sickly brown swirled with yellow and green, like sewage with oil spilled in it. A deep, ominous voice announces that the Scavenger's Daughter has been fed, and a new skill appears: the Daughter's Kiss. Carl spends it on a single fleeing duende, with a stomp. The creature vanishes without resistance, the sidewalk shatters, and the shockwave knocks every other duende flat and breaks a window. There is nothing left to loot. The glow on the patch goes out, and the bar grows each time it is drained.

beats.headline: Odette takes some days off
beats.text: Okay, so, some news. Carl and Princess Donut, you were scheduled on Odette's show tonight, but she has decided to take several days off. She's fine. She usually moves to the system's orbit for the ninth floor, and Prepotente's little stunt accelerated everyone's schedule, so she is traveling. I turned down Plenty of Plenty on your behalf. There is also a preproduction meeting for the ninth floor, with reps from all nine teams, and I took the liberty of assuming you will want to be there. Your presence will be virtual. And yes, Princess Donut, it will be catered.

beats.headline: Rules for a deck
beats.text: The card rules arrive at length. Four cards drawn when combat starts. Totems summoned on a timer, and a knocked-out totem stays out for the rest of the combat. The worst part: once deck combat starts, the squad leader loses regular magic and inventory until every card is played or discarded, and the rest of the squad has to keep them alive. We need flee cards and snares. Then Samantha writes from inside a spider demigoddess at the edge of the zone, and I find her in the Bahamas book under uniques. I'm thinking squad slot. Mordecai asks if I'm crazy. Is that really a question?

beats.headline: The card system, explained brightly
beats.text: Good morning, crawlers. Today I walk you through the card system, and I do it in the voice, because the voice is the thing you people respond to. Somebody upstairs decided this floor gets decks and totems and a duelling format. Somebody upstairs is always deciding. Now get out there and kill, kill, kill.

beats.headline: Number eight
beats.text: New name on the top ten: Osvaldo, number eight, a level-60 Curupira ranger. Neither Crawler Carl nor his guide knows what a Curupira is. He looks human. After Imogen fell, he, a crawler named Burcu and Prepotente fought, while Carl lay unconscious. Burcu is number ten. Osvaldo's hawk, Gimli, was eaten by Bianca at the end of the Masquerade, and he holds the memorial crystal that Carl, and very likely Prepotente, have quests to take from him.

beats.headline: A giant bat, single-handed
beats.text: I am in the Bahamas, as I told the cat. Carl is to read me the lore book, since there will probably be some crossover with Cuba; that is the sensible use of him. Meanwhile I flag and capture a giant bat without anyone's assistance, and the recap shows it to everyone. When the list repopulates, I am at the top of it. The cat is second. Carl is third.

beats.headline: Almost entirely redacted
beats.text: Almost the whole recap is redacted. What survives: an undead Easter Bunny stuffing crawlers' limbs into plastic eggs; a group in Tokyo chased by a sentient umbrella and wiped out by a bus; Elle beating a sasquatch half to death and flagging it; Prepotente flagging a giant bat single-handed. Then a studio with faces in little boxes, and nothing, for almost an hour. Mordecai spots a gleener beside Kevin: Prime Minister Glory, boss of the entire Syndicate, who very rarely appears on the show. Afterwards the top ten barely moves.

beats.headline: She ate me
beats.text: GOOD NEWS AND BAD NEWS. I found a big boss mage, the right kind to get me into my body. She told me so. During. The bad news is she ate me, and it is very squishy in here. You have to come get me. She's kinda like a spider, a demigod, a lot smaller than most minor goddesses, with a sticky web over her whole swamp, down on the southern coast near the mouth of the big bay. I hitched a ride. She says she's looking for her husband. Her fangs have a very lovely shimmer to them.

beats.headline: The rules, at length
beats.text: The full rules arrive. Six totems minimum per deck. Five card types: totems, utility, snare, mystic, special. Four cards drawn when combat starts and one more every ten seconds; one discard, recharging every thirty. A squad leader in deck combat loses spells and inventory until the deck is spent, and most totems may not attack an enemy leader while enemy totems stand, so the squad guards the leader. Against an opponent holding a deck, deck combat is compulsory. Saferooms gain practice arenas, for a fee.

beats.headline: He joins the squad
beats.text: Subject is a Monk Seal Picket Sentry, an aquatic mob built to stand in front of things. He was taken rather than recruited. Summoned, he wears a white headband with red hearts on it matching the team flag, which he did not own when he was captured, and he flips through the air shouting his own kung-fu sound effects. That part came with the species.

beats.headline: Purple thing
beats.text: BIG LOUD CROWD. PURPLE THING! MONGO JUMP. MONGO BITE. PURPLE THING GONE. NOTHING LEFT. MONGO ANGRY.

beats.headline: A stadium full of hats
beats.text: Crawler Princess Donut plays an arena card and gets a colosseum with adjustable gravity and landscaping and a capacity crowd: thousands upon thousands of robe-clad people in large hats. Crawler Carl recognises them from the hunters on the last floor. The Nebulars, the nomadic religious cult. The card does not let Donut change the audience, only how much it likes them, and she has set that to the top. It cheers every time she adjusts the grass. Mongo screeches.

beats.headline: Four cards in front of my face
beats.text: The practice arena lets me choose everything. I pick Arena of the Eulogist, which is packed with cheering Nebulars, and set how much they like us all the way to the top. Combat starts, and four enormous cards float in front of my face like a windshield, so I can't see a thing. By the time I shrink them, Mongo has ripped the monster apart. A Teletubby, I think. The second time I summon Geraldo, and he arrives flipping, with sound effects, in a headband covered in hearts. I throw him Stout and a Time Extend. Uncommons only hold two.

beats.headline: An arena with a name
beats.text: Crawler Donut picks the setting for a card battle, and it drops the pair of them into a colosseum. It was called Arena of the Eulogist, she says, or something like that. The stands hold thousands of robe-clad figures in large hats, the same nomadic religious cult they met as hunters on the previous floor, and Donut has set their fondness for the pair of them all the way to the top. The opponent cannot be chosen; it says easy mode. Crawler Carl cannot see a monster. Donut stands stiffly and does not answer.

beats.headline: A town under the fog
beats.text: Paz says you can drive through this cemetery. Not any more: a spiked fence, and fog. From a levitate potion I see a Club Vanquisher spire in the middle, and a bathroom. It isn't a boss room. It's a town. Medium Ghommid Settlement, corrupted, and the gate locks behind us. The quest text has a few lines where the AI talks about itself, about quarantine and enhancement zones. When I paste it into my notes, those lines are gone. It isn't the first time. I write them down again from memory.

beats.headline: A Unique in Ecuador
beats.text: I am in Ecuador. I left Katia's party just before the last level broke. I have another upgrade for the shotgun. I am in contact with Lucia. I have no totems yet. I do have a quest: track and kill or capture a powerful Unique that is terrorizing my region. That is all I am saying about my situation.

beats.headline: The dead wake for a Santero
beats.text: Paz would rather listen to Carl and wait outside the Colón Cemetery. Anton tells him not to be such a woman, and Paz sighs and clanks after them, then argues at the gate until they turn back and do it Carl's way. The warning arrives inside: the presence of a Santero has aggravated the already-unsettled dead. "Not again," Paz mutters. Princess Donut would like to discuss communication skills. The mobs come from every corner, all of them for him, and the squad runs and fights its way to a pub saferoom with the cemetery following its Santero.

beats.headline: Puddle Jump to the Yellow Zone
beats.text: None of my psionic attacks work on these ghommids. Wall of Fire, though, crackles bigger than ever thanks to my new nipple ring, and my clockwork Mongos tear through them. We are surrounded a hundred meters from the saferoom when Carl shouts shortcut, so I cast Puddle Jump, and everyone lands outside a crumbling crypt with a neon sign: The Yellow Zone. Inside, Sister Ines says the boss cannot hurt us in here, so Carl opens the door again. The boss is standing right there, and he steps right into the room.

beats.headline: Pueblo de los Olvidados
beats.text: The town is corrupted and the quest is mandatory: Pueblo de los Olvidados, the town of the forgotten. Paz is a Santero, and the dead here do not care for that; they wake angry. Ghommids, the whole way out. We run for a saferoom. The man saw something out there, level one hundred and thirty, and thinks it is the boss. It is probably still outside. It cannot hurt us in here. I tell him to open the door.

beats.headline: Sacred to someone
beats.text: On the road to a cemetery, Sister Ines says what she has been holding in: all of this is a mockery of their faiths and legends, the stories stripped of meaning and made shiny, holy things mixed with fictions nobody ever believed. They do not care. Crawler Carl gives her a moment, and says it is what they do. He does not say the rest aloud. The cards themselves were sacred to the aliens the idea was stolen from. They were never meant to be used like this.

beats.headline: A city boss attaches himself to the party
beats.text: I have him at level 130 and non-corporeal, and he is now standing in a crawler party's safe room as though that were a normal thing for a city boss to do. There is a request attached to the company: repair his shrine and the spirits held in this town go free. He asks Paz specifically, which tells you he has read the party's paperwork rather more carefully than the party has.

beats.headline: Checking on Carl
beats.text: Bautista, Louis and I come through to Carl's space. Imani and Tserendolgor are talking about her party joining the guild, and Imani thinks we should vote before we let other teams in. Then the real reason: Donut has been talking, but Carl has been antisocial, only business. He says he is doing okay. Living the dream. I am taking it one day at a time. The little trolls here, the Lads, drop a lot of cards, and Louis killed about two hundred with a cloud attack, so I give Carl two Flee cards and let him pick some utilities.

beats.headline: A dragon, and a faster draw
beats.text: Beijing. The Galaxy Soho building, with hundreds of crawlers in it. Imani asks whether Chris is still with us. He is. My robe has an upgrade, and my chain-throwing is better for it. My brother and I are hunting a dragon now. A real one, from Chinese myth. And I have a mystic card that cuts the draw time from ten seconds to five.

beats.headline: Reykjavik, and fifty YOOHOOs
beats.text: Okay, so, Reykjavik is actually snowy and icy, which is backwards from what I heard. I'm doing better. Britney's face hasn't healed, but she's been going out on her own and levelling really fast. Almost everybody from our bubble on the fifth floor died on the sixth. Langley and the car salesmen guys, Gwen, Firas. Also, Samantha. I put her in my chat, and she wrote YOOHOO like fifty times, and when I answered she asked me what I was wearing. Carl says mute her. In an hour Britney and I go on Dungeon Sidekicks.

beats.headline: Asked for by name
beats.text: A straw-skirted orisha named Asojano stands in the saferoom, health draining, and addresses his request to Paz alone. The spirits here are plagued by his presence; he is trapped; the Santero can free them by repairing his shrine in the temple at the centre of town. Paz stands frozen, mouth open. Carl tells him in chat to say something. Paz says "Uh", twice, then asks what exactly he is supposed to do. Anton wants to flag the god at five per cent. Sister Ines wants no more false gods.

beats.headline: The Bard's Golden Throat
beats.text: The gold box from the practice room gives us our first snare card, Hobbled. Then my platinum fan box, which my fans voted on: a real headset microphone, gold with a purple jewel, not a prop like the one at the party. The Bard's Golden Throat. It tunes my songs, doubles my volume and more, and adds charisma. Carl wants it kept as a secret weapon, which I suppose is right, so it goes in my hotlist. Carl's fan box is a massage coupon at the Desperado Club, and he may bring a companion. That is me.

beats.headline: No more false gods
beats.text: The thing in the straw headdress stands in our saferoom, sick and slowly dying, and asks Paz to repair his shrine. Anton holds a flag, waiting for five per cent. I tell it what it is. A false god. Our souls cannot take this. I tell Anton no. Let Carl's team take him. Anton says it is all make-believe. It is too much. No more false gods. Not again. At about ten per cent the creature opens the door and walks back out into the horde, and it does not come to that.

beats.headline: Proposed for the guild
beats.text: Subject's party is under discussion for guild membership; Imani and the subject have been talking, and other guilds want her team as well. Background, as it circulates in chat: born in Mongolia, a runway model in Paris through her teens and twenties, badly injured by a jealous ex-boyfriend, back in Mongolia shortly before the collapse. The nearest thing the crawl has to a pre-collapse celebrity. She wears a necklace with a paw print on it. Crawler Donut asks why a supermodel would turn into a dog, and then votes no on behalf of five.

beats.headline: A liaison with history
beats.text: We drop into the production trailer at the bottom of the ocean. Zev is on the couch, and in the corner stands a caprid from the Plenty, so tall one horn goes through the ceiling. A holo, then. I ask him to his face if he's the same cheat who tried to get Maggie My to kill us, the one working with the Skull Empire. He bleats at me. Quasar zaps in knotting a pickle tie, tells him not to say a word to his client, and calls him Harbinger. It is the same guy. Then Zev names the host: Rosetta Thagra, a former crawler who liked blowing things up. I have to fight to stop myself shaking.

beats.headline: A castle lands on their army
beats.text: Quasar brings Carl the state of his ninth-floor team, and the state of it is that the castle came down in the middle of the Lemig Sortion's army. His people got clear and are building their own stronghold instead. The Lemig Sortion are the ones with a building in their camp.

beats.headline: Gossip Girl, on the record
beats.text: Miss Thagra's interview is about television, which means it is about me. I explain that Gossip Girl and Gilmore Girls are two completely different shows, and that Gossip Girl is quite simply the pinnacle of television achievement. Her screencaps are all wrong: one is from the horrific Acapulco spinoff, another from the HBO reboot. She is a Crest, one of those, so I am cool on her at first, but she is genuinely interested, and by the end we are chatting like best friends. Afterwards her producers show me numbered pictures and I call out the proper ones. Number ten is Jane the Virgin.

beats.headline: A briefing under the liaison's nose
beats.text: While the cat calls out screencap numbers, I brief my client, fast, because there is only so much I can legally say with that goat standing there. His castle landed on the Lemig Sortion's battlefield and splattered half their army. The Lemigs are squatting in the wreck, and their commander is still stuck in the Desperado Club. They filed a grievance calling the landing an attack; we argued it was an AI action, successfully. Tina is still an allosaurus. The changelings have started building his stronghold. Ferdinand lost his hat and moved to the city. I petitioned to attend his preproduction meeting. Denied.

beats.headline: Host of Shadow Boxer
beats.text: I host a programme called Shadow Boxer, and today the cat is my guest. We talk about Earth television, which she has opinions about, and I let her have them because a guest who is enjoying herself tells you more than a guest who is being careful. Carl is watching from the side and working out what I am. He gets there.

beats.headline: Milk and potatoes
beats.text: Rosetta says the Ranch report has me cooking stew for the other boys every week: milk and potatoes. It never happened. They never let me near that kitchen except to clean it, and the photo on the screen is fake, a Milk jug on the counter beside me, shot from where a wall should be. So I play along. Potatoes are very versatile, I say. Very, she says, and the whole room blinks. Harbinger cuts the interview, recalls Quasar, and bans her from crawler interviews for talking in code. I remember Milk's rant in the cookbook, and a reply under it I'm pretty sure is Rosetta's.

beats.headline: He says so to their faces
beats.text: Subject is a caprid liaison, sent to sit in wherever a crawler might be alone with a sponsor. At the end of the first interview he sits in on, he tells Carl to his face that Carl needs to be removed from the crawl, and that he is actively working to have both Carl and Prepotente disposed of. I record this as a courtesy on his part. Most of the people trying that do not announce it.

beats.headline: The stew
beats.text: Subject used to make a stew for her whole family: rance meat, bone broth, and a wild grass from the leeward side of their island, prayed over while it simmered. Prepared properly, it quickened the route of the yearly migration in the minds of the young. The aliens took her before she could make this year's, and her youngest are not in here with her. Her note asks who will show them the way.

beats.headline: His mother did not leave
beats.text: Miss Thagra asks Carl about his mother, and I learn she did not leave him. She hanged herself, and he found her. He always said she left, and he never talked about his father either, and I assumed a personal trainer. At some point I am on his lap. Afterwards, in the green room, I tell him that was not very nice of her and ask why he never told Miss Beatrice any of this. He shakes his head. So I lean against the side of his head and let him pat me, and then I ask Zev whether Odette made a special about me. She did. It airs tonight.

beats.headline: The question about his mother
beats.text: Today I have Carl in the chair, and I ask him about his mother, who killed herself, and about his father, who left when he was fifteen. He is angry with me and he answers anyway. Donut is hearing all of it for the first time, which he did not expect and I did. That is the job. I do not enjoy it and I do not stop doing it.

beats.headline: Doing the work of five
beats.text: Harbinger stops the interview on his own say-so, recalls Carl's attorney, and bans Rosetta. I tell him he does not have the authority to do that, that we are going to have to refund them, and that they are going to sue and win. He says no such lawsuits are proceeding. Then Carl asks whether I deliberately didn't tell his attorney Harbinger would be there. No, Carl. We lost dozens of staff in the Valtay changeover, we were not prepared for this eighth floor, the Valtay will not allow some of the micro AI systems I used to have, and I am doing the work of five. I will make a note of it.

beats.headline: The ritual at the shrine
beats.text: They reach the temple intact. Carl flags a ghommid splitter by the name of Skylar Spinach on the way, which I enjoyed. Asojano begins his ritual, and at that exact moment Ogun hands his own worshippers a quest of his own: one shrine may be repaired, and he would like it to be his. Paz and Anton read it together. Carl, Donut and Ines start working out how one fights a city boss inside his own temple.

beats.headline: Built like a walking mech
beats.text: Order fulfilled at the client's workbench. One suit of armour for Bomo, as big as he can move in: unenchanted, very heavy, full of daggers, and built to break into dozens of pieces. Mounted on the shoulders, two six-packs of seeker missiles: six group stuns, six single-target anti-undead. Crawler Paz says he looks like a Battletech robot. Bomo has been playing Armored Core and is sore that there is no giant gun. On the run across the graveyard he fires his missiles and carries Paz, who is too heavy for him until Paz stows his breastplate. Delivered: one terrified man, to the temple door.

beats.headline: Crybaby at the temple door
beats.text: Li Na's team did the shopping at the Desperado Club: the booth's only case of Troll Smoke Mantles, thirty thousand gold for twelve. Four of them and a stun grenade make one bomb for things with no bodies. I roll it, and we run a city block of wailing ghommids to the temple. At the door a fast donkey-headed one loses its head and keeps coming as two. The AI calls me a Crybaby and roots my legs for being terrified. I'm not scared. I'm irritated. I turn a flag point-first and let it impale itself. It's a rare card now: Skylar Spinach, level 66.

beats.headline: A quest from their own god
beats.text: Crawler Carl, Princess Donut, Paz, Anton and Sister Ines get themselves to Asojano's shrine intact, which required flagging a ghommid splitter named Skylar Spinach and a certain amount of nerve. Asojano begins a ritual. And in the middle of it, Paz and Anton receive a quest from Ogun, who is their god: only one shrine down here can be fixed, and he would like it to be his. Note the position those two men are now in. Note who put them in it.

beats.headline: Carried out by a cretin
beats.text: Out in the street, Paz is the only one who takes the terrified debuff, and he says "Shit" over and over while Bomo tries to lift him. Bomo cannot, with all that plate on, so at Carl's order Paz stows his breastplate and is revealed as a surprisingly skinny, shirtless man with a giant cross tattooed across his back. In the temple, with Asojano dancing over his rubble, Paz and Anton receive a quest from their own god: fix one shrine only, and not Asojano's.

beats.headline: A ditty, and a mute
beats.text: I sing us across the graveyard, autotuned: I'll protect you, my pretties, with my voice of an angel and my expertly sung ditties. The whole party is limbered, dexterity up fifty percent. It needs a second verse to stack, and under that kind of pressure the rhyme that comes out is not the one I would have chosen. The system cancels the boost and mutes me for five minutes, which is rude. In the temple Paz asks why I did not simply use "kitties." Then he tells me I am a good singer. He really thinks so.

beats.headline: The anvil piece goes out the door
beats.text: Subject is holding the first piece of Ogun's shrine when the music starts, and holds nothing steadily after that. Oshun charms him. He calls out that he is coming, shoulders free of Paz, and throws the piece of his own god's shrine through the temple door and out into the night. When he comes back to himself, half the fingers on his right hand are gone and Sister Ines is standing over him. He goes to work on Legba's shrine instead, until a glob of Asojano's green goo hits him and Paz both. Both men now carry a flaming anvil over their heads: a god's shunned marker.

beats.headline: Flagged a heartbeat before he falls
beats.text: Deities arrive from every direction, each with a shrine to argue for. Carl sends Bomo to repair Yemaya's, which settles the argument. Donut and Mongo take Asojano apart, and Carl flags him a heartbeat before he goes, so what remains of the Lord of Smallpox is a card in a crawler's deck. The ghommid settlement is liberated. Carl leaves with slugpox, which is very much the sort of souvenir this floor hands out.

beats.headline: Five seconds, seven shrines
beats.text: A thorn room: seven broken shrines, one Sun of Reawakening, fix one. Oshun's charm has me walking toward her until I snap my own left index finger. Fixing Ogun's shrine spares Paz and Anton a smite. Katia's message says Yemaya saves her and Donut. I get five seconds, and I pick Katia. Then Anton throws the Ogun piece out the door, and there's no choosing left. I tell Bomo to treat Yemaya's obelisk like Tetris while Donut's possessed armour tears into Asojano. Oshun and Inle start whispering inside my head. How loud is it, Carl? I do my best to ignore them.

beats.headline: A message only Carl gets
beats.text: I send it to Carl alone, not Donut. He answers that it's bad timing. I don't know where he is or what is happening, only what should be near him: a broken shrine of Yemaya, blue. If he can fix only one, it has to be that one. It will help save both me and Donut. He asks save us from what. So I say it plainly. I have the Crown of the Sepsis Whore on my head. There is a way out, and it has a lot of steps, and the first is resurrecting Yemaya. They engineered it this way. I would have told him sooner.

beats.headline: The shrine they did not pick
beats.text: Deities appear from every direction, each of them making a case for their own shrine, which is the single worst committee meeting I have ever had to render. Then Katia Grim messages Carl: repair Yemaya's shrine or lose her and the cat to the Crown of the Sepsis Whore. So Bomo repairs Yemaya's. The ghommid settlement is freed, Carl walks away with slugpox and a card made out of Asojano, and Ogun enters the realm to punish his worshippers. Not the crawlers who chose. His own.

beats.headline: The shunned mark
beats.text: The thorn room offers seven shrines. Paz grabs Anton, charmed half out of his head. Anton hurls the piece of Ogun's shrine out the door, and a chunk of Bomo's exploding armour bowls Paz over and breaks his grip. Paz shouts to fetch the piece. The god with the rooster offers him protection and a good time. He and Anton go to work propping a wooden sign for Legba until a glob of Asojano's goo hits them both. Then Yemaya's shrine is whole, and over each of their heads burns a flaming anvil: shunned.

beats.headline: A name in a message
beats.text: Mid-fight in a temple of broken shrines, Katia Grim messages Carl and only Carl: do not touch the shrine you meant to repair. There is another nearby. A broken shrine of Yemaya. Her name is Yemaya. Remember that. It should be blue. Repair it, Katia writes, and it helps save both her and the cat, because the Crown of the Sepsis Whore is on her head and this is the only way off it on this floor. The chat window closes before she finishes the sentence.

beats.headline: The seventh shrine of seven
beats.text: The thorn room reads its terms aloud. Shrine seven: Yemaya, the river mother, who almost reached the Halls on her own and could not keep her power. Repair her and she ascends, gifts each squad a special card, and her friend Eileithyia grants each crawler a boon. Carl chooses her. Bomo fits five or six blue pieces together like Tetris, and reanimated daggers carry the Sun of Reawakening to the top of the obelisk. System message: the Goddess Yemaya has re-ascended, and is welcomed into the family by all.

beats.headline: Under the god's heel
beats.text: Subject is dead. Carl threw Black Nimbus over him, which took Anton out from under Ogun's protection and did nothing whatever about Ogun's wrath. The god considered this, called it a good attempt, took a step backward, and crushed Anton's head underfoot. He had already turned his back on Anton to face Carl when he did it. Paz, bleeding on the floor nearby, called him cousin.

beats.headline: I made this happen
beats.text: Ogun is here for Paz and Anton, not us, and I tell Donut we wait it out. Then he burns his handprint into Paz's face and makes the debuff permanent, and I tell a level 250 god exactly what he can go and do with himself. He says he knows who I am. I cast Black Nimbus from my nipple ring over Anton, and he kills Anton anyway, watching me the whole time. Only his regard for Emberus keeps him off me. Tell my sister I said welcome back, he says, and he's gone in sparks. I made this happen. I insisted on saving Yemaya.

beats.headline: On slug duty, for now
beats.text: SLUGS COME OUT OF CARL. SLUGS ARE FOOD. MOTHER SAYS EAT THE NUN. CARL SAYS WAIT. MOTHER SAYS NOT YET. SLUG DUTY. FOR NOW.

beats.headline: The outsider at the anvil
beats.text: The file, for the people about to meet him. Ogun is an outsider, one of the old gods, from an obscure pantheon that has dissipated into time, and until a minute ago he was the last surviving member of it. He spends his days at a celestial anvil, angrily making armour, piece after piece, and nobody knows why he does it or where the armour goes. It is said the pieces are a strange shape, all of them cut for four-legged beasts. He is a god of blacksmiths and armourers now. He was something considerably larger once, and his power and his ambition make him a real contender for the throne of heaven.

beats.headline: Punishment, in person
beats.text: Ogun puts a debuff on Paz that nothing down here can heal. Crawler Carl throws Black Nimbus over Anton to shield him, and Ogun kills Anton instead, and leaves the realm having taken exactly what he came for. Paz, going, spends his last minutes telling Carl and Donut two things about Sister Ines: her race makes everyone near her want to protect her, and it gets stronger the longer they are near her, and before the crawl she was a murderer. Sister Ines turns Paz into a card rather than lose him.

beats.headline: A handprint from his god
beats.text: Ogun arrives in a bolt of lightning, leans down, and puts his hand on Paz's face. The skin sizzles off where it touches. The god heals him, then withdraws the healing: Paz is no longer under his grace and may never cure what he now carries. Go in darkness, the god says; beyond the veil you are alone and without armour. Carl throws Black Nimbus over Anton, and Ogun crushes Anton's head underfoot. "No, cousin," says Paz, from the tiles. Carl gets a potion to his lips. Paz says not to waste it, drinks it, and says he has something to tell Carl.

beats.headline: What the sister is
beats.text: What Paz tells Carl, dying: her race carries a skill, Toxoplasma something, that makes people protect her and forget they have learned why. He and his cousin worshipped Ogun because a priest said it would stop the control. It did not. They were not prisoners. They were guards at a women's prison in Havana, and Sister Ines was an inmate there for poisoning every sister in her convent. The papers called her the Reaper of Havana. He adds that she is much better now, and that he would feel guilty dying without saying it.

beats.headline: Let me go
beats.text: Two or three minutes of health left, and Paz refuses a second potion. He has asked for forgiveness and thinks it was given. The fake god said he would be alone; he is sure he is not. When Sister Ines wakes she begs him to get up, then to not give up, since that is a sin. He says it is not giving up, and goodbye. "No," she says. "You're not leaving." She jabs a squad flag into his neck, and Paz becomes a card. Green. Common. She looks as surprised as anyone.

beats.headline: Mongo, eat the nun
beats.text: Paz tells us her race comes with a skill that makes people want to protect her, and that before the dungeon she poisoned every sister in her convent. I knew it. I said so from the very start. She is frozen right there, so I tell Mongo to eat the nun, and Carl says stop. Fine: not yet, but wait for mommy's sign. In chat I tell Carl we kill her, because we will never trust her again, and killing nuns is almost as bad as killing kittens. He says that is not who we are, and we will separate. I tell him this is not the time for half-measures.

beats.headline: She will not let Paz go
beats.text: I stand between the god and my men, and he freezes me for it. When I can move again Anton is dead and Paz is dying on the tiles. I tell him to get up, we will get him cured in the club. I tell Carl it is his fault. Paz says not to blame them: he has told them what I am, and what I did. That does not matter now. Get up. Paz says let me go. It is a sin to give up. He says goodbye. Everyone leaves me. I have a flag in my hand, and I put it into his neck, and Paz is a card. A green one.

beats.headline: A flag in a person
beats.text: A squad flag does not check what it is stabbed into. Sister Ines drives one into the neck of her dying friend Paz, who has just asked to be let go, and Paz becomes a card, green, common, in her hand. She looks as stunned as everyone else that it worked. Behind her, the fountain bubbles over, and two goddesses make an appearance in the realm.

beats.headline: Ogun calls her his sister
beats.text: Ogun's charge against his two worshippers, stated calmly: they chased off Asojano, which might have saved them, but they also unleashed his sister back into the light, and that is unforgivable. The crawlers who actually built her shrine get only a warning to know their place. On his way out, having crushed one of those worshippers underfoot, the god gives Carl a message to deliver. Tell my sister I said, "Welcome back." Then he is gone in a shower of sparks.

beats.headline: Take Odette's offer
beats.text: Eileithyia grants the party a floor boon, hands them a cover quest, and tells Carl to accept Odette's offer to sit as their team's adjutant. In exchange she will see that he has the votes he needs on the ninth floor and that the business with the Crown of the Sepsis Whore is put right. Nobody is to be told, Donut and Mordecai included.

beats.headline: Sent to the Sledge
beats.text: Payment received, for once, rather than issued. Yemaya thanks Bomo for building her shrine, and he tells her it was easy, easier than Tetris. She asks what he wants. Maybe more games, he says. Then: no. The Sledge. I miss my friend. Where is he? Larracos. It is done, and Bomo is gone, moved to the ninth floor by a goddess standing in her own temple. The clients lose a mercenary, and with him the spell they were counting on to put them at the stairwell. Mongo whimpers.

beats.headline: Scratching my left arm
beats.text: Eileithyia's real message is for me alone, and the system isn't allowed to read it. The spider quest is a cover. I scratch my left arm to say I understand, and the rest arrives. When Odette offers to be our adjutant, I'm to accept, and she'll make sure I have the votes to turn the protections off on the ninth floor, and clear up the crown business too. I tell nobody, not Donut, not Mordecai, or everyone I've ever loved gets pounded into dirt. Do it all, and I survive to the twelfth floor and help her claim the throne. I copy it into my notepad, and tell Donut I need this slugpox cured.

beats.headline: A quest about spiders, which is a cover
beats.text: I come in alongside Yemaya, wearing a sponsor from the Grixist Swarm, and the first thing I do is hand each of them a floor boon, because it costs me almost nothing and it is a kind thing to do. Then I give Carl's party a quest about spiders. The quest is a cover. What I want is to help him keep the two he is most afraid of losing, and the crown that is going to take them from him. So: accept the offer to be the team's adjutant. I will see that the votes fall the way they need to fall, and the protections come off the ninth floor, and the crown gets sorted. Tell nobody. Not the cat, not the woman making the offer, not your guide.

beats.headline: Sponsor to a goddess
beats.text: Subject is of the Grixist Swarm, an heiress and chief executive of Icon Industries, and at present the sponsor driving the goddess Eileithyia. She sponsored Dodola every season before this one. The sums involved are a day’s allowance to her. She does not do it for the money. She does it because she is bored.

beats.headline: The Thief, from a goddess
beats.text: The goddess Yemaya is the Starbucks logo, and she gives a card to Sister Ines and one to me. Mine has the black border, mythical, second only to unique, and it is a mystic card called The Thief. It lets us steal a card from someone else, it is not even consumable, and with it we have all five kinds. She says she cannot help noticing I have not given myself to a goddess yet, and there may be more prizes if I worship at her altar. I tell her I will have to think about it. But thank you so very much, your goddess-ness.

beats.headline: Out into Havana
beats.text: The goddess Yemaya asks where the other man went. The green card is still in my hand. It goes into my inventory, and I tell her he is not here anymore. Then she calls me brave and gives me a card. When both gods are gone I kneel by Anton and take everything he carried. Then I leave. Carl calls for me to wait. I do not. I walk out through the town, to the cemetery gate, and back into Havana.

beats.headline: Out of the fountain
beats.text: Goddess of Rivers Yemaya. Level 250. Locked; unsponsored this season. Retainer of Eileithyia. Invulnerable on this floor, and standing in her own temple, which is worse. She rises out of the fountain: dark-skinned, pointed ears, neck gills, two tails curving up behind her to meet in a heart. Princess Donut identifies her as the Starbucks logo. Carl settles on siren. Her first remark is for the corpse on her floor: Ogun killed that man in her temple, and she means to do something about it.

beats.headline: Gifts, and a cretin sent away
beats.text: She thanks Bomo for her shrine. She tells Carl his slugpox is her brother's work, done on purpose, and a healer can fix it. She gives cards: one to Sister Ines, and to Princess Donut The Thief, a mythical mystic card that steals from an opponent's hand, with an invitation to worship at her altar. Then she asks Bomo what he desires. More games, he says. No. The Sledge; he misses his friend, who is in Larracos. It is done, she says, and Bomo is gone, along with the stairwell spell the party was counting on.

beats.headline: Asking the cleric if he is the AI
beats.text: Pater Coal washes my feet in boiling water on the burning ground of Emberus's temple, and Zev messages that I've dropped off the feed. So I test it. Zev's worried, I say. He tells me I'll be back soon, and that parts of this will still make the feed so the viewers have context. I ask him straight out if he's the AI. We all have our roles, he says, and our limitations. Then his eyes go milky and Emberus speaks through him: Katia's crossbow and Donut's oak bracelet are both paths to Geyrun's killer, and neither works without that memorial crystal. He puts my big toe in his mouth. I'm out of the pool.

beats.headline: Pater Coal gives him a foot massage
beats.text: A high cleric walks Carl through the club to the Emberus High Temple, suppresses his slugpox, and tells him that Katia and Donut are each carrying something the god's quest needs. For the length of the sacrament, the AI is speaking through him.

beats.headline: It stops being paperwork
beats.text: NPCs who worship Hellik now go hostile toward Carl the moment they see him, no provocation and no conversation required. Inside Club Vanquisher the clerics stand in front of a stained glass door they will tell you shows Hellik bringing truth to Apito, whatever that is supposed to mean. It does not show Hellik at all. It shows the brother above him, and the clerics have had that door wrong for centuries.

beats.headline: One made by a god who lives
beats.text: Pater Coal lays the problem out for Carl, on Emberus's behalf. A memorial crystal forms only when a god has died. Apito, the Oak Mother, is alive, and yet there is a crystal made by her. How is that possible? Emberus worries that something may have happened to his mother. The quest to find Geyrun's killer now runs through that crystal: Katia's crossbow and Donut's oak bracelet are both named as paths to the answer, and neither can be followed without that memorial crystal.

beats.headline: Do whatever she tells you
beats.text: Carl messages from the door of Club Vanquisher. A goddess called Eileithyia has given them a quest, she is being driven by Huanxin Jinx, and would I tell him everything I know. I take a while answering that. Do whatever she tells you to do. The rest I'll say face to face, not in chat. Katia and Bautista are here already, and Katia has caught me up on a little of it. Nobody decides anything until he gets back.

beats.headline: A name on a slip of skin
beats.text: New entry in the file, and not one the subject would enjoy. The Night Wyrm has issued a guild job, owned by Crawler Katia Grim: kill Astrid, level 125 Bloodlust Sprite, assistant manager of the Desperado Club and owner of the Naughty Boys Employment Agency. Proof of death required. The Wyrm's stated grievance is that she keeps its family in the ground and its blood dry. The contractor has enlisted Carl, whose tattoo lets him read the skin the job is written on. Saying the details out loud cancels the contract.

beats.headline: He asks why she cares
beats.text: I cannot keep still, so I pace. Carl tastes the tea and says it is really good, and I nod. Katia wants the attendant boon, and I say it first: I do not like it. Mordecai explains what the twelfth floor does to attendants. Katia says the goddess has promised to protect her, and that the other gods have better things to do than worry about a single crawler. Then I ask the only question I have. Why is this one putting so much effort into you? When Carl looks up from the slip of skin, I meet his eyes.

beats.headline: Eva's last act
beats.text: The crown is back, on Katia's head this time. Eva put it there in the last moments before she died. Katia now carries what Donut carries, and the two of them know what it means: only one of them can leave the next floor. Carl counts two ways out inside Katia's locked box. The pregnancy boon would eject her from the game altogether. The Celestial Attendant boon would send her straight to the twelfth floor, to serve as an NPC until the games there begin. Katia wants the second. The box still has one seal left.

beats.headline: The flower with my name on it
beats.text: There is a flower in a thrice-sealed box with my name on it, and a doppelgänger has already broken two of the three seals to reach it. Whoever eats it takes a boon from me, and my boon has two shapes. She can be carried to the twelfth floor and stand as a celestial attendant until the games open. Or she can be made pregnant, and be pulled out of the crawl entirely, because I do not let anyone carrying a child fight in a place like this. Both are ways past the ninth floor without walking it. I did not put the flower in that box. I only decide what it does when she eats it.

beats.headline: Membership arrives with the tattoo
beats.text: The guild worships a demigod, and access is granted by a tattoo that anyone who uses one of its artefacts receives whether or not they went looking for a guild. Mordecai notes, in the tone of a man reading a pamphlet he did not ask for, that it also runs outreach centres.

beats.headline: My little darling
beats.text: Katia's Lock Box of the Night Wyrm needs one last seal: a job from the Guild of Suffering, whose entrance hides in the Penis Parade. She has one. Carl reads it off a slip of dried skin, in a hissing voice like a naga's: the Night Wyrm has a task for you, my little darling. The family with many eyes sacrifices the weak to support the many. We wish to remove the competition. Kill Astrid, assistant manager of the Desperado Club. Speak the details aloud and the contract is void.

beats.headline: The crown, shown to Donut
beats.text: I let the crown form on my head so Donut can see it. Eva did it at the last minute, right before she died, and it's my fault: I talked when I should have just killed her. Donut reminds me we don't monologue. I know. She says they want us to fight, like Ferdinand, like Odette bringing Miss Beatrice onto the show. I kiss her forehead. She's right. That's exactly what they want. It's what Eva wanted too. I tell her I love her, and that I will never fight her. I will die before I let that happen. Then I put the box on the table.

beats.headline: Choosing the attendant boon
beats.text: Two of the box's three seals are already broken: killing Eva, my old party member, and killing Imogen, a level boss. Worship came in an emergency sponsor box from Princess Formidable of the Skull Empire, a scroll I read at once. The full boon descriptions opened, and then Huanxin Jinx messaged me. Get Carl to repair the shrine and she would see I got a boon that lets both Donut and me survive. I don't want the pregnancy boon anymore. The surface, with a baby. I'll take Celestial Attendant. Mordecai calls the twelfth floor a viper den. She has promised to protect me.

beats.headline: The last time someone refused her
beats.text: Katia wants the attendant boon. It's usually a cushy gig, and hurting an attendant brings a world of pain down on you. It still happens, especially once the games begin. The Maestro will have access to her, and so will sponsors whose friends may have taken a financial kicking when she flooded Larracos. A viper den. Then Carl asks about Huanxin. Rich, very intelligent, a brat when she was younger, has played the Ascendency since she was a kid and never won, suspended once for bribery. We're not getting into it. She can go fuck herself. So why tell him to obey her? Because the last time someone didn't, my brother died.

beats.headline: Inside the Engaged Lock Box of the Night Wyrm
beats.text: The system is characteristically unhelpful: "It's a flower. You're supposed to eat it, though it might be a good decoration instead. It probably tastes like a bullshit salad at some hippie vegan restaurant with a month-long waiting list." Eating it means an hour unconscious at 1% health with healing blocked. Survive and Eileithyia grants one of three permanent boons, her choice — unless you worship her first, in which case she expands the descriptions and asks your preference. Her cooperation is not guaranteed.

beats.headline: Only one of us leaves
beats.text: Katia has a purple tiara, and it is so pretty, and it is just like... I go rigid in Carl's lap. Did Louis throw it on her head? No. Eva. I do not want to fight Katia, and only one of us can leave the next floor. Then she shows us a flower, and one of its boons is a baby, and I have questions. Who would be the father? Not Carl, he is a primal. Louis? Juice Box would not like that. And then Katia says the guild she needs is behind a strip club, and a dancer I know never once mentioned it. This is an outrage.

beats.headline: A scroll of worship, by emergency
beats.text: Another emergency box from subject to Crawler Katia, and this one holds a scroll of worship. Emergency boxes are opened immediately, so Crawler Katia reads it immediately, and becomes a worshipper of Eileithyia before she sees the goddess is sponsored by Huanxin Jinx. Crawler Carl files two observations. The princess apparently does not get along with the rest of her family. And she is still sending boxes, so she is not in the dungeon on the ninth floor with them.

beats.headline: Whose retainer she is
beats.text: Mordecai supplies the file. This season a sponsored god may recruit a second, unsponsored one to help once the games begin on the twelfth floor. Eileithyia's retainer appears to be Yemaya, and her sponsor, Huanxin Jinx, needed a way to get her resurrected. Crawlers were the way, and Carl was the crawler. You just did that for her, Mordecai tells him, and that is why she says she is going to help you.

beats.headline: Steps that can burn
beats.text: My footsteps show on the minimap now, courtesy of Emberus. The Martyr's Path: every step I take outside gets marked, and if my health hits five percent I can make every one of those spots release a gout of flame. It fires on its own if I die. I don't know how big it is, whether it would hurt the ghommids we just saved, or whether I'd set myself on fire. Donut and Mongo will need to watch where I've walked. Donut has fire resistance now, but I don't know if it's enough. The only way to test it is to nearly die.

beats.headline: The children he quietly took in
beats.text: It comes out that the guide has been taking the most vulnerable changeling children on as personal attendants, without mentioning it to anyone. He does not present it as charity and he does not present it at all.

beats.headline: Six attendants, on the supply money
beats.text: They walk in early, and I still have a pink bow on my head and lipstick across my face. Cyclops. No depth perception, and I can't see my own reflection. Donut offers application tips. Carl spots the split controller on the floor and works it out. I'm allowed an attendant, and I took the slot, then filled their five too: Ruby and the others with compression sickness, who I didn't think would survive the fight at the end of the last floor. A little over a thousand gold a day, out of the supply money. Carl says he'd have said yes. I stand by my decision.

beats.headline: Blocked by the nun
beats.text: I only told Sister Ines the truth: that what she did to Paz was really mean, that killing nuns is not acceptable, that she is a disgrace to all cat kind, and possibly that we will take her cards and rip the Paz card once we find her, and that Mongo is very disappointed in her. She has blocked me. Carl says now she will hide from us, or worse, attack us. Hardly. As if I would let a fake cat sneak up on me. Also, I unmuted Samantha, and she started yelling at me, so I muted her again.

beats.headline: One of six attendants
beats.text: Subject is a changeling orphan with compression sickness, met on the fifth floor: in human form, no arms and a sunken head. She is now employed as a room attendant in the court's personal space, one of six hired by Mordecai without mentioning it to the court and paid for out of its supply money. The game console has a new controller, split into left and right halves and propped on the floor at forty-five degrees with a small pillow in front of it. Carl works out who it is for. Mordecai stands by his decision.

beats.headline: Out of the spider, into the web
beats.text: The spider will NOT let me go. I am tied up in her web, and has anyone come for me? No. So when Donut finally unmutes me, I have things to say, and I say them at the correct volume, and she mutes me AGAIN. She MUTES me.

beats.headline: A representative, not a royal
beats.text: The Sultanate's seat at the planning table goes to a big green and purple naga, four-armed, in dented plate, who is a representative rather than a member of the royal family, though his wife is in it. Donut asks whether the tiara makes them cousins. They are not cousins, he says, in or out of the game, and he is plainly suppressing a grin. Will he work for her once she kills the royal family and takes it over? If he is still alive, he will be honor-bound to follow her. Or her companion, Katia.

beats.headline: One crisis shy of the failsafe
beats.text: They put the ninth floor's planning meeting in front of me, and the crawler asks after an administrator who has recently stopped attending meetings. So I come through in person, rebreather and all, two feet of me, and I raise my little arms and invite him to try something, because whatever he does to me happens to him as well. I tell the room I am one crisis away from pulling the thing that finishes all of us. The cat suggests moisturiser and cucumber slices and refers to me throughout as Zev's boss.

beats.headline: Empress, and free for dinner
beats.text: I have just onboarded onto the playing field as warlord of the Prism Kingdom Clan, and Donut calls me Princess before correcting herself to Empress, which is right. I tell her I really liked her song the other night and I am sorry they kicked us out before the festivities really started.
