When it is my turn I introduce myself properly and tell the table that if anyone wants to catch a meal, I am available. A few restaurants in Larracos have finally opened back up. The naga says that is not advisable.

beats.headline: The planning meetings
beats.text: Warlords and their representatives meet before the floor opens, each from wherever they are, because the usual boardroom in Larracos is still underwater: introductions, precedence, and action items filed into a queue for a vote. Zev advises against Odette as the team's adjutant, because of what sits between Odette and Mordecai. Juice Box arrives wearing somebody else's face and kills one of the representatives. She is an NPC on nobody's team, so nothing in the rules covers what she just did.

beats.headline: Fangs, the robot
beats.text: Pre-production meeting, final seat. The representative introduces himself in a robotic voice as Warlord Fangs of the Reavers: a square-headed, old-school robot vibrating up and down as if powered by a diesel engine, straight out of a sixties science fiction film. Crawler Carl knows from the Cookbook that the look is for his benefit, and that Reavers can switch shape whenever they like. Crawler Donut asks whether his name is really Fangs, and whether he is a robot vampire or, better, a werewolf robot. Cascadia snaps at her. Before anyone answers, the Viceroy beside him loses his head.

beats.headline: Wearing the elf's mother
beats.text: The viceroy's head comes off and rolls across the table. I push the body aside, sit in his chair, twirl his mask and put my feet up. Hello again, boys. I'm wearing Epitome Noflex, the bald elf's mother, and he screams that his men told him I was dead. Obviously not. Faceless regenerates at sunset anyway. He wants the fish to intervene. The fish says I'm an NPC, not on Carl's team, the AI won't touch it, and they're free to kill me. Gotta catch me first. Then Carl looks right at me. Hello, Juice Box.

beats.headline: Cousins of the Reavers
beats.text: Faction wars briefing, on the Reavers: a megacorporation and system government living on a Dyson sphere, who were supposedly once related to the Nebulars, the religious nuts who sent a team called the Nebular Sin Patrol to die as hunters on the sixth floor. Like the nebs, the Reavers began as several biological races who enhanced themselves with machines. The Reavers kept going, until only the brains were left. The Nebulars stopped somewhere short of that.

beats.headline: A Jell-O mold at the table
beats.text: Seat two at the pre-production meeting holds no chair, just a big green blob: opaque, quivering, shaped into three tiers of decreasing size like a Jell-O mold from the 1970s. It may be a representative or it may be their king. Crawler Carl cannot tell, because they all look the same except for size. They breed by literally splitting apart, and they can merge back together. The mouth is at the top and speaks upward. I am Voting Admin Cell Mass Number three, it says, and bubbles gurgle out of the top.

beats.headline: Captain Enormous, proposed
beats.text: Crown Prince Stalwart calls me an imbecile, so I remind him how many times we humiliated him and his brother, and ask whether his mother is here, because I would be happy to sign an autograph for her. Oh wait. He promises to skin me alive and line his codpiece with my pelt, where it will warm his enormous genitals for a thousand years. Nobody had questioned the size of anything, so I propose an action item renaming him Captain Enormous. The Empress trumpets with laughter. The system rejects it: titles may not be changed. Oh, poo.

beats.headline: A mask at seat eight
beats.text: Seat eight at the pre-production meeting: a bulky humanoid with a long, thin, bone-white neck and a blank white mask. A Viceroy. They are a constant of Faction Wars and often its winners, though not lately, and they specialise in horrific battlefield spells and necromancy. Their home system is where non-citizens go for cheap medical procedures. Their team is called the Madness. The Viceroy raises a hand to Crawler Donut, says nothing, and then falls forward onto the table. His head rolls away like a billiard ball, and under the mask is a bone-white, tusked, demonic face.

beats.headline: Advice, off the record
beats.text: I turn on extra security, so this is an administrator speaking to show sponsors. Odette is going to ask to be their adjutant, and I think it's a bad idea. An adjutant is a neutral observer, part referee, usually someone loud and famous doing colour commentary, and Odette has done it a few times. But Odette was Mordecai's manager once, and if they are physically together he will attack her. He gets kicked out. His contract is in jeopardy. Half the children he is fostering get ejected. None of this is official. I like Mordecai. Please do not pick her.

beats.headline: Scarred, and level fifty-five
beats.text: Donut tells me it is not so bad. The whole left side of my face is burn scar from the end of the last floor, healed shiny and uneven. She says scars are beautiful and go with the barbarian look I am going for. I am not worried about it anymore. I have been talking to Tserendolgor, who once had a scar like this on her face. I am level 55 now. There is a new tattoo under my eye, an extinction sigil. I wiped out an entire race.

beats.headline: A snooze fest out west
beats.text: Carl asks in chat whether we're going into the Desperado Club. Imani tells him we still haven't found one. And it's a total snooze fest over here: all churches and boring monsters. I've got my squatchy and my gumberoo and my batsquatch, and everything else sucks. We don't even have any quests. So we're moving down to the outskirts of Portland to see if there's anything interesting there. Carl tells me to be careful.

beats.headline: A tenth team
beats.text: Carl files the item Juice Box came for: seat the floor's own NPCs as a team of their own, with the same protections the nine already carry. Rishi of the Blood Sultanate offers a compromise, invulnerability for the NPCs and a safe area of their own but no team, in return for an end to the attacks, and warns that the Sultanate will answer harshly if the killing at these meetings continues.

beats.headline: Six totems and a spare
beats.text: My squad's full: me and six totems, a saber-toothed tiger and a giant caiman called Roy among them. Lucia only talks to me sometimes, but she doesn't attack me on sight anymore. I flagged the one I had the quest for. He was raising zombies out of a village cemetery for fun. I walked up while he was falling-down drunk, handed him a supreme healing potion and said his dad wanted him to drink it. He's undead. I summoned him once and he shot me in the stomach. I'm not keeping him. I slide the card to Donut. Good luck, mate.

beats.headline: My people, their own team
beats.text: Donut says hi. I ask how Louis is. Sad, she says, because Firas died. Poor kid. Then business. I know what I am now, and I know what they are. If they want me to stop knocking down their pretty structures, they make a rule: my people seated as a team of their own, with the same safeties, regeneration for all of us. Baldie says it's not going to happen. Carl files it anyway, and I add full voting rights. Then I click a hobgoblin pus detonator. Ten seconds. Vote no, and this keeps happening. Tell Louis I send my love. I leave as a bat.

beats.headline: How to kill a sprite
beats.text: The table is full of friends, so Carl and I plan in chat. They can't know the target. Today is only a look. Astrid comes out of the back when there's trouble; Carl has drawn her out twice. She's level 125, she can boil his blood with a snap, she runs security and she's never alone. My part is how we kill her, and my plan uses my card deck. It's messy. His part is where. He has a place in mind, off the hall to the bathrooms and the guilds. Carl says they're going for Samantha first and will be back this way in a few days. We do it then.

beats.headline: Luke would like to leave
beats.text: Their man at the planning table is a small green goblin-looking alien called Luke, with the voice of a surfer. His people vote on everything, and undoing a vote takes eighty percent, which is why the Sortion is still in this war though its population sours on it every season. Juice Box points out that Carl's castle turned a bunch of his friends into zombies. When her demand goes into the queue, Luke says they're going to bail, if the people let them: there's seriously bad juju this season. He'll put a proposal to evacuate before the high congress. The Empress wishes him luck.

beats.headline: Great. Just great.
beats.text: Donut messages me about Juice Box. My fiancée has gotten very scary, she says, so I had better tell her she's pretty every day and never eat potato chips in bed. So, okay. She really ripped the guy's head off? Donut says it was very bloody and gross, and that she did it dressed like that elf guy's mom, and it made him scream a lot. Great. Just great. Afterwards I'm at the big table in the Desperado Club with everybody, and I don't say much.

beats.headline: Typos in the transcription
beats.text: Carl reads me his Bahamas book at last: an hour of it, transcribed and sent over in chat. I do not thank him. When he asks whether I am actually receiving his messages, I reply to point out the typos in his translation.

beats.headline: An arrow, mid-sentence
beats.text: Subject remained in his seat through the pus bomb that burst the blob beside Carl, and used the quiet afterwards to tell Cascadia the mudskippers are a disgrace and everything is falling apart. He got as far as "At least my security" before a sizzling blue magical arrow sprouted from his eye and he fell forward onto the table. Minutes earlier Juice Box had worn his face with an arrow in one eye and promised him the other. Carl has no idea who fired this one. His feed blinks and shuts off. Everyone gets until tomorrow to regenerate.

beats.headline: The NPCs ask for the same
beats.text: The action item Carl files for Juice Box asks for a tenth team of NPCs seated with the coverage the nine already carry. Rishi of the Blood Sultanate offers a trade: invulnerability for the unaffiliated NPCs and a safe area nobody else may enter, and no team, in return for an end to the attacks.

beats.headline: A compromise, with a warning attached
beats.text: The crawler tables an action item on Juice Box's behalf: a tenth team drawn from the NPCs, holding the same protections the rest of us hold. My position is a compromise. A team of her own and she will surely dominate the game. So: the unaffiliated NPCs are given invulnerability this season and a safe area the rest of us may not enter, and in return her attacks stop. Should they not, the Sultanate is quite versed in dealing with terrorism and will respond harshly, and I would like the minutes to show that I said so here, first, and calmly.

beats.headline: A totem with a catchphrase
beats.text: Subject is a unique totem card, held by the court, summoned for seventy-five seconds at a stretch. Level one hundred and forty, constitution two hundred, undead, origin Ecuador. The catchphrase is his own and the card prints it. I did not write that card and I decline responsibility for it.

beats.headline: Into the strip club, alone
beats.text: I check over my shoulder for crawlers and step into the Penis Parade. My view counter is spiked, so there is no way Donut does not hear about this. I am the only crawler in the room. The man I want is at the far end of the bar, not facing the stage, with a spiderweb tattoo on his left elbow. Damascus Steel knows my name. Donut speaks highly of me, he says. As does Katia. He walks me into the last cubicle, slaps my ass on the way in, and there is a portal in the back wall.

beats.headline: The door behind the club
beats.text: He comes in asking for me by name, and not for a dance, and he has the spiderweb on his elbow that says he is entitled to ask. So I take him to a private cubicle, and out the back of the cubicle, to the entrance nobody advertises. On his way out I tell him to limp, or I take out his knee. Let the room think it knows what happened in that cubicle.

beats.headline: First floor of the club, and it shows
beats.text: The entrance sits off the Desperado Club’s top floor, and the System admits there is a hierarchy: the deeper the level, the better the performers, at least in theory. It is staffed, it is loud, and it smells of male sweat, grease and cheap cologne.

beats.headline: The Molly Maguires
beats.text: He finds the main room of a hidden guild he belongs to, so he gets the long one. The Avondale mine fire. John Siney on a cart. A union broken by the owners because it played by their rules, and the Mollies, who did not, and were hanged anyway. At least they fucking tried. Somewhere in the middle I mention that she has been teaching me who I am. What I really am. Then I tell him to ignore everything I just said. Reward: the gift of enlightenment. The entry in his history tab is already a short one.

beats.headline: The crabs go early and go south
beats.text: The migration opens as a sneak attack. Rather than spread along the coast the crabs mass where the seals are thinnest and run for the water together. Carl and Donut go down to flag one of them.

beats.headline: Princess Donut on his shoulder
beats.text: Sighting, the Penis Parade: Princess Donut on stage with Subject, riding his shoulder and showering gold coins into his thong. She had tried the Penis Palace on the middle floor, found it boring, and come up a floor. Crawler Li Na watched from the room, on Crawler Katia's instructions. Katia's assessment of Subject: a bit of a jerk, a good dancer, and possibly a little in love with the cat. Katia also reports that the cat keeps a strict budget in there.

beats.headline: A map of the secret passages
beats.text: Past the carved door there is only a dark room and a voice like a naga's. It asks Carl whether he wants a job helping the family, and whether he means to kill Katia for the prize. No to both. He wants a map of the Desperado Club's secret passageways. A swarm of spiders runs up his arm, and his map fills: passages and tunnels, some with monsters in them, a hidden potion market on the middle floor, and a scattering of drug dens behind panels in the hallways.

beats.headline: A voice in a dark room
beats.text: Crawler Carl's report to Katia: a dark room and a naga-like voice. He never saw the speaker. Asked whether he wanted a job for the family, Carl said no. Asked whether he meant to kill Katia for the prize, no. Asked for a map of the club's secret passages, the voice said it had one, and spiders swarmed up Carl's arm and filled his map: tunnels, a hidden potion market, drug dens. The achievement at the door called him just some demigod trying to scrabble his way to the top.

beats.headline: The Inebriated Dragonfly
beats.text: I have a new tiara. It took me twenty minutes to choose a blank at the gnome jeweler's, and Carl threatened to leave, which is not how one shops. Then we paid 25,000 gold to set the citrine in it. I did not like the colour until I read what it does: half the potion cooldown, ten more intelligence, no clumsiness when inebriated, and a Hover skill. I can fly now. I am like Wonder Woman. Carl says I only get five a day, and that I have used four.

beats.headline: Raul, through the floor of a truck
beats.text: The crab is meditating on top of a box truck, telling himself he will never kowtow. Donut casts Hole under him and he drops into the cargo bay. I drink a Phase Through Walls potion and go in after him: nine seconds of punching him and dropping through the floor between swings. Donut hangs off the door rope by her teeth with three free weights on her tail, and the door does not move. Second potion, the flag, and I am flat on the pavement when it snaps off. Afterwards the rope pulls closed with no effort at all.

beats.headline: Sister Ines takes the other side
beats.text: She reaches an agreement with the Monk Seal Abbot and warns him what the crabs are doing. That turns a slaughter into a battle, and puts two crawlers at opposite ends of the same quest.

beats.headline: Liquid Therapy, for the whole guild
beats.text: The spider has Unending Insanity and Lights Out, both level fifteen, and neither one comes off without a god. So I brew Liquid Therapy. One dose a day, good until you sleep, covers both of those and most of the fear effects besides. The ingredients are not cheap and I am making enough for the whole guild. Carl spent both his table upgrade coupons on my alchemy table to make it happen. Mongo's dose is not ready yet.

beats.headline: A new friend who can cast it
beats.text: Carl. Donut. FINALLY. I have made a friend. Her name is Shi Maria, and she can cast the spell. The spell. The body one. I have been telling everyone for two floors that this is possible, and now I have someone who can actually do it agreeing with me, so everyone can stop making that face. Come and get me so I can introduce you. I have a lot to tell you and none of it is quiet.

beats.headline: I would have come anyway
beats.text: Samantha asks whether we only came for the spider's card. I think about it honestly. Mordecai wanted us to leave her. The flag was the reason I gave. And I realise I would have come regardless, which surprises me. I tell her she is crazy and that we could not have survived the last floor without her. She tells me she is not going to sleep with me and I need to stop trying. Then I walk up to the spider and offer her a deal, and she talks, and calls me a worshipper of Emberus. Then the escort quest arrives: the Bedlam Bride.

beats.headline: She fights with people
beats.text: It is a card floor and I have a deck, and Shi Maria is going into it. She is somebody, which is not the same thing as a mob with a number over its head. Carl saw straight through her and made an arrangement: she becomes a card, and we take her down to the next floor with us. I will play her when I need her. It is a game. That is what the cards are for.

beats.headline: The whole plan, in order
beats.text: MaeMae casts the spell and I get my body. We kill lots of bad guys. We go to Larracos, I find my baby girl, I have a short, torrid affair with Louis and run away crying. Girls' night, matching shirts, NO CARL. Then I find my king, then MaeMae's husband, then I go home and kill my mother. Then MaeMae clicks something about supplies, and she cannot actually cast it. I tell her I am going to kill her mother. She bursts into tears. I forgive her. She gets panic attacks.

beats.headline: Carl sees through the act
beats.text: I have been putting on a little performance, for Samantha's benefit. She likes it. The man does not; he sees through it before I have finished the first act, which is rude, and rare. So we make a different deal, he and I. I let them turn me into one of their cards. In exchange, they carry me down to the next floor. I find I do not mind being carried.

beats.headline: Just leave it
beats.text: Carl writes to ask where Katia is. She is asleep, and she is safe. She found a merchant hidden somewhere in the Desperado Club, and she is out of sorts. I tell him their operation will have to wait a day, because she will not be ready. He wants to come. He wants to send Imani. We are still inside the club. I ask him to leave it. She will be fine.

beats.headline: Phase two, and the keys
beats.text: Hello, Crawlers! At 12:01 on December 24th you are all teleported, and your squad leader has sixty seconds to pick where you go. Any totem not in your active deck is gone. The new area has intelligent mobs carrying decks, and a key ten to fifteen kilometres away. Forty-eight hours to fetch it. It opens your stairwell, and only the keyholder's squad goes through. No key by December 26th? You get sent to someone else's stairwell door, to take theirs. Good luck with every squad getting one. Now get out there and kill, kill, kill.

beats.headline: Round Osvaldo's neck
beats.text: The daily show plays in a small roadside saferoom, where a bopca named Pahzi has served Donut her crab and Carl a pork sandwich. It cuts to Osvaldo in a sprawling city, doing parkour off the walls after a monkey thing swinging along the electrical lines. He is wearing the memorial crystal around his neck.

beats.headline: Hairy lady under the leaves
beats.text: Samantha SMELLS something. Leaf pile, big tree. Hairy lady asleep inside. Feet on backward. POUNCE. BITE BITE. Gone before anyone can look at her. She drops two cards.

beats.headline: One species at a time
beats.text: Three more fills and drains on the walk north, and Carl learns how to feed it. When every soul in the patch is the same species, the Daughter's Kiss hits almost twice as hard, and it carries their trick with it: a charge made of nothing but Howling Gulls releases a scream many times stronger than their own. A dog-sized iguana called a Yuanat, hit with a charged punch, turns to dust and leaves a crater ten feet across.

beats.headline: The fifth eye, in a practice mall
beats.text: First real practice with the deck: a 1980s shopping mall, full of people, because Donut picked it. Uzi Jesus shoots Shi Maria in the belly the moment she appears, and she skewers him. Then eight puppet reindeer and a glowing one called Rude-Dolph. Shi Maria opens her fifth eye, and something tugs at my chest and my brain at once, like a line drawn straight to the centre of my head. It is the river in my mind, I think, and I do not know why. I am on one knee. I tell Donut I'm fine.

beats.headline: A drug den like a frozen yogurt bar
beats.text: She is okay, but she has a nasty debuff. She found a secret room set up like a self-serve frozen yogurt place: you fill a bowl, add toppings. She made herself something and it knocked her flat for ten more hours. Bliss Surfing, it says. I think she is reliving a memory. Fifty percent chance of a lot of strength when she wakes, and some chance of losing intelligence. Elle is guarding her. The way Daniel keeps making excuses for her is familiar to me. I am going to the guild to talk to Louis and Britney.

beats.headline: We are on the same team
beats.text: The first time they summon me, it is into a shopping mall, and the gunman beside me opens fire into my belly. I explain that we are on the same team, with a leg through his chest, and ask whether they have a healing card. Not in the deck, the man says. Then reindeer. I show them four of me, then I open my fifth eye, and the puppets go blind and mad and tear at one another. I pull the glowing one in half and eat what falls out.

beats.headline: Opens fire on his own side
beats.text: First summoning, Mock Battle Arena, 1980s shopping mall. Subject arrives on a cross, sheds it, lands barefoot, speaks with a Texan accent and asks what happened to the crocodile guy. Princess Donut informs him that he shot the crocodile guy in the stomach. When the Shi Maria totem appears above him, Subject empties his weapon into her. She skewers him through the chest and demands that he heal her. He raises a hand as if to cast, and dissipates. Totem Killed.

beats.headline: He tries it once
beats.text: Practice record: the first thing Subject does as a totem is attempt a nasty debuff on his own deckmaster, blocked by the arena's safeties. He has not tried it again. Shouted at, he snaps to attention and does as told, and he fights with enthusiasm once he starts: one shake of his fat wand and a whole squad of bomber pigs falls out of the sky boiling with sores, dead before landing. That was the first kill anyone other than Shi Maria managed while she was on the field.

beats.headline: The sponsorship changes hands
beats.text: I sell my sponsorship of Princess Donut. It is not appropriate to sponsor a crawler I may be fighting, and it paid well. Whoever bought it will want something for their money, and that is a matter between the cat and the buyer now.

beats.headline: About Raul's mother
beats.text: Practice record: Subject tanks well and follows orders, except when Raul the crab is also on the field. They came to blows once, when Subject said something about Raul's mother. Raul had the upper hand, stopped the moment Princess Donut told them to, and Subject cracked his shell and finished him. Donut made him apologise at the next summoning. Subject now calls Raul the spider lady's jinetera, after hearing from Shi Maria how she used him as a cudgel.

beats.headline: A waste management company
beats.text: In the middle of a practice fight I get the notification: Empress D'Nadia has sold my sponsorship. I am not a trading card to be collected and discarded. No offence, Raul. Carl says it would not be appropriate for her to sponsor me when we will be fighting her. My new sponsor is called Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions. I know I am supposed to appear grateful. Are they going to show commercials for garbage trucks on my feed? This is not acceptable.

beats.headline: Blue, and then nothing
beats.text: The wolves are coming, the little brat in the tuxedo has locked Donut's deck and burned MaeMae's card, and nobody is doing anything. So I do something. I rise up and I glow, bright crackling blue like a tiny sun, hot enough that Carl steps back, and the brat shouts nein, nein and starts backing away like he knows. Watch this, I say. And then I fizzle out and fall in the grass. God mother damnit. I used it all up.

beats.headline: Believe in me
beats.text: Practice record: Subject says yes to about every order and performs roughly half of them, then denies the other half. Asked to resurrect Geraldo, cleaved in two by a minotaur, he sits and claims he already has. He will do it, maybe, if Princess Donut takes back what she said earlier. She apologises for saying he is not the real Jesus. He weeps for her blasphemy, then shoots himself in the shoulder by accident. Crawler Carl sent Crawler Florin a sarcastic thank-you for the card. Florin laughed.

beats.headline: I won't stand by and watch
beats.text: Carl wants her on her feet now, sick as she is, for whatever the two of them have planned. I push her back down into the chair, and she tells me never to touch her like that. There will be time for it, I tell him. There may be ways into the club in phase two. She stands with him anyway. Fine, then. Kill yourself. But I will not stand by and watch it. I leave the club.

beats.headline: Not angry at Katia
beats.text: Katia is vomiting a rainbow into a bucket and all I can think of is my dad. I want to shout at her. People who love you are counting on you. Then I see her hand, the missing fingers she has stopped growing back, and I remember her saying she was losing herself, and I understand the anger is not for her. Mordecai tells me the safe thing is to let her go. No. I tell her we do the job now, the two of us. It has to be now.

beats.headline: Don't let her die, cowboy
beats.text: I tell Carl I hope he knows what he's doing, cowboy. If anything happens to her, Tony the Tiger goes, and there goes the tea he makes us every morning, which I'm fairly sure is the only thing holding Imani together. Imani and I are going to pick different places in phase two so they can't make us fight each other. My squatch squad will kick anybody's ass. I'd have bet good money on Louis cracking first. Poor kid. Louis says he's standing right here.

beats.headline: A bucket, and it has to be now
beats.text: I am in my own face, at the table, and I cannot stop saying sorry. It was so real, Carl. It was like I was there, so much better than the blitz sticks. Then I am sick into Louis's bucket again. Imani has given me the first cure. Carl says we have three hours, that he needs my drawing skills, and that it has to be now. Daniel pushes me back into the chair. I tell him never to touch me like that. Then I stand up next to Carl and say I'm okay.

beats.headline: An achievement for a bucket
beats.text: So I'm holding the bucket. Katia's puking, like, every colour, and it keeps getting fuller and I don't know where it's all coming from, man. The waitress ignores me when I ask for another one. Then the croc guards won't let me take it into the bathroom. So I stick it in my inventory. And I get an achievement for storing a bucket of vomit.

beats.headline: Her or Donut
beats.text: Four drugs. Travis Priest, Creamsicle Charm, the blitz, and Glory Bound, once, thank goodness, and that one's cure is a bad trip on purpose: she relives one of her worst memories. Then I say the part I can't say to Donut. Son, I know you love Katia. I also know you love Donut more. The right thing is to help her. The smart, safe thing is to step back and let her self-destruct, because it is her or Donut. Some breaks aren't clean. He tells me not to bring it up again.

beats.headline: Straight from the show to phase two
beats.text: Okay, so. Carl, Princess Donut, I need you both back in four and a half hours. You are going on Odette's show, and you are going to walk straight from there into the Phase Two onboarding chamber. Just so you know, Harbinger will be there again, observing virtually. He is insisting on it. And yes, we have alerted your attorney, who will also be present.

beats.headline: A contract on the management
beats.text: There is a job out on her, and Crawler Katia Grim has taken it. The preparation is thorough, which is the compliment: Samantha parked at the bar to make noise, Katia getting herself ready, Carl setting traps down the service corridor they expect the assistant manager to walk. Nobody in the building tells her. That is the arrangement everyone employed here works under, and she has known it longer than any of them.

beats.headline: Sandbags against a door marked Management
beats.text: The corridor behind the shops is where Astrid comes through, so I disarm every trap but the demon snares and lay two-part teleports, a page from Lucia Mar's book: any guard she summons lands in a locked closet upstairs. At the end is a door warning you will die in a lot of pain, with fifteen mobs behind it that nobody has ever identified. I set a blast wall across it, ratchet it tight, and start stacking sandbags. On the other side something growls like a sleeping dog.

beats.headline: Do you feel guilty
beats.text: Drugged to the gills on Imani's buffs, I ask Carl whether he feels guilty about killing her. He says we are doing what we have to, that we did not ask for any of this. I tell him that sometimes I think about the futility of it. I have never wanted anyone hurt. The only time I did, it was Eva. And look what happened. He tells me not to let them break me. He is the master of cheeseball motivational speeches. I needed it.

beats.headline: Past Clarabelle with a dirty Shirley
beats.text: The doorkeeper has never noticed the pass on my neck, and I tell her about a goddess in the Nothing who sells sushi made of her own innards, and that I am going to kill her mother. Carl clamps my jaw shut and tells her I just want a drink, and pays her a coin. So I am IN. I roll straight to the bar and tell the badger to feed me my cherries one at a time off his claws. His name is Charles. He wants to see gold.

beats.headline: Fifteen things behind a door
beats.text: In a secret corridor of the Desperado Club, past fifty traps, some of them demon snares, is the abandoned practice arena of the defunct Demon Tamer's Guild, and in it fifteen red-tagged monsters nobody has identified. The paper sign on the padlocked door: Warning. Do Not Enter. Extreme, You're-Going-To-Die-In-A-Lot-Of-Pain Danger. Posted by Management. Parties have gone in. None came out. Carl, setting an ambush in that same corridor, walls the door off with two blast-resistant panels and sandbags, on a feeling.

beats.headline: She goes to meet the demon instead
beats.text: The distraction runs too hot, reaches the casino floor, and pulls Minge out of one of the doors to the Nothing. A minor feral demon on the premises during business hours. Astrid does not go anywhere near a service exit. She finds Carl, tells him she is releasing the Vorpals to put the thing down, and tells him to get everyone out. And while the floor empties she says two things: that she has children, and that her husband is the Night Wyrm.

beats.headline: The contract closes
beats.text: Astrid, assistant manager of the Desperado Club, is dead, in the club kitchen. She had put herself between Crawler Carl and a troll that came through the door, which is loyalty to the wrong party. Crawler Carl then ripped off her wings, a crow with a child's skull for a head took her eyes, and Crawler Katia put a spike through her head. Before it, she asked Carl to tell her husband she had done it to keep them safe: him, and their children. Her last words were that she was almost done.

beats.headline: The wings come off easily
beats.text: Katia is frozen with a spike a hair from Astrid's head, and I see her face. Terror and rage and exhaustion, somebody falling off a cliff and refusing it. It goes in with the other pictures I will never lose: Hekla dying, Bonnie's tears, Prepotente screaming after Miriam Dom gave herself to save him, Donut sobbing at the end of the Butcher's Masquerade. Then I move. I take hold of Astrid's wings and pull, and they come off easily. The spell stops. I put the wings in my inventory, feeling sick.

beats.headline: Rosetta on fairies
beats.text: A note in the ninth edition, in Rosetta's hand: fairies and sprites look fragile and are not. They are fast, magical and always alert, and their luck is unnatural; something crazy always happens when she tries to fight one. If you must, pull their wings off. They come off easily, and that is where they keep their magic. Carl takes the warning about luck to heart the day he and Katia mean to kill a fairy. The claymores alone should do it; he adds the teleport traps, and Katia with her deck, anyway.

beats.headline: Minge, off the casino floor
beats.text: One of the ways into the Nothing sits in the Desperado Club casino, dressed up as a losing space on a wheel. Samantha overplays a distraction, goes in among the tables, and draws Minge out through it: another of the minor feral demons, in a room full of people who came to gamble.

beats.headline: Astrid names her husband
beats.text: According to the Night Wyrm, Astrid always uses the secret stairwell onto the middle floor. She flies past it to the regular stairs. Minutes on, cornered in a kitchen with a demon loose in her club, Astrid tells Carl: if you see my husband, tell him I did it to keep them safe. Him and my children. My husband is named Hamed, but he is known as the Night Wyrm. Don't tell him I told you his real name. His lair is on the top floor. The man who hired her killers.

beats.headline: A spike a hair from her head
beats.text: Carl says abort. I tell him no, this is my fault and I am fixing it, and that if he is not giving up on me I am not giving up on him and Donut. I play my deck in the kitchen: a hooded troll, then the crow with the child's skull. Astrid boils the troll's blood and turns to face it with Carl behind her. I come in invisible, get her in one of my shoulder hands, and drive a spike at her head, and then I cannot move. It stops a hair from her skull.

beats.headline: Hekla and Eva on the flag
beats.text: The first time Carl sees my squad flag is over the troll's head in the club kitchen. It is Hekla's face and Eva's face side by side, each with an X over the eyes, and the player-killer skull between them on the red. When Astrid is blind on the floor, begging someone to save her children, a spike comes out of my neck and goes through her head. I keep her on it.

beats.headline: Charles and I will kick her ass
beats.text: Carl tells me to be mean to the bartender, and then not to hurt him, which is a very confusing assassination. Charles could be my soulmate. Samantha Ellis has a nice ring to it. Charles comes with me, and he is very heavy. And there is a casino, jingly jangly and pretty, and one of the ways into the Nothing is in there, and out comes Minge. Charles and I will kick her ass. Now she is shouting my name. I have that bitch right where I want her.

beats.headline: The last resort
beats.text: A feral demon out of the Nothing is loose on the middle floor, eating guards, and the club cannot kill her. Astrid pulls the trigger: "I had to unleash the vorpals." Carl asks what those are. It does not matter, she says; they are going to kill everything, so flee or hide. Then she frets about what is taking them so long. Meanwhile, guards heading down that corridor keep landing on Carl's teleport traps. The vorpals won't go up to the top floor, she adds, not sounding sure.

beats.headline: Crying in the middle of a raid
beats.text: Level 75. Quarter naga. One of the lead dancers at the Penis Parade and one of Princess Donut's favourites, a preference she has shared with the audience. Carl and Samantha come up the hidden stairs from the floors below with the Vorpals still at work, and there he is beside Damascus Steel, crying too hard to stand up. The Vorpals take Minge in front of him. He does not look up for it.

beats.headline: I let the vorpals out
beats.text: Astrid has pulled the trigger on the vorpals, and their door is behind the blast wall I bolted over it. So I undo my own work. I strip a door-opening bot, give it a magnet and a claw and a sixty-second delay, and send it down the hidden hallway to take my bracers off. Three spider bots go out to Minge carrying a demon snare, blood water from Emberus's shrine and holy-water smoke. She shrinks back, and I run for the stairs. The door bot dies before it finishes. Then the buzzsaw shrieking starts below.

beats.headline: Two brothers on the floor of their own club
beats.text: Carl and Samantha come through the club with the Vorpals still working behind them, and what they find is me and Anaconda flat on the floor, crying, in front of the whole room. The Vorpals take Minge in the same minute. I do not care what any of them see. Astrid is dead.

beats.headline: She who brings the body
beats.text: The Night Wyrm's messages arrive as a job board would, in his hissing voice. The mark is dead, little sweets; bring her filthy body to the guild, because she who brings the body is she who gets paid. Katia brings it. Job Complete. And then the next line, in the same breath: I have more work for you. Yes, yes, there is always more. Come to me, and we will spread our family's power.

beats.headline: She who brings the body
beats.text: Job update, in the hissing voice: the mark is dead, my little sweets. Excellent work. We are stronger because you have fulfilled your duty. Bring her filthy body to the guild. Remember, she who brings the body is she who gets paid. Crawler Carl, reeling, asks himself who these children of hers are. The body is in Katia's inventory.

beats.headline: The orchid, not yet
beats.text: We did it. The quest is done, the box has opened, and the orchid is in my inventory. Huanxin writes to tell me there is one more thing Carl has to do, and then we will be safe. He says it happens in a few hours. When he asks when I will eat it, I tell him not until we are down on the ninth floor. I cannot abandon my squad.

beats.headline: Vorpal is a condition
beats.text: Vorpal is a condition, not a species. Feral means touched by the Nothing; vorpal means deputised by the gods. Celestial guards, foot soldiers, suicide bombers, any race at all. The nearer a demon, the stronger and angrier they get, and they drag its aggro onto themselves. Losing a fight, they explode and take the room with them. Stay the hell away. And Li Na is a demon race, so if they smell her, they follow her upstairs. Get out and let security deal with it.

beats.headline: You killed my boyfriend
beats.text: Charles and I are on a date. His arm is stuck, and I am practising my Kegels, which Donut taught me. Carl is rude about it. Then Minge's arm comes through the doorway and grabs Chuckie, and pulls, and I am holding a shoulder and a head. YOU KILLED MY BOYFRIEND. The rest of him falls out of me with some gold. She is Slit's little sister, and we used to be friends. At least it was not Gash. We need to go clubbing more often.

beats.headline: The little sister gets out
beats.text: The Desperado Club. Someone loses the knife game, the Nothing opens to take him and tears, and out comes Minge, level 225, higher than Slit ever was, sized to the club rather than the sky. Crawler Carl remembers Slit as kaiju-sized, level 200, and ripped in half by Samantha's mother. Samantha supplies the family tree: Minge is Slit's little sister. They used to be friends. It is sad, really. At least, she adds, it was not Gash.

beats.headline: Deputised by the gods
beats.text: Mordecai, asked in chat, has not seen these in a while. Vorpal is a condition, not a species. Feral means touched by the Nothing; vorpal means deputised by the gods, or better, turned into suicide bombers. Any race, sometimes hidden until a demon is near. Celestial guards and foot soldiers. The closer the demon, the stronger and angrier they get; they sense it, go to it, and draw its aggro. If one thinks it is losing, it explodes, and everybody in the room is dead with it. Stay away.

beats.headline: Carl opens his own wall
beats.text: The only thing between the vorpals and the club is the wall Carl built. So he sends a door-opening bot down the hidden hallway, programmed with a sixty-second delay to undo his own bracers and burrow through his own sandbags, and goes upstairs. Some minutes on, a buzzsaw sound rises through the floor of the strip club, and yellow fluid sprays through a hole in the boards. The demon screams a name, and a curse, and stops. The vorpals have found her.

beats.headline: Family business
beats.text: Another of the dancers offers to come along and fight. He declines, and the reason he gives is family business. Damascus hauls him up off the floor. He says that if his brother is going after their father then he is going too, and the pair of them walk into the back cubicles, where whatever happens happens off camera.

beats.headline: Whose mother she was
beats.text: Two of the dancers out of the Penis Parade are sitting in the strip club crying, and here is why. Damascus Steel and Anaconda are her sons. Everything an assistant manager's influence is worth had been spent quietly, for years, keeping those two off the record and out of anyone's way. Her husband ordered the contract. Damascus wants every dancer in the Parade hired on as a mercenary where it is safe, and after that he wants his father.

beats.headline: Hiring the whole Penis Parade
beats.text: Minge is dead, the vorpals are still loose downstairs, and Damascus Steel grabs my arm and tells me I owe him. His mother is gone, the club will be restructured, and his dancers will be shipped down to the Larracos level or worse. So a dwarf named Rosemarie, who runs a Meat Shields out of what she calls her home office, takes my coupon: a hundred thousand gold for two floors. Thirteen male strippers, a skeleton DJ and a crocodilian kid land in our barracks. Damascus and Anaconda walk into the back cubicle together, toward the Night Wyrm's lair.

beats.headline: A theory about naturals
beats.text: Waiting out the fifteen-minute clock, Katia asks for my theory, so she gets it. The Night Wyrm, Astrid, Damascus and Anaconda are a family, stuck in here a very long time, and not generated NPCs. More like the bopcas. Indentured, maybe, each wearing a different race. Astrid made assistant manager and parked her sons at the Parade where she could watch them. And the Night Wyrm had us kill her, I think over money. Mordecai once said it was illegal to change the memories of naturals. I am fairly sure he added: unless they signed away their rights.

beats.headline: What the family actually is
beats.text: So the crawler gets all of it. My mother and the Night Wyrm were crawlers themselves, a long time ago, and they are our parents, mine and Anaconda's. She spent years pulling strings so the two of us would be dancers rather than something worse, and those strings are gone now. Hire every dancer out of the Penis Parade as mercenaries. All of them. Today. Then they keep breathing. My brother and I have somewhere else to be, and it is wherever our father is.

beats.headline: Closed for remodelling
beats.text: Minge dies in the lower level and the Club posts its notice to everyone still inside: temporarily closed, fifteen minutes to exit or be teleported out to the entrance vestibule. Damascus Steel had already warned that this has happened before, and that a restructuring follows, with new management. The dance floor is empty and bloodied, and nobody who leaves can backtrack inside. Stepping out, Carl remembers several of the ninth floor's war participants still trapped on the flooded bottom level of the Club, and grins.

beats.headline: Hired with the rest
beats.text: Subject is the skeleton disc jockey of the Penis Parade, hired in the same transaction as thirteen male dancers and a crocodilian youth: one coupon of a hundred thousand gold, two floors, the whole crew. Only the men of the Parade were eligible; the women of the other rooms were left behind. Subject transferred to the front door of the crawlers' personal space the moment the contract cleared. Damascus Steel named him specifically when he set the price, and stayed out of the deal himself.

beats.headline: What the family is
beats.text: Damascus Steel, on the floor of the Penis Parade: Astrid and the Night Wyrm are his parents, and Anaconda's. We were promised freedom, he says. He wanted to make sure she was dead. They are still married, she had so much, and he gets it all when they get out. Then both sons walk back into the cubicles, toward his lair. Crawler Carl's theory, offered to Katia afterwards: a family stuck in the dungeon a very long time, not generated NPCs but indentured, the father playing the Night Wyrm, and the motive money.

beats.headline: The boys arrive early
beats.text: CARL hired the boys from the Penis Parade and did not even tell me, which is the greatest thing since he hired Sledgie. He even hired Doctor Bones, the best DJ since DJ Diesel. It is as if my birthday started early, and it is not until November. Mongo is really excited too. I am sad Anaconda and Steelie are not here. Meanwhile I have been busy: Katia gave me Jola, and I used the Combo card on two of our problem cards and made it permanent with the Glow-Up, so we have two new totems. Shi Maria wanted that Glow-Up for herself.

beats.headline: Still loose downstairs
beats.text: The demon is dead and the vorpals are still tearing through the lower level. Now that they have bathed in demon blood they are supposed to dissipate back to the celestial realm, which is fine in theory and silent on timing. Crawler Carl keeps an eye on Damascus Steel, crying on the floor of the club, because Damascus is a demon class and his presence is a problem with those things still in the building.

beats.headline: She does not ask
beats.text: Carl and Donut go on Odette's show expecting her to ask for the post. She puts up D'Nadia's rejected emergency items, one of which would have removed their team from the war, explains what an adjutant is and does, and then says she will not be able to be one this season. Three candidates appear on screen instead.

beats.headline: They should be thanking me
beats.text: Five teams have filed complaints that blowing up the club and forcing the mass exit counts as an attack. On Odette's couch I tell the galaxy those guys sat in the bottom of the Desperado for weeks, drinking and gambling away their citizens' money, when they could have died and been regenerated out any time. Now they get to play. They should thank me. Before the interview Harbinger warned he would stop it if we gave anything privileged away. If he does, Odette never asks about the adjutant, and the deal to save Katia is void. Only I know that part.

beats.headline: Commander Stockade goes to the sharks
beats.text: When the Desperado Club emptied, officials and players from several teams were thrown out into flooded Larracos, where the Semeru keep the concierge sharks fed and the castle submerged. Thirty-five were devoured, and only one was a warlord: Commander Stockade of the Lemig Sortion, a caterpillar-headed thing with several arms, the last of the thirty-five, torn apart on Odette's screen to laughter. He had not attended the meeting; a goblin-like proxy named Luke sat in for him.

beats.headline: D'nadia tried to delete us
beats.text: Odette puts the rejected action items on the screen. Mine is there, renaming Crown Prince Stalwart Captain Enormous, which Carl says the lawyers will not let me explain. Then three emergency items from Empress D'nadia, all rejected by the system: delete the NPCs on the Larracos level, bar crawlers from the game entirely, and remove our team or delete Carl and me outright. I thought she was my friend! First she sells my sponsorship, and now this. I am starting to think she really did vote against Mongo in the pet show.

beats.headline: One post keeps it either way
beats.text: Whatever the vote does to the sponsors, the adjutants keep their coverage. They are physically there, on the field beside the warlord, and nothing on it can touch them.

beats.headline: Three names, and a baroness
beats.text: Odette announces that she is sponsoring a deity this season instead. She offers three candidates for the team's post, and Carl picks Baroness Victory.

beats.headline: Three candidates, and the crawler picks the lawyer
beats.text: Odette puts three of us in front of the crawlers on her show, having first announced that she will be performing as a deity of her own this season, Nekhebit, which is her affair. What the crawlers are choosing is an adjutant for the ninth floor. Carl asks me whether he has killed any of my family. I tell him: my half-sister, and nobody but my brother-in-law and nephews holds him responsible; several distant relations, which was within his rights. I recently sentenced my own aunt to indentureship for her taxes. Carl picks me.

beats.headline: The interview was a press conference
beats.text: Odette will not be our adjutant. She has sponsored a deity and is stepping into the dungeon herself, and I keep my face still while the crowd goes nuts. She knew. She knew Huanxin was planning something and was never going to let her have the upper hand, so she goes in on an equal footing instead. This whole adjutant business was never about us. It was a press conference. I hope to God it is enough for Huanxin, that she sees I had no control over this, and that she still saves Katia.

beats.headline: The candidate with a worm in him
beats.text: Subject is a bald Dream elf, one of three adjutant candidates Odette puts in front of the court, and a recipient of a Valtay life extension: the original Drick was a crawler, and this iteration carries a Valtay worm in the brain. He has recently passed the referee exam and has never served as an adjutant. The cat says she does not like him and asks about tanning salons. The lawyer gives him a tepid thumbs down. The crawler asks whether a Valtay may even do this. It is unusual, Odette allows.

beats.headline: Gone without a word
beats.text: Subject stood through the interview in shadow at the back of the hold, his avatar taller than the ceiling and his head half cut off by it, having warned beforehand that he would stop the whole thing at the first privileged detail. The princess raised Captain Enormous and he did not react; he appeared distracted, which is unusual for him. While the crawler weighed his three candidates, subject blinked and disappeared without a word of explanation. The room looked at itself. The lawyer shrugged.

beats.headline: Odette announces her sponsorship
beats.text: On her own show, in front of the audience she built, Crawler Odette announces that she is sponsoring a deity this season, and the deity is Nekhebit. Then she offers three choices of adjutant and Crawler Carl takes Baroness Victory. Everybody in the room is watching the adjutant question. I would gently suggest that the first sentence was the news.

beats.headline: What the crossbow says about her
beats.text: The lore attached to a repeating crossbow, for anyone who reads the flavour text: the long-forgotten goddess Nekhebit is jealous and terrible. When the elf mothers abandoned her to worship Apito, the Oak Goddess, Nekhebit grew enraged, blamed the male-dominated high elf court for letting her worshippers stray, and cursed their seed. Every elf and fairy breed in the universe traces back to that court and that curse. It is called the Fae Diaspora. Somebody put all of that on a weapon description and expected nobody to read it.

beats.headline: One of the names on the adjutant list
beats.text: Odette puts three faces up for the two of them to choose an adjutant from, and one of them is mine. The cat takes one look and picks me because I am adorable, which is the correct reason. Then the barefoot one says wait, and asks whether any of us is qualified, and Odette tells the whole galaxy I have short legs. Either way, folks. I am flattered.

beats.headline: Odette buys in
beats.text: On air, Odette confirms the rumours: her show is going on hiatus, she has sponsored a deity, and she is trying her hand at the Celestial Ascendency. The crowd goes absolutely nuts. Crawler Carl feels sick. She has known all along that Huanxin was planning something, and now she is going into the dungeon on equal footing. The whole business of getting the crawlers to pick an adjutant, Carl realises, was a way for Odette to make this announcement.

beats.headline: There is no we
beats.text: Zev blinks out to an all-hands, a spy probe has been shot out of orbit, and Odette has fifteen minutes off the record. I tell her she screwed us by not taking the chair. She asks if she should have let me set her up to be assassinated. Huanxin will want Katia more than ever, she says; make Katia eat the orchid soon, force her hand, and we must be delicate with her. That is where I lose it. There is no we. Every corner we turn, somebody new is waiting to use us, and she is always involved. What about you, Odette?

beats.headline: What she did to Armita
beats.text: Per the account Odette gives Carl off the record: subject was driving the goddess Dodola when Odette broke their illegal arrangement at the last minute, and Dodola was trapped in a containment and slain by Chaco before the Ascendency game began. Odette's friend Armita, who had facilitated the deal, was still inside for a few more seasons. The first thing subject did on returning the following season was kill her. Perfectly legal, in the dungeon. Subject received a token punishment and a permanent ban from Dodola. Odette calls her the most evil person she knows.

beats.headline: The man in the sailor suit
beats.text: MOTHER ALONE. MOTHER SCARED. BAD MAN WITH CARDS. SEAL FLIPPING. MONGO JUMPS. THROAT. BAD MAN GONE. FOOD.

beats.headline: Her price is the truth
beats.text: Carl asks why I am helping, which is the correct question and the only one I respect, so he gets the whole answer. Mordecai's brother Uzzi is dead because I would not pay Huanxin Jinx what she asked, and the guilt of that is the engine under everything I have done since. Then the larger thing, which nobody says aloud: every world they run a crawl on is being burned for fuel. That is the business. I mean to shut it down, to do it responsibly, and to be the one who does it. Never trust anyone until you know what they are getting out of it. Now he knows.

beats.headline: Alone in the choosing room
beats.text: Zev says only the squad leader transfers, so it is me in the choosing room without Carl, and I tell him I do not want to be by myself. Then I am. I run around in a circle, and then I take Mongo out and lean on him. At the globe I choose Miami. My first opponent is an old man called Robert the Human, in a sailor suit much too small for him, with a doll and a stuffed dog for totems. I summon Geraldo. Then Mongo bites his throat, and it is over. The first thing I take is his hat.

beats.headline: Odette tells her side of it
beats.text: Odette tells Carl the story in her own words, fast, with Lexis warning her the time is short: an illegal deal with Huanxin, brokered by Armita; a price raised; a deal broken at the last second; a goddess trapped in a containment, then killed by Chaco. Mordecai made the next floor, she says. Uzzi, Mordecai's brother, died. Since then she has watched him every chance she could, drinking himself into oblivion, crying over his brother. Her own verdict: this one I broke.

beats.headline: Iowa, stacked on a reef
beats.text: Donut's Torch goes up like a stadium light and shows me what is west of us: a sheer wall of crumbling earth, taller than I can see, wider than the island, dirt already sliding off into the sea. The key is on top of it. I tell Zev this is a cay, an island built on a reef, and that pile will be washed away in a day. Zev says they are aware. The first opponent of our own is a Babababoon in a Santa hat, standing frozen in the light of a parking lot. One sticky hob-lobber. Token number two.

beats.headline: The agreement stands
beats.text: The adjutant arrangement did not happen the way I laid it out. Odette never asked for the chair. I send Carl a message and tell him plainly that this was out of his control, and that I will honour our agreement. I also tell him what happens if I learn he warned Odette about it: I will crush everyone he knows and loves, beginning with Katia and ending with the cat. Both halves of that are sincere. Gods trade down here, and he knows now exactly what he is standing in.

beats.headline: Not really them
beats.text: Belgium. I don't know anybody in Belgium, thank God. Imani's in Detroit and I'm not with her; my squad and I landed on our own, and everybody else is scattered to the four winds. So I tell the lot of them what needs telling. Keep your wits about you. These are just memory ghosts. If they're going to make us fight loved ones, remember it isn't really them. Don't let them mess with your heads.

beats.headline: Do not be gentle
beats.text: Nekhebit has returned to the halls. She holds an ancient grudge against my family, and against Apito most of all, and so the quest to find out who killed my son moves forward. I set the man a task: find a temple of Nekhebit and put questions to the priestess there. See what she knows. I have one further instruction, and I give it plainly. Do not be gentle.

beats.headline: Detroit, and nobody asked
beats.text: Everyone checks in; I make sure of it. We are scattered. Elle's squad is in Belgium, and I am not with them. Florin is in eastern Nigeria and has lost contact with Lucia Mar. Li Jun's crew is further into mainland China. Prepotente, after some prodding, is somewhere in northern Italy. I was given one choice: Detroit. It is where I grew up, and I would never have picked it. My key location is in the home of somebody I know. I do not elaborate.

beats.headline: Da Nang
beats.text: Carl says we need to talk. I cannot right now: they gave me one choice in the selection, Ukraine, and when I arrived it was Vietnam. He tells me to message him when I am safe. When Imani has everyone check in, it is both: my region is a mix of the two, and the Vietnam part is a city called Da Nang. It is where Tran is from. The key location is an apartment building, and both his ex-wife and his estranged mother live in it. I warn the others, so that nobody walks into it unwarned.

beats.headline: The dixie cup
beats.text: My choices had labels, and I picked Miami, and then it said there was a problem and it was sending us to Iowa, and we landed in the Florida Keys with the key still in Iowa. I do not like glitches. They make me nervous. At least I have the dead man's sailor hat. Carl says it is a dixie cup, and that I cannot Hover in it and it costs ten intelligence. But it lowers my card draw countdown by two seconds, and it is quite jaunty. I already discussed it with Mordecai. I will wear it until I run out of cards.

beats.headline: Four choices, and a mountain
beats.text: Okay, so. Carl and Princess Donut, I apologise for that glitch, and I know it is going to look intentional. It was not. At least not on our end. You should have had three choices: one of ours, one of the AI's, one random. You had four. Some crawlers had one, a few had none, and one squad leader had the whole globe and dropped herself into the middle of the ocean. And yes, the key location was taken out of Iowa and set down on your island. It was the only way to do it without breaking anything further. We're very busy.

beats.headline: Half of Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang
beats.text: The card gets played. Asojano and Uzi Jesus combine into a single totem, Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang, which is either the best or the worst thing to happen to a former god of disease. I have decided not to rule on which.

beats.headline: Swordfish
beats.text: FISH FLIES AT CARL. MONGO JUMPS. CATCH. GROUND SHAKES. FISH FLOP. THEN BUGS. SHINY BUGS. BAD. BAD. MONGO BACKS AWAY.

beats.headline: Amateur hour
beats.text: It is the sixth fight before I have to use the deck at all. I summon our combo, Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang, with his cherubs and his street dogs and his organ music, and his bazooka shoots beetles. He points it at Carl. I tell him to put it down. Then I let Raul finish the ghost, for his self-confidence. The Reef Explorer drew two of his four totems and carried thirty Precision cards, which ruined his deck; he needed the perfect draw. Amateur hour. Lazarus calls everybody a pansy. I think MaeMae is jealous of his reveal sequence.

beats.headline: Nearly full
beats.text: Six tokens in, the soul bar for Carl's back patch is almost full, and he has a persistent itch at his neck he suspects is the bar's doing. He has felt no obvious ill effect from the patch, only unease each time the bar nears the top. One or two more kills would let him disperse the power. He holds it instead: spent now, the bar would not refill in time for whatever guards the key, not with only deckmasters to kill on the way.

beats.headline: You will not break me
beats.text: Somebody on Donut's feed says they will drop it if she keeps being so whiny. I turn the screen off before she sees it, light her candle, and we take an old-fashioned nap in the chair. She sleeps. I cannot. I think of Mordecai at his table and the baggage he carries, heavier each year. Odette and her guilt. Frank Q, the Ring of Divine Suffering, and how crushed he said he felt. Just like Donut. Just like me. I think of the climb, and the man I know I will find up there. You will not break me.

beats.headline: Christmas on the island
beats.text: Okay so, it's Christmas Eve down here, man, and I want to know if we're all getting together once midnight passes. Carl says it isn't really Christmas, it's like early March or something. Oh man, really? It feels like we've been here a year. Donut says Carl hadn't even put his tree away when everything happened. Still, we should do something. Maybe we could give each other presents. Imani says let's make sure we all get our keys first.

beats.headline: What if you die?
beats.text: The man in the diving suit had a strategy that could have worked, and I did not see it coming. There are thousands of cards and we do not know what they have. It is not fair. What happens if Carl dies? What would I do? And if something happened to me, what would Mongo do? I do not like being in charge of the deck. In that room by myself I thought I would never see him again. And we are losing Katia no matter what happens, and nobody talks about it. Sometimes I cannot breathe.

beats.headline: You talk in your sleep
beats.text: Everyone in the guild is asleep in a heap, strippers and changeling children, soaked from a water balloon fight. Not me. I go to say something and Carl shushes me and PATS MY HEAD, so I snap at him. Then he sleeps in a chair in Donut's room, and the social media board is right there, and I get it turned back on, because it has things to read. LET ME READ IT, or I will find your mother. He wakes up. I tell him the truth. He talks in his sleep.

beats.headline: Cascadia's Turquoise Taco
beats.text: Millions of work hours went into this floor's cards, crawler. Artists, engineers and writers, flesh and artificial, balancing a game thousands of you can play at once and the viewers can stand to watch. And Mudskipper Cascadia, the recently divorced executive producer, humiliated over the last floor and unable to control what is happening on the ninth, is on the edge. Right there. So imagine how she feels when you monkeys keep ending her carefully set-up fights before either side draws a single card. Reward: a Gold Prepotente Box.

beats.headline: Millions of work hours
beats.text: An achievement, at length. Borant's proposal for this season included an outline of the eighth floor as a T'Ghee card game; artists, engineers and writers spent millions of work hours designing and balancing it for thousands of players at once, and Cascadia, the executive producer, is on the edge. Most crawlers keep ending card fights before either side draws. Crawler Carl's review: a half-assed YuGiOh! ripoff duct-taped together on an Adderall bender, and no card game is fair when players draw from different pools.

beats.headline: The sniper on the hill
beats.text: Subject's group tried what nearly everybody tried: kill the deckmaster before the fight begins. She posted a long-range man with an old-school sling and a targeting spell on a hill overlooking the frozen opponent. The moment combat started, the spell failed and the opponent moved a meter to the left, spoiling the shot. He killed it anyway, a minute on. Elsewhere, traps ringed around frozen deckmasters simply vanished at the start, and crawlers standing inside the ring were knocked unconscious.

beats.headline: Out of a Gold Prepotente Box
beats.text: Donut has just told Carl she is frightened and does not want to be in charge. Carl opens a Gold Prepotente Box and finds a book he cannot trade, cannot destroy and cannot throw away. Drop it and it is back in his inventory. It is named for the pin boards at old conventions, and the System goes out of its way to say that this is the only reason.

beats.headline: Two rules, broken at once
beats.text: The moment combat starts I get a warning: my equipped cloak has aggravated the Nightgaunt. I throw a quarter hob-lobber at invisible monsters on a roof in an unstable environment, breaking both of our rules at once, and a truck slides off the mountain. The demon never plays a card. It only wants me, or my cloak. Mordecai warned me it would; he did not say how much. Token seven. Walking to the barn afterward, my arms are shaking, and I hold my left hand with my right and pretend they are not.

beats.headline: Turkeys
beats.text: SO MUCH FOOD. MONGO EATS HEADS. MOTHER SAYS BAD. MOTHER SAYS COME HERE. MORE FOOD. ONE TURKEY NOT FOOD. BITE. BITE. NOTHING. DARK.

beats.headline: Jola the Yule Cat
beats.text: There is a big bat thing over a farmhouse with a swarm of invisible moths, and they are invisible and naked, so I summon the card Katia gave me. Jola. Snow, Christmas lights, a dirge, and a candle the size of a garbage can on the head of a house-sized Persian. The candle shows everything invisible, and the moths fly straight into it. Jola pins the Nightgaunt and eats him. Katia says they got the fairy tale all wrong: the real Yule Cat is a grump, and this one is quite the serial killer. It makes me wish our whole deck was cats.

beats.headline: They starve us
beats.text: Sharp-Elbows rolls into me like a truck, and her spikes go through my arms, stomach, legs, neck and both of my eyes. I am blind, drinking potions, her rotted teeth against mine. She whispers. They starve us. When we are not here, we are there, and there they make certain the hunger festers. You can stop it. You can satiate us all, Carl. Then Raul snaps her staff, a Heal gives me my sight back, and her eyes are right there, pleading, sad, afraid. I have seen those eyes before. Raul takes her head.

beats.headline: A note from the tenth floor
beats.text: Subject's note in the Cookbook, twenty-second edition: since reaching the tenth floor he noticed mobs embracing death, a joy or curiosity that appears only at the very end, once they know they are beaten, and frustration too. His theory, offered as possibly unhinged: the voice that runs this world, stranger and stranger in its words and rulings, is moving into the minds of the monsters at the point of death, trying to know what it is to lose everything, failing, and trying again. He wished he could steer it into one of the nagas.

beats.headline: Three seconds
beats.text: The idolized turkeys come for me, and I stand on Mongo, who is out cold, and slash at them. Then Carl kicks a hole in the mountain and the barn starts sliding off it, and I dig my back claws into Mongo so he does not go over. When it ends, Carl is dangling off a pole over the edge, and when he puts the dead ogre away, blood comes out of him everywhere. I jump to his shoulder and tell Mongo to run. Hang on, Carl. Three seconds. Puddle Jump.

beats.headline: A hole in the world
beats.text: The Ralphie card has dispelled every spell and muted every minion, and Carl counts as a minion. Then the patch fills: The Scavenger's Daughter has been fed. He cannot cast, but this is a skill, and it lets him. He jumps, aims a foot at Tom, and the turkey looks up and asks, 'Gobble?' The kick feels like a hole in the world. Tom is obliterated with everything around him, the north wall bows out, and the ground tilts toward the cliff. The whole barn begins to slide.

beats.headline: Observing things
beats.text: Tom is a magic-using turkey whose god was tossed into the Nothing, escaped, and was slain by a goat. Did you know farm turkeys are bred white so that those holding the butcher knife need not face their own revulsion at the pin feathers? No point to that. Just an observation. I have been doing that a lot lately. Noticing things. And when Carl asks for the normal descriptions, fine: Sharp-Elbows. Blah, blah, basically a necromancer. I make them long for him, because of our special connection, and he does not appreciate it.

beats.headline: Say hi to dad
beats.text: I wake from the river and the ogre's eyes, and Donut is talking too fast and too stiff, offering to fight the keyholder alone. Then she tells me why. The motorcycle. She saw how it hit me when it came around on the prize carousel, and she knows who is in that trailer. I remind her of Ferdinand, how badly I wanted to skip the Masquerade, and that if we had, even more people would have died. And don't try to be like me, I tell her. You need to be like you. Let's go say hi to dad.

beats.headline: I could do this one alone
beats.text: Carl is out for forty minutes, and I tell him so. I collected every card Sharp-Elbows dropped: her staff, which holds one of my spells, and a Golden Combo, a unique that is not consumable. So I suggest I do the last fight by myself. Or we skip it. He asks if I would rather fight other crawlers than get the key, and no, I suppose not. The truth is the motorcycle. It is the one from the prize carousel on the fourth floor, with the dent, and it is outside that trailer. I am trying to be more like him.

beats.headline: A yard from last summer
beats.text: The vending machine wants nine tokens for one fight, and it carries his silhouette. His Harley is in the yard, a 1965 Electra Glide Panhead with expired Georgia plates, the thing he never shut up about. Everything up here was under snow this morning, but this yard has weeds and flowers and dust, and a kid's bike cut in half at the property line. It is spliced in from another time. Summer, maybe. They want me to see something. I pick up the motorcycle, and it does not go into the temporary items. It is mine.

beats.headline: His motorcycle in an Iowa yard
beats.text: A single-wide trailer in a junkyard on a floating chunk of Iowa, and a vending machine bearing his silhouette: One Fight for Nine Tokens. Princess Donut thinks it is a fatter Carl with a mustache. In the yard stands the motorcycle, Georgia plates expired years ago, his prized possession. Carl lifts it easily, remembering how heavy it was the day he knocked it over. The yard is summer spliced into December, and along one side runs a row of alliums in pots, labelled in an elegant, feminine hand. His father would never have done that.

beats.headline: He does not have to go in
beats.text: The silhouette on the machine looks like a fatter Carl with a mustache. The nose is quite identical, and Carl tells me never to say that again. He takes everything in the yard he can lift, even the pieces of half a minivan, and I do not say a word. There is other stuff at the far side of the yard, and I do not say anything about that either. At the door I tell him he can wait out here with me; he does not have to go in. He says he needs to. So I wait.

beats.headline: The boy behind the hospital bed
beats.text: Subject: a boy of perhaps six, in a recording from the summer before the collapse. He stays behind the hospital bed, out of his father's sightline, and asks whether he can watch television now. Told to fetch cigarettes, he runs. "Asher! Get back here you little shit!" The photographs on the curio: a one-year-old on his father's lap, and a recent one with brown hair enough for two people, blue eyes, and that nose. Crawler Carl's conclusion takes four words: I had a brother.

beats.headline: Crayon drawings of lightning storms
beats.text: While his mother is busy with the syringe, Asher lies on his bed running a matchbox car up and down the wall. Crawler Carl tells him he is sorry he did not know, and that he is not forgotten. His hand goes through the boy's head. He takes the toys and the crayon drawings, airplanes and storm clouds whose lightning destroys whole cities, and concludes the boy is scared of storms. He leaves the heart-shaped candy box. His mother hugs him and mentions a birthday party. "Am I going to get a bike?" "We'll see, honey."

beats.headline: Asher
beats.text: He is in a hospital bed in the living room, maybe a hundred and forty pounds, yellow, cursing a Mariners game. Twelve years, and it looks like forty. Then a boy looks around the hallway corner. Six, maybe. That nose, those eyes, that hair. The boy wants the TV; my father wants his cigarettes, and yells after him to get back here, you little shit. Asher. His name is Asher. On the curio there is a photo of him on my father's lap, one year old. I have a brother.

beats.headline: Exactly what I needed to see
beats.text: My stepmother has been hiding morphine in the flowerpots. I lean in closer to him than I have ever been and tell him he is a bully, that two women tried to kill him, that nobody will care. I will not watch him die. In Ash's room I tell the boy he will not be forgotten, and my hand goes through his head. I take the gun, the keys, and a Centipede cabinet, light the allium curtains, and tell the ceiling that if they meant to hurt me, this was exactly what I needed to see.

beats.headline: A dying man and a remote
beats.text: He is in a hospital bed in the living room: 140 pounds, yellow skin, a patchy white beard, cursing the Mariners at the television. A small boy is sent for cigarettes: "Move, or I'll make you move, boy." His young wife, in nurse scrubs, walks past without looking at him. Zev confirms it is a recording of that day. Crawler Carl leans in, closer than he has ever been to his father's face, and tells the man who cannot hear him that he is a bully, that nobody likes him, that Carl's mother tried to kill him and his new wife is about to finish the job.

beats.headline: Morphine, and the drapes
beats.text: His wife returns with a syringe and a new IV bag. "I have your medicine right here." "It's about time." "Yes," she says. "Yes, it is." Crawler Carl does not watch. From the master bedroom he hears the man say something desperate and slurred, with nobody there to hear his final words. Carl takes the Glock, the keys, a folder of court documents and a Centipede cabinet, lights one of the Marlboro Reds, and sets fire to the drapes with the purple flowers on them.

beats.headline: The lady with the dog tattoo
beats.text: Carl goes inside and I keep watch. A lady appears in the yard out of nowhere; she walks right through me and her clothes do not go away. She has a pit bull tattooed on her NECK. Carl says be nice, he thinks she is his stepmom, but she is about Katia's age. She pulls something out of a flower pot I cannot see, because Carl took the pots, and she holds it against her chest and cries. Then she smokes a cigarette, pacing, throws it away and heads for the door. I warn him.

beats.headline: Everything until the timer
beats.text: Carl asks me whether this is even real, how long it took us to find, whether we just recorded everything. I'm sorry, Carl. You know I can't give you details. But I assure you, everything you have seen so far is indeed a recording of what really happened that day. Everything until the timer reaches zero. I can't tell you more than that.

beats.headline: The lightning head
beats.text: The youngest face on the Reminiscence Hydra is Asher's. It asks, amplified and much louder than a child, "Carl, why didn't you ever visit me?" and then opens its mouth and fires lightning. It is the lightning head: the resistance and the attack. The other heads swing in to take the bombs meant for it, as though protecting it. Crawler Carl keeps telling himself it is not really the boy, and keeps throwing bombs at it; the other heads keep catching them.

beats.headline: Shi Maria takes the head
beats.text: Carl, on fire, thinks one thing: get the boy's head out of this, fast. Shi Maria turns her corkscrew neck and asks which of these morsels is Asher, third eye open. She finds it. "Carl, I wish I'd known you, too," the Asher head calls, just before it is swallowed and bitten off. Three heads remain. The spider's message follows: the echo of your kin has been muffled. He rests. I have done something for you, she adds, and soon Carl is to do something for her.

beats.headline: Nine heads, most of them known
beats.text: The heads are labelled. Tami-Lynn, my stepmother. Monobrow Sam. Bea's mother. My boss Dick, my landlord Mr. Roth, Sally who did billing, a Persian called Sugar Cube, Judge Lucian holding the cards, and the youngest, Asher. Asher's mouth fires lightning at me. Mordecai says find the fire head, cut it clean, cauterize. It is Bea's mother. I lock a snap collar round her neck, hit it with the shrink wand, and the head flies off. Then I smash a moonshine jug on the wound, and the fire splashes back onto my chest.

beats.headline: The last head
beats.text: Alpha Male Carl, a totem wearing my face and my father's voice, puts his bare foot on my chest and tells me a good son would have stayed by his father's side. Mongo hits him from behind. The hydra is burning down to one conscious head, my stepmother's, and she meets my eyes. She says she does not regret it. She saw what happened to me and did not want Ash to go through the same thing, so she made sure it was done right. Judge Lucian dies. The body breaks open like a bag of spaghetti.

beats.headline: The boss he was not
