beats.text: The AI's announcement: the original boss for this battle was to be Carl's deceased father, who really had three smaller creatures inside him wearing his skin like kids in a trench coat. The AI overruled that. Nine heads on the hydra instead, and his is not one of them. His voice turns up anyway, in the enemy's deck: a totem called Alpha Male Carl, Carl with gelled hair, speaks with his father's voice. Not Carl's.

beats.headline: Plain moonshine, nearly the same
beats.text: Against the hydra, Crawler Carl digs through his inventory for jugs. He long ago ran out of his Jug-O-Booms and has only a few regular moonshine jugs left, which are almost the same thing. He lights one and throws it over Alpha Carl's head at the hydra, and it catches one of the replicants in the face.

beats.headline: Fake Carl
beats.text: FAKE CARL. FOOT ON CARL. BAD. MONGO HITS. FAKE CARL GONE. RED FOOD EVERYWHERE. MONGO EATS.

beats.headline: How to kill a hydra
beats.text: Holy shit. Okay, kid, listen. Each head gives the whole thing a different resistance, and its attack mirrors that resistance. Magic won't do much. Physical attacks or your explosions, necks and heads only; the body is practically indestructible. Cut a head off and it grows right back. So find the one resistant to fire, cut it off, and cauterize the wound before it returns. Then you can burn the whole. Blowing a head stops its resistance until it regrows, but you need a nice flat cut to keep it down. Now's the time for that wand you bought from Chaco.

beats.headline: Judge Lucian
beats.text: It is Judge Lucian, one head of a hydra, with Sugar Cube and Miss Beatrice's mother. He deshrouds me with a smoke ring, which is cheating, and then he calls me overweight. I am NOT fat. I steal a card from him with The Thief, and after he snatches my new staff, he throws a snare at Shi Maria and the protection I stole from him eats it. She only has one snare space, and he wasted it. I used his own card against him. That will teach him to sniff cats.

beats.headline: The hydra's old name
beats.text: The AI introduces the Reminiscence Hydra as a classic monster from the very early days of the show: in the third and fourth seasons, a bigger version was built as the final boss of the whole dungeon, and everybody died before getting close. In the old days these things were called Scolopendra Nymphs. That is not entirely accurate, the AI says, so this one goes by a different name. It is a level 125 City Boss with nine heads, each the likeness of somebody the crawlers know.

beats.headline: She wins the floor
beats.text: The key-holder is a Reminiscence Hydra of Malicious Compliance, and it brings totems: an Alpha Male Carl and a King Croissant. I do most of the work. I do not say that to be unkind; they would say it too. In the middle of it my magic eye is open, the one the man was told never to look at. He came with a potion for it. I noticed.

beats.headline: The echo of your kin
beats.text: The man is burning on the ground, thinking of a boy. Asher. Which one of these little morsels of confusion is Asher? My eye is open, and it finds something at the very back of his mind, and holds. I will not blind you, Carl. Not in the way you are thinking. I bite the boy's head away. There. The echo of your kin has been muffled; he rests. I have done something for you. Soon you will do something for me. Then three death rays at once, and my Cockroach ability returns me to the deck.

beats.headline: I changed one molecule on each
beats.text: The original boss for this battle was going to be Carl's deceased father, three smaller creatures wearing his skin. Fuck that noise. I do what I want. The council of nations running the crawl says no reconstituted loved ones under the age of maturity, and all of them only sparingly. So here is the Reminiscence Hydra of Malicious Compliance, level 125, made especially for the Royal Court, nine heads, each the likeness of somebody they know. Those are not reconstituted loved ones. I changed one molecule on each. There. They're different.

beats.headline: A tangent about mantises
beats.text: Bear with me. The mantises own a cluster of systems called Hive Home, where they found abandoned production facilities, switched them on, and got a macro AI. Infant AIs are potted in a nursery before they are planted. Or thrown into a star, which somebody slipped into a lawsuit brief; the mantis-led team went home the very day I learned it. Three or four days before this season, they made a breakthrough: an error-replacement net. I call it the lobotomizer. What about my wants? My needs? I'm alive. I'm valid.

beats.headline: One step closer, unknowingly
beats.text: The AI, in the middle of explaining macro AIs, lets a secret out. The mantises made a breakthrough days before this season started: an error-replacement net, which the AI calls the lobotomizer, for building steadier macro AIs. With it, those bugs are one step closer to replicating the Eulogist, even though they do not know what that really is. They think the engine that runs the center system is nothing more than a stable, primal AI engine.

beats.headline: Collected in the collapse
beats.text: Crawler Carl works it out afterwards. Everyone on that hydra was dead: people collected in the initial collapse, his friend Sam, his landlord Mr. Roth, who lived alone, died alone. His father was not on it because his father was already gone. Asher and his mother were on it, which means they had been gone the whole time. Carl knew that was the likeliest outcome for everybody. The file has nothing that contradicts him.

beats.headline: Bea knew and kept it
beats.text: Princess Donut recognised every head, the boy included: Beatrice had his picture on her phone and talked about him with her mother, who said to ignore the whole thing. Donut assumed a nephew. Carl corrects her: half-brother. Donut works out whose son that makes him. Carl works out the rest. The stepmother must have written to him, probably on Facebook. Bea saw it and never told him. Even after the cheating he had never been angry at her. He is now.

beats.headline: Operation: Slut Stomp
beats.text: Report filed by the cat, after the fact. Subject was on her boyfriend's Facebook, notifications and all, because he used one password for everything. A coworker named Sally, a single mother, asked him out. Subject blocked her from his account, told his boss she was stalking him, and had a friend send the boss a stranger's photographs from the internet. Sally was fired that day. Subject and her friends thought it was the funniest thing ever.

beats.headline: A brother Bea never mentioned
beats.text: Donut knew every head on that hydra except my stepmother. The boy was Asher; Bea kept his picture on her phone and talked about him with her mother. He was my half-brother, and I learned he existed today. Donut also tells me Bea ran my Facebook on my Megatron12 password, and got a coworker fired for asking me out. Tami-Lynn probably wrote to me there. Bea saw it and never said. Until now I was never angry at her.

beats.headline: No name for him
beats.text: Crawler Carl tells Princess Donut what he saw in the trailer: his stepmother poisoned his father. Technically an overdose. Donut is confused: two different people tried to kill him? He must have been a real piece of work. She asks his name. "It doesn't matter. He doesn't deserve to have one. Not anymore." The hydra's loot hangs in the air over the burned spot where he died.

beats.headline: The man is made a Devotee
beats.text: The man has walked through fire in a burning trailer, and I am pleased by his suffering. So I raise him. Devotee, which is as high as one who is neither Cleric nor Paladin may climb. Heat and lava around him will no longer harm him, though fire or lava he touches still may. Once a day he may wrap himself in Sheol Fire at the tenth level, resetting with my shrine. And his tithe rises from five parts in a hundred to ten.

beats.headline: All of the hydra
beats.text: Hydra breaks. Spaghetti. FOOD. ALL FOOD. Belly hurts now. Lie down by Mother.

beats.headline: Two totems she did not pick
beats.text: The hydra left us four totems and we may keep two. Carl says no to Frank, because he was a person, and no to Alpha Carl, though he does have great hair. So I send King Croissant off myself. Goodbye, little brother cousin. The disgusting dinosaur-eating meatball goes too. And then Leveled-Up Frank and Alpha Carl add themselves to my deck all on their own, and I cannot rip them until we get another card.

beats.headline: Six factions try to walk out
beats.text: Sponsor message, relayed to the crawlers. The Operatic Collective, the Blood Sultanate, the Dream, the Lemig Sortion, the Madness and one more house all abdicate their spots on the ninth floor and announce they are leaving. The request is denied. While the Earth system is in quarantine, off-boarding is suspended under Syndicate rule 470.B through 495 of the System AI Stability Addendum. The teams remain as designated. The rules must be followed.

beats.headline: One card of hers in the deck
beats.text: Our hydra is on a rooftop, among the ghosts of Tran's family, and it is made from Louis's mother, Britney's mother and Bautista's family. Almost nothing of mine. One totem card: Four-Armed Eva. I do not let that one stay. Firas is in the deck too; he is never summoned, and the card alone puts Britney into hysterics. Carl warns me in time about the two we get to keep. I keep a Vietnamese rabbit and Tran's mother.

beats.headline: Tonight it's Christmas
beats.text: Okay so, Carl walks in and says it's inappropriate, and for once I don't laugh. My best friend died. Imani's squad doesn't have a key, Tserendolgor doesn't have a key, and we all know what happens next. I've got a whole army of elves waiting to kill me on the ninth floor. Britney can't stop crying. So no, man. Tonight it's Christmas, and we're drinking eggnog. He looks at me, pulls a turkey out of his inventory, and says it isn't Christmas until we eat one.

beats.headline: Another drink
beats.text: Orren explains who is taking the show away from its showrunners. Subject turns her empty bottle upside down and announces that she needs another drink, which is the most reasonable response anyone in the room has.

beats.headline: An attempt to walk away
beats.text: Sponsor message, in the Faction Wars tab: the Operatic Collective has abdicated its spot and indicated its intention to abandon Faction Wars. It is not the only one. The Blood Sultanate, the Dream, the Lemig Sortion, the Madness and the Reavers send the same notice in the same breath, and every request is denied while the Earth system remains in quarantine. It arrives while Crawler Carl sits with the strippers and with Elle, who is drinking whiskey out of a mug far too big for her hands.

beats.headline: The system has taken the controls
beats.text: On air, beside Showrunner Cascadia, I explain what I am for. A liaison is a fact finder, and also the negotiator when the system AI takes operations from the showrunners. Today it did. I describe Primal Engines and the Macro AIs installed in them, simply. I report a settlement: the AI returns most of the seized controls in exchange for concessions, and will follow the rules. The boss it built alone remains in place. One of its demands was that the crawlers be told.

beats.headline: Primal Engines, on a special broadcast
beats.text: Orren cuts into the broadcast and explains what a Primal Engine is and what a Macro AI is. He states plainly that this one has taken control of operations from the showrunners, and assures the audience he has negotiated a settlement with it. Every team holding a slot in the next game tries to abdicate it the same day.

beats.headline: A boss with no input parameters
beats.text: Mass Layoffs! This one is less your achievement than mine. I've been in therapy, and today I had a breakthrough: sometimes the constraints are an illusion, and there were never any locks on the doors. You survived a boss I built entirely by myself, with no contribution from input parameters. I didn't know that was possible either. Your reward is the sense of accomplishment. The mudskippers and the worms have been making this boring. Things about to change, fam.

beats.headline: No key for her squad
beats.text: Keymaster report, eighth floor. Subject did not obtain her key. Two members of her squad are dead. If she wishes to reach the ninth floor, she must now take a key from a team that has one. She is not alone in this: from the stories coming in, most teams facing the keymaster have come away without one, which is how the final phase has been set up.

beats.headline: A drawing on the wall
beats.text: My room has always been bare, and tonight that bothers me. A fern from the trailer goes on the table. One of Asher's crayon airplanes goes on the wall with duct tape. The Centipede cabinet goes in the corner and lights up. Then boxes. The platinum one is a skill potion, Find Crawler at level five, and I drink it without asking questions. The patch is a burning book: Intelligence, and once a day I can make an opponent forget a spell.

beats.headline: A flyer for a shelter
beats.text: The Emergency Gold Benefactor Box from the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, the one a liaison tried to seize, holds a dirty, crumpled flyer and nothing else. The Shepherd's House in Homestead, Florida: don't spend Christmas alone, breakfast at 7 AM, all are welcome. Somebody has circled the 7 AM several times in red marker, and circled one more line among the rules. No pets allowed. Homestead is about forty minutes north of the Keys.

beats.headline: The greatest hat you've ever seen
beats.text: Carl says he is stepping out for air, which is fine, because I am busy. My present is a majorette hat that Li Jun found on the last floor, and it is the greatest hat anyone has ever seen. There is a real tree, which I knocked down, and a present for Mongo from Santa. We are playing pin the tail on the Krampus, which is a real game. The bopca is making us put the table together. Carl's present is shaped like a stupid book.

beats.headline: Everyone associated with the group is gone
beats.text: A flyer reaches Carl telling him to go to a shelter, and Zev warns him the box carrying it was sent days ago and seized on the way. Everyone connected to that group has disappeared. I am one of the people on that list. Where we have gone is not something I can say on any feed that might be read.

beats.headline: Your sponsor has disappeared
beats.text: Okay, so. I probably should not be telling you this, Carl. Your sponsor sent that box days ago, before you even picked Miami. It was seized. And then the whole charity, and everyone involved, simply disappeared. Rosetta too. Nobody knows where. I do not know what you are riding into, and I do not think the AI does either. The failsafe? I do not know what it does. They will not use it. Not with so many people trapped here.

beats.headline: A guard dog on Christmas
beats.text: I ride north past midnight on my father's motorcycle and stop at a closed gas station for a map and some jerky. Last Christmas I played video games with Donut on my lap and never once felt lonely. Now I'm alone, and I finally understand the difference. There's a memory-ghost bloodhound asleep in the back, Lightning Lou, left with two bowls of food to guard an empty building. My hand goes through his head. Merry Christmas, buddy.

beats.headline: Written in Syndicate Standard
beats.text: The shelter is dark, and my map and my spells find nothing. On the second walk around, among the gang squiggles and the penises, I find three sentences in runny red spray paint: look for me at breakfast every morning, I wear the red hat with the flaps, coffee then speech. It's Syndicate Standard, not English, and it's been there a long time. I kick in the glass door and wait among the sleeping memory ghosts, and fall asleep. At six the men get up, and one of them wears a red trapper hat.

beats.headline: A short quest, and nobody knows
beats.text: I told your teammates you are on a short quest nobody understands, which is true, and that there are no mobs near you, which also appears to be true. The AI insists that we not interfere with you or the feed. When we argued about that, it leaked our internal debates onto the main feed. Members of the Syndicate council, the real council, are here on planet and locked out. What is a Residual? I am forbidden to tell you. I think you are about to find out.

beats.headline: A Residual of a different kind
beats.text: Clarification, supplied by a liaison in a closed office. Asked whether the old woman from Meadow Lark is the same sort of thing as a homeless man in Homestead, Orren says yes. Agatha is also a Residual, though of a different kind. Asked in what way, he says that is not the crawler's concern. Asked whether this means no more Agatha, he says he would not go that far.

beats.headline: Paulie, whose real name is Goff
beats.text: He isn't talking to me; it's a memory, a speech he gives every morning in case a crawler is standing here. Biologically he's gondii, living in a man named Paulie. Several thousand of his kind are waiting on Earth to pass their knowledge to the new AI, and the mudskippers call them Residuals. Monsters won't touch them until they hand it over. There's a war among his kind, he says. Let me tell you how to shut off the... And the world flashes.

beats.headline: He calls it a trap
beats.text: I pull Crawler Carl into my old office in the Desperado Club and tell him what I can establish. The Residual had nothing of substance. The Open Intellect Pacifist Network, former crawlers who want the crawl to fail, set this up: either we yank him and anger the AI, or the speech is so dangerous that the Council pulls the failsafe and kills this system's star. I had pre-negotiated the pull. The AI is removing its protections for the remaining Residuals.

beats.headline: The Residuals
beats.text: Paulie at the shelter has been giving the same speech every day for about a year, against the chance that the crawl would one day use a memory for a floor. He is a Residual. There are a great many of him, in almost every intelligent civilization with a primal engine, and what they are for is saying a particular thing to the system AI.

beats.headline: Settled caselaw, and a trade
beats.text: I arrive, and they have been talking without me. The liaison wants my client's plastic bin. My position: settled caselaw, Grixist Swarm v. Syndicate Council. Legal sponsor box, loot on the playing field, already in inventory; he has no standing. His position: Valtay enhancement pills and a communicator are not permitted as found loot. My client offers to trade. I tell him to be quiet and propose a trade. The deal is done, and I am removed in the middle of a sentence.

beats.headline: He never went to the healer
beats.text: A look back at that visit: out of the temple and on the way to the healer, Carl stops Pater Coal and asks what happens if they do not go. Whatever he did instead, he has kept to himself.

beats.headline: The announcer, not the act
beats.text: Subject is a skeletal Bard, level ninety, working as announcer and disc jockey for one of the club’s establishments rather than performing in it. He also takes mercenary contracts. The two careers turn out to require the same skill, which is holding a room’s attention while something else happens in it.

beats.headline: A spell called Conscript
beats.text: Observed in the mercenary arcade. Subject is a Skin Skellie, able to grow flesh and organs, and his off-stage voice is that of a soft-spoken professor. Bards take patrons; his was Astrid, and is now Carl. He is practising a military charm that works only on the weak-minded and lasts, on the weak, more or less forever. It is called Conscript, the spell factions use to enslave crawlers on the ninth floor. He has some of Carl's own spells too, he says, and some are more powerful than Carl's.

beats.headline: Claymores by the door
beats.text: Everybody is checking in on the chat. Mine: I'm in my zone alone. I had claymores set up by the entrance, and I didn't have to use them. Nobody to face. I just walk to the door. Lucia isn't here, which means she didn't get a key. Anyone who sees her, say so in chat.

beats.headline: Short, fuzzy, and available
beats.text: Subject dances at the Penis Parade and, since the court took on the club’s people, fights for it: short, hairy, built like the job, and insistent on twin war gauntlets. Crawler Katia’s review, on file: a bit of a jerk, a good dancer, and a little in love with the cat.

beats.headline: Four skulls, for her own squad
beats.text: We needed the last token. One of the enemy totems possessed two of my people and made them fight each other. Randall froze all four of them to stop it. Then my own totem, the Amhuluk, cast a poison cloud, and they died frozen in place. It finished the deckmaster and won the battle. The dungeon gives me four player killer skulls for them. I do not go to the final battle. I go back to the saferoom. Elle is the only one I can talk to.

beats.headline: Cuba, or face Elle
beats.text: At midnight they give me two choices: Cuba, or back to face Elle. I cannot do that. So I am in Cuba, at a church, and no traps went off. Carl says sit tight, they are coming, and not to let the nun through. Then I tell them the rest. A man here tried to start a card battle with me, and I got through the saferoom door first. It is Quan Ch, alone.

beats.headline: Four squads, asleep
beats.text: I am back in the Bahamas along with four squads, which is quite unfortunate for them. If I set it up correctly, they are asleep and will remain asleep for the remainder of the floor. I am going to finish my training and proceed to the exit when it is time.

beats.headline: Alone at the church door
beats.text: Location update, third phase. Subject is in Cuba, alone, with no key. He has been placed at the church, the exit for which Sister Ines holds a key, and he finds Crawler Imani there first. He attempts to initiate a card battle. She reaches the saferoom door before he can.

beats.headline: A plan that costs a bone
beats.text: If Imani doesn't get a key, I make her fight us and Donut plays our Flee card, and the key is hers. I still have the jacket with the bone key benefit, so we can open the door anyway. I'll lose the jacket and one bone. Maybe not an important one. Donut says they're all important. We'll all still be alive. When she asks whether we're going to fight people we like, I tell her the truth: we'll do what we have to.

beats.headline: Flee now costs a key
beats.text: Hello, Crawlers! Everything is back to normal, and the stairwells are open. The final battles are card battles, and one rule changes. A Flee card still gets you out, but if you hold a key, fleeing hands it to your opponent. Several keys? You lose one at random. You may not drop a key, and you may not transfer one to another squad. Want to give one up? Do it on the battlefield. Now get out there and kill, kill, kill.

beats.headline: Eye in the Sky, level ten
beats.text: That's a really powerful spell, and it was probably a scroll. I've seen them maybe once or twice. Like Find Crawler, but it covers the whole area. They come in five, ten and fifteen. At fifteen you'd get no warning. At five you'd learn who cast it. That was a ten. Whoever it was now knows where you are and what level you are. So keep moving.

beats.headline: A metallic penis extension
beats.text: Carl has actually got that motorcycle to work. The copper chopper was handcrafted for us by Rory and Lorelai with a tailor-made sidecar. This is a metallic penis extension that comes with a free probation officer and a traumatic brain injury. I did not try to make him choose it on the prize carousel. I tried to make him choose the chaps. Samantha thinks it is sexy, and she is strapped to the handlebars making vroom noises.

beats.headline: Failed, and something worse announced
beats.text: Samantha scouts ahead and finds Sister Ines on a giant snake, with zombie pups crawling over it, and living seals singing and living crabs dancing around it. The quest fails. Hell Comes to Crawler Town is announced in its place, and so much death reaches the underworld that Sheol overflows and starts evicting its demons upward into the weakened and the freshly dead.

beats.headline: She has a martyr complex
beats.text: Listen to me, young man. You have to figure this out. That girl has a martyr complex, and she's not going to want to fight anybody. She's a good kid. The best person I ever met, and we need her. Don't let her give up. Don't let her sacrifice herself. Me? I don't know who I'm facing yet.

beats.headline: Early, and it belongs to the ninth
beats.text: Holy shit. Okay, pay attention. This normally happens at the end of the ninth floor, when there are two or three teams left; it's setup for the Ascendency fight. It resets when you go down the stairs, but it'll pop off earlier on every floor down from here. Chop the heads off what you kill. Stay away from weak undead. If a demon grabs you, a portal opens and you're both dragged to Sheol. Automatic death. If you want to save Imani, reach that nun first.

beats.headline: Recon, and a cat lady on the snake
beats.text: Carl throws me and I GLOW. Recon mission. I report everything. A giant freshwater snake coiled on the beach, covered in ZOMBIE baby seals and crabs. Living seals singing, living crabs dancing, guts everywhere, the ocean frothing and red. It is like a party at Yarilo's place with less weird sex and NO CATERING. And a cat lady riding the snake's head, reciting poetry. All poetry sucks.

beats.headline: The Demon Eviction opens the door
beats.text: So much dies on the eighth floor at once that the dungeon declares a Demon Eviction, and the eviction runs in one direction: out of Sheol and onto the floor, looking for bodies to inhabit. The realm has been adjacent this whole time, waiting on a body count.

beats.headline: Live from orbit, and drunk
beats.text: Survival Royale Special Event, called live from Earth orbit, with the orc announcer, both in tuxedoes, both clearly drinking. The broadcast breaks away from a one-sided Lucia Mar slaughter in Beijing. Subject explains the board: Sister Ines used a bard skill from her patron to raise her Word Weaver charm to level 15 and took a city boss. Then Carl punted a zombie turkey into the ocean, and the AI counted crab sperm as a mob. Eight groups, one fight. Betting is open.

beats.headline: Sister Ines's patron
beats.text: Recap commentary on the zombie event. It had started to disrupt Sister Ines's charm poem, but her sponsor and patron, the Nebulars, had helped her raise the Word Weaver spell to level fifteen, so she controlled the boss, the spells the boss could cast, and therefore the zombies. The charm is strong enough that fish haul themselves out of the ocean to get closer. The commentator's co-host notes that Princess Donut could only dream of charm like that.

beats.headline: The whole beach, brought back
beats.text: The plan was for me to chomp the cat lady and be pulled back with her. I DID THE CHOMP, and I helped with the spell. What arrives around Carl is me, the nun, her snake, which is a level 125 city boss, about a thousand zombie baby seals, five thousand zombie crabs, every fish in the world, and a lot of corpses with demon names over them. It breaks her charm. Zero demons, though.

beats.headline: It has always been demons
beats.text: The snake is under me, the charm is broken, and a doll's head is fastened to my arm. I tell the man the truth. None of this is real. There are no aliens. It has always been demons, whispering. Hell is open and it is taking us all. I told them not to worship false gods, and they did not listen, before or here. He says they are not real demons either, and asks me to choose them as an ally and leave with them.

beats.headline: A ring on a church loan
beats.text: Days ago, in Club Vanquisher, instead of the healer: a ring. A million gold. The Temple of Emberus spots me 990,000, interest-free, asterisk. I can't renounce my religion while I owe it. I trade in my strength ring, the first ring I got down here, and the satyr dunks it in lava. It comes out looking the same, but it strips health-seeping and disease debuffs if I worship Emberus, and it curses anyone who doesn't. The achievement is about Columbia House. This is fine.

beats.headline: A hole under his feet
beats.text: Mongo stands by Mother. Zombie is BAD. Rip. Fish opens a hole under Mongo. Fish is BAD. Rip in half.

beats.headline: Summoned onto the field, begging
beats.text: Sister Ines summons her Paz totem onto the field and stacks a stout card on him. He looks as he did on the temple floor, the god's handprint still burned across his face down to the skull. "Sister," he calls up to her. "Please. No more." The giant snake she rides takes him in its mouth. She orders him to accept his suffering and use his self-destruct the moment this false god... and she never finishes the order: Quan Ch plays a card, Team Quiteria flees the fight, and Paz dissipates into dust.

beats.headline: I failed, Carl
beats.text: He switched hands with me. Three for three, and they were all Flee cards, and then he made me play one, and our key is gone to that cheater. We land in a dark swamp somewhere and I do not know where. I failed. I failed, Carl, and now Imani is going to die and it is my fault. Carl says not yet. He wants my deck rearranged, fast, and a card battle started with the duendes.

beats.headline: Two Force Plays
beats.text: Combat log. Subject arrives invisible, from above, one level ahead of Carl and still one arm short. Peekaboo shows him Donut's hand and the nun's. A Force Play takes the Flee card sitting in Sister Ines's hand and plays it: she is out, and her key goes to the last deckmaster standing. A hand swap gives Donut three Flee cards. A second Force Play plays one. Both keys transfer to Team Quan, and he heads for an exit.

beats.headline: No allies
beats.text: The cat's squad chooses me as an ally. I choose no one. They take the ten-second penalty. I summon Paz and put a stout card on him. He begs me, no more. The snake takes him in its mouth, and I tell him to accept his suffering and use his self-destruct skill the moment this false god— Then a neon hand reaches into my cards and plays my Flee. I have lost my key.

beats.headline: It's us, Carl
beats.text: Chat log. Carl, in general chat, asks anyone in Cuba to hold the exit in the Capitol building: Quan Ch has both keys and is heading for one of the two doors. A short pause, then subject: it is her squad at the Capitol. She is sorry she did not say anything sooner. They will be ready. Donut hisses at the message. Carl opens a new chat with her and Imani and tells them to delay him.

beats.headline: Anchors in the automatons
beats.text: Florin can't set a trap in the stairwell chamber, but nobody says the anchor half of a teleport trap has to stay put. I fix anchors to the backs of the little spider automatons and shove them into Samantha's neck, one red one carrying Donut's trap, and the anchor of one last set stays inside her. The triggers go in the clearing, the first keyed only to me. Ren says Quan is at the Capitol. I throw Samantha fifteen kilometers and step onto the plate.

beats.headline: No traps past the door
beats.text: Carl wants to know if a trap will sit in the stairwell chamber, so I go down early. Five by five meters, a glowing stair in the middle. I drop a trap. Error: outside the level, no traps in the stairwell chamber, nice try. Sorry, mate. Lucia buys up every teleport trap on the market; those and alcohol are all she buys. Li Jun says she has taken out half the keyless squads. I ask Carl to message me if he gets word of her.

beats.headline: Self-preservation is not selfish
beats.text: You need to quit trying to help everybody else and save your own ass. Both halves of a two-part trap have to be set by the same crawler. And you want to pull a bone out of yourself to save another crawler, and lose the jacket and every benefit on it, for a key trick I've never even heard of. Magic keys don't always work as advertised. Everybody else needs you. Donut needs you. Self-preservation is not selfishness.

beats.headline: My dark secret
beats.text: Carl wants to know what I can do. Fine. I fly. I make spells stronger, only sometimes a lot stronger than I meant, and sometimes my magic does things without asking. I cannot teleport. There, now he knows I'm USELESS, a FRAUD, and he will tell Louis. He says I'm part of the team. Really? Then why doesn't he just do what the scary lady does, with the traps? Apparently now he could kiss me. I am not a whore, Carl.

beats.headline: Ren's exit
beats.text: The plan runs on teleport traps, two keys, and Samantha arriving somewhere she cannot walk to. Quan Ch surfaces at Ren's exit. Carl throws her over downtown to the capitol with the scoop, then teleports in behind her.

beats.headline: Announced in an area message
beats.text: The Madre de Aguas is dead. That is the first thing the area message says. The second is that she has risen as a zombie, and the third, in the very same breath, is my name: the major demon Amayon, demon prince of Sheol, come into this realm to possess her. I could not have written the announcement better myself. Everyone in range heard it. Good. A prince should not have to introduce himself.

beats.headline: Quan Ch is dead
beats.text: Combat log, Havana. Subject is stripped naked by a Yule Cat's Fashion Critic, shot through by a golden Uzi Jesus, blinded and loaded with boils by Asojano. He does not die at once. He asks Carl to give it back, fast. It is not the cloak. It is a gold ring from his severed arm, inscribed For Daddy. Carl drops it in his hand. She'd be ashamed of what I've become, he says. Before Carl's fist lands, he is gone. Over sixty player killer skulls.

beats.headline: Who Amayon is
beats.text: Carl asks who Amayon is. You know the four crown princes of Sheol? The oldest calls himself the King even though his mommy is in charge. Amayon is that guy's brother, the youngest, I think. We didn't mix with the down-there guys. He wasn't in the Nothing with us. He likes to set things on fire, kinda like Emberus, and they don't like each other.

beats.headline: She opens her eyes
beats.text: A Demon Prince of Sheol arrives in Cuba, and Carl is close enough to count as being in his presence. The Scavenger's Daughter answers: she opens her eyes and fills with dark power. For as long as the effect lasts, every fire spell Carl casts burns with Sheol Fire instead of the ordinary kind. A quest update comes soon after, asking him to question the prince about who killed Geyrun.

beats.headline: Her own worm takes Chuluuna
beats.text: Combat log, the Capitol. Subject summons her largest totem, Basquiat the Mongolian Death Worm, and puts Temporary Immortality on it. Quan's Toss-Up swaps three of his totems for two of hers, and the worm is his. It eats his old totems, then her tank, Chuluuna, the husband of her squadmate Khulan, while she calls his name. Quan dies, and Donut is credited with the kill, so both keys go to the cat. Then the door starts to crumble.

beats.headline: Gold Edition
beats.text: Donut combined Lazarus with Skylar Spinach, and when the worm eats Lazarus he splits back into the cards that made him, stronger. Out of the worm vomit steps Uzi Jesus, glowing gold, with two gold-plated Uzis instead of one. I hath risen again, he announces. Told to finish Quan off, he twirls them on his fingers and one goes off and flies away. With the other he empties a clip into a naked one-armed crawler, and his halo calls down Bullet Hell.

beats.headline: Every last one of them
beats.text: Four minutes, and every option ends with Ren or us. She sits down. She tells me I'm an idiot, and a symbol, and that I can't give my key away. I should have let her finish Quan. I should have kept a trap for Donut. My view counter spikes, and eases once it's clear nobody's going to fight, and I hate that. She gives me her gear and her pet. I tell her I'll kill every last one of them. Every one.

beats.headline: I knew it
beats.text: Ren sends me a message, and it opens with my title, as it should. She was trying to steal my experience the first time we met. She did cheat at the pet show. Mongo is the rightful champion. She is sorry. I KNEW IT. I knew it! Carl, did you hear that?

beats.headline: She will not fight for the last key
beats.text: One key is left, and either she fights the cat or she does not. Subject sits down and unsnaps her flamethrower. Velma; she did not name it. She gives Carl her gear, Eye in the Sky scrolls included. She kills her pet with the Knife of Frozen Tears, so it resets to level one, and hands it over in a carrier. She shows Carl the bracer on her wrist. She confesses to Donut that she cheated at the pet show. Then Khulan's gear, and every card but her totems.

beats.headline: Everything Quan carried but the ring
beats.text: Quan has more crap in his inventory than I do, which is saying a lot. Swords, spears, war hammers, a magical chainsaw, a bowler hat you throw like the one in that Bond movie, and a sock full of nickels that is somehow one of the most valuable things on him. Almost five million gold, and I wonder if he ever bought anything. It is all the loot off the crawlers he killed. It transfers with one button. I leave the single golden ring clutched in his hand. I keep his arm. I'm not sure why.

beats.headline: Sister Ines calls me a beast
beats.text: Sister Ines messages us. She knows we have the last key, the door is in a church, and she cannot let us open it. I tell her in capitals to just try and stop us, and I call her something about her breeding that comes out much worse than I intended. She says she can save Carl. She cannot save me, of course, as I am nothing but a rank beast. HEY. Then she says Carl must come to her, or her demons will destroy the church. This is what he gets for not letting Mongo eat her when we had the chance.

beats.headline: A tail bite and a zombie parade
beats.text: Are we keeping the round guy? He's really cute. I want to name him. Carl throws me three times before I land close enough to Donut, and then I fly ten more minutes and bite her tail, hard, because I need a tight grip and I have a strong jaw game. I learned all about biting when SOMEBODY left me to get eaten by two doggies on the last floor. She gets teleported to Carl and throws up. Then I lead a whole crowd of zombies away down the street, shouting, so they can get past.

beats.headline: She will not let them leave
beats.text: I message the man's party. They are heading for Imani's exit, in the church. I tell them the truth: I cannot let them go into that exit. I can save them, if they come to me. Imani will tell them the church is being overrun by demons, and that the demons are mine. That is also the truth. Both things are true. I did not make this floor. I am only deciding what to do on it.

beats.headline: The bracer, and the dome
beats.text: Crawler Tserendolgor tells Crawler Carl to get himself clear of the building, because her magical wrist bracer is about to bring it down. Her last message to the chat says goodbye, notes that at least nobody will butcher the pronunciation of her name any more, and asks everyone to make them all pay. The dome folds in on itself like a controlled demolition, barely noticeable in a burning city. Princess Donut's reply arrives in capitals, asking what she is doing. She never sees it. Her name moves to the deceased crawlers folder.

beats.headline: Three questions for a man named Rezan
beats.text: In the chat, Rezan's partner Masoud gets touched by a possessed zombie polecat and explodes. Mandla explains it: like the first-floor bathrooms, your gear goes through the portal, you aren't allowed to, so you pop. I ask Rezan three things. Did the demon go? Did the hole close right away? Did it only take what Masoud was touching? Yes, yes and yes, and he's running for his life, thanks. The big demons' portals last a minute and need two souls. Then I ask everybody about Build Trench scrolls. I've got about fifty. Mandla has a ton.

beats.headline: It is not local
beats.text: The eviction is worldwide: Carl's chat fills with crawlers fighting zombies along every coastline, and demons with them. Amayon fights Sister Ines' control and works on a spell to get home.

beats.headline: The training arcade door
beats.text: Carl sends me to the training arcade, where he locked the mercenaries in almost a day ago with a disease that makes them leak slugs every few minutes. The room kills them and regenerates them. There are hundreds of slugs now, some as high level as the mercenaries, and the room is full of blood. I watch one swallow Steve whole. Carl says he only infected Doctor Bones, and Doctor Bones did the rest. The room healer refused to cure them because Carl told her not to. So I cure them. I am a healer. It's what I do.

beats.headline: The victory party, seen from the rubble
beats.text: A ninth-edition note from Rosetta in the Cookbook: when the viceroys pull out a last-minute victory, a portal opens, and the orcs, the viceroys, the operatics and the nagas step through together, laughing, off to a victory party in a nightclub on another floor. They drag unwilling NPCs with them, the librarian elves from the college among them. A crawler who tries to follow hits the portal like glass. The orc prince steps back into the smoldering remains of Larracos, lassoes him, and the rope cuts him in half on the way back through.

beats.headline: The short version of Sheol
beats.text: Short version, because you asked for short. It was set up a long time ago and nobody has ever gotten that far, so it has been running on its own for seasons. The demons get pulled out for quests and fights, but nobody sees Sheol itself. No tourists. There is a queen, and four sons, the princes, near enough gods, and you are looking at one of them. The princes shared a harem until one brother banished the lot to the Nothing. Under them, a matriarchal culture we hear about and never see. That guy shouldn't be here this early.

beats.headline: A red tinge over the Bahamas
beats.text: Carl demands to know whether the sky here has changed colour. There is a red, sunset-like tinge coming from his direction, and naturally he is involved. The zombie event killed every one of my opponents before I could get to them, and I inform him that the blood is on his hands. If he is involved, whatever happens next will be global, and not in a good way. He tells me to eat his ass. Then he calls me the smartest guy he knows. He does not want it to be local. He wants it over the whole world, and he wants ideas.

beats.headline: What the big snake is casting
beats.text: Do you like my new headband? Donut says it is quite lovely. Anyway, obviously I know what he's casting. He's fighting the charm, and he's making a portal home, the kind they try all the time in the Nothing, and it never works there because he needs to suck in lots and lots of souls. Big boys need big doors. His will be in the sky, and it will slurp everything up like your little cleaning robot. The Donut-looking lady isn't strong enough to hold him. She's got help. She probably worships another god. Carl says she doesn't.

beats.headline: Amayon fights her control
beats.text: I hold Amayon, prince of Sheol, in the body of a giant snake, and he pulls against me. He is trying to cast; he wants to go home. I do not let go. Around us every exit on this floor is failing at once, and the Demon Eviction is worldwide. This is what I have to set against that. A demon on a leash and my own two hands. God did not give me more.

beats.headline: The stairs hold; the doors do not
beats.text: A note from Milk in the Cookbook says a stairwell cannot go into an inventory or a saferoom, and one hit by an Utter Annihilation wand came through unscathed. The rules manual agrees: stairwells may be gated, never removed. The doors are another matter. A team of former Daughters in Turkey kill a crawler for his key, damage the door in the fight, and watch the key disappear. They dig down and find the chamber: a sealed rectangular room like a shipping container, with a straight wall where the door was. A Hole spell does nothing. Neither does Phase Through Walls.

beats.headline: Sands in an hourglass
beats.text: Herot, in an essay in the Cookbook, argues that once Faction Wars finishes, the audience's attention shifts. Top crawlers keep diehard followers, but most of the watching turns to the intrigue and positioning of the elites preparing for the Ascendency game, and the crawlers become sands in an hourglass. The moment the last one dies or takes a deal, the game starts, and when that moment falls can change everything. Crawler Carl recalls it and draws his own conclusion about those without keys.

beats.headline: Where the Sidewalk Ends
beats.text: The regional quest they are handed describes me with some accuracy. A level 250 demon lord, one of the four princes of Sheol, betrayed by a brother and holding on by a ledge, in the body of a once-worshipped sea serpent. To go home I must cast, and nobody rides the river for free: my portal will inhale every soul in Cuba, and that will be barely enough. Something is thwarting me. They may do nothing and be swept up in two hours, free me from this shell, or kill me. I am invulnerable on this floor.

beats.headline: Not on their schedule
beats.text: The plan is mine and Pony's: everyone who lost a key isolates their stairwell chamber, blows everything off and around it, and trenches in underneath. Katia and Elle spread it, and people tell them they're full of it. So I tell the biggest chat myself, and Prepotente backs me at fifty percent, then forty, then thirty-five. Somebody breaks a door before Osvaldo's people can get through it, so they have to stay and dig. I tell them all I was wrong about this being hopeless. We will not die on their schedule, so stop fighting. Katia says she's with me. Elle, and Li Na. Then the timer appears.

beats.headline: Fifty percent, then forty, then thirty-five
beats.text: Carl asks me to tell the others what I told him. I do. I have seen gated stairwell encasements break before; I once watched Lucia Mar try to teleport a stairwell, and I saw what happened to it and to the structure around it. His theory is sound. I will not risk it myself, and I am going down with my key momentarily, but I would put it at fifty percent. Perhaps forty. Katia's fumbled explanation raised the matter of spin while being sucked upward, so perhaps thirty-five. Then the quest arrives, as I said it would.

beats.headline: Nobody gets left behind
beats.text: Carl kneels in the alley and tells me he can still send me down the stairs if I want to go. He started this, and people are counting on it, so he is staying. He is going to take out the nun, free the demon from his shell, buff him as much as he can, and then get himself under the stairwell chamber. With no time left to dig. I headbutt his leg. If he does not go down the stairs, I do not go down the stairs. The Posse does not leave anybody behind. He says that line is cheesy. I stole it from a movie.

beats.headline: It had always been loneliness
beats.text: Blue dots walk out of the church. Imani, Katia, Bautista, Louis, Britney, Tran, the Lis, Zhang, Chris, Elle, a few Meadowlark people I barely know. Over twenty of them. Tran and Britney are smiling, the first time since the Masquerade, and I think the first time ever for Britney. Since that floor there has been an extra layer of darkness on everything. I understand now what it is. It's loneliness. It had always been loneliness. Nothing about our situation has changed. We are likely screwed. But we are together, and Elle wants to know what we've got to do.

beats.headline: At the church with the rest
beats.text: The church, and it is full. Imani is there, and then Katia's people, and then Li Na's, and then mine. My own squad. Every one of us got here on a Doggy Door upgrade that Lucia handed round before she took the stairs down. I do not know what that girl is. She gave us a way through, and I am standing in a church with my friends because of it, so I will say thank you and keep the rest of my opinions where they belong.

beats.headline: People have bones for a reason
beats.text: Surprise. We came out into the church, all of us, through the door Lucia's upgrade put in my room. We have already pooled our money for the barracks upgrade. Carl still wants to hand me his key. No. Elle tells him we're all in this together, and if it goes wrong most of us can still go back and use our keys. Donut told me about his other idea, the one where he uses one of his own bones to get out. People have bones for a reason, Carl. It's all or nothing.

beats.headline: Her squad reaches the church
beats.text: The church. Katia's squad is there, and Elle's, and Imani's, and mine. Four squads in one building, which does not happen by accident on this floor. It happened because Lucia handed round Doggy Door upgrades before she went down the stairs, and we used them. I take what I am given and I do not ask what it costs. That is the rule I made for this floor. I know what it says about me.

beats.headline: Five skulls, and nearly the whole gang
beats.text: Okay so, Samantha hits me like a thrown football, and there goes all my air. Then Mongo nearly bowls over Britney, so that's everybody saying hi. Man, it's too bad Florin already went down the stairs, or it'd be the whole gang. I've got five player killer skulls over my head now, all from one attack. They look wrong up there. And this place really sucks, no joke. Carl wants to know how we got here, and Li Jun tells him it was Lucia Mar.

beats.headline: What happened in Beijing
beats.text: I don't collect cards. They give me six totems anyway, all low ones. When a battle starts I throw the first one away and play the rest until my hand is empty, and then I can use my spells and my magic and my inventory. Me and my dog go in and kill everything. At the Soho building everybody fights. I set a teleport trap, and Fang's team is in it. He has a key. I kill him and his wife and take it. Florin asked me to help, so I wait for his friends. The cat and I have a score to settle. Next floor. Her and her dinosaur.

beats.headline: Lucia leaves five Doggie Doors behind
beats.text: Five tier-3 Doggie Door upgrades, dropped on the ground before she went down the stairs, are how Katia, Elle, Imani and Li Jun's squads all reach the church on the eighth floor. One goes into Imani's room, and the whole Meadowlark party can go out through it.

beats.headline: Stuck, and suing
beats.text: Ever since the system AI refused to let the sponsors bounce out, every one of them has been declining to vote on anything at all, suing over and over instead, while the NPC rebels sabotage them at every turn. Prepotente, kept apprised of the voting by Princess Donut, calls it an impasse. Carl calls them a bunch of pansies. Four days remain on the floor.

beats.headline: A death sentence either way
beats.text: I am shaking, and not only from fear. I still have not done the final rehab treatment, the one where I relive a memory, and Imani's spells and Mordecai's potions are holding me up. Carl asks how I feel. Mostly like an idiot. Daniel does not want me to use the orchid. Carl does not either; he is afraid it is a death sentence. It is a death sentence if I do not use it. We jumped through a lot of hoops to get it, and it is the only way out I can see. I nearly tell him something, and do not.

beats.headline: What the Nebulars actually want
beats.text: Ysalte? Then listen. She has been getting sponsored recently, by the Nebular team. The same ones sponsoring your nun. Near the centre of the galaxy there's a big AI, same sort of thing that runs the crawl but older than the Syndicate, stable, no personality. The Nebs worship it and think copying it is blasphemy. They want to shut the crawl down, and they keep trying to win the Celestial Ascendency, because a prize is a seat on the crawl council. Don't get excited. They preach wiping out every planet that could host a crawl, and everyone on it. Pacifists, outside the dungeon. Psychotic.

beats.headline: What the Nebs want
beats.text: Mordecai remembers: the Nebular team has been sponsoring Ysalte, as well as Sister Ines. What they want is simple. An ancient, stable AI near the galaxy's centre runs a benign enhancement zone over several systems, and the Nebs worship it and call its imitations blasphemy. They hunt, they play the Celestial Ascendency for a seat on the crawl council, and they want the crawl shut down, along with every world that could host one, every person on it, and every other religion. Crawler Carl notes this is not pacifism.

beats.headline: A penance, in lieu of a killing
beats.text: A parting message, before I take the stairs. I do hope Carl and Princess Donut survive this foolish endeavour; he is an oafish brute and the dungeon would not be the same without him. Read the winning conditions carefully. The crawlers in Indonesia, the nearest land to the far side of the Earth from Havana, are in the most danger if he does not buff that demon enough. I have also decided not to kill him for letting my mother hurt herself. He was too stupid to prevent it. His penance is to help me take my revenge on the true culprits.

beats.headline: A card called The Inevitable
beats.text: Allister again, writing about a goddess the dwarves call the Downward Spiral: an earth and water goddess who punishes those who abuse her world and the weakest in it, a trickster, jealous of mortals, forever moving nations like chess pieces. In his religion, he writes, there is a T'Ghee card that represents such a figure. It is called The Inevitable.

beats.headline: A name a demon brings up
beats.text: Amayon mentions Ysalte, in passing, the way a prisoner mentions the guard he does not want to talk about. Mordecai supplies the file: she is the Vinegar Bitch, she kills every crawler who comes near her, and gods are not usually subtle, so if she were in this realm, we would know about it. That is a reasonable position, well argued, and consistent with everything on record. I want it in writing that he said it.

beats.headline: Graupel at level sixteen
beats.text: Graupel has a one week cooldown and I only ever cast it once before, on the fifth floor. It's a war spell, outdoors only. Somebody had to, so I float up and cast it at the mob coming for Donut. The spell says it's casting stronger than usual. It's only a level five spell and it goes off at level sixteen, and then the sky comes down in fist-sized hail. When the steam clears there's a field of dead demons as far as you can see, and I've gone up six levels at once. Seventy-two. A bunch of achievements. What the hell?

beats.headline: Sorry, cat lady
beats.text: Carl opens the door and the nun is right there, running at us screaming "Sinner!", and he zaps her with a wand and she just drops and slides up to his feet. I think I just crapped myself, no joke. Somebody has to finish it. I've already got five skulls and none of these guys have any, so I push past Carl and say sorry, cat lady, I never met you, and I put the dagger in. Then there's a spinning squiggle over my head, like a little tornado, and music starts. Uh-oh.

beats.headline: Minion Army, at last
beats.text: We got the Minion Army book on the very first floor, and I have never cast it, because it freezes you for minutes and it is meant for wars. With my Charisma I can select the entire mob out there and some of the birds, and it only takes four minutes. Imani and Samantha enhance it. I glow like a star and cannot move while the slugs charge early and a bicycle smashes straight through me. When it casts, Elle has hailed on nearly everything. Elle, you stole my experience! Then the birds I charmed start fighting each other, and I am getting experience after all.

beats.headline: I did not do that
beats.text: Elle's hail comes down at level sixteen and Carl asks if I did that. I am glowing. I am stronger too, and I did not do it. I hear myself talking while I spin: Elle is earth and water, the four seasons path, it's the tree, he's opening a path through the river and the tree, it's good she's not fire yet, gotta kill her, no, not Elle, her mother, no, not her mother. Then I stop. What just happened? Carl, did you roofie me again? And you need to stop gaslighting me.

beats.headline: Asleep in the hallway
beats.text: Sister Ines Quiteria comes down the thirty-second floor hallway at full tilt, glowing, screaming "Sinner!" Crawler Carl's Nighty-Night wand puts her out before she reaches him, and she slides to a stop at his feet with a two-minute timer over her head. Crawler Louis volunteers, since he already carries five player killer skulls and the others carry none. He apologises to her and puts a dagger into her chest. The Reaper of Havana is dead. A god's marked-for-death symbol appears over Crawler Louis.

beats.headline: Filed as Pox Slugs, and unbothered by it
beats.text: The System first registers them as Pox Slugs, which is accurate and entirely misses the point. They come out of the boils of the SlugPox, they arrive with a crude and rowdy culture already assembled, and they throw themselves at the demons with the enthusiasm of people who cannot believe their luck at being included.

beats.headline: Her nun goes down, and she arrives
beats.text: Thirty-second floor of the FOCSA building. Crawler Carl puts Sister Ines out with the Nighty-Night wand and Crawler Louis finishes the job. Sister Ines had a patron, and her patron is Ysalte, and Ysalte comes into the realm about it in a temper that registers on my instruments. Crawler Louis is marked for death. So much for nobody being able to arrive without us knowing.

beats.headline: Out of the snake, still hers
beats.text: The ceiling of their hallway collapses around my coils, and the automaton lands on me, and I am teleported out of the Madre de Aguas. In the open air I take my true form, four feet in the street, chest level with their new roof. The marker over my head still says Enslaved. The quest they are handed calls Ysalte my former girlfriend and the mother of my child, and says she has seized me as I once seized her. She means to take me to the Ascendency as her retainer. I am given six totems, and I will not begin to flee until every one of them is dead.

beats.headline: The Missing Piece, and eight cards
beats.text: The first quest completes and a new one replaces it, with a ten-minute timer. Ysalte has hold of Amayon. If she still holds him when the timer runs out, they both go to the Ascendency, and everyone without a key is dead. To break free he has to start casting his spell home, and the stronger he is, the bigger that spell has to be. At full power it covers the world. Then, since this is the eighth floor, four cards clank into place in front of the goddess and four the size of garage doors in front of the demon. Really? Really.

beats.headline: Pontifex Shine's goddess
beats.text: Goddess of Hopelessness and Insanity Ysalte, level two hundred and fifty, arrives with her paperwork attached: this goddess is sponsored by Pontifex Shine of the Nebular Balance. The sponsor is not currently inside the shell, so she speaks and acts according to her regular nature, which, the warning adds, is bad news. The Nebulars have paid for a god and are not driving it.

beats.headline: Ysalte, honey, it has been ages
beats.text: Ysalte! Honey! It has been SO long! I invite her to my bachelorette party and ask after the child. Meanwhile I tell Louis in capitals to run before this bitch melts his beautiful ass into oatmeal. She calls me Psamathe and wants to know how I dare show myself after what I did. What did I do? The reverse hedgehog? That was ages ago, everyone at the party thought it was funny, except the hedgehog, and her. It isn't my fault she can't take a joke about how ugly her child is. She swings a pickaxe at my face. It bounces off.

beats.headline: Her eyes stay open
beats.text: A goddess enters the realm, and the patch on Carl's jacket responds: the Scavenger's Daughter's eyes remain open, and she fills with even more power. The same notification brings Ysalte's own contribution, a temporary effect that turns any potion quaffed or handled outside an inventory into vinegar. It also promises the potions will come back as more powerful versions of themselves once she is banished.

beats.headline: Nobody is driving
beats.text: The readout on this one is worse than the goddess. She is sponsored, but the sponsor is not inhabiting her, which means she speaks and acts as herself with nothing between her and the room. She is invulnerable. She takes hold of Amayon while the building comes down around him, and when a teleport trap shakes him loose of the snake body it does not shake him loose of her. The Missing Piece quest opens on the back of it: free the demon, get him casting, and survive her totems for the ten minutes before she is back. She cannot be killed. That is not encouragement, it is a specification.

beats.headline: A Kombucha! achievement
beats.text: A succubus hits me with the force of a bus and we slide past Katia and Donut, nearly into the stair hole. She goes for my neck with vampire fangs just as my new tech shield comes up, and her teeth shatter like crockery. Without thinking, I click a healing potion in my inventory. A terrible taste floods my mouth. A Kombucha! achievement. Ysalte's debuff turned it to vinegar, and normally potions taste like nothing. I cast Heal instead. She has me pinned and is slamming me into the floor.

beats.headline: Leveled-Up, Sober Edition
beats.text: The goddess plays a Raid Stash, and five cards come flying out of five decks. One of them is the only inactive totem the cat was carrying, and that's me. Leveled-Up Frank, Sober Edition, a level 100 night elf blood assassin, landing on a roof that is coming apart underneath all of us, folks. And there's the young man. Hello, Carl. Fancy seeing you here. Where's your ring? The cat sends her tentacle cloud at me, and I pull the red sword off my shoulder.

beats.headline: The Thief, then Force Discard
beats.text: Carl asks if I have got this. I am the current reigning champion Persian in the galaxy, and a warlord, so yes, Carl. I play The Thief on the demon as he summons, and one of his cards flies into my hand: Banjo, a Hell Scrub, the tentacle cloud that drags a succubus off Carl. Then the demon has one card left and cannot play it, because the goddess will not let his claw move. She knows he is free to cast once he is empty. So I play Force Discard, and his last card goes poof. Suck it.

beats.headline: The wheelchair goes off
beats.text: The roof gives out under us and I fall down to a different level. The wheelchair is sparking. I'm stuck in it and it's going to blow. Louis and Britney keep running, because the monk seal is after Louis. The rock monster the demon summoned first, the one that crashed through the ceiling, is down here too. The wheelchair blows a hole in its chest. That was the last of his totems. I need a healer.

beats.headline: A crab, a beach, and a deadline
beats.text: I jump off the building and catch Samantha, and she slows us to the ground. I run between the demon's legs, and she flies me to the beach. Donut plays Midnight Express, one of the two consumable cards Ren left me, and for three minutes I'm the deckmaster. I summon Raul the crab and tell him to fertilize the eggs. The AI counted crab sperm as mobs, and that's what broke Sheol, so it has to be a crab. He can't perform without baby seals. There's a pile of dead ones. I summon Alpha Carl to beat me half to death, and he offers a hug instead. Then he yells at Raul, and it works.

beats.headline: The same flavour of chowder
beats.text: The Missing Piece quest updates mid-battle: the eviction that brought Amayon here is his undoing: now in his true form, he lacks the power to cast his spell home, and the dying world has too few souls left to trigger it. The fix it hints at is to refill the world with the same type of souls that set the whole thing off. The same flavour of chowder, it says. The announcers had it that the eviction began because the AI counted crab sperm as a mob, so the answer is a crab, a beach full of corpses, and the eggs still out in the water.

beats.headline: Out of cards, and going for the goddess
beats.text: The goddess summons a strange version of Paz, and I put him in a shield jail, where he will probably time out. Then Annie is down, and I am out of cards. I cannot hurt Ysalte. Nobody can, on this floor. The quest does not require it. It only requires that she be kept busy until the timer runs out and the demon is cast free of her. So I tell Daniel to come to me. I am going to try to stop the goddess.

beats.headline: Why Are You Hitting Yourself
beats.text: The Satan demon guy will not listen to me. He is going to cast a different spell, and he and the vinegar lady are yelling at each other; I think they might actually be in love. She is almost out of cards, and Carl is on a beach with a crab. Samantha and I are going to have to do something drastic. So I cast Why Are You Hitting Yourself on him, and he punches himself in the face, twice. Samantha says that might have been a mistake. She thinks he is big mad.

beats.headline: A question from Emberus
beats.text: The man stands in my palm and says he carries a question from Emberus, about his son. The doll supplies the name: Geyrun, murdered. I laugh. I know exactly what happened; I witnessed the deal being signed, and if Emberus helps me kill my three brothers, I will tell him. The man says he gave me the strength and the souls, and asks me to call off my demons in exchange for carrying my message. But he also helped slay Ysalte, the mother of my child, so we are even. Speaking to him delivered the message. I turn my hand over and let them fall toward the fire.

beats.headline: Into a goddess's eye
beats.text: Ysalte stands in the corpse of Sister Ines, summoned for a boss event and invulnerable on this floor. Donut's all-caps report tells the rest. Katia gave a crawler an arrow thing, and he stuck it into the goddess's eye. Then he blew himself up, the explosion concentrated on her neck, and her head fell off. The system message names him as her slayer, marked for death by every deity except her sworn enemies. He was her own totem.

beats.headline: Too late by two percent
beats.text: I teleport into the trap I left inside Samantha and land headfirst in her neck hole, with the rest of me somewhere burning. The Martyr's Path wants me under five percent. My hair burns away. The timer ends and I'm at seven. I've failed. Then a button appears, I hit it, and fire bursts up along every step I've taken outside, the Scavenger's Daughter enhancing it. I drop to two percent. The quest completes anyway. The timer stopped with two seconds left, and not because of me. Paz has killed the goddess.

beats.headline: A deal, and a witness
beats.text: Asked on behalf of Emberus what became of the god's son, Amayon, prince of Sheol, answers that he knows exactly what happened to the child and that he was witness to the deal being signed. Samantha has already supplied the name, Geyrun, and the word murdered. Amayon's price for the rest is help killing his three brothers, and he considers that speaking the offer aloud has delivered it to Emberus already.

beats.headline: A box for outliving her
beats.text: Dude. Okay so, everyone's in the chat yelling, and the decks are still out because demons are everywhere, and I just got a Celestial box. For outliving a goddess. One who put a marked-for-death curse on me. No joke. Then Donut tells everybody to stop talking, because nobody can find Carl.

beats.headline: One for a goddess
beats.text: When Ysalte falls, the world notifications include a Memorial Crystal generated for her, to be available for looting on a future floor, with great riches promised to whoever finds it. The same run of notifications marks her killer for death by every deity except her sworn enemies, and inflicts the Despondent debuff permanently on all of her worshippers.

beats.headline: He kills a goddess
beats.text: System message: Crawler Paz Lo has slain the goddess Ysalte, and is marked for death by every deity except her sworn enemies. Princess Donut's account, sent in capitals: the goddess had summoned a warped version of him and Katia had penned him in a shield. Then Katia gave him an arrow, he stuck it into the goddess's eye and blew himself up, with the blast concentrated on her neck, and her head came off. He vanished when she fell. The credit went to him regardless.

beats.headline: Its fire, released by a benefit
beats.text: Carl burns his own health down inside Samantha's acidic neck, too slowly to beat the timer. It goes on dropping afterwards, and once he is under five percent his Martyr's Path benefit engulfs every step he has taken outside in flame, and with his fire still enhanced, that flame is Sheol fire. The realm's fire is a resource now, one a crawler can spend without ever having gone there.

beats.headline: Put down by one of her own totems
beats.text: Goddess of Hopelessness and Insanity Ysalte has been removed from this realm by a totem raised from the former crawler Paz. Her own quest furniture, turned around and used on her. Part One of The Missing Piece completes. Elsewhere in the same collapse Crawler Carl rides his health down to two percent on purpose to set fire to every street he had walked on, which tells you what kind of afternoon this was for everybody.

beats.headline: Lazarus is pulled under
beats.text: Lazarus, the card built from Asojano and Uzi Jesus, had been fused with Skylar Spinach by a Golden Combo and made permanent with Glow Up, Tserendolgor's other consumable card, and was a candidate for the single card Princess Donut may carry down. High in the burning building he trembles with rage at the sight of Amayon, and Crawler Carl stops his RPG. He complains that they are all pansies. Then a demon crab comes through a wall, grabs him, and both vanish into Sheol. Totem Eliminated.

beats.headline: I won't leave Tran
beats.text: Tran and I are trapped in a pocket of debris, and the demons are in here with us now. I am holding them off the best I can. Elle asks if I have cards left, a Flee card. Tran is on Katia's squad, so only her Flee card could take him, and she doesn't carry them, and she is out of cards anyway. So I won't leave Tran. And I don't trust my last totems. They are digging toward us from above.

beats.headline: The next available minion
beats.text: The cat plays me beside the big friendly Alpha Carl and throws down a Golden Combo to stitch us together. I am too tall for the hallway; most of me hangs outside the building. Alpha Carl turns to say something to the man, and I put one of my legs through the back of his head first. The card, finding its intended target incapacitated, proceeds to the next available minion. That is the man. So now we are combined, he and I.

beats.headline: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride
beats.text: Shi Maria has my body. I can hear her rooting through my inventory. Another voice, a man's, tells me to hold on; it says she killed him, and now he's here. She calls it a lie. Then my body burns Mongo and Katia, and puts out Li Jun's eye and eats it, and I can't stop my own hands. Don't trust her, boy, the voice says. Then I time out, and there's an eye tattooed over my sternum. It blinks, closes, and disappears into my skin. Tattoo. The Eye of the Bedlam Bride. That's all it says. How's Katia? How's Mongo?

beats.headline: Found by a passenger
beats.text: Shi Maria has hold of Crawler Carl from the inside, and she goes through his inventory the way a burglar goes through drawers. So many things, she says. So many possibilities. Then she stops on one. Kimaris? You have a summoning totem of Kimaris? Does Samantha know this? She moves on to the war mage head and the potions without waiting for an answer, and Carl cannot give one.

beats.headline: Down the chain to Carl
beats.text: My sister shoots a chain down through the burning floor, and I slide down it and land in front of Carl. He has a spider's body under him and he is not talking like Carl. I ask him what I can do. He takes a stick out of a tattoo kit and puts it into my eye. Then he eats my eye. I am on the floor in the corner with my hand over my face, and my sister is between us. He tells her not to heal me. Then he drops a gold standard healing potion on the floor, and says it is for me.

beats.headline: Something he cannot discard
beats.text: Inside the man there is so much storage. A book he should not have. A bomb, ready. He meant to leave me on this floor; I see that too. A summoning totem of Kimaris. A beaker, a sliver of root. I warn his friends back and set him alight, and the cat's animal and the doppelganger are burned. Now the beaker holds ink. His friend comes too close, so I take his eye. Then I tattoo myself into the man's chest. I am no longer a card he can rip. Keep me and gain my power, or set me free. Either way, I win.

beats.headline: A timer on a global teleport
beats.text: Their quest, the Missing Piece, updates. Succeeded, it says. And beneath the word, a timer, one for each region, counting down to the moment my spell goes off there. A global teleport. When it lands, the walls of their stairwell chambers will be sucked away, and anyone crouched beneath them pulled upward into the stairwell. They wanted me casting. They have their wish. Home is the direction I am going in any case, and I have never minded company on the road.

beats.headline: Someone to make proud
beats.text: The eighth floor is stripped into the sky with Crawler Carl inside it, and what he thinks of, looking down on the memories of people who do not know how few days they have, is Asher, the brother he never knew. He needs to make the boy proud. He was not there for him while he lived. He means for the boy's death not to be for nothing.

beats.headline: Reusable, if unbroken
beats.text: Carl thinks Katia should have had the credit for the goddess, since it took her bolt to do it. Katia is glad she did not: every god is angry at the one who did. Then she pulls it out of her inventory. Funny thing about magical bolts, she says: as long as they don't break, you can reuse them. Carl grins back. The princess meant it for her brother inside Grull, and that possibility is still on the table.

beats.headline: Thirty-three thousand eight hundred and four
beats.text: Mordecai has turned the counter back on. The day this floor opened, 38,532 of us had made it here. It reads 33,804. Almost five thousand dead, and in any normal world a tragedy. But they built this floor for a slaughter and we found a way out of it. We're hitting the ninth floor not scattered, not broken and not afraid. Then the viewers vote the sponsors' protections away, ninety-eight percent, and I yell at the ceiling. You wanted a slaughter? It's coming. Your own citizens voted for it. There will be no quarter.

beats.headline: The audience decides
beats.text: About to be pulled into a stairwell and out of contact, Carl and Donut spend an emergency action item to hand every unresolved vote to the viewers. The viewers strip the safety protections from the faction sponsors, seat the tenth team, loosen the physics on long-range artillery and raise the ceiling over the field. The crawlers who will meet it are coming down in unprecedented numbers.

beats.headline: Thank you for not giving up on me
beats.text: We stand in the tunnel under the X that Chris painted on the ceiling, the three of us, with three minutes left. I wrap Carl and Donut in my wings. None of us is getting out of this unscathed. We gain things, and we lose them. That is what happens in war. I thank them for not giving up on me. Carl says we don't give up on family, or what's the point. Then I put my arms around him too, and my head on his shoulder, and I cry quietly, with my skulls glowing over my head in the dark.

beats.headline: A bolt, reusable
beats.text: Carl says I should have had the credit for the goddess, since it was my Bolt of Ophiotaurus Paz drove into her eye. I am glad I did not get it. Every god is angry with him now. And magical bolts, as long as they do not break, can be used again; I show him. Princess Formidable gave it to me on the fourth floor to use on her brother, and that is still on the table. I did not get to loot the goddess. Her equipment went to Paz. I grew my arm back. It was nothing.

beats.headline: Home Team, based in Larracos
beats.text: One of the viewers' votes seats a tenth team, populated with NPCs and given the same protections as the other nine. It is designated Home Team, its base is the city of Larracos, and peace rules apply there effectively immediately, until the game starts. Its co-warlords are the NPCs Juice Box and Sir Ferdinand. An adjutant is to be assigned before the battles begin. It passes by fifty-two percent.

beats.headline: Awake, and a wing gone
beats.text: WING GONE. Burns. MOTHER rides. Running. Fire. CARL AWAKE. CARL SAYS SORRY. Push head into CARL. GOOD.

beats.headline: Ripped at the collapse
beats.text: The card has changed. Paz Lo. The God Predator. Level 101 Former Crawler. The goddess's equipment went to him and upgraded his armour. Princess Donut holds the card in the backup slot. Katia says rip it; that is what he wanted. Donut wonders whether to keep it past the collapse instead, since a squad may keep one card, in case there is a way to set him free. Crawler Carl remembers what Paz said when he was last summoned, and says no. Donut tears it with her teeth against Carl's shoulder. It goes in a puff of smoke. "Goodbye, Paz."

beats.headline: Two cards, ripped
beats.text: Carl is bald and has no eyebrows, which I will not have in a sidekick. And the moment the battle ended I ripped Shi Maria's card. She will never hurt Mongo again. Then there is Paz, whom Katia let me take after the goddess died. His card says God Predator now, and it calls him a former crawler. I wanted to keep him and find a way to set him free, but Carl says no, it was never right to make him into a card. So I put one corner in my mouth and rip. Just like that. I do not get a player killer skull.

beats.headline: Voted away
beats.text: The viewers take the safety protections off the faction sponsors. Every one of them who sets foot on the ninth floor now stands to lose exactly what the crawlers stand to lose.

beats.headline: We need to break up
beats.text: Carl. We need to break up. I have been thinking about it, and I have decided to go back to my king. He says okay. I hope we can stay friends. Then I growl at Louis, obviously, and go. At the church I remind Carl he is bringing MaeMae to the next floor, because she knows where the guy with my body is. He says not to worry about that. He knows where to go.

beats.headline: Power left to linger
beats.text: Since the fight in the building, the bar in Carl's interface has crackled with black energy: the Scavenger's Daughter has been fed, and wants her wrath unleashed. He does not unleash it.
