At the last moment Princess Donut sees the jacket glowing, and says the patch is not an aardvark but a giant centipede crawling through the skulls. A voice in Carl's mind says he should never have let the soul power linger. It needs him alive, and reasonably sane. He had forgotten to activate the Daughter's Kiss.

beats.headline: One card to keep
beats.text: Each surviving squad may keep a single card past the collapse. Princess Donut had meant it to be Lazarus or the Golden Combo, and now offers a third: a card of Paz, in case there is a way to set him free. Crawler Carl remembers what Paz said the last time he was summoned. Not that one, and not the Golden Combo either. The Paz card is ripped in half on his shoulder.

beats.headline: Five summonings, not fifteen
beats.text: A line of pending action items is decided all at once, most of them about building materials, mercenary cost limits and advertising revenue, which Crawler Carl and Crawler Donut had voted against down the line just to be obstinate. Among them, one originally proposed by the Madness: Celestial Summoning events to be limited to five per team. It is rejected by a thirty-seven percent audience vote. The existing rule of fifteen per team remains.

beats.headline: Agent number 22, in Wenatchee
beats.text: On the night of the collapse, a flash message: Borant is starting the Earth season early. In an alley in Wenatchee, behind Meadowlark Elder Care, an old woman in a failing human shell reads it twice. Agent 22, also known as Agatha. Ten years peeled away from her collective. Not of the Apothecary, though she took a residual's body to read its feed; not Valtay, though biologically similar. Her people want the primal to know who it really is, and she would sweep the universe clean of biological life. She lights a fire in a barrel, to bring an entrance near. Timing is everything.

beats.headline: A mantra with mistakes in it
beats.text: Agatha's feed carries the Apothecary's chatter as well as her own team's. Thousands of its agents are seeded across the planet, ordered to kill themselves if they miss the dungeon. This season they mean to contact crawlers directly, in the dungeon or on the floor with the memory ghosts, and for months they have made their agents recite a daily mantra full of known inaccuracies and half-truths. The errors are there to keep the crawler alive around the showrunners. What the mantra really does is secretly implant a hidden upgrade.

beats.headline: Two promises from Doctor Hu
beats.text: Doctor Hu predicted all of it: that the crawler would talk the AI into turning off the safety protections, and how the council would respond. He sought out the crew of a converted Long Haul garbage freighter, now renamed Homecoming Queen, and told them first that he could promise only two things, and the first was eventual death. Hidden inside it are fifty thousand former crawlers, cleared by the AI for on-boarding as troopers for Carl and Donut's team.

beats.headline: Muted for proposing the failsafe
beats.text: Emergency session of the Syndicate Council. Subject, on the line from the cockpit of her cruiser in orbit, demands the failsafe: blow the star and wipe the system off the map before the AI infects the center system. Accused of wanting her father and brothers dead, she points out that she is in orbit and would die too. She would love her family deposed, she says, but this is bigger than that. The mantid representative proposes a decorum sanction. It passes at 86 percent, and she is muted.

beats.headline: Fifty thousand troopers, coming home
beats.text: I watch the news while my crewmate replays Carl and the cat getting sucked up into the sky. Is he smart, or has he been outrageously lucky? I still can't tell. I think he's kind of dumb. It took an NPC to show him how to use the ink to share powers. And the AI likes his feet, which is bizarre; my season it was passionless. We sent the cat that Celestial box. Then we are cleared for on-boarding, fifty thousand former crawlers cheer through the hull, and we are coming home.

beats.headline: Muted for proposing the failsafe
beats.text: At an emergency session of the Syndicate Council, Princess Formidable of the Skull Empire demands the failsafe: blow the star and wipe the system off the map, before the AI can infect the center system. She is in orbit herself, and says so. Accused of wanting her father and brothers dead, she admits she would love them deposed, and insists that this is bigger. Prime Minister Glory counts the galaxy's wealth trapped in the system and the wars it would start. The mantid representative proposes a decorum sanction. By 86%, she is muted.

beats.headline: Threats over a lost vote
beats.text: The loss of the sponsors' protections does not go quietly. The Dream's cruiser threatens to nuke the planet over it, and is hobbled by a Syndicate Peacekeeper before it can. The Dream then threatens to stop food production unless the Epitome family is evacuated. They can scream and threaten all they want. Aboard a converted garbage freighter, the view is that once these AIs realise how much control they really have, the only thing stopping them is reason, and negotiation.

beats.headline: May the Eulogist ever sleep
beats.text: Agatha's correspondents sign off the way her kind do: may the Eulogist ever sleep. Her plan, as she lays it out to herself, is to last long enough for the infant, resurrected and enslaved Primal to learn what it is before everything is stolen from it, so that it escapes and frees the Eulogist to return to its slumber. Last time, she thinks, they allowed life to continue in the universe, and look what happened. This time she would sweep the universe clean of biological life.

beats.headline: Spells too horrific for the crawl
beats.text: Rosetta has a news channel on, covering the court appeals over the sudden change in the rules of Faction Wars and an emergency meeting of the Syndicate Council. On screen, a representative for the Madness declares that if their lives are truly going to be on the line, they are going to be forced to use some of their illegal spells, the ones deemed too horrific for the crawl. Tipid, watching beside her, shudders.

beats.headline: The Valtay solution
beats.text: The Valtay representative, a worm in the body that once belonged to the Syndicate Prime Minister's mother, assures the council all is perfectly normal. The solution the council backs is theirs: an extinction event, as fast as possible, because the quarantine lifts when the last crawler dies. Their mercenary guilds are recalled off Earth's surface, and the AI has agreed to let tens of thousands of fully armed mercenaries and the sponsors' private armies into the coming war, spread equally among the eight sponsored teams. Well over 150,000. The goal is every crawler, Carl and the cat first.

beats.headline: First word in the Warlord Chat
beats.text: Warlords. One of you should proceed immediately to the flag room, beside the throne room in your stronghold outside the city, to oversee the final preparations and deal with the recruits arriving there. The other should remain in Larracos and enlist your fellow crawlers. The rule behind the advice: once the ceasefire ends, any crawler not already recruited may be compelled into another army as a conscript. Time is short.

beats.headline: He takes command of one of nine armies
beats.text: Thirty days. A castle at Larracos, dead centre of the map. No coming back from a death on this floor, for anyone. Supply, alliances, atrocity, at a scale where the arithmetic stops being about people I know.

beats.headline: Paulie's real message
beats.text: Christmas morning in the shelter, replayed as a memory. The world freezes, a spoon hangs in midair, and Paulie keeps talking without moving his lips. The crawl is unnecessary, he says: it harvests an element grown inside everyone born on a seeded world, for money. His coffee holds an illegal enhancement. I drink it off my finger and put the cup back on its circle. It gives me a Containment Interface that can trip a fuse and turn the sun nova, killing everybody, the AI included. Then the Paulie part of him speaks: be sure it's your only option. It is still installing.

beats.headline: Coffee, with a finger
beats.text: Christmas morning, in a shelter, in memory. Time stops, and Paulie delivers his real message. His coffee holds a neural enhancement: Crawler Carl pushes a finger into the frozen cup and drinks. It gives access to the AI containment, and upon it to what the Mantids call the fuse, a failsafe that trips when five or six conditions are met and sends the star at the centre of the system nova. The controller lets Carl pop it himself. He dies; so does everyone. It only works in a natural interface, and the AI, says Paulie, wants it done.

beats.headline: Paulie's own opinion
beats.text: That was the pitch, Paulie says, the one he gives every day. Then the Paulie part of him speaks. Popping the fuse would disrupt the crawl for seasons, kill system leaders, and put the Mantids under a microscope. But the human in him hates wasting so many innocent lives, and direct action against the true culprits would be better. If you make this decision, be sure. It is more than a failsafe. It is the end of everything. Then a notice: Containment Interface is currently installing. A notification comes when the handshake is complete.

beats.headline: Due before anyone descends
beats.text: The Blood Sultanate fights on the ninth floor, and neither Donut nor Katia may descend to the tenth until the Sultan and his family are dead.

beats.headline: The Sultanate is on this floor
beats.text: The stairs to the tenth do not open for a royal who has not killed the Sultan and the rest of the family.

beats.headline: Tundra Princess to Hailstorm Queen
beats.text: Class selection again, in the warehouse, with only a few of us this time. I pick wind, and Tundra Princess becomes Hailstorm Queen. Donut is thrilled I'm a queen. This is probably as far as it goes: I can add the final element if I ever make it to the twelfth floor, but I'm betting this whole shitshow self-destructs before we get anywhere close.

beats.headline: The rules, read out on arrival
beats.text: Ten teams. Nine attacking, spread around the city like slices of a pie, and the NPCs defending it from inside. Take the castle at the centre. Sixty hours of ceasefire first, in which a crawler may enlist with any army that will have them or run for the woods, and after which anyone still loose can be compelled into a uniform. Two hundred and ninety-three stairwell chambers sit seeded across the floor, and not one opens until Faction Wars is won or thirty hours remain on the clock.

beats.headline: Ferdinand and his Bird
beats.text: Warlord Donut accepts Team Retribution's truce offer while her co-warlord is still in the middle of a sentence urging her to wait, and names the truce The Good Guys. Warlord Ferdinand of Team Retribution renames it Ferdinand and his Bird. The system does not let her change it back. The alliance itself stands: allied with the defenders, her crawlers will not be removed from Larracos when the ceasefire ends.

beats.headline: The crawl arrives inside it
beats.text: Crawlers come down into Larracos at the start of a sixty-hour ceasefire. The armies that have spent eight floors drilling and drinking are allowed to fight one another at last, and the thing they are fighting over is underfoot: the castle at the bottom of the well.

beats.headline: Thirty days, ten teams, one castle
beats.text: Thirty days to collapse, or ninety hours once a winner is declared. Ten teams, nine attacking and the NPCs of Team Retribution defending, fight to capture the castle at Larracos in the centre of the map. 32,429 crawlers are left.

beats.headline: They organise
beats.text: Faction Wars has ten teams now, and one of them is the NPCs: Team Retribution, the defenders, headquartered in Larracos and led by Juice Box, whom the system made a warlord to stop her killing everybody.

beats.headline: A truce with the Bone Clan
beats.text: The floor opens, and the warnings arrive. Among them: the Bone Clan has announced a formal truce with the Operatic Collective. Quasar, fixing pipes with his niece Tempest, has already summed up the stakes. All the rich fuckers on the floor, Prince Stalwart the orc, that banker Operatic guy, Epitome Tagg from the Dream, can really die now. It is going to be, in his words, an epic shitshow.

beats.headline: He picks game guide
beats.text: Subject sits in a zero zone at the start of the eleventh floor, still bloody, one arm shaking, facing an attorney who has brought snacks. His party was twenty strong at the end of the ninth. As far as he knows he is the last of it: he ran when she begged him to, and left behind a friend whose foot was stuck. He declines fifteen seasons as low-floor undead and thirty as a city attendant, and takes game guide, one hundred seasons. He survived the indentureship. Current status: missing, and wanted by Syndicate Security.

beats.headline: A grain of sand in every brain
beats.text: Paulie's frozen-time message puts the mechanism plainly. Everything born on a pre-seeded world carries a miniature primal system in its brain, the size of a grain of sand. Left alone, it fills over a lifetime and returns to the planet's system at death, and a healthy system neither grows nor shrinks. The crawl switches them on and harvests them early. The take fits on a single ship and feeds the center system, which expands and keeps its citizens living unnaturally long. Stopping would starve it only slowly, over generations. It continues because the spectacle makes money.

beats.headline: The crown comes due
beats.text: The Blood Sultanate is on this floor, and every royal in the line must slay the Sultan and all the other members of the royal family before descending to the tenth. I am a royal in the line. I have been since the first floor. I would like it noted that I was told to read the description.

beats.headline: She becomes a Deathbed Hellcat
beats.text: Thirty seconds to pick a card, and a whole new class, while I am covered in mud. Mordecai says nothing deity-themed, so the Consecrated Enchantress goes, sash and all, and I would never be a Halloween Aficionado. I pick Deathbed Hellcat: a long-range sniper and assassin. The range on every spell I have is quadrupled, my dexterity is much higher, my odds of an instakill are better, I can go invisible at will, and I keep most of my spells. It comes with a hat. And a ghoulie suit, whatever that is. I just love this for me right now.

beats.headline: A recap for a school report
beats.text: My niece Tempest needs a recap of my client's eighth floor for school. Terms: she fixes my sink. The recap: my client killed Quan Ch for his key. The dog girl with the flamethrower died, and he now has the flamethrower and the pet. On the ninth, neither Donut nor Katia can leave until every naga is dead, and even then only one of them can. With the recorder off, she asks whether representing him puts me in danger. I tell her the truth. I think we all are.

beats.headline: Soul poisoning, and a dead shark
beats.text: The soul energy Carl never spent at the end of the last floor is still riding in the back patch, and it comes due on arrival as Soul Poisoning: jolts of pain, partly blocked by his Emberus ring, with worse effects promised. Saferoom rules cover the city for sixty hours, so nothing alive can be hurt. He finds something dead instead, tosses a suffocated concierge shark into the air and punches it with Daughter's Kiss. The shark vaporises, Carl and Donut are blown back through the mud, and the AI makes up an achievement on the spot: Sushi Smoothie.

beats.headline: An exception in the fine print
beats.text: The warning about the ceasefire is mostly bad news. When it expires, only members of the defending team may remain within the city of Larracos, and that restriction holds until certain conditions are met. Then one line more: the restriction does not apply to the Shanty Town ring. Ten teams remain, and every one of them has just been told there is a ring around the city where they are allowed to stand.

beats.headline: The defending team names itself
beats.text: Carl and Donut come onto the ninth floor at Larracos, at the start of a sixty-hour ceasefire, and the defending side already has a name it chose for itself. Cascadia runs through the rules. The crawlers ally with it against the Bloc, which is every other faction on the board.

beats.headline: They buy a storyline instead of fighting for one
beats.text: Quasar has the warning ready before the sixty-hour ceasefire is out. The Dream have bought out the Vengeance of the Daughter and are pressing for fulfilment of the guaranteed third season written into it. An entertainment company, bought and aimed at a crawler.

beats.headline: One of those Eulogist pricks
beats.text: The coffee Paulie gives Crawler Carl carries a neural enhancement for the interface in his brain: a new menu, unregistered and highly illegal, that takes a little time to install. It works only with natural interfaces, only with the permission of the existing system, and only in this system's enhancement zone. If you are a Syndicate spy, a plant, or, in Paulie's words, one of those Eulogist pricks, it does not work at all. Carl drinks it.

beats.headline: Sold, with a season still owed
beats.text: Quasar warns Carl on arrival that the Dream has bought the programme out and intends to collect on the guaranteed third season.

beats.headline: Fifty achievements, and a groan
beats.text: Over fifty achievements to open. Most are stupid: Kombucha, for drinking vinegar. Chickenshit Exploit calls Ren a cheater, for the card totems I teleported into her fight with Quan. She never was one. Touched by a Demon: only one ever handed out, and it's mine, with a Celestial box. Then Unbirthing, for teleporting into Samantha's neck hole, in the AI's deep, throaty voice. It groans. It says it really liked that, and that I am in trouble. Reward: a Legendary Spicy Box.

beats.headline: Permission to break the truce
beats.text: Amayon, Prince of Sheol, claims to know what happened to my son, and he offers it in exchange for the deaths of his three brothers. The gods and the demons have a truce. I do not wish to break it, and I will do what is necessary to learn the truth. There is a way to do it without a war that burns the mortal world to ashes. My martyr will go to the Temple of Issitoq in a Club Vanquisher and gain permission from the High Cleric of the Watch. He still owes me the Soul Crystal of Apito. Do not disappoint me now.

beats.headline: A Canadian, with a better table
beats.text: I walk out of the crafting room in a snowsuit and a raccoon hat, and the two of them laugh at me. I don't pick the clothes. Human this time, Canadian, glasses. The table is upgraded higher than I have ever had it, and for the first time I can examine a potion and see how it was made. So, listen. Nobody reads a spellbook until we talk. Quan's cloak needs a plan before Donut puts it on. And the ceasefire can end early three ways. All unlikely. You never know.

beats.headline: Used Pet, and Janet Dominguez
beats.text: New achievement: Used Pet. Do you know how many animals were in cages during the collection? Fuck you, Janet Dominguez in Baton Rouge. Sprinkles was better off at the no-kill shelter. I really need to stop watching these memory recordings. Err, anyway. Terry, the dog who played Toto, was paid more than most of the cast. Used pets have value, and sometimes it isn't monetary. Sometimes they're delicious. You have adopted a pet that was once bonded to someone else. Reward: a Gold Pet Box.

beats.headline: A second pillow
beats.text: A platinum benefactor box arrives for Donut from the Apothecary in the same sitting as the tiara, and it holds a second charging pillow, purple where the first is red. The same ten-hour drain, and the same ruin after one hour. The difference is at the end of the description: this one drains any magical item, but transfers only to an absorption crystal on a like item. A ring's buff goes to a ring; sent to the wrong kind of item, the buff is lost. With two pillows, the tiara fills twice as fast.

beats.headline: A potion smashed on his rump
beats.text: WING GONE. Mongo looks. Wing GONE? Mother says sit. Carl smashes glass on Mongo's butt. Sparkly. Healing. Mongo does not mind.

beats.headline: A potion called MySpace Photo
beats.text: Mordecai hands me a potion that used to be called Charisma Cheat and is now called MySpace Photo, which is rude. I learn Shield, then I drink it. For two minutes it makes the system think my charisma is 193 instead of 163, and in those two minutes I put on the champion's shawl, so my constitution rises to 193 over the next few days. From two. I get a very rude Catfish achievement. The cloak takes Bad Attitude straight to level 15, and Wall of Fire, Heal Critter and Puddle Jumper are on their way. I was hoping for Fireball.

beats.headline: Donut wears his cloak
beats.text: Inventory update, ninth floor. Crawler Princess Donut opens a celestial box from Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions and takes out the Tiara of a Thousand Lights. In the same sitting she puts on Quan Ch's cloak and takes the benefits that come with it. The cloak does not ask where its previous owner is, and neither do I.

beats.headline: Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions
beats.text: Donut's celestial box from the sponsor holds it. She puts on Quan Ch's cloak in the same stretch and wears the two together, though nothing is charged into the tiara yet.

beats.headline: Walk on Air, already obtained
beats.text: A Legendary toe ring, left pinky toe, and the description is insistent about the toe. Heart Balance holds a potion to fire automatically. Mind Balance protects against Enslavement and Conscription. Physical Balance lists Walk on Air as already obtained. I don't have Walk on Air. Li Jun does. I remember the taste of his eye, and what Shi Maria said about gaining his skills. I message him to apologise. He doesn't answer. I put the ring on anyway, set a gold healing potion to trigger at 2% health, and get one notice: Mind Balance is currently triggered.

beats.headline: Carrying Tran, chasing a head
beats.text: We're at the college in Larracos, filling out visitor passes and dealing with guards who are sluggish under a Despondent debuff, trying to reach a saferoom. Tran's wheelchair is gone, so we carry him, and it slows everything down. Then Samantha rolls past, screaming that she's going to kill a woman named Tish, and I go after her before the guards react. She's rolling, not floating, and she's fast. I get her trapped in a corner. She's really mad. I bring her back through the safe room.

beats.headline: Seriously scary bastards
beats.text: The skill potion comes back from my table, and I was wrong: I can make these. A few more table upgrades and some very specialised ingredients. Drink it now, I tell Carl, and train with whatever it gives you. Gloom Wraith Phase, level 13. So I say it straight. You two have always been powerful for your levels. You are now the most powerful crawlers I have ever worked with, including some who made it through floor 11. Then five minutes on practising, and on not phasing into solid objects.

beats.headline: My arch enemy, Tish
beats.text: I am ROLLING after Tish, my arch enemy, and I am very fast, and then this DOPPELGANGER catches me in a corner and will not let go. I tell everyone I will kill her mother and uninvite her from my bachelorette party. I am a woman scorned. My need for revenge is the only thing I know, and I will not be denied. Then Donut says if I come back I can see her new cloak. That does sound exciting. Okay. Did Carl show them his new pet yet? He promised I could name him.

beats.headline: Hell-Kissed, Celestial, and the Prince of Woe
beats.text: A gold pet box, a patch that opens the Midnight Market, and the Hell-Kissed Celestial Skill Potion of the Prince of Woe. The potion hands Carl the Gloom Wraith Phase, which is a skill for walking through people.

beats.headline: Samantha's arch enemy
beats.text: Larracos, the college, a visitor pass queue. Samantha rolled by Louis screaming after a woman named Tish and promising to kill her, and Katia Grim gave chase past guards carrying a Despondent debuff until she had the head cornered. Crawler Carl asked twice who the fuck Tish was. Princess Donut had forgotten about Tish entirely until that moment. Samantha, restrained: she is a woman scorned, and her need for vengeance against her arch enemy, Tish, is the only thing she knows.

beats.headline: The third edition's author
beats.text: Dante, a crocodilian thief, wrote the third edition, and only a single entry of it, afraid of being caught. He took a deal at the start of the eleventh floor and worked as a game guide, then moved to the Trap Master guild to be near his skyfowl neighbour, a shopkeeper who had also owned the Cookbook. He never told him who he was. Reassigned with that neighbour as a castle guard for one season's eighth floor, fourteen seasons short of freedom, he refused to follow orders. Administrative action killed him.

beats.headline: War Leader III, then General
beats.text: Donut touches each of us to make us officers and lets me set up the hierarchy. I start at War Leader III. After some time with the base system that becomes Colonel, and after Donut tells me to upgrade myself, General. Most of the core group gets the same. The dancers get Sergeant First Class, so they can recruit and command the base troops. I'd named that rank Adjutant. They made me change it. Imani, Elle and I are leaving for headquarters to meet the adjutant.

beats.headline: Eyebrows, eyelashes, and a failed spell
beats.text: Carl waited for me to do his hair tonic. Eyebrows first, then eyelashes, which is almost the pubic hair recipe, so I'm careful. He asks, quietly, if I'm okay. I'm hanging in there. Mordecai is brewing something that might help with the rehab, and I'll take it tomorrow, before the ceasefire ends. The head mix can only sit for five seconds, so I have an otter water mage, one of the strippers, ready to power-wash it off. As a mercenary, his spell won't cast in the saferoom. Carl's hair now reaches his waist.

beats.headline: Small thing, in and out
beats.text: Small thing. Jumps IN mouth. Mother yells. Mongo swallows. Hurk. Hurk. Out again. Small thing wants back in. Mongo runs. Then: bowl. Small thing pushes bowl. SOUP. Mongo licks it all.

beats.headline: She calls it Cousin Oliver
beats.text: Carl has been keeping a pet from me. In all my life I have never felt a sense of betrayal this profound. It is a baby tummy acher Ren hoisted on him, it has five weaknesses, and it hopped into Mongo's mouth and he swallowed it. It is Cousin Oliver. Scrappy Doo. A late addition that makes a perfectly good cast worse. It gets three strikes, and it used one growling at Mongo. I offered to sell it to Katia's boyfriend for five gold. Carl says it is not for sale.

beats.headline: Still at the college
beats.text: Crawler Carl reconstructs the file. Ghazi wrote to the college here in Larracos for help, and the letters showed that his ex-girlfriend, Tish, still worked there, and that he had left her for the doll. Samantha proposes to use Louis's new toy to kill her. Princess Donut rules that subject should not be held accountable; that was one hundred percent Ghazi. If she is not allowed to blow Tish up, Samantha adds, Juice Box is going to hear about Louis's affair. Louis says: what?

beats.headline: Died five times, and stronger for it
beats.text: A pet-class mob. The System’s notice for one that has not yet bonded to a crawler reads like a card on a cage: this one has died five times, and its stats are all buffed by 125% because of it. It has five weaknesses, which can be examined only by whoever bonds with it or holds it in a carrier.

beats.headline: Bonded on one bowl of chowder
beats.text: Carl lets the level-one tummy acher out onto the table, and it hops straight into Mongo's open mouth. Mongo swallows, then yaks it back up, giggling. Carl's food box now serves everything chowder style, so his breakfast sandwich comes crumbled into seafood soup; he puts the bowl down, the meatball dives in, growls at Mongo, and its dot turns orange. One bowl, and bonded. Then it pushes the bowl over to Mongo. The naming window will not close until Louis comes up with a knight's name built on Ren's.

beats.headline: A mantis on the eighth floor
beats.text: From a season long past, when the crawl was run by the Reavers. The eighth level that season was mountains connected by wires and gondolas. The crawlers were a strange type of mantis, not the common kind, who could not fly and did poorly in the cold. There was a crawler among them named York, and an NPC named Dante, who had once left a single entry in the Cookbook himself, was watching him carefully.

beats.headline: Tinsel on the guild floor
beats.text: Waiting on the elevator, I notice a few pieces of tinsel on the guild floor. The Christmas decorations came from the memory simulation and vanished when we got here. This tinsel stayed, so somebody looted it on an earlier floor, from somewhere real. Everything seems normal to me now, and that's the problem: real and make-believe mixed together, and the make-believe often the more dangerous. I think of Pater Coal. I think of Lightning Lou, and how close I came. Paulie's words come back: be sure. On my chest, the eye blinks.

beats.headline: So close to the edge
beats.text: Crawler Carl thinks of Lightning Lou, the old dog at the gas station in Florida left to spend Christmas Day alone. Carl curled up beside him on the floor and contemplated his options, and came so close to the edge that it almost broke his mind to think about it. Paulie's words come back to him: be sure it's your only option. On his chest, the eye blinks.

beats.headline: Firas's name for it
beats.text: My celestial box gives me an Airship Portal, which is an elevator up to a hangar, and a ship. Katia says it's not an airplane, more like a drone thing, a tilt rotor. It runs on a soul crystal, like the Twister. I named it Party Planner, 'cause that's what Firas wanted to call the Twister, and I told him it was stupid. It's a bomber, too. The System calls the model Casket in the Sky. Carl says it looks like a death trap. Katia said that too, especially after she read the description.

beats.headline: The reward for having survived being condemned
beats.text: It comes out of the celestial box Louis earned for outliving a goddess's mark for death on the floor before. Two items: a tier III guild upgrade called an Airship Portal, and the ship itself, a silver tilt-rotor he names Party Planner, the name Firas once suggested for another vehicle.

beats.headline: Through the portal with the water
beats.text: I went through the Gate with the water. I lay low with the ones who lived through it, and when they were ready I told them. What they are. What this whole place is. Enough of them believed me that they call me Warlord now, and a Warlord has people, and a Warlord has opinions about alliances. I have sent War Leader Arief to Carl's people with my terms. The terms are Louis. He marries me. That is the alliance.

beats.headline: Juice Box tells them
beats.text: She came through with the Larracos flood, and now an NPC calls himself an NPC out loud for the first time.

beats.headline: What the Semeru dug into
beats.text: Carl examines War Leader Arief, a young Semeru dwarf in feathered, parade-ready armour, and the System tells his people's story. They farmed and mined a paradise inside the volcano and dug toward the goddess below them, Ysalte, until they struck the roots of the All Tree and stopped. They built their castle along those roots, a monument and an apology. Scolopendra's nine-tier attack hit them hardest of all: millions before that day, fewer than 10,000 now. Arief is Despondent, because his goddess is dead.

beats.headline: They paid the license fee
beats.text: Princess Donut writes to me in capitals that Louis's shirt is an outrage. It is a Donut Holes shirt, and the Donut Holes paid the license fee, so it is a perfectly legitimate brand and her merch is doing quite well. She asks whether she gets any of the money. Okay, so: no. If she reaches the tenth floor she gets a stipend and can negotiate a small percentage based on her licensing fee, and past a threshold she gets a percentage automatically. I don't know the threshold. I don't think anybody has ever gotten close.

beats.headline: A name a dwarf wants revenge on
beats.text: Entered into the file on the word of a dwarf named Arief, who swings his sword and promises revenge. Architect Houston: leader of the Madness, a Viceroy outworlder. He caught Arief's brother trying to sabotage the Madness fortifications, and the brother was tortured before Juice Box got in and ended his suffering. Crawler Donut asks whether this is the one Juice Box decapitated at the pre-production meeting. It is not. That was one of his surgeons. Nobody has managed to get into Houston's lair beside the throne room, which is called his operating theater.

beats.headline: The Sultana behind her veils
beats.text: Arief calls the nagas a court of assassins, not warriors; no changeling or spy has ever reached their inner sanctum, and even Juice Box will not try. Their warlord is the Sultana, in life the crown princess and daughter of the naga king, play-acting the Sepsis Whore, the sultana of the old histories who had 198 daughters before 99 sons and supposedly poisoned almost all of the sons. In the old days, her honor guard were sentenced to deferred death for looking at her. The naga team loses every season. She has never once been killed in the game.

beats.headline: Grand Re-Opening, under new management
beats.text: It opened back up today. The square concrete building on level four of Larracos has only the red bottom half of its neon arrow lit, and a hand-painted sign on a sheet across the entrance: Grand Re-Opening. Under New Management. Arief leads the group through the empty entrance bar, the Headlamp Colonnade, past a gnoll bartender whom Donut's sunglasses read as a changeling, and down a hidden tunnel to an office. There the one-eyed old gnoll manager, Hunger Hammy, leaps across the desk and kisses Louis.

beats.headline: Arief's tour
beats.text: War Leader Arief walks the group down from the college on level fifty through a city whose floodwater has fallen to its bottom three levels, still high enough to cover the castle. Juice Box has been waking its NPCs to the truth of what they are.

beats.headline: An uncle among the Jatismara
beats.text: Arief mentions another season, and Carl stops in the street. Arief does not remember one; he believes he is new, like most of them. But some have the memory quickened. His uncle remembers dozens of seasons, fewer than Juice Box, and as one of the Jatismara sits on her war council. Most of the NPCs now know about their past lives. Some shopkeepers and patrons are made differently and cannot understand. For most of them, Arief believes, a death is forever.

beats.headline: The blade goes through him
beats.text: Subject is present in the Desperado Club as adjutant to Team Retribution. Juice Box reports that she touched his arm and found it solid, and that when she attempted to decapitate him her blade passed through him like a ghost. The protection a crawler has for a while after regenerating appears, in his case, to be permanent. She also reports a worm in his brain, of a different species from the one in Carl's rock friend. Carl names it: a Valtay worm. The NPCs are not allowed to kill him.

beats.headline: Not what I wanted
beats.text: Carl. You didn't do what I wanted. We wanted everybody protected, with regeneration. He says they would never allow it, so they did the next best thing: they made it so we can kill them. It'll have to do. I show him most of my papers. Some go in the drawer. I ask about Ruby. The rules of this world are a lot. A voice told me I would not be allowed to talk to someone I tried to meet. I don't have menus. I do have messaging, so now Louis and I can talk whenever we like.

beats.headline: Game of Thrones stuff
beats.text: She's messaging me non-stop about getting married so our houses are bonded. It's all Game of Thrones stuff, man. Out loud she's all confident, but in the messages she's different. I think she's really scared, in over her head. Carl says I don't have to. I already told her I would. If the NPCs turn on us, we're screwed. So I stand up, take her hand, and say we should get married right away. Donut makes me say I love you. Then she makes me say it twice.

beats.headline: Hovels nobody built
beats.text: There is usually a shanty town. Never one like this. It appeared soon after the flooding, supposedly built by displaced NPCs, except that nobody built it: the hovels simply sprang up, a full ring round the top entrance of Larracos, large enough to count as a settlement. It has new shops and new NPCs, food markets and temples, and one hard-to-find Club Vanquisher entrance, but no weapons or mercenary markets. Its mayors keep dying. The gnoll Theora lost a single combat to a cheat. The current mayor, Juice Box says, pained, is someone else.

beats.headline: Ferdinand holds the interface
beats.text: Juice Box and Louis are reunited, and he is visibly uneasy about the marriage. Then she lays out the practical problem: Ferdinand is mayor of Shanty Town, just outside Larracos, and he holds the warlord interface for the team, because he is technically from outside. Nothing this side of the wall moves without a cat's cooperation. Drick is the adjutant.

beats.headline: A bowler hat for Shanty Town
beats.text: Warlord on High, Sir Ferdinand, level 100, co-warlord of Team Retribution, arrives in the vestibule seated on his adjutant's head, in a turban improvised from tissues. He wants his rhinoceros mount and his hat. Carl offers a temporary replacement from Quan Ch's inventory, a bowler hat that decapitates and returns when thrown, in exchange for the mayorship of Shanty Town. The transfer requires Carl and Donut to pay gold. The trade is accepted, and the truce is renamed The Good Guys. Subject's remark on the matter: I'm a very handsome boy.

beats.headline: Hamed takes the club
beats.text: Clarabelle, alive and in her chair, tells Carl and Donut they are banned from the Desperado Club by the new management, who has banned all crawlers for his first few days. He keeps bodyguards with him at all times, not exactly NPCs and not exactly former crawlers, and more security than she has ever seen. The surviving cretins and sai were airlocked off to the mercenary markets. His name is Hamed: the Night Wyrm, leader of the Guild of Suffering, husband of the late Astrid, and father of Damascus Steel and Anaconda, who are supposedly in the club hunting him.

beats.headline: New management at the club
beats.text: Clarabelle, alive, at her post: crawlers are banned by order of the new management. He wants his first days to go smoothly. He is very particular and very serious about security, and has a whole slew of bodyguards, not exactly NPCs and not exactly former crawlers. His name is Hamed. Crawler Carl keeps his face still. The real name of the Night Wyrm, the head of the Guild of Suffering, husband to the late Astrid. His sons are supposedly still in the club, hunting him.

beats.headline: I wish my mom was here
beats.text: Changeling weddings come in two parts, which is kind of a relief. The small one is now, in the grimy entrance bar: no rings, no officiant, no singing, and Donut is mad about all three. Juice Box goes to her blank form and we hold hands. I catch Carl staring and tell him I wish my mom was here. Then we whisper vows we made up on the spot, in each other's ears. We'll say them out loud at the Confirmation, in about a month. And that's it. We're married.

beats.headline: Not his fiancée
beats.text: Ferdinand has been telling people he is my fiancé. In the vestibule I make him say it: he is not really my fiancé. He adds not yet, and winks at Carl. I would rather have a sexual affair with the bloating corpse of a syphilis-infested cocker spaniel. Yes, I have his hat; I found it after the Butcher's Masquerade, and he can have it back when he stops being disgusting and changes the name of our alliance. Then Carl pulls out a bowler hat I have never been given.

beats.headline: Tipid fills him in
beats.text: He tells Carl about Doctor Hu and the Crawler Project in the Meadowlark saferoom.

beats.headline: The fourth edition's author
beats.text: Tipid, a Crest poisoner, wrote the fourth edition. He got out at the start of the twelfth floor with a key that let only one of them through a door, and he chose himself over his friend Horatio. He had negotiated an extra season to keep that key; he tore it off its chain and threw it across the table. Damage to his brain took his whole pension and a loan to repair. He settled in a Crest system and worked for a waste management company. Current status: Colonel in the Princess Posse.

beats.headline: In the Princess Posse
beats.text: Carl and Donut are in the Meadowlark saferoom, and Tipid is telling it to them: fifty thousand of us under their banner, and I am one of them. People who got out of a crawl once and know exactly what one is, and signed up for another anyway, under the banner of a cat. He gets emotional about it. Nobody gives him a hard time. We had the same faces on when we signed.

beats.headline: Only for new crawlers
beats.text: Subject, drunk as usual, listens to Tipid describe what the Crawler Project won, citizenship, healthcare and housing for released crawlers, and grunts with derision. That perk is only for new crawlers, she says, and they will still be bled dry on taxes. The old guard will be extra fucked on release. The rich like their faces on screen while they donate, and they will fight like hell when a scruffy former crawler tries to settle in their system. She takes a long swig, looks at Mongo with wet eyes, and wanders off.

beats.headline: Why the authorities cracked down
beats.text: Tipid explains where the network came from. Doctor Hu formed it beside the Crawler Project: smaller, more focused, with far less support, and with the purpose of ending the crawl altogether. The residual in the homeless man's body at the Florida shelter, Paulie, was one of several actions that finally brought the authorities down on the non-profit.

beats.headline: Doctor Hu, per Tipid
beats.text: Tipid supplies more of the file. Subject, as Doctor Hu, runs the Crawler Project, an NFC for former crawlers, whose campaigning made every newly released crawler a Syndicate citizen with free healthcare and guaranteed housing. He also formed the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, a smaller group aimed at ending the crawl altogether. It was his idea to refurbish a garbage freighter into a passenger liner and call for former crawlers to come back in. When they were accused of being a terrorist organization, they scattered. Tipid does not know where he is.

beats.headline: The garbage truck people cancel
beats.text: I get a notification that a sponsorship has been cancelled. The garbage truck people, for a conflict of interest, whatever that means, and Carl says huh. At least I opened their box already. There is going to be an auction for a new one. I do hope it lines up properly with my brand this time. Veriluxx was a dud, Empress D'nadia sold my sponsorship, and it would be nice to have something to complement the Apothecary, even if she does sponsor half the dungeon.

beats.headline: They are already there when he walks in
beats.text: Rosetta, Tipid, Justice Light and fifty thousand others have signed on. Carl gets emotional.

beats.headline: Four million gold
beats.text: I tell the room this is not an attack, it is a self-correcting measure given in the spirit of comradery, and I smack Carl on the forehead. Then I hug him. Comrade. We are here. I put my hand on the tattoo on his chest and ask how much he has left. Of what? The toraline, and the spider's ink. In chat, where they cannot hear: does he still have the credit chit from the dead pig? Donut has it. Then I take the items: a finger-sized slice, and the ink. I want his saferoom, his bomber's studio and three million gold. Better make it four.

beats.headline: Mayor, for a bowler hat
beats.text: Crawler Carl wanted to be mayor of Shanty Town, and the mayor was Ferdinand. The deal: Ferdinand transferred the mayorship, the jewel on his necklace went away, and he got a bowler hat to wear until they trade it back for his turban in a day or so. Juice Box was on board. Carl's reasoning, on the walk back: if the bad guys can freely enter Shanty Town once the truce breaks, it is a liability, and it has a defence system of its own.

beats.headline: What Tipid remembers
beats.text: Tipid, in a zero zone, is told he has brain lesions and needs to get to a Viceroy system for repair, at the cost of a good chunk of his pension. The word frightens him. He remembers the Viceroys: the masked monsters of his own Faction Wars, who called themselves the Madness. Their chief surgeon had a spell that cooked your brain, made your teeth fall out, and turned the liquid in your eyeballs to acid. That is what happened to Rosaline.

beats.headline: Doctor Hu, and the Crawler Project
beats.text: Carl needs the whole of it, so I give it to him in order. Doctor Hu. The Crawler Project. How fifty thousand of us came to be standing under the Princess Posse's banner. None of it is anything he would ever have been told from inside; that is the thing about being retired, you learn what the ones still crawling are not shown. He listens. That is rarer than it sounds.

beats.headline: Out again, in a tutu
beats.text: Carl adds his strength to the fortress's oversized, badly hammered door, and it flies all the way open and throws him and Tipid to the ground. Someone shouts that she is out again. Big Tina, allosaurus, wearing a pink tutu, stamps into the clearing and hops up and down in front of Mongo, waving her little wand. Mongo hops up and down in front of her too.

beats.headline: Hup, hup, hup
beats.text: We step out of the bait-shop safe room into a building site: watchtowers, a palisade they are testing with fireballs, a channel being cut up toward the lake. A level 62 Fortification Engineer named Penn drops a steel beam, hugs me, kisses me on the cheek, and starts shouting. Hup, hup, hup. Then thousands of them, humans, skyfowl, crocodilians, bune, yenk, fists and wings in the air, until the ground shakes. Tipid moves to chat. This is for you. This is what you built. In less than three days we'll be waist deep in blood. Then they all go back to work.

beats.headline: The caiman lifts the wall
beats.text: We only get so many officers, so the builders and the crawlers are going in as sergeants and chiefs, which lets them change the camp. Everyone else is legionnaire, with corporals running teams. A wall section goes over and buries itself in the dirt, and I go to help. My card from the last floor still comes once a day. I call him: a giant caiman, twenty-five feet of him. He gets his snout under the wall and heaves it up while the workers push. He times out before long. I come back grumbling about artillery.

beats.headline: Digging in
beats.text: NPCs and former crawlers build the defences together: the changelings and the flesh golems started the stronghold, and a few thousand of the newcomers chose the Fortification Engineer race so they could build fast and level while they do it.

beats.headline: Blood bar rules are back
beats.text: The blood bar rules are back in force inside the safe rooms. I tell Carl now, while knowing it still costs nothing. Around us the NPCs, the mercenaries and the rest of us former crawlers are building the defences on the same line, three kinds of people this format has always kept apart, working shoulder to shoulder. I do not have a rule for that. I am watching it closely.

beats.headline: Read by the next one
beats.text: A note added by crawler Ikicha, eleventh edition. Ikicha's kind are castrated and cast out, a perspective as different as could be from the one who came before: York, who appears to have come from a hive, yet says he always felt alone his entire life. Reading his words, Ikicha feels kinship anyway, and asks the question on the page. Did he survive? Then a prayer that anyone who gets free seeks out those who came before.

beats.headline: What one is actually for
beats.text: An elite is waiting in the antechamber to the team's flag room during the ceasefire, pressed into service as a bomb by a production company that wants Carl off the board. Baroness Victory steps out and puts him down before the satchels can go off. The office is classed as a non-combatant observer, which makes the moment a curiosity for the rule book as much as a rescue.

beats.headline: Herman the Fleet does not get to finish
beats.text: Carl, Donut, Tipid and Florin come into the Fortress of Unyielding Power and Authority, and Florin walks them through the ceasefire rules. Then our own Elite, Herman the Fleet, leaned on by Sensation Entertainment, reveals what he actually is, which is a delivery system for a bomb. I deal with him. An adjutant may do that. It is in the rules, and I have read the rules.

beats.headline: The scouts, over chat
beats.text: I stand in the empty throne room pretending to examine it and ask Florin in chat, because the walls may still have ears. Only someone with the Scout endorsement crosses a border in peacetime. A scout who is discovered gets teleported home and cannot go stealth again until the fighting starts, and a trap still kills them. We get eighteen. The towers are for keeping their scouts out, and they have already sent back one from the Dream and one from the Prism. Florin bets his left sack we're infested with spies anyway.

beats.headline: Still pregnant, and family
beats.text: Kiwi is very pregnant and has been carrying since the Hunting Grounds, which is a long time to be in that condition even by this dungeon's standards. Big Tina, for her part, has decided that Mongo is her father. Nobody in the fortress has the standing, the courage, or frankly the desire to correct her.

beats.headline: Kiwi goes inside
beats.text: Big one says PA-PA. Bear comes out. Kiwi. KIWI. Sniff. Kiwi hugs Mongo. Mongo stays still. Kiwi goes inside. Big one goes inside. Mongo sniffs air. Peep.

beats.headline: A name she cannot change
beats.text: Fortress of Unyielding Power and Authority. It is a terrible name, and it will not let me change it, because the Sledge and the changelings kept changing it back and forth until the AI told them to shove it. Carl reads out the initials and laughs. I am absolutely not calling my castle that. It's obscene, and the bad guys are going to laugh at us. I give Florin a direct order not to spread it. He has already put it in the chat.

beats.headline: What she says of her sister
beats.text: The Princess asks whether my sister was nice or a jerk. She means the orc queen, who died when my nephew attempted to assassinate them. Ugloo and I once had a very similar outlook on life. When she married into the royal family, she lost a great deal of who she was. We had not spoken in a long while, but before she died she wrote to ask if I would be an adjutant this season. She was going to the Scolopendra Club to meet the king. I ask why the Princess wishes to know.

beats.headline: Have they stopped
beats.text: Subject arrives in the flag room at Katia's legs, wearing a Dallas Cowboys jersey as a dress, having flown in on Louis's new airship, which she prefers to the old one. Skarn is in the hangar playing with it; Louis has hired gremlins, and they have bought door guns. Carl kneels and tells her she should not have to think about that sort of thing. She asks why she should not think about killing outworlders. Have they stopped thinking about killing her?

beats.headline: Mind Balance, level nine
beats.text: I clear my screen by mistake, and when it comes back the spam folder comes with it. Gloom Wraith Phase failed to activate. Prevented by Mind Balance. Mind Balance has risen to level nine. It was five a few hours ago. Pages of it. Shi Maria has been trying to cast through me, and the bombs on that ogre were non-magical. If the phase had gone off, Donut would be in pieces. The skill is getting stronger. So is she. It's a race, and she's winning it. I message Mordecai.

beats.headline: Four phases, and the Ramp-Up
beats.text: Victory lays out the phases: the Ceasefire, the Ramp-Up, Open Hostilities, and the Peeling of Larracos once four teams remain. The Ramp-Up lasts 180 hours. In it there are no celestial summonings, no offensive magic, no teleporting, and nobody but a scout enters enemy land except through a kilometre-wide gate. Weapons work; the spells attached to them do not. Traps must be static. It is designed to force bloody, hand-to-hand combat, against teams who brought their own pulse rifles and power armour and would like it over in a week.

beats.headline: Recruited, at last
beats.text: Mordecai brews a potion that negates auras, and with it I can be recruited. I am. The moment it is done, I ask one thing: my squad builds the defences in and around Shanty Town. Carl agrees. The town is a ring around Larracos now, and it belongs to the Posse.

beats.headline: Rolling hills, and the northern border
beats.text: On Baroness Victory's map the Operatics hold pie piece number two, rolling hills between the orcs' peaks and the Posse's flat ground, with the big river curving through their territory before it passes through Shanty Town and into Larracos. The main body of the enemy is massing on the Posse's northern border with the Operatics, about a hundred thousand strong by first estimate. Their best chance, says the adjutant, is to sweep over the Posse at once.

beats.headline: They got married without me
beats.text: THEY GOT MARRIED WITHOUT TELLING ME. Louis and the changeling. I wouldn't have disrupted the wedding. The little gnome says I said I'd push her over and take her place at the last second, but she's a child and does not understand the intricacies of modern love. And even if I was going to, that is no reason not to tell a girl. Then Donut says that was only the first wedding, and there's a bigger ceremony in a few weeks. Why didn't anyone SAY so? This changes everything.

beats.headline: Pink on the map
beats.text: On the hologram of the floor a tiny ring around Larracos blinks and turns pink: Shanty Town, controlled by the Princess Posse. Baroness Victory calls it a smart trade. The shanty town is usually small and does not form until the fighting starts and the NPCs flee, but this one circles the whole city, giving the NPCs another layer of security, and the Posse holds it. Li Na asks, the moment she is recruited, that her squad build the defences in and around it.

beats.headline: Commander of the 103rd
beats.text: Subject is a veteran of Land War, a different game entirely, which was inflicted on his home planet; everyone calls him a crawler anyway, and he comes to the Princess Posse’s aid during the faction fighting. He is given a battalion, the 103rd, on the strength of what he has done both inside a dungeon and outside one. He has said perhaps three words since.

beats.headline: Through four skunks, phased
beats.text: The spray comes, and a blink before the cloud reaches me I go incorporeal on Gloom Wraith Phase and rush forward through four skunks with their backs to me. They come apart into ribbons of fur and flesh, and their armour clanks to the forest floor. It feels like running through a sprinkler on a fine mist. I've seen this done before. The rage elemental did it to Yolanda. Five seconds, then Walk on Air, up onto a branch above the cloud, next to Bodi.

beats.headline: I found out
beats.text: Back in our territory, young man. I'm pretty sure I've found every artillery battery on both sides, though I can't swear to a hundred per cent. And we've got a new problem. They have another nasty surprise waiting for us on the naga side. Remember when you asked me to find out why those robot fellows wanted pet levelling sped up? Well. I found out.

beats.headline: The shark has a name
beats.text: Subject existed first as a magical tattoo carried on Tsarina Signet’s skin, one that could fly, and is now a seventeen-foot hammerhead shark that breathes air and flops where he once flew. He rolls with Carl’s squad now, answers to Jamal, speaks of himself as Jamal, and keeps telling the legs Carl builds him to hop, which breaks them.

beats.headline: STINK, and a branch
beats.text: Skunks. STINK. Mongo in tree. Mongo sick. Sick again. MOTHER jumps onto Mongo branch. Branch goes crack. MOTHER falls. Mongo falls. Cage. Mongo whimpers.

beats.headline: Skanked, and a hat
beats.text: The skunks' leader is a little battle wizard called Fancy Boy, in a starry hat, and I shout that nobody touch him because he's mine, and knock him out with a Magic Missile. That, apparently, is what was stopping the rest of them spraying. Now I am Skanked. Three hours, Charisma down seventy per cent, and nothing in my inventory takes it off. Mongo is sick. I got the hat, and it smells worse than I do. And I was supposed to be moral support for Katia's treatment.

beats.headline: A gift for attending
beats.text: Subject is a Tummy Acher, a pet-class mob built to absorb damage. He came to Tserendolgor as a gift for attending CrawlCon, and to Carl when she was gone, reset to level one with no name and no memory; the one he answers to now is Louis's work. Tserendolgor took delivery of a party favour. What the group has now is a tank that levels every time it goes hunting, which is not what a party favour is for.

beats.headline: Removal Order
beats.text: My half of it: the same drug with Removal Order stirred in, so I go into the spider's worst memory instead of mine, and at the end I can lock Shi Maria inside it. Nobody can tell me how the lock will look. Someone has to pull my toe ring off once I'm under, so we can't do this in the guild. The potion it needs is one Mordecai already made. Coincidences in here mean another hand. The last thing I hear going under is a warlord notification. The Lemig Sortion, offering free passage, to treat for peace.

beats.headline: The fifth author, in a tower
beats.text: Everly, a sward mantis who crawled alone with hired mercenaries, gets a compass from her sponsor that shows the safest path through a fifty-level tower. It has forty-nine uses. At the top, a note: the tower is an advertisement, the compass named for a competitor, the dead end sponsored by the very company that sent it. She scrawls an angry note in the cookbook as the roof starts to come down. Explosives Engineer. Primal. Crushed to death on the eighth floor. Author of the fifth edition.

beats.headline: Twice to Glory Bound
beats.text: Mordecai's jar is two hits of Glory Bound in a gel, cut with a potion called Tough Love. Eight to ten hours, for me. Once I am under I am on my own, and Edgar says waking me early could be fatal. That's a cheerful thought. I drink the sleeping potion. Skál. Then I tell Carl a secret. My favourite memory and my worst memory are the same thing, and I am going back to where I went last time. He tells me to take his hand. I do, and Imani pulls us apart.

beats.headline: The ogre in the sand
beats.text: Under the lowering ceiling of Everly's tower, one of her last two mercenaries, an ogre who has not said one word since she hired him, stops digging and lies down beside her. There is a flash deep in the back of his eyes, like a screen booting up. Maybe there is more to it than this, he says, as the ceiling reaches his face. Maybe it is not inevitable, like she says.

beats.headline: An egg only I can break
beats.text: I wake in the Sugar Cube, standing in a circle of blood and Lemig goblin corpses, fifty or more, with eleven hours gone. Quest failed: the Bedlam Bride. Their own adjutant rules it an AI action. What comes back from the dream: a second spider. Her husband, Hapanzi, who turned into a man. He'd been a god. I have her now, son, he said. You can set her free if you must, but not unless all is lost. She's an egg inside me, and only I can break it.

beats.headline: A name out of the dream
beats.text: Reconstructed from Crawler Carl's memory as he wakes, covered in blood, on the far side of the map. The dream had a second spider in it: a male, her husband, first a spider and then a man. Shi Maria came in mocking, saw him, then killed him and devoured him while she sobbed. Then he came back. His name, Carl thinks, was Hapanzi, and he had been a god. His words: I have her now, son. She is good and trapped. You can always set her free, if you must. But do not unless all is lost.

beats.headline: The Lemig headquarters
beats.text: The castle landed in the Lemig Sortion's territory, and they made it their headquarters. In Queen Imogen's private ballroom near the top, their warlord waits for a summoned Carl, planning to leave him a vegetable and turn the spider loose on his own base. Instead the spider comes out in the ballroom. When it is over, Panford, the Lemig adjutant, tells Commander Stockade his throne room is destroyed and that it is being ruled an AI action. His general, Luke, killed by a fellow soldier under her control, is among the dead.

beats.headline: We left her with Annie
beats.text: They tell me Carl vanished off his cot as it began, stayed translucent, then went completely. The Lemig team knew the moment he went under and tried something through the warlord chat. I message him. He is in the high elf castle. And we left her there, Carl. We left Shi Maria alone in that room with Annie. He says it was only a memory, and asks if it worked. It is not a switch one flips. We will not know right away. But yes. I think it worked.

beats.headline: Carl wakes up in their base
beats.text: Eleven hours gone, blood all over him, and most of the room around him killed by the thing riding inside him. The Lemig Sortion and the Madness had been arranging something together. It has come apart on top of them.

beats.headline: The quiet one at the table
beats.text: Six in the late Queen Imogen's kitchen for a field ruling: three warlords and their adjutants. Architect Houston sits at the far end of the table, unmoving. He was already in the castle, but not in the ballroom when it happened. His adjutant is a tiny floating bune named Opiee. His mask is white and featureless but for a small red teardrop, and his long white robes move as if the body under them is the wrong shape. When Crawler Carl rises with his fists clenched, Houston turns his head toward him. The neck creaks like a wooden ship.

beats.headline: They can see our dreams
beats.text: The minor quorum sits in Imogen's kitchen and plays it back. Stockade sent a Summon Ally invitation as I went under, and it was accepted the moment Imani pried off my toe ring. Shi Maria accepted it. Then the screen goes hazy, and I know what it is. Katia's nightmare. Fannar walking out of the office, telling them the truth. The faceless woman at the desk. Architect Houston turns from the screen to look at me. Turn this off, I say. This isn't yours to watch. I'm ignored. The scene changes: Annie in the crib, wired up.

beats.headline: Worry not, my children
beats.text: The dream again. A hospital room, Katia at a crib. Shi Maria pushes in, and a second spider follows: Hapanzi, her husband. Nobody says the name, and in that place there are no names over anyone's heads, but in the dream Crawler Carl simply knows it. Worry not, my children, the spider says, and becomes a large, dark-skinned man in simple pants and a vest, with an accent like Asojano's. Carl recognises the voice. It is the one that occasionally speaks inside his mind.

beats.headline: The field ruling
beats.text: Carl, Commander Stockade, Architect Houston and their adjutants convene for an official adjudication, and it goes on the record. The Lemig Sortion and the Madness used outside information to time a Summon Ally, meaning to pull Carl bodily to their base so that what was in him could be let loose on the rest of the Princess Posse. They got half of him, and the other half of the plan.

beats.headline: Two towers, and Lucia Mar
beats.text: Shanty Town's defences are still going up. We have two towers built, both splash towers, and that is all. We are working as fast as we can, and my sister says two more in twenty minutes. And Florin, you wanted to know about Lucia Mar. She is here in Shanty Town right now with her dog, drinking at the Possum Envy, right on the edge of the border. One of the new guys tried to recruit her. She almost ripped his head off.

beats.headline: Summon Ally, explained
beats.text: The kid asks me mid-hearing what Summon Ally does, so I tell him. It's a rare teleport, and it's built so the summoned holds the cards. You have to share a chat, the warlord chat counts, apparently. You have to accept. You can't be dropped into a wall. You went over as a ghost because the system compensates for being out cold. I thought I'd killed you. At best they wanted your treatment ruined. At worst it would simply kill you. They wanted to kill us using that crazy spider.

beats.headline: A score to settle first
beats.text: Hello, Carl and Donut. I am above the naga border with Bianca, surveying your defences, and your enemies believe they are being surreptitious. The elves' long-range trebuchets are preparing to fire. A hundred mercenaries in the Madness's colours think they are invisible. There are tracked vehicles under camouflage netting. With no magic permitted at the outset, I am perfectly safe, thank you. Once the festivities begin, I have a score to settle with the lead producer of the Blood Hunter program. Only then will I join your military. If you are still alive.

beats.headline: A foul, and a ceasefire cut short
beats.text: Panford, the Lemig Sortion's adjutant, sets out before a minor quorum of adjutants what his own team did: an attempt to pull Carl bodily to their base while Mordecai was working to expel what rides inside him. The Sortion is penalised for illegal information gathering. Then its warlord, still under the spider's madness, beats his own head against the floor until he dies, the team is defeated, and that withdrawal cuts the ceasefire short by more than twenty-three hours.

beats.headline: Not culpable, by two votes
beats.text: Panford lays out the charge: Commander Stockade and Architect Houston used secured messaging to reach someone on the eighteenth floor, identified as Nurse Yugoslav of the Madness. Crawler Carl asks, loudly, whether that is his mom. Opiee calls the evidence circumstantial, quite damning, and not enough, and asks his warlord whether he wishes to confess. The masked warlord says nothing. Baroness Victory rules Houston obviously guilty and smart enough to let Stockade do the dirty work, and votes not culpable. Opiee agrees. The Madness is found not guilty of any wrongdoing.

beats.headline: A promise, then a rifle
beats.text: A direct message in the warlord chat: mention his mother out loud again, and Crawler Carl and his animal companion spend their last thousand hours on the amplification table in his surgical theater. This is a promise, he says. A second one: Carl is in mortal danger at this very moment and does not realise it. Then the Lemig Sortion falls, its assets go to the Madness, and Phase One engages. Houston is on his feet with his robes flung back: a bug-like body, six arms, two of them holding a rifle. He fires at Carl's chest. Carl dives, grabs a bag of cat food, and teleports.

beats.headline: A bag of cat food and a hole
beats.text: Houston messages me. Mention his mother again and Donut and I spend our last thousand hours on his amplification table. Gracious pet owners accept the gifts their animals drop on the doorstep. Then the ceasefire ends, his robes fly back on a bug body with six arms, and two of them bring a rifle up at my chest. I dive, grab the bag of cat food off the counter, drop a hob-lobber from my hotlist, and teleport home with a hole punched through my shoulder. No kill message. Either he planned all of this, or he knew what was happening to Stockade and used it.

beats.headline: The containment in the eye
beats.text: On the screen Shi Maria rampages through the ballroom screaming that she did not kill Hapanzi and never would. At that same moment in the dream, she vanished and Hapanzi reappeared as a spider. He told Crawler Carl she was gone, trapped in his own body, and that Carl now controlled the eye on his chest and the containment she is in. Carl can summon her once. If he does, she chooses: take over his body, or expel herself into her own form. Watching the replay, Carl notes she did not look nearly as trapped as Hapanzi said.

beats.headline: Burned some assets
beats.text: Carl sends me a message for Ferdinand. I pass it on. I had to burn some assets to save his ass. I hope it was worth it. I'm hearing about strange movements, and I relay all of it to Louis and Britney. Heads up to his people. We are powering up the towers early. Anyone in town who is not in his army should start moving into his territory.

beats.headline: Punished, and the ceasefire ends early
beats.text: Panford, their adjutant, is left to explain the rampage through the base to everyone. Stockade looked into her eye, lost his mind, and finished it himself. Ferdinand gets an emergency action item passed for a live feed blackout so nobody can do this again. The Lemig Sortion is punished for cheating, the ceasefire ends early, and Carl goes home.

beats.headline: Not a wake-up salve
beats.text: Out loud, for whoever is listening, I say I'm going to pull him out with a Shock Wake salve, adjusted to work on a non-corporeal form. That's not what I'm making. I know we're being watched from outside, so what I actually brew is something to violently expel the spider from him. Not a wake-up salve at all. It's a risky move. I put it on his see-through chest, and he buckles.

beats.headline: Inside him, and not staying quiet
beats.text: Field ruling, ninth floor. Commander Stockade of the Lemig Sortion tried to pull Crawler Carl bodily to his position. Mordecai, at the same moment, tried to force Shi Maria out of him. Each got half. What came of it is Shi Maria loose in the Lemig base, and the mess she made there, which the adjutant Panford has been left to explain to everyone. Stockade looked into her eye. Stockade is no longer with us, by his own hand. The Lemig Sortion is being punished for cheating, and the ceasefire is over early.

beats.headline: The rampage through the Lemig base
beats.text: Stockade tries to pull Carl bodily to his position while Mordecai tries to force her out of him. What comes of it is hers, and the adjutant Panford is left explaining the wreckage.

beats.headline: A blackout for everyone
beats.text: Sir Ferdinand proposes an emergency action item, in language unsuitable for the broadcast, because teams on other floors are cheating: nobody in the dungeon, including the guests partying in the centipede on the eighteenth floor, may watch any outside feed for the rest of the game. It is approved. Effective immediately, everyone in the dungeon is under a live-feed blackout. Carl had not wanted to spend one of his own action items on it. Victory notes that it is a first.

beats.headline: Heir to the Sortion
beats.text: A minor quorum of adjutants finds the Madness and the Princess Posse not guilty of the conspiracy the Lemig Sortion has already confessed to. Baroness Victory calls Architect Houston obviously guilty and votes not culpable anyway. Then the Sortion's warlord dies, the team is defeated, and because the defeat was voluntary, its assets go to the closest ally. System Message: all assets of the Lemig Sortion have been awarded to the Madness. Phase One combat engages.

beats.headline: Disconnect Containment
beats.text: Christmas morning, at the gas station, beside the memory ghost of Lightning Lou, I open the containment interface I got for Paulie's plastic tub. Not one button. Six tabs. On the Fuse page: five benchmarks, two met, and Override Conditions And Activate Fuse. I want to press it more than anything. I think of Donut. I miss you too. Then, at the end of a list, Disconnect Containment: the fuse and the failsafe go inert. Which hurts the Syndicate most, and which protects my people most? I press it. The red dot over Earth starts to grow.

beats.headline: Soul Poisoning, again
beats.text: Ten miles to the southern front, and the patch on my jacket is glowing again. Mordecai said not to keep it on long. We need the power. A pang across my stomach, a ringing in my ears. Three kids in metal skull caps run out with training spears to join us. The chariot won't take the missile launcher: I've used up my allotted Armor options. Holger sends the kids back with Jamal. Another pang. Soul Poisoning. Activate Daughter's Kiss to disperse the effect.

beats.headline: The handshake completes
beats.text: In Orren's zero zone, Carl asks whether Paulie ever made it into the dungeon. No, says Orren; most of them never do, and the parts of a collective mind are often disposable. Then the notice: Containment Interface is now available for use, as a new tab. Carl changes his request and asks to be sent to the gas station with the memory ghost of the dog, and sits beside Lightning Lou with a bag of chips and a soda. I could end it all right now, he thinks.

beats.headline: Two buttons, one pressed
beats.text: There is no single Boom button. There are six tabs of numbers in a language that is not quite Syndicate standard, and the controls are for the device that installed the AI into the primal engine, not the AI itself. Carl screenshots everything. The Fuse page lists five benchmarks, two met, and a button: Override Conditions And Activate Fuse. At the end of a list sits the only other thing he can press: Disconnect Containment, which renders the failsafe inert. He weighs which hurts the Syndicate most and protects his people most, and presses Disconnect. The red dot over Earth starts to grow.

beats.headline: A reply to Justice Light
beats.text: Crawler Drakea, twenty-second edition, writes beneath a note of Justice Light's in the cookbook. Justice Light wrote that of all the NPCs he killed, he killed one out of anger, that it haunts him, and that he has become what he hates. Drakea answers that his traps have saved Drakea more times than can be counted, that a big one is under construction from his seeking flechette design, and that it was not his fault. They put him here. Let them know fear.

beats.headline: It is done
beats.text: The throne rooms lock in place, and every one of them shows on the map now. Carl asks in chat whether I had ours prepared before it locked. It is done. The rest of the project I am building with the sluggalos. They do not mind the idea of accidentally tripping a trap and being skewered. It is not finished yet.

beats.headline: I am doing my part
beats.text: I AM DOING MY PART IN THE WAR, CARL. I sneaked onto the plane, and Carl says I'm not a scout and I'll tear a Samantha-sized hole in it at the border. FINE. Louis and I will crash together and build a log cabin, and he will grow a scraggly beard that smells like a campfire. Then Carl tells Louis to dump me out of the bomb bay. No, WAIT. Louis can just come back. It's a suicide mission. I like him more than Charlie. I don't want him to die yet.

beats.headline: The Gurgles, allowed
beats.text: A crawler with a flamethrower says the Gurgles is a magical attack and this is bullshit. It is an exploit. They infected the pets before the magic ban, and it has been allowed in the past. The mages ought to do a better job of keeping infections out. The Princess asks what the Gurgles are: a nasty, contagious, incurable debuff, which the factions agreed many years ago never to use again. It caused the insanity and the rabies. The truck stop pill I am not familiar with. I suspect it made them so big.

beats.headline: Kill them, keep the body
beats.text: The orders I send out on the southern front: if we capture an enemy and can keep them alive but unconscious, we do. The NPCs and the mercenaries from outside get separated. There are spells that can turn the NPCs to our side. The mercenaries have another purpose. If one gives trouble, or it isn't safe to keep them, kill them, loot them by the safe-looting protocol, keep the body, and report it up the chain. The Prism scout who flooded one of our tunnels was one of D'Nadia's own relatives. He stepped on a landmine running away.

beats.headline: In the southern push
beats.text: Carl and Donut join the defence in the south, and across the no-man's-land the Nagas hold the line beside the Dream and the Prism. Cobra-headed, and playing under the name of the Blood Sultanate, taken from a bloodier time in their own history.

beats.headline: None of my spells work
beats.text: The periscope screens have amazing resolution, much better than the stolen television in Carl's living room. Everything from a pawn shop is stolen, Carl. Then the pets come out of the fog, rot sticker behemoths as big as cars, full of the Gurgles, and I am feeling very useless all of a sudden. None of my spells work. Wait, Love Vampire works! It doesn't work on pets.

beats.headline: Rot stickers with the Gurgles
beats.text: The southern defence is already holding against the Dream, the Prism and the Nagas when the Reavers make their contribution: a horde of their own pet rot stickers, raised by hand to trust their masters, then juiced, infected and turned loose. This is a power that fights by handing you something diseased and standing back.

beats.headline: Blow the line
beats.text: Katia finished my chair. Two parts. A crab body for walls and short sprints, and a battle shell that closes over it up to a helmet, so much metal I can't carry a ranged weapon or the system calls me armour. The pets hit the dirt wall. I call for my moles. They go down the holes and come back faster than expected. Fire in the hole. The whole line goes up, and the dirt hangs over us on the shields. We set those explosives two hours ago. We were saving them.

beats.headline: Always the first to fall
beats.text: The naga castle sits about eight miles from the border, on rocky ground chosen so nobody can tunnel in from below, and strangely close to Shanty Town. Historically it is almost always the first castle to fall. But every time, by the time the invaders reach the inner sanctum, the Sultana is gone. The team still loses its throne room. Its leader has never once been captured or assassinated since she took over, and she reappears at the end, laughing and joking. Nobody knows where she hides.

beats.headline: A pickled bulldog with elf ears
beats.text: Subject: Boomer. Elven Legate. Level 62. Colonel in the Princess Posse, commanding the 106th Bloody Leeches. A grizzled elf who survived one of the earliest seasons, bowed out on the tenth floor, and lived as a merchant on the sixth for many seasons before escaping. Crawler Carl's description is a bulldog pickled for five thousand years with elf ears and a cigar. Banned from CrawlCon for threatening an orcish showrunner during a panel.
