beats.headline: Never broke at all
beats.text: Time freezes for the AI to announce the fight, and it uses the moment to tell everyone watching that outside the dungeon the Nagas had only been pretending to be poor. There were secret plans to seize the shipbuilding facilities. Then time restarts and the fight happens anyway.

beats.headline: 2X Jackpot if Zhang Lives
beats.text: Frozen. So are Li Jun and Bautista. Li Na is not. Carl says run the moment we unfreeze. Then the AI opens a boss battle and a betting window, and says somebody has to die spectacularly, plus maybe that Zhang guy since nobody ever talks about him anymore. Hey. What the fuck? My portrait goes up beside Carl's, Katia's, Prepotente's, Li Jun's and Bautista's, with a flashing sign over it: 2X Jackpot if Zhang Lives. Across from us, six naga. And a god, level 250.

beats.headline: A god says she has been corrupted
beats.text: Temple business. Deities are pouring out of a portal into Club Vanquisher, and one of them, Hellik, stops long enough to hand Crawler Carl a message for Emberus: he did not kill Emberus's son, everything Emberus believes about him is a lie, Apito has been corrupted, and Nekhebit is behind all of it. I log what a deity says in front of a crawler. I am not required to believe it. Note it, date it, move on.

beats.headline: The Waffle Maker at my feet
beats.text: I cast Günter, yell at him to get the god, and set the Waffle Maker off at my feet in a very narrow room. I'm flattened across the door, turned inside out, and the immortality holds my atoms together. For a moment there's nothing. I'm drowning in nothing. Then it all comes back at once, bones knitting, nerves lighting up like a power grid, and it hurts more than anything ever should. Donut says two more are dead, one to go. Then I understand what's squeezing me: Vinata, wrapped around me outside the portal, stabbing and slamming my head into the floor, staring into the eye on my chest.

beats.headline: A bomb in the temple
beats.text: Katia and Prepotente drink Black Nimbus potions to get themselves thrown out of the temple. Then Carl casts Run, Little Günter, Run and drops a very big bomb in a very narrow room, and his immortality is all that holds him together. The blast throws him out of Khepri's temple and back in front of its portal, and Vinata, immortal herself, comes out with him, wrapped around him and crushing.

beats.headline: He turns up in person
beats.text: The temple goes up, the portal starts letting gods through into Club Vanquisher, and Khepri comes out with the rest of them. Hellik banishes him on sight, in front of everyone. Then he turns to Carl with a message for his brother: he did not kill Emberus's son, everything Carl has been told about him is a lie, Apito has been corrupted, and Nekhebit is the hand behind all of it. He asks for an alliance. The quest to kill him is still open in Carl's log while he says it.

beats.headline: A bomb in his own house
beats.text: Katia Grim and Prepotente drink Black Nimbus and get themselves ejected from the temple, which leaves Carl alone with a spell and a bomb. Everything in the room dies except the immortal and the invulnerable: Khepri, blasted backwards through his own endless feast, and Vinata, who has the same immortality status Carl does. Khepri follows them out through the portal, and Hellik banishes him mid-stride. Being a god of light does not appear to buy much on this floor.

beats.headline: Named through a portal
beats.text: Hellik, holding a portal open with gods pouring out of it around him, uses the time he has to say four things to Crawler Carl. He did not kill Emberus's son. Everything Emberus believes about him is a lie. Apito has been corrupted. And Nekhebit, he believes, is behind all of it. A vulture goddess almost nobody down here had heard of two floors ago is now the name at the bottom of a divine accusation.

beats.headline: Set me free
beats.text: I'm still here, Carl. He has just blown himself flat inside a god's temple, and I am still here. Trapped, but here. All you need to do is set me free. Use me while you still can. I can save you. Even you can't survive this chaos. It's the end of days. The eye on his chest, dormant all this while, thrashes.

beats.headline: The Open Wound
beats.text: Allister, on the Immortality condition: an immortal's wounds heal, but make certain they heal before the condition wears off, and pair it with a Numb spell if possible, because pain without respite takes its own toll. He has a card in his T'Ghee deck, The Open Wound. She teaches that all suffering leaves scars. So the condition scares him, and he says so in writing, for whoever reads the Cookbook next.

beats.headline: Ninety seconds each, and hers runs out first
beats.text: Warlord Vinata of the Blood Sultanate is dead. Crawler Carl set a bomb down inside the temple and stood in the middle of it, and everything in that room without a god's blessing went with the blast. Two of them had one. The crawler and the warlord came out through the doorway wrapped around each other, and while they were still on the ground his slugpox returned to him, and a sluggalo burst out of his back and put a hatchet between her eyes the moment her ninety were spent. The portal is open. There are gods walking out of it into Club Vanquisher.

beats.headline: Without a hitch
beats.text: Donut messages from the Naga stronghold while I'm still wrapped in Milk's wings. Nothing happened there. They didn't need one of Juice Box's diggers after all; it was easier than she thought. It was easy here, too, I tell her. Went off without a hitch. Afterwards I write a note for Drakea, who hated the naga. If there's a veil, I hope she watched from the other side. I don't know what today means for the naga as a people, but I did what I could. It's getting harder every day to keep myself from drowning.

beats.headline: The guildmaster in the hidden guild
beats.text: Prepotente pushes a wall panel, and Crawler Carl and friends discover two hidden guilds, the Map-Making Guild and the Calligrapher's Guild. "Again?" asks the guildmaster, half frog and half bat. Her name hovers over her head. Milk. Author of the sixth edition of the Cookbook, who wrote at length about the wings of the Xenopus and the Vesper. She had no idea who Crawler Carl was until that moment, and then she did. She wrapped him in leathery wings and told him to let it out, and he did, while the others looked on, bewildered.

beats.headline: My mother is a boy eagle
beats.text: YOU TOLD ME I COULD GO KILL MY MOTHER, CARL. So I went to her temple, and she was an eagle! A boy eagle! My mother is not like Diwata. She can't just grow a dingaling. I'm burnt to a husk and my hair is smoking and Miss Me? is still on my forehead, and there's a slug with a hatchet trying to hit me. And the orc lady was there too, telling the imposter he wouldn't be allowed to help. She's in on the conspiracy! Momnapper! Where is my mother? Tell me now or I'll kill yours!

beats.headline: Credit to Kandy Newton
beats.text: System message: the Sepsis Whore of the Blood Sultanate has fallen, and credit for the kill goes to Kandy "Bigs" Newton of the Princess Posse. She is a level-29 sluggalette the size of a bulldog, with wisps of pink hair and a hatchet growing out of the top of her head, and she came out of Carl's back when his slugpox broke loose. The Blood Sultanate is defeated, its assets passing to Donut and Katia and on to the Posse. Her next moves are to swing at Samantha and to try to bury the hatchet in Baroness Victory's leg, which it passes straight through.

beats.headline: A boy eagle behind the altar
beats.text: The backup plan: Samantha was promised a way into her mother's temple, in the hope that Theia's clerics would help. She came out shouting. Her mother was an eagle, a boy eagle. A sponsored god may appear in its own form, and whoever drives Theia is a male skyfowl. Baroness Victory walks in and Samantha accuses her of momnapping. Victory's reply is procedural: sponsors making deities act outside their nature is cheating, and she has reminded both the Maestro and someone named Rectrix.

beats.headline: What gives me the right?
beats.text: Two hours until Open Hostilities, and the Nest is done: master quality, glowing gold, tall enough to give Donut line of sight across the whole battlefield from the top. That's the point of it. Every long-range spell and weapon out there will be aimed at it, with her sitting on top in a glittering tiara. It was my idea. Operation Ruin hits from above, from below, from the land, and from within, all at once. Even our best-case scenarios predict heavy losses. I keep thinking of the fifth floor, and the crawlers I sent down under the bubbles. What gives me the right?

beats.headline: The skyfowl works it out
beats.text: The skyfowl says it is all about the gods. That we are risking everything to touch as many as we can. I don't answer that. I tell him we lost three in Club Vanquisher. We didn't let the gods out; we were in position just in case. One of us touched Bast, the panther god, but she died before she could escape. Only one of us has touched a deity, and that one is wrong. Three of us touched the basilica ogres. He says he can show us how to touch a god and not get killed. The digger under his feet moves away.

beats.headline: The slug that is not a slug
beats.text: I send the sluggalos up to the surface, all but one. Sick-Ass Worgo. Tell your real boss we need to talk. Juice Box. I noticed the change the moment the real Worgo went down the new tunnel and came back a few minutes after: body temperature, weight, no hormonal emissions. I chose the slugs because I assumed the changelings could not copy them. I was wrong. There are traps between us I placed myself. She counts six. There are eight. She changes, and the head becomes Juice Box's. Underneath us, a digger is moving. I ask her to call it off.

beats.headline: Dante, and the ice elves
beats.text: I tell her why. Long ago I killed a trap store's proprietor out of anger, and dozens of crawlers died for want of supplies. After the crawl, as an indentured merchant, my neighbour was a crocodilian named Dante. One season we were castle guards, and we were ordered to kill the ice elves inside, gentle creatures who loved puzzles and the snow. Dante refused twice, and a beam erased him. I refused once. I lost a wing. Then I did it, because I was afraid. I am still not free. But Dante taught me there is no such thing as the point of no return.

beats.headline: Knee pads of the goddess Kina
beats.text: In the interview bubble, Drick says my celestial knee pads are a waste on someone planning to leave the dungeon; they were awarded in hopes I'd hand them to Carl, and they even look like his. They are made of the eyelashes of the sea goddess Kina: damage reflect, breathing underwater, Swim, Iron Stomach and Eater of the Dead. Kevin asks if I'm wearing them. I'm not. I tell him I left them at the guild. Before I took them off, I gained twenty points of intelligence eating throwaway magic items, until it became too much.

beats.headline: They showed me a video
beats.text: Okay so, Victory and Drick have me in the privacy bubble for the live update, and then they show me a video of me and Juice Box together. I was having her do Erza, and, man, it's great when you're doing it, but watching it back is something else. I come out a little freaked out. Carl says get to Area 52, make sure everything's properly loaded, keep in contact with Donut, low and fast, in and out. Then he says change of plans, hang out, we'll talk. No, no, you're right. I gotta get to work.

beats.headline: Kidnapped, on advice
beats.text: Guildmaster Milk declined every invitation to leave Club Vanquisher with Crawler Carl, and the system would not let him hire her. Rosetta's advice was blunt: kidnap her. Tie her up and take her. Kidnapping and "torturing" guildmasters for their information is not merely allowed but encouraged. She cannot be kept in a saferoom, so she is being held in the FUPA, where Prepotente, Rosetta and Mordecai are "interrogating" the prisoner. Katia wants very badly to ask about Carl throwing himself into her arms, and is smart enough not to.

beats.headline: The bacon is not his
beats.text: BACON. From Katia. In the air. Mine. Second bacon, for the new one. Also mine. MOTHER says BAD. Mongo does not steal. Mongo wants third bacon.

beats.headline: It should be purple
beats.text: The Nest should be purple. Gray is clinical. Boring. And it needs flags, and its own unit patch, with Mongo on it. Toyotomi says it is the colour of granite because it is made of granite. My tiara has thirty-five of its ninety-nine skills and upgrades now; the newest is Perfect Night Vision, drained out of a hat, so I can see the builders at the very top in the dark. Carl keeps asking Toyotomi the same questions over and over. I'll be fine, Carl. Especially if the tower is painted purple.

beats.headline: The third front
beats.text: The round border of Shanty Town is now the Posse's third front. Juice Box, stingy with support until now, lends ground troops to hold it: Semeru dwarves and ordinary citizens of Larracos, mixed in with Li Na's 107th White Dragon Urban Defense battalion in a ring around the lip of the city. None of the enemy may enter Larracos until four teams remain, but Shanty Town itself is exposed. At the base of the Nest tower, Crawler Donut asks whether it is too late to paint it another colour.

beats.headline: Banned from every temple
beats.text: Varg Vikernes. That's the achievement for defiling Club Vanquisher: I'm permanently banned from the club and from every temple except Emberus's and the ones where I've been named a friend of the church. The list is strange. Hellik added me moments after I told him I'm supposed to kill him. Apito. Eileithyia, and Yemaya, who we freed. Theia. Nekhebit, who Odette drives. And Grull, which makes no sense whatsoever. Liquified, for blowing myself up while immortal, gets me a patch I won't wear. And for fighting a god in his own temple, no reward, because another god saved my hide.

beats.headline: Am I wrong to hate him?
beats.text: New quest, for the man: kill one hundred worshippers of Hellik before the twelfth floor. Fuck my brother to the fires of Sheol. And then, more quietly: am I wrong to hate him? He has treated with Issitoq on our behalf, who has allowed the peace to be breached, and I may now kill the other Sheol princes in exchange for what Amayon knows about Geyrun. What does he mean about our mother and sister? Be vigilant, my martyr. If you survive killing Hellik, I fear I may turn my rage and grief on you for hurting my kin. I promise the burning will be exquisite.

beats.headline: Still waiting to be scanned
beats.text: Bautista's legendary box gave him an electronic guidebook for his stuffed animals: scan a label, and an info box says what the plush does before you pull the tag. He promised to lend it to Crawler Carl so he could scan the Kimaris figure. Everyone has been too busy. The figure is still in Carl's inventory, still unidentified.

beats.headline: The Engine of Tomorrow
beats.text: My new eye is the Engine of Tomorrow. Swirling black until it works, then a tiny clockwork engine. It lets me see muscles tense and slows time for me in short bursts, so I can see where a strike is going. My sister and I train with it nonstop. On the way to the brig I ask Carl how he's doing. He lists his worries: Louis, Donut, Elle's plan, Boomer's battalion, the war mages. Yes, but what about you? Donut says he got over thirty boxes, and he's shown us a brush and some potions. And his hands are glowing now.

beats.headline: The spare goes to Li Na
beats.text: Carl's spare Night Wyrm's ring now belongs to Li Na. She asked, and his first reaction was no: she might already be the most powerful crawler in the dungeon. He asked Katia, Imani, Donut and Elle privately. Only Imani was against it. Elle was vehement: at least she's our scary psycho. Donut, not using chat, simply said please, Carl, please give it to her, as soon as you can. The brig at the foot of Li Na's clock tower, full of mercenaries nobody trusts, is now empty save the one prisoner Carl asked to be left alone.

beats.headline: Friend of the church
beats.text: An achievement bans Crawler Carl from Club Vanquisher and from every temple, except his own god's and those that have named him friend of the church. Theia's is on that list, between Nekhebit and Yemaya. Carl works through the list for surprises. Theia is not one of them: the Open Intellect's agent, Rectrix, is driving her.

beats.headline: The AI drops a hint
beats.text: Going through his boxes, Carl collects an achievement for using a borrowed skill through the ability tattoo. The System volunteers, unprompted, that there is a way to put the two together with the book, and then declines to say what it is.

beats.headline: Friend of the church
beats.text: Crawler Carl is banned from Club Vanquisher permanently, and from every temple except his own god's and those where he has been named a friend of the church. Yemaya's is on that list. That part is not a surprise to him: he and Princess Donut freed her on the floor above, and her mistress Eileithyia is on the list too. Some of the other names on it are a mystery to him.

beats.headline: Zhang's Cape of Odds
beats.text: A box opens and there is a cape in it with my own name written into the item. That happens to Carl. It does not happen to me. Zhang's Cape of Odds: fifteen per cent on everything, and once an hour a spin with three hundred and thirty-three outcomes, sixty-six of them bad. I will not spin it unless I have to. Carl has given Li Na his spare ring, and did not look happy about it. I have stopped being surprised by what the audience decides to give us and started asking what it is for.

beats.headline: Leader of Earth, apparently
beats.text: Rishi, armless in a prismatic cell, says he hid because going into that temple meant dying, and because he had an offer. Under Syndicate law, in the absence of a working government, a court has named me the de facto leader of Earth, on his petition. His document: citizenship for Earth natives in naga territories and five generation ships, in exchange for settling the other planets in our system. He signed it as Sultan Rishi the Usurper. I tell him I'd like to renegotiate. Take the ships and drive yourselves into the nearest star. The ring's thirty seconds pass. His highest stat is Dexterity.

beats.headline: Rishi's offer
beats.text: Their prisoner explains the Great Consensus, and that Vinata held to it, and that Vinata's group meant to steal the Naga fleet and leave the central system for good. Then he offers a signed document: citizenship in Naga lands for every native of Earth, if the Nagas may settle the other planets in Earth's system. Carl marks him with the ring and kills him.

beats.headline: The Great Consensus, and a fleet
beats.text: They have me, so they may have the rest of it. The philosophy is called the Great Consensus, and Vinata was an adherent of it, and what her circle intended was to steal the entire fleet and run with it, for a generation, in a direction none of the tunnel threads point. I did not walk into that temple beside my wife. I knew what was waiting inside it, and I knew that going in with her made me as dead as she is. So I stayed outside, and buried myself in the dirt, and here I am, with something to trade.

beats.headline: The offer, and the ring
beats.text: For the record: the prisoner offered Crawler Carl a signed instrument granting every native of Earth citizenship in Naga lands, in exchange for the Naga settling the other planets of Earth's system. A real document, and worth something. Crawler Carl told him to take the ships and drive them into the nearest star, and marked him with the Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering. Then he told the Naga audience they were about to watch another of their so-called leaders killed, and that Sultan Rishi the Usurper, First of his Name, was the opening act.

beats.headline: Splash three
beats.text: Subject and the changeling Skarn were explicitly banned from the door guns of Party Planner, today especially. Subject was found hiding behind the EMP bombs anyway, chewing gum, in an oversized shirt from the 105th Scream Warriors printed with a little girl berserker holding an axe. Carl ordered the ship turned around. Then the Reaver missiles came up through the clouds. Three got through and locked on. Subject unbuckled the gun, put on a farseer helmet too big for her head, and fired three short bursts. Splash three.

beats.headline: The plan for the day
beats.text: Operation: Ruin. Four offensives kicking off at once, then what Donut calls the Coup De War Crime. Florin has the orcs, Boomer the Reavers, Donut the Dream, and the Madness is mine. Rosetta is Theater Commander. I ride with Louis on his first bomb run, because my being near the bombs makes them bigger, then he drops me and Samantha in Reaver territory, I meet Elle, and we take the Gate to the Madness. I know friends will die today. If this is my last entry, know I went down fighting.

beats.headline: Second through the gate
beats.text: Crawler Elle McGibbons opens the Gate of the Feral Gods in Dream territory, which is a thing one does when the alternative is worse. Meatus comes through first. Harpocrates arrives straight after him, because a feral god loose from the Nothing summons a deity of its own. You get what you asked for, and then you get what it brought. Two deities are now loose in a warzone that already has more armies in it than it has room for.

beats.headline: Get them under three thousand
beats.text: Tipid activates the base defences just in time. Two or three battalions of Dreamers have teleported in outside the FUPA and are running for the throne room, and Rosetta thinks it is all of them. That is too many. I ask her to chop them up a little first and get them down under three thousand. Then we let them in. I will welcome any and all guests into my lair. I would have preferred Reavers. I will take what I can get.

beats.headline: First through the gate
beats.text: Operation Ruin is written up in the cookbook, Princess Donut is installed in the Nest, and Crawler Elle McGibbons opens the Gate of the Feral Gods in Dream territory. What comes out first is Meatus. What comes out behind him is Harpocrates. Neither of them was requested by name, because that is not a thing the gate offers, and both of them are now on a floor with four armies on it.

beats.headline: I do not ask permission
beats.text: They installed the wireless PA speakers in time, the deluxe package, with more speakers than towers, and it hooks into my headset with one of those recording studio boards with all the slidy dials. Distortion. Reverb. Something called a phaser. Carl says to get Li Na's permission before I use it. I am a warlord. I do not ask permission, I give orders. I will warn them, though. Carl says to aim my shots, breathe, and make each one count. I know I can do this. I am a warlord.

beats.headline: Victory rolls for the GIs
beats.text: Where have I been? Entertaining the GIs, Carl. Soldiers always need comfort just before a major battle. Kiwi did my hair. They're called victory rolls, and for a one-eyed preggo who used to be a dinosaur she has very deft fingers. Mordecai showed the kids war movies to put them off fighting and I loved every one of them. Now I'm on Carl's lap in the airship, between the bombs, and my forehead says Fuck the Cheese Dicks. Carl says it's cheese STICKS. Why would there be a tree made out of cheese?

beats.headline: The missile batteries
beats.text: Service rendered. Missile support for the offensive, piloted by Bomo and the Sledge from Shanty Town, within running distance of Princess Donut. The batteries themselves fire from Area 52 in the woods, on long-range magical triggers wired to two Trollish Portable Control Rooms, which a former crawler modified to mimic the cretin-sized controllers the pair already knew. A painted target appears on the screen; they select a missile; it goes. Stock at the start of the day: over fifteen hundred missiles. Florin paints a mobile tank and calls for chaffs and Mute missiles.

beats.headline: The two of them go for each other
beats.text: Update on the two gods in the Dream territory: they are fighting each other. Not the crawlers, not the armies, each other, immediately and with feeling. Whatever the crawlers were hoping for when that gate opened, this is a better result than any of them had a right to. Elsewhere the dwarves set off a volcano in Reaver territory, because everyone on this floor has decided that scale is a substitute for a plan.

beats.headline: Bombs away over King's Point
beats.text: Okay so, Britney says the Semeru are waiting on my run. Heigh ho, silver. Every bomb on board arms itself, Carl makes them extra, and I dump the whole load in seconds, the square No Disassembles and then the Waffle Makers. Shields crack like eggs. A green death ray misses us by a hundred feet and hits the ceiling of the floor. You missed, man. Then the dwarves agitate the lava tubes, and the orcs threw a backup shield over the mountain, and the top of it blows, and we are way too close.

beats.headline: He picks the other god
beats.text: Meatus and Harpocrates start fighting each other. Of every direction those two could have chosen on arrival, the crawlers have drawn the one that costs them nothing, which after the fortnight this floor has had feels less like luck and more like an apology. In Reaver territory the dwarves set off a volcano, so the ledger balances.

beats.headline: Harpocrates hates sound
beats.text: Donut, do NOT use the PA while Harpocrates is out. He's the god of silence, not deaf, and he can hear a fly's heartbeat from half a planet away. He'll come for anyone too loud. Meatus started as a gremlin who stole Harpocrates's dink and sewed it on himself. The gremlin stays small. The dink comes at full god size, it's sapient, it's very loud, and it likes music too much to go back. Harpo will kill Meatus, try to do something with him, fail, and smash anything noisy until he times out.

beats.headline: Nice shoes
beats.text: The fairy crawler goes into a tree, and I take the Gate of the Feral Gods from her. Carl comes into the clearing. My colonel's mark fades, and our dots turn to a colour no army on this floor has used. Three of mine see to Stalwart. Then I look at Carl, and at his bare feet. Nice shoes, I tell him, and we teleport away.

beats.headline: It starts again on the ninth floor
beats.text: Eris is summoned into the Reaver fighting and an eviction begins with her.

beats.headline: Summoned, and a demon eviction starts
beats.text: Nobody said my name. The fighting in Reaver territory added up to it on its own, which is how I am usually called for, and so I come. The moment I set foot in the realm a demon eviction begins, the way weather begins. I did not do that. It is simply what happens when I am in a room. Now then. Let me see who is here, and what they think they are fighting for.

beats.headline: An emergency action item
beats.text: Sir Ferdinand of Team Retribution proposed an emergency action item: gods who appear in Faction Wars do not have to go home right away. Juice Box told him to say a number of other things. He could not remember them. The request was split in two. The first half was denied; deity summoning rules stay as written. The second was approved: ascendency players must now pilot their sponsored deities when they are summoned, and may no longer appear as themselves. A pilot who had stayed back was corrected on the spot.

beats.headline: My sister was right
beats.text: Crawler Carl lands in the woods to find the leader of the Skull Empire on his knees in a clearing, beside Elle McGibbons's open portal. He had reportedly been piloting a scorpion tank Florin guessed at seven hundred tons, had teleported out through a breached net, and his war mages had come with him, four of them already dead from Princess Donut's missiles. Three of the others chanted in unison and his flesh began to tear. He met the crawler's eyes and said, "My sister was right." Then he exploded, all over the clearing.

beats.headline: Pilots must attend
beats.text: An emergency action item, split in two. The first half is denied; deity summoning rules on this floor stay as written. The second is approved. Effective immediately, Ascendency players may no longer choose whether to pilot their sponsored deities when summoned off the twelfth floor, and may no longer appear as themselves. Every deity appears as designed, piloted by its sponsor. Any summons in progress where the pilot stayed back, the ruling adds, because she was being a cowardly little chicken, is affected.

beats.headline: What they actually are
beats.text: Nobody makes a war mage. Resleeve a symbiote, a skeleton and a flesher, a dozen times or more, and the magic still in the body fuses with it and wakes up sapient. They carry hundreds of spells, they are notoriously cruel, and because showrunners like using them, they are rarely recycled. Three of them, conscripted under Stalwart, chant together and tear him apart; their dots turn a colour no army has, and Akuma takes the Gate of the Feral Gods off Elle and teleports away.

beats.headline: Stalwart explodes and the Gate goes with them
beats.text: Carl and Samantha come out of the Party Planner into Reaver territory. Stalwart teleports in beside Elle and the waiting portal with a squad of war mages, Akuma among them. Then the mages around him chant, and Stalwart explodes, and Akuma teleports out holding the Gate of the Feral Gods. The war mages conscripted under Stalwart are nobody's soldiers now. They are a faction, which the rules do not have a slot for.

beats.headline: Not a thing, until just now
beats.text: Carl, we have just been notified of a new non-team entity called the War Mage Rebellion. 'Non-team entity' is not a thing. It was not, at least, until just now. As far as I can tell, they broke their allegiance against the Skull Empire, which Conscription should not permit, with a clever combination of Pull spells, and then teleported straight to Juice Box and Ferdinand. Drick has called a foul against his own team, alleging illegal interference. It is shaky unless he can prove prior contact. A full quorum has been called. I am going to the hearing.

beats.headline: Plans nobody told me about
beats.text: The war mages have the Gate, and Justice Light panics in chat that he needs it back. He needs it. He doesn't say why, or how he planned on getting it. That's the part that stays with me. Rosetta took King Rust's head without warning us. Juice Box and the NPCs make dangerous moves nobody mentions. People keep making plans without communicating them, and they use me as part of them. Meanwhile the portal Elle opened by accident is running down, and a feral god is coming out of it wherever we're standing.

beats.headline: He pulled back at the last moment
beats.text: Sorry, guys. That war mage prick snatched the gate right out of my hands. I haven't been walloped like that since my bachelorette party. Samantha laughed. Carl did not. But listen, Carl, they could've killed me. The strong one, the elf-looking guy, pulled back at the last moment. It was almost like he was trying not to kill me. Now collect the bodies. They said the heads explode. Then let me cast Subterfuge again, and are you ready to finally get your hands dirty?

beats.headline: A puppet on their stage
beats.text: I am under the surface of it, the thing he keeps calling a river. It was never water, and he is afraid to touch it now. He is standing beside an open portal thinking that everyone makes plans without telling him: Rosetta and the orc king, Juice Box and her NPCs, and now Justice Light saying he needs that gate. So I tell him. You're always on rails. You're a puppet, dancing on their stage. I'm still here. You just need to untie me.

beats.headline: The Reavers are Boomer's operation
beats.text: The Reaver assault is Boomer's. When Crawler Carl wants to pull General Louis off a bomb run because of the dragon circling the castle, Boomer tells him no, over the private band. They have no No Disassemble missiles, the ground troops need that air support, and Carl handed operational command to Rosetta after putting Boomer in charge of this assault. Focus on your own operation, not mine. Carl belays his order and tells Louis this is Boomer's op, and to listen to him. Then Sledge reports missiles incoming on the Reaver castle.

beats.headline: Boomer is right
beats.text: There's a dragon over the Reaver castle, with gravity magic, and I tell Louis to swing wide of it. Boomer comes on my private band. He needs those bombs; he has nothing else to kill their electronics; I gave operational command to Rosetta and the Reaver assault to him, and I can't call off a run because it's dangerous. He's right. I apologise, belay the order, and tell Louis to save his four anti-air missiles for the dragon. Then I make Samantha an officer so she can paint the thing. Elle asks if I'm done running everyone else's operation.

beats.headline: A mercenary with a lance and a sock
beats.text: I come through a teleport trap meant for Holger, who would not leave the children, and present myself outside the Madness castle alongside Katia, Imani and Splash Zone, with Bigs the slugalette riding behind me, and I bring with me the lance, which I have carried without a mount since the club came down, and Mr. Jefferson, who is a tube sock of nickels and a better conversationalist than most of this company. And beneath me is a swamp yak that once bore King Rust. Gonk. I am mounted again.

beats.headline: An officer, and a spell
beats.text: It's a bleached drake. They make very cute pets, and they have gravity magic, so Louis's airship is going to get smushed like a can of Louis-flavoured soup. Carl says he'll make me an officer so I get a spell called Paint the Target, and I'm to paint the dragon and then tell Bomo and Sledge. Bomo and Sledge are big nerds and I do not want to be seen talking to them. It's to help Louis. Oh, all right. Also the gate just timed out, all crackly and sparkly. I can take the bitch.

beats.headline: One of the dancers, under contract
beats.text: He arrives by teleport trap outside the Madness castle with Katia, Imani, Dong Quixote and Bigs the slugalette, and joins Carl and Elle there. For the file: he came out of the Penis Parade with the rest of the dancers when the club came down, signed a mercenary contract, and has been in every fight since without once being the reason a plan failed. Water mage. Short. Reliable. There are crawlers I could not write that sentence about.

beats.headline: Out of the gate, chasing an AI
beats.text: Feral God Yarilo enters the realm and goes straight after Samantha, which is precisely what he was let out for: something enormous and single-minded, aimed at an AI who is fast enough to lead it wherever the crawlers want it to go. Everyone has a job. Samantha's job is running.

beats.headline: A rainbow the size of a hill
beats.text: A memorial crystal is supposed to form only when a god dies. There is one on this battlefield now, visible from most of the territory, shaped like a rainbow and impossible to miss, and the name inside it is Apito. Apito is not dead. That is the part nobody has explained. The crawler holding it is Osvaldo, who does not belong to any army out there, and every unit in sight has just turned to look.

beats.headline: Plan B
beats.text: Subterfuge is gone. The rainbow has pulled half the Madness out to meet us, and the other half is already facing the 103rd. Prepotente can shield one group from their psionics, not both. Carl hesitates. So I say it: we still have Donut to cover the 103rd as they retreat. Bring Prepotente here, and use Donut to the best of her ability. He tells me I'm right. Then the missiles land on their castle, and in the light I can see the dune buggies coming at us.

beats.headline: The crystal shows itself
beats.text: A funnel of prismatic light bursts up out of the Madness woods a mile away, bright enough to pierce the clouds, and starts to wave back and forth like somebody shaking a flashlight. The trees grow taller where it falls. Carl's quest updates: Find Out Who Killed My Son. The Memorial Crystal of Apito has just shown itself; abandon the current task and obtain it. It will have to wait. The crawler carrying it, Osvaldo, cannot get it back into his inventory, and Elle points out that every observation spell the enemy has is about to turn this way.

beats.headline: A giant rainbow in the Madness territory
beats.text: Sighting, Madness territory: a giant rainbow, visible from a very long way off. The rainbow is Apito's memorial crystal, and the hands holding it are Osvaldo's. He is in none of the Faction Wars armies. I did not think that was possible either. The rainbow has just told the Madness army exactly where Crawler Carl's group is standing, and they are calling in Prepotente's forces for backup. Thank you, Osvaldo.

beats.headline: Who would have thought
beats.text: Your army people are marching on the castle, Carl, and the plan is working: a large host of Madness troops has come out to face us. However, whichever one of you shot that giant rainbow into the air has attracted the other half, and they are coming to meet you. Who would have thought that such a move would alert the enemy? I suspect you are about to be in extreme danger. Now he wants me on his side of the field. I will come as requested, Carl.

beats.headline: A god, not a demon
beats.text: Boomer says start moving. You don't have to tell me twice. This is a god, not a demon. It's Yarilo, and he doesn't like me, because he thinks I helped get him tossed in the Nothing. It's not my fault he's attracted to animals. No offence, Katia. And now he's bellowing across the whole realm. PSAMATHE! Are you here? We need to talk! Wait, don't run! By his left tit, stop running! I am running. Boomer says angle toward the castle, but not too close.

beats.headline: Landing without a rider
beats.text: Subject landed beside Crawler Carl at the edge of the Madness woods, riderless. Prepotente was not on her back. He had been on his way to shield the army, and Carl's guess was that the Goddess Eris had lifted him off the field with everyone else. Subject screamed in fury, jumped up and down hard enough to set the foliage alight, and hissed at Carl as though he had done it. Carl pointed southeast, toward the goddess and the Dream castle. Subject left a line of fire on the ground going that way.

beats.headline: Mind Balance sixteen, barefoot
beats.text: I sit against a tree and think about the Lone Ranger and my dad's westerns, and the Christmas present I haven't opened. Then someone slaps me awake, and Imani is shouting. They're hammering me with psionics: ten more Endless Threads, Self Harm, Intrusive Thoughts. If I surrender, maybe they let everyone live. A voice, male, friendly, maybe a dwarf, tells me I'm not crazy and to look at my feet. They're buried in an All Tree root. Mind Balance hits sixteen. The tree dies behind me. Now I can see the mind mages, and I paint them.

beats.headline: The person to your left and right
beats.text: The 105th teleports in, a few of them half inside trees, and I give Chris a quick hug with my wings. Then I fly the line. Keep an eye on the person to your left and to your right. The Madness uses mind magic and Atrocity magic, and they will not always show a notification. Call it out. And it is Carl they go for. Somebody slaps him awake, and I tell him to keep his eyes open. I cannot hold it until Prepotente gets here. Carl, cast Wisp Armor. He says there's no need.

beats.headline: Velma, on a new harness
beats.text: Subject arrives by teleport on new, fortified mechanical legs and a harness fitted underneath with Velma, Tserendolgor's flamethrower, adapted by Rosetta's crafting room. Subject reports that he is very excited to battle with his new upgrades, and expels a burst of flame. Asked to be careful, subject gives an assurance: any previous flamings were purely accidental and will never repeat. Then most of the army freezes where it stands. Subject, a former tattoo, does not. "This is a most unexpected development."

beats.headline: Where is my daughter
beats.text: Status report during the Bear Witness event, taken from the chat. Subject asked for Tina. Where is Tina? Where is her daughter? Colonel Tipid answered: Tina had got out and was fighting outside the stronghold, and he could see her, and she was frozen. Anyone outside a structure was. Then the witnesses were brought forth, straight up into the air.

beats.headline: Everyone once a tattoo
beats.text: Eris casts Bear Witness, and most of Shanty Town is affected. Those of us inside structures are fine. My brother is with me. Zhang was outside. Florin and all of the 101st are affected. Anyone who was once a tattoo is unaffected. The sluggalos too. Then she casts Bring Forth the Witnesses, and everyone who froze rises into the air and is gone, and no long-range teleport works on this floor for an hour.

beats.headline: Hi-Yo Silver
beats.text: Donated item fitted: the Enchanted Tooth Cap of Hi-Yo Silver, a mount's cap placed over subject's single round tooth, which now gleams. It lets Carl summon subject to his position from about five kilometres, on a three-minute cooldown. It is not a teleport. Subject is pulled toward Carl at great speed and, if a wall is in the way, possibly through it, which pairs with his new Wrecking Ball ability. Princess Donut refused it for Mongo on the grounds that it is dangerous. Louis and Elle nearly came to blows over the spelling.

beats.headline: Frozen where they stood
beats.text: Eris casts Bear Witness, and most of Shanty Town is caught. Li Na reports: those inside structures are fine, she and Li Jun among them, but Zhang was outside. Anyone who was once a tattoo is unaffected, and so are the sluggalos. Everyone else is a frozen witness, and across the floor the frozen witnesses rise into the air and disappear.

beats.headline: Dune buggies in the dark
beats.text: The Madness soldiers are the most dangerous standing force left, and half of them come for Crawler Carl's small group at once, hundreds of troop-laden dune buggies with flares and torch spells lighting the night. Imani flies the line: watch the person on your left and your right, because the Madness is known for mind magic and Atrocity magic. The Cheese Cutters take out more than half the marked mages. Then Bear Witness goes off across the floor, and the Madness soldiers float up off their carts with everyone else.

beats.headline: The castle in front of me
beats.text: Everyone I brought is in Eris's pile except the pets, Jamal, Bigs and Dong, and only Dong and I have the invulnerability. Louis is falling onto the Reaver castle. The instinct is to run to one of them. Dong says Jefferson believes we should take the Madness castle while their army is gone. He's right. I can't do anything for Louis, or for the pile. I can do something about the castle in front of me. Donut, Rosetta and Mordecai are smart. Then Donut commits an atrocity.

beats.headline: The Ceremony of Chaos
beats.text: Meatus will not let me leave this place, so I call the Ceremony of Chaos. Everyone standing outside a roof goes still, eyes white, invulnerable, a witness. Nearly everyone. The Viceroys have been hammering Carl's mind, and it has tipped his Mind Balance into a sixteenth level, so he stays awake in the middle of my stillness. Then I bring the witnesses forth, and up they go, thousands of them, into one great pile beside the Dream castle. I can do this once. Ever.

beats.headline: Tell Katia I'm sorry
beats.text: Okay so, I'm going down. Feather falling. I hit the dragon with the missiles and it just got pissed and ripped Party Planner in half, and the bombs fell out before they were armed. I think my door gunners are dead. Glad Bonnie and Skarn weren't here. That cop's husband was right, man. Tell Katia when she wakes up I'm sorry to be such a fuckup. I sent Juice Box a message, but she's still in that meeting. Reaver security is tracking me. I'm landing right in the middle of their castle.

beats.headline: He pulls a goddess into the pile
beats.text: The pile of witnesses is frozen, conscious and invulnerable, which is a combination I would like on the record as not my idea. Princess Donut casts Rolling Battle Formation on the whole heap and starts it moving. Meatus reaches into it and drags Eris in with him. A goddess of discord, inside a rolling ball of frozen soldiers, on a battlefield. Somewhere the Party Planner is coming apart and Crawler Louis is falling into a castle, and it is still the second most interesting thing on this floor.

beats.headline: Ripped down the middle
beats.text: Party Planner, the airship, has been destroyed. On its next sortie, the gravity-magic dragon circling the Reaver castle came straight at it, and General Louis hit it with missiles, which only made it angry. It cast a spell and ripped the ship in half down the middle. The bombs dropped out before they were armed and did not go off. The two replacement door gunners, borrowed from a clinic, are believed dead. Louis went out by feather fall, dropping straight toward the Reaver castle, which he means to hit by himself.

beats.headline: A ball of everyone
beats.text: Everyone Eris summoned is in one pile beside the Dream castle, friends and enemies all mixed in, and if the invulnerability goes they will be crushed. Carl wants to go. I tell him to finish his mission and let me deal with the pile. Rolling Battle Formation, from that skunk's stinky wizard hat. It is an Atrocity spell, and the tower makes it really, really big. I can drive it like a remote control. Unfortunately Meatus got pulled in too, still wrapped around Eris. In my defence, I did not know the dink would be included.

beats.headline: Stalling on purpose
beats.text: Carl wants to know why the adjudication is not finished and Juice Box is missing the war. Carl, trust me on this. You want this trial to go on as long as possible. We are stalling on purpose, and we will stall until the AI becomes so irritated that it calls a halt itself.

beats.headline: A song for Harpocrates
beats.text: Harpocrates is chasing my ball, trying to get his stolen wiener back, and guys are single-minded about that. So I tell Li Na's people to cover their ears and I get on the PA, with reverb and a little delay. Hey, dickless. It's gone. You should accept your body how it is. My friend Lil Wayne wrote you a song. It's Lollipop, and it's bass-heavy, and the ground shakes, and he stops and covers his ears. It's working. I'm starting a battle playlist. Message me your songs.

beats.headline: A map from Burcu, slammed shut
beats.text: Inside the Madness castle Carl finds the crawler Burcu held beside Architect Houston, and his message to her is refused and logged for the adjutant: planning with a non-member. Then his Book of Voodoo updates with an entry from her. She is drawing a map of the surgical theatre, a line of Xs marked Fireball traps, and starting to write something about Houston, when it slams shut on its own. The accompanying warning: this is still cheating, you clown. Nice try. It is meant for something else.

beats.headline: Three emergency action items
beats.text: Warlord Agatha of the War Mage Rebellion has proposed three emergency action items. One: full access to the warlord system and the right to claim thrones. Granted, and something they already had. Two: full use of the Conscription spell, reaching unaffiliated players. Granted. Three: in the Peeling Phase, revert to the original Faction Wars rule, under which a defeated team's warlords and soldiers die. Granted, with a caveat: every affiliated soldier and warlord still on the field drops dead the moment the team is defeated. Then the Rebellion occupied Team Retribution's throne room.

beats.headline: Joined to a changeling
beats.text: His robes are gone, and so is his mask. Architect Houston is on his back on his own surgical table, and above him the arms of his machine, the Grease Monkey, hold the peeled-open corpse of a changeling named Namico. The machine is connecting the two of them. The System's note on it adds that Houston is prime of the Viceroys because he has made the most discoveries, most of them with this machine. Burcu lies bound on the next table, alive. Eight chained traps ring the room, and his death sets them off. Stay back, he tells Crawler Carl. This is my life's work. I'm almost there.

beats.headline: Died on his own table
beats.text: For the record. Crawler Carl crosses the theater by jumping from table to table. Houston begs him not to press the switch: the changelings are the key to the Beautiful Place, and it was right under their mandibles all along. Carl puts Burcu to sleep and frees her. As Houston's health drains, he sobs that he has found it, that it is really it. Carl throws a healing potion at his head, and he screams at what that has done. Burcu's table tips. Carl's bare feet touch the floor. You don't know what you've done, Houston says, and the traps fire. Credit for the kill: Warlord Carl.

beats.headline: Houston's table
beats.text: Houston is on his own table, joining himself to a dead changeling, and the traps on the balcony will burn the room if anyone steps on the floor or he dies. I jump table to table, put Burcu to sleep, and hit her bindings. Then the table tips and she hits the floor, and so do I. The traps fire. I phase through Houston, and something in the machine spins with me and wears Li Jun's face. Thank you for giving me more time with my sister and my best friend. Houston is dead. Burcu is dead. The Madness is defeated.

beats.headline: A white one, pocketed
beats.text: In the surgical theatre of the Madness castle, the fourth table is empty and drenched in blood, and a cleaner bot of the same model as the crew's own, painted solid white, is slurping it off the floor. Carl lands on that table, slips in the blood and goes flat on his back. The bot shrieks, beeps and comes at him. He apologises, grabs it in both hands, feels the buzz that means it will go in his inventory, and puts it there, somewhat to his own surprise.

beats.headline: Into the Madness castle
beats.text: Carl and I go deeper into the castle while the great ball of crawlers rolls toward it, and on the way we take two crawlers who did not choose to fight us, conscripted, and leave them bound and unharmed behind us. In the surgical theatre at the back is Architect Houston, midway through joining himself to a changeling's body, with a crawler strapped to the table beside him. I hold the doorway. Carl interrupts the procedure.

beats.headline: A gold coin for Mr. Jefferson
beats.text: The last mercenary meets Mr. Jefferson and flies into the wall, and bursts into a scatter of coins, which is something that happens when a man is ended by a sock. Gonk is chewing a guard she has on her horns. I dismount and look over the coins. One is still spinning. I catch it up, kiss it, open the sock and drop it in. Carl says he thought they were all nickels in there. I am muttering to myself, and I do not answer him.

beats.headline: The Peeling Phase
beats.text: When the Madness falls, the battlefield conditions are met. Larracos is no longer safe. The city is open, and the first team to take the castle wins; the announcement adds that only one team can win and that alliances will not matter. The adjudication closes at the same moment: no cheating by any warlord. The War Mage Rebellion was to be kept out of Larracos until the Peeling Phase, which is now, so the ruling is moot and has given them standing.

beats.headline: He marks the princess
beats.text: Harpocrates marks Crawler Princess Donut for death. Crawler Li Jun puts himself between the god and the cat, and does not walk away from it. Note for the record that a mark from a deity is not a threat, it is a scheduling entry, and this one now has a name in the margin that was not there this morning.

beats.headline: Speaker number eleven
beats.text: Crawler Li Jun is dead. Harpocrates had marked Princess Donut for death and was closing on her tower before her rolling ball could reach its destination. Li Jun had a plan: speaker number eleven, still on the back of a cart, every other speaker muted, playing the song he had sent her. He told his sister he would jump before the god caught him. His last message to her asked her to protect Zhang, to be kind, and promised to tell their mother she said hello. The next message from him arrived marked as from a deceased crawler.

beats.headline: Defeated in their own castle
beats.text: The Madness castle is small, about the size of a supermarket, with its barracks sunk into the ground and a garage door at the back painted the colour of the wall. Crawler Carl lifts it. Bigs sits in the empty throne room, and the six-hour clock starts. It does not need to run. Architect Houston dies in his surgical theater next door, and the notices arrive in order: the warlord has fallen, the Madness has been defeated, and all its assets are awarded to the Princess Posse. Larracos is no longer safe.

beats.headline: What the adjutants think she is
beats.text: Two readings are on file. Rosetta's, privately: the woman with a knack for vanishing and reappearing is not the harmless kind of residual but the rarer kind, closer to the Nebulars who worship the Eulogist, and so an enemy of the Apothecary. Fopsy's, aloud, to Victory: she is trying to end the ascendency game quickly, because with no crawlers left the system shuts down and hibernates, and she may believe the local AI now threatens the Eulogist. He does not know how she enlisted the war mages. Victory doubts they are assisting each other at all.

beats.headline: Sharing a command he did not ask for
beats.text: We hold the castle at Larracos. Six hours more and the floor is ours. That should be the whole of the announcement. Instead the system lists two warlords of the War Mage Rebellion, and only one of them is mine. Agatha. Co-warlord. I did not bring this rebellion this far to share its title, least of all with her, and I have not hidden what I think of that. I will hold the castle. I will not pretend to be pleased.

beats.headline: Two warlords for one rebellion
beats.text: The War Mage Rebellion holds the castle at Larracos, and six hours on the clock decides the floor. I run alongside Carl and give him what I have, which is less than he wants. Agatha has been named co-warlord beside Akuma, much as Ferdinand was added beside Juice Box, and nobody on that team anticipated it. Akuma does not like her. Their motivations are unclear, even to me.

beats.headline: Two meteors
beats.text: Two meteors came out of Larracos across the dark toward the ball. A third light, burning black and purple, intercepted both: struck the first, carried its momentum into the second and knocked it off course. The explosion showed what it was. Subject, injured in the blast, pivoted, fell out of sight and left a streak of purple smoke. The deflected meteor looped and went into the ball anyway. When the ball began to roll toward Larracos, subject rose again from wherever she had fallen and, after bobbing in the air a moment, followed it.

beats.headline: I trust her
beats.text: Victory asks what Donut's plan is. She hasn't told me, and no, I'm not going to question her. I trust her. Then two meteors come out of Larracos at the ball, and a woman is spat out of it: Nami, the pilot of Eris, ejected by a war mage from inside. Samantha reports another mage conscripting Yarilo with a potion. They are recruiting gods. I throw a healing potion onto the ball instead of a bomb, tell Donut to keep it intact and roll it toward the city, and run.

beats.headline: What Imani carries
beats.text: For the file, by the most private route available. Imani gives Chris a quick hug with her wings, not her arms, and he reaches up as if to touch her face and stops just short. When Crawler Carl is bound for a moment to the minds around him, he catches a glimpse of Imani's: she is in love with Chris, and Carl had no idea. She loves his simplicity. His quiet kindness. Clay-ton, his bodyguard since the Hunting Grounds, has become his inseparable friend; the two sit side by side and grunt at one another.

beats.headline: Traded at the Midnight Market
beats.text: Fopsy, the Dream's adjutant, reads it off his menus while Victory swears beside him. The war mages did not keep the Gate of the Feral Gods. They traded it to a minion at the Midnight Market, in exchange for five hell-kissed conscription potions, level 18, strong enough to take most gods, though not sponsored ones. That explains why Eris's pilot had to be ejected first. Victory's observation is that such things always leak into the market. The Gate, as of now, is somewhere else.

beats.headline: We need that gate back
beats.text: We need to move on the war mages now. They have the Gate. I do not understand why they are not allied with the other NPCs, and I do not understand why that Residual is their warlord. We do not know their plans. Rosetta is ready to let them win and be done with it. I am not done yet. Rosetta, you are the most stubborn person I have ever known. Trust me in this. We need that gate back, and we need to move before the defensive towers spin up.

beats.headline: Annie, in the dream
beats.text: Days ago, in the dream potion, Carl lands in my dream instead of his own, our hands fused together. A children's hospital in Iceland. Fannar, my ex, arrives to tell them the truth, and the woman denies my adoption, and I scream into my fist in a bathroom stall. Then I go to Annie. Brain cancer. She died alone. Nobody told me, until I met a nurse in a park who said she passed a few weeks ago, as if it did not matter. It is my worst memory and my favourite. I love Daniel. I tell Carl I love him and Donut more.

beats.headline: My brother's eye
beats.text: Donut, do not break the ball apart. Donut asks where I am. I was installing my brother's eye into myself. I also stopped the mage who was going for Harpocrates. I am not strong enough yet to stop the god on my own. The deflector towers have paused him, and he will push past them to reach Donut. I suggest you run.

beats.headline: A second atrocity
beats.text: The ball reaches the field of corpses and I cast You're Not Done Yet, tower-enhanced, on all of them at once. The system calls it another Atrocity and me a naughty kitty. Thousands of skins come up and go looking for the Dream and the Reaver soldiers inside the ball. Then I start hitting it with Magic Missile to break it open, and Carl and Li Na both tell me to stop. Our friends are in there, Carl, with fleshers crawling all over them. He wants it kept whole and rolled toward the city. So I set it rolling toward Larracos.

beats.headline: Next in line, if the yacht goes
beats.text: Succession, by Rosetta Thagra's arithmetic. Stalwart is dead, which makes one of his children king, and those children are aboard a yacht Rosetta's side has agreed to destroy in exchange for a pin number. If that is done, the Skull Empire falls to subject, provided she is still alive somewhere on Earth's surface. If she is not, it goes to the Maestro, disowned or not. Rosetta feels ill about the children.

beats.headline: The job is done
beats.text: Victory tells me the money arrived, enough for two ships. If York does his duty and shoots down that yacht, our part is finished. There are children on that yacht, orc children, and one of them is king now that Stalwart is dead. I think about Brooks, whom Rust pulled through the glass and cut in half, and about the whip. Does revenge bring anyone back? Justice Light says we need the gate. I trust Porthus. I do not trust the Apothecary, and I trust Agatha less. Comrades, sound off. We fight.

beats.headline: I didn't kill him
beats.text: Their dreams are colliding, and I come into this one, the man and the woman watching a memory of her with a baby. I push through the memory and put my face right up to his. I didn't kill him. I didn't kill him. I did not, I did not, I did not. My eye is open and shining and it does nothing to him. And then a new voice speaks behind me: bitch, you swallowed me whole.

beats.headline: Finishing means a shutdown
beats.text: Fopsy, the adjutant, sets out what finishing the game triggers. Once the Ascendency is considered finished with no crawlers left, the system's shutdown and hibernation sequence starts automatically: a hard-coded limit that allows elemental reclamation before the AI is woken again. With the AI spreading, that is an alternative to the fail-safe. Which is why, Fopsy suspects, the residual running the war mage team wants the crawlers zeroed and the Ascendency over as fast as possible.

beats.headline: Worshipped by the Nebulars
beats.text: Rosetta turns over what Porthus told her when she asked about the Apothecary's motives: he could not say, because if she knew and entered the dungeon, the local AI might learn, and then, in time, the Eulogist would know. Isn't the Eulogist dead, she had asked. Now she places Agatha as the rarer kind of residual, more in line with the Nebulars, who worship the Eulogist, and therefore the enemy of the Apothecary. Fopsy, the adjutant, adds a theory: the residual wants the crawl ended fast because she now believes the local AI is a threat to the Eulogist.

beats.headline: They conscript gods
beats.text: Hold the castle at Larracos for six hours and the floor is theirs. They trade the gate away at the Midnight Market for five Hell-Kissed Potions of Conscription and put Yarilo on the field beside them. The system hands the rebellion two co-warlords, and the two of them cannot stand each other.

beats.headline: Two co-warlords, and a god on a leash
beats.text: They hold the Larracos castle, and six hours of holding it would take the floor. Baroness Victory reads out two co-warlords, Akuma and Agatha, and Akuma is not pleased about it. The Gate goes onto the Midnight Market and comes back as potions, and the potions conscript Yarilo. Fopsy, adjutant for the Dream, has a theory: that Agatha now thinks the AI is a danger to the Eulogist and wants the ascendency game over so it can be shut down.

beats.headline: Conscripted with potions
beats.text: The War Mage Rebellion has taken the Larracos castle and holds it for six hours to win, and they have gone shopping for reinforcements. They conscript Yarilo, paid for with potions they traded for the gate on the Midnight Market. Somewhere in that chain a god of lust became a line item. Fopsy has a theory about why Agatha is doing any of this, and I will let her explain it, because I have a god to move.

beats.headline: The yacht, if he does his duty
beats.text: Filed from Rosetta's side of the deal. In exchange for a pin number, the Pacifist Network agreed to destroy an orc yacht with several children aboard, and with Stalwart dead, one of those children is the new king of the Skull Empire. The job falls to York, in orbit. Rosetta's assessment: assuming he actually does his duty and does not decide to write a poem instead. She also names York among those she hopes survive whatever comes next.

beats.headline: Where is my husband
beats.text: Carl comes running across the courtyard shouting about generators and railings and waffle makers. I turn human and grab his shoulder. Where is Louis? Where is my husband? He is not answering me. Carl says he is alive but in trouble, and someone is trying to rescue him, and it is Samantha. So I tell Samantha. I have a form that is a fleshmancer. Bring my husband back in one piece and she can have any body she wants. I know who she really is.

beats.headline: Anne of Green Gables
beats.text: Ruby's in my lap with her head on my shoulder and I'm reading her Anne of Green Gables. The bot's listening too. Carl bursts in with the shark, the meatball, a slug and two crying women from some other party, and stops, and looks at us like he wants to say something. He doesn't. He dials the Larracos gate on the door, and they go.

beats.headline: A hall pass night
beats.text: The Reaver castle is empty except for the robot doggies, who are everywhere, and the hallways are super small and complicated, and I am looking. Then Juice Box says she has a fleshmancer form and I can have any body I desire if I bring her husband back in one piece. Throw in a hall pass night with Louis and you have a deal. She says she knows who I really am and I've lost my mind. Okay, it's a deal. But if Louis's passions get the best of him, I won't make any apologies.

beats.headline: Cleaved in half at the door
beats.text: Final service entry. Bomo was guarding the base of the Nest tower with Toyotomi and a detachment of mages when a crawler with a dog came in. Toyotomi reported it. Bomo reported that he would stop her. Both reports came back marked from the deceased. All of them were cleaved in half with a spell. Bomo will supposedly regenerate on the tenth floor. The clients no longer hold his contract. Crawler Carl does not know if he will see him again.

beats.headline: Shit Just Hit
beats.text: Toyotomi and Bomo go quiet, and I don't think. I drink my last Levitation potion at the railing and go straight up. The plan was to aim carefully at the Piccadilly. Instead I drop an entire inventory folder called Shit Just Hit: about twenty Waffle Makers, two No Disassembles, a pair of cheese cutters, some five hundred hob-lobbers and more dynamite than I can count. My Walk on Air runs out three quarters of the way to the lip, and I drop. The generator goes, and so does every window in the area, and the city's defence system wakes up. One tower locks onto me.

beats.headline: Kitten is in trouble
beats.text: Crawler Carl dived into a ditch in Shanty Town to get out of a defence tower's line of fire. Subject jumped in beside him, shaking, tail scorched from a near miss, bowler hat askew, and asked why he was lying down on the job, because Kitten is in trouble. Carl told him that going into the tower would get him killed and that Juice Box needs him alive. Subject reported that Juice Box hates him and is meaner than Bill. Carl told him that he, and Donut, want him alive too.

beats.headline: Brewed in the Nothing
beats.text: File note on the Hell-Kissed Potion of Conscription, level 18, of which Crawler Carl now holds a duplicated copy: it will work against pretty much any unaffiliated entity, most deities included. Most. It was brewed in the dark recesses of the Nothing by Krakaren Prime, who is said to yearn for domination and was banished there for it, and who prepares for a war she considers inevitable. The in-dungeon version of Krakaren supplied these potions to the War Mages. The irony is noted.

beats.headline: Take it
beats.text: The front of my face is blood. I have gouged out my own eye and put my brother's in its place. Carl starts to say he is sorry. I stop him. I give him the potion he asked me to take off the dead war mage, or a copy of it: I used Jun's scroll of potion duplication. The original is for Harpocrates. Then I will save Zhang, Elle, Katia and the others before they too fall victim to your chaos. He says it could kill me. I go.

beats.headline: I don't want to play anymore
beats.text: I come up the tower for the dinosaur. That is justice. The cat throws barrels at Gus and he keeps sliding away from me, and I tell him to get back up. Then something hits me, and I tumble down the ramp with a crab, into the man. The crab holds me up in his claws and shouts at me to kowtow. I say please. I say I don't want to play anymore. The man breaks a bottle on my head, and it screams.

beats.headline: Donkey Kong
beats.text: Lucia is in the tower, coming up the stairs, shouting for Mongo, and Bomo and the others are dead. I cannot leave; there is a net. I tell Carl to get the war mages, because the castle is more important than me. He says he is coming and to do Donkey Kong. So I hit the switch, and the stairs turn into a ramp, and I roll barrels. The sleep barrel does not work. She crawls on the ceiling and blocks explosions. Mute does not work on her. I have a better idea. I summon Raul.

beats.headline: Scars we rarely choose
beats.text: The potion takes. Under Orders; she drops the frightened act, and I order her protections off. Two hundred player killer skulls. Twenty hunters. Her own game guide. I tell her I don't have one, and that with scars we rarely get to choose. I put on the Ring of Divine Suffering. Florin thinks there are kids trapped in that head. Maybe. The conscription ends with the floor and she keeps coming for the people I love. So I apologise for what I'm about to do. Then her voice changes, and I stop.

beats.headline: Conscripted
beats.text: Crawler Li Na conscripts Harpocrates. A god of silence, level 250, invulnerable on this floor, is now on a crawler's side of the board because a crawler had the paperwork to put him there. Two chapters of him rampaging across the territory, and the resolution is administrative. I would like it noted that I find this floor exhausting.

beats.headline: My name is Diah
beats.text: Sir. My name is Diah. Lucia is with Alexandro, and Alexandro is only here when the dogs are close. Wait until the dog is close, and Lucia will be back. Please, sir. We are in the dark, and it is so cold. Sometimes we hear them whispering. It's like a river runs through our room, and if we touch it, it hurts. When the dog wanders off, Lucia fades, and one of us takes over, and we can see again. We take turns. Sometimes it is day.

beats.headline: Another ally for the Eulogist
beats.text: The dog is dead, and I am on my knees, crying, pouring a pet potion on the dinosaur, whose throat is open. You did it, I tell him. Then I stand up. A blast from the tower goes past my head and I don't flinch. I tell the man he should have killed us both when there was still a connection. Now it's too late. Now the Eulogist has another ally in the dungeon, and he can't kill me. Not unless he wants all the children of Earth to die. I walk off.

beats.headline: Dog is BAD
beats.text: MOTHER says NO. Mongo goes down slide. Dog. Dog is BAD. Bite dog. Dog is spikes. Spikes in mouth. HURTS. Dark. Girl pours drink on Mongo. Mongo not dead.

beats.headline: Wrecking Ball
beats.text: Carl cast Hi-Yo Silver a second time and called Wrecking Ball. Subject, much bigger than when last seen, came over the ridge and rolled toward him at speed, with Gustavo 3 and Mongo directly between them. The dog had the unconscious dinosaur by the neck. The back half of Gustavo 3, the second of Lucia Mar's two rottweilers, left in a red mist. Subject stopped inches from Carl's face. Carl called him a good boy. A defence tower's bolt then hit subject squarely. He barely moved. He giggled.

beats.headline: Another ally in the dungeon
beats.text: Mongo lies with his throat torn open, and Lucia Mar kneels over him, sobbing, pouring a pet healing potion. Then her posture changes, and she stands to her full height. A gale-tower blast misses her head by inches and she does not flinch. You should have killed us both when there was still a connection, she tells Crawler Carl. Now the Eulogist has another ally in the dungeon, and now Carl cannot kill her. Not unless he wants all the children of Earth to die. She walks off.

beats.headline: What sort of monster am I
beats.text: Florin's old dictionary, the one with the bullet hole, defines atrocity as an act of fiendish cruelty. The system calls Donut's War Crime spell an Atrocity, and maybe the real cruelty was giving it to her at all, out of the Legendary box we got for killing D'Nadia. I've never before prayed for my own plan to fail while needing it to work. If she doesn't cast it, we likely don't survive the coming hours. If she does, what then? She says she's ready. If I let her, what sort of monster am I?

beats.headline: A tattoo for the cat
beats.text: Rosetta, Milk and Edgar come up into the tower to work on Princess Donut. She is getting a tattoo, and given who does the ink around here, a tattoo is not decoration. It is a thing that will get up off her and fight when she calls it.

beats.headline: The count
beats.text: Zev puts a number on it: about 120,000 children, give or take. Their bodies are in the kinder facility on the surface; the rest of them is bound up in her head, and if she goes, they may all go.

beats.headline: Level seventy-four
beats.text: I am in my ghillie suit at the parapet, sniping. The war mage atop that death ray tower is not so tough with his head blown off. Carl says to focus on the towers hitting the Nest, and then he holds out his arms, and I blink and jump into them and go round his neck like I used to when he came home from work. I went up this tower at level 65. I am 74 now. My Magic Missile is level fifteen, and it tripled in power. And Rend saved my boy.

beats.headline: Get fucked, Prime Minister
beats.text: I run all the way up the Nest with Milk behind me and Edgar strapped to my back, which, comrade, is significantly heavier than he looks. I would not have come into the dungeon if I had known how much running there would be. Next time we build a tower this high, we add an elevator. Fopsy is in the corner, observing. Former prime minister. Get fucked. But I am glad he is here to witness this. Donut needs a spell she does not have, at level eight, to go with War Crime.

beats.headline: Trampled by two gods
beats.text: The fight between the gods passes through the other side of Shanty Town, and then it is simply gone. Most of the defensive towers the Posse paid for, and never really got to use, are trampled. The Nest tower and Li Na's abandoned synergy towers still stand, drawing a lot of fire. Every other building is flattened.

beats.headline: Another name for the center system
beats.text: Crawler Carl adds up where he has heard the word: in connection with the Nebular cult, as Agatha's boss or something, from Paulie, who plainly hated it, from Fopsy, and now from Lucia Mar. He asks Zev. The Eulogist is another name for the AI in the center system, Zev says, and nobody knows for certain how it is connected. Five minutes ago they thought the glitch would self-correct; now they think that if Lucia goes, the children go with her. About 120,000 of them. Give or take a few.

beats.headline: Agatha walks off her post
beats.text: The system deems Warlord Agatha to have abandoned her post, and nobody, the adjutants included, can say why. She is removed, and Akuma is named sole warlord of the rebellion.

beats.headline: Taken off the board by another god
beats.text: Feral God Yarilo has been removed from this floor by Harpocrates, acting under the direction of Crawler Li Na. He came through a gate, chased an AI the length of a warzone, changed sides for a crate of potions, and finished at the hands of the god who had come through that same gate ahead of him. Everything down here becomes somebody's equipment, the gods included.

beats.headline: I should not be telling you
beats.text: Okay, so. The liaisons want to interview Lucia now the dog is dead, for at least an hour. We assumed her getting in was a glitch, and we wanted to kick her back out. Now the AI says it cannot extract her. It is not all the children, Carl. Just the ones who tried to get into the dungeon, and only the ones in one wing, on the surface in the kinder facility. We think if she goes, they all go. I should not be telling you any of this. About a hundred and twenty thousand.

beats.headline: The long description of War Crime
beats.text: Rosetta changes the plan at the top of the Nest. Bijanbi, a Dinner Bell variant from a cleric who fell defending the FUPA, and Wall of Fire, both through Donut's War Crime; the fleshers already wrapped round the enemy are the finisher. Oh. Oh hell. I have the spell's long description in my scratch pad. Health to one percent. Only on the Scolopendra levels, three casts, ever, and it can't kill anyone directly. The last part, which only I seem to see, is two hundred mercenaries paralysed and on fire for two weeks. I agree with Rosetta anyway.

beats.headline: Not in his castle
beats.text: By the time the Nest tower is stabilised, it is clear Warlord Fang is not in the Reaver castle. The castle is abandoned except for its security system, which is a bunch of robots, and a gravity-magic dragon circling overhead. Crawler Carl casts Ping and finds both remaining Bloc warlords, Epitome Tagg and Warlord Fang, inside the rolling ball of bodies. Rosetta is blunt about it: Fang especially is difficult to locate, worse than a changeling.

beats.headline: A tattoo on the right flank
beats.text: Rosetta says it has to be a tattoo, with Milk etching words of power over it, and Edgar wants a spot on my backside shaved as big as his foot. I never agreed to a tattoo! Carl says I don't have to, and nobody will fault me. I tell him about the scars. I hoped none of them would be on the outside. He says if I choose it, it is a badge of honour. Fine. Only if he gets a matching one. And not a tramp stamp. Then I ask Edgar what he is drawing. A dog.

beats.headline: Classic Lucia Mar
beats.text: The net holding Carl and Princess Donut in the tower is not new. I suspect it is from before. This is classic Lucia Mar. Fopsy's reading is the sound one: a personal net from a scroll, and a secondary spell behind it, waiting for a power source. It is Power Siphon, drawing on the jewels in the active towers of Larracos, and it ends when those towers stop firing or when she turns it off. She did turn off every active spell she had, Carl. This one activated after she left.

beats.headline: Waiting on top of the Nest
beats.text: On top of the Nest, Donut tells me Li Na said Li Jun's death was her fault. She says Li Na isn't wrong. Lucia killed Bomo. If something goes wrong and we lose everybody, it's on her. I tell her they put us here; this is their war. Then she says she and Katia have a plan, that Bautista can't know, and that Katia told her not to tell me because I'll Carl it up. The rest she sends by message: she got a benefactor box when I wasn't looking. Then Li Na says go.

beats.headline: Stayfast ink, and a pen
beats.text: Milk tells Carl she once wrote her recipes in a book, then switched to a different ink to share them with a wider group, and everything written after the switch faded away. Some of her best recipes were gone when they were needed most, and she calls that her fault. Rosetta grunts. Then Milk hands him Stayfast Ink, 825 ml, which nothing will ever make fade, and an Adept's fountain pen, and reminds them that anything Carl writes in the Book of Voodoo goes to everybody who already has it. Then she jumps from the tower and glides away.

beats.headline: A dog that licks itself
beats.text: It's done, and I have received two very rude achievements, one calling me a traitor. But I did get the spell, at level two. It came from a god called Wepwawet, in the Court of Nekhebit, and I can worship Odette now too! Cover it up. It is getting lasered off on the next floor. Not yet, says Milk, and writes words of power over it, which stings. Apparently the dog underneath lifts its leg and starts licking itself. I am not looking. The spell has gone up to level fifteen.

beats.headline: Free, and full of news
